body.text: // Daśabhūmikasūtram //
body.translated_text: The <s>Daśabhūmikasūtra</s> (Sūtra on the Ten Stages)

body.text: 1 pramuditā nāma prathamā bhūmiḥ /
body.translated_text: 1. The first stage, called <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful).

body.text:
evaṃ mayā śrutam / ekasmin samaye bhagavān paranirmitavaśavartiṣu devabhuvaneṣu viharati sma acirābhisaṃbuddho dvitīye saptāhe vaśavartino devarājasya vimāne maṇiratnagarbhe prabhāsvare prāsāde mahatā bodhisattvagaṇena sārdhaṃ sarvairavaivartikairekajātipratibaddhaiḥ / yaduta anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāvanyonyalokadhātusaṃnipatitaiḥ / sarvaiḥ sarvabodhisattvajñānaviṣayagocarapratilabdhavihāribhiḥ sarvatathāgatajñānaviṣayapraveśāvatārāpratiprasrabdhagocaraiḥ sarvajagatparipācanavinayayathākālakṣaṇādhiṣṭhānasarvakriyāsaṃdarśanakuśalaiḥ sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānābhinirhārāpratiprasrabdhagocaraiḥ kalpārthakṣetracaryāsaṃvāsibhiḥ sarvabodhisattvapuṇyajñānarddhisaṃbhārasuparipūrṇākṣayasarvajagadupajīvyatāpratipannaiḥ sarvabodhisattvaprajñopāyaparamapāramitāprāptaiḥ saṃsāranirvāṇamukhasaṃdarśanakuśalaiḥ bodhisattvacaryopādānāvyavacchinnaiḥ sarvabodhisattvadhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpatyabhijñājñānavikrīḍitābhijñāsarvakriyāsaṃdarśanakuśalaiḥ sarvabodhisattvarddhibalavaśitāprāptānabhisaṃskāracittakṣaṇasarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalopasaṃkramaṇapūrvaṃgamakathāpuruṣaiḥ sarvatathāgatadharmacakrasaṃdhāraṇavipulabuddhapūjopasthānābhyutthitaiḥ sarvabodhisattvakarmasamādānasamatāprayogasarvalokadhātukāyapratibhāsaprāptaiḥ sarvadharmadhātvasaṅgasvararutaghoṣānuravitasarvatryadhvāsaṅgacittajñānaviṣayaspharaṇaiḥ sarvabodhisattvaguṇapratipattisuparipūrṇānabhilāpyakalpādhiṣṭhānasaṃprakāśanāparikṣīṇaguṇavarṇanirdeśakaiḥ / yadidamvajragarbheṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / ratnagarbheṇa ca / padmagarbheṇa ca / śrīgarbheṇa ca / padmaśrīgarbheṇa ca / ādityagarbheṇa ca / sūryagarbheṇa ca / kṣitigarbheṇa ca / śaśivimalagarbheṇa ca / sarvavyūhālaṃkārapratibhāsasaṃdarśanagarbheṇa ca / jñānavairocanagarbheṇa ca / ruciraśrīgarbheṇa ca / candanaśrīgarbheṇa ca / puṣpaśrīgarbheṇa ca / kusumaśrīgarbheṇa ca / utpalaśrīgarbheṇa ca / devaśrīgarbheṇa ca / puṇyaśrīgarbheṇa ca / anāvaraṇajñānaviśuddhigarbheṇa ca / guṇaśrīgarbheṇa ca / nārāyaṇaśrīgarbheṇa ca / amalagarbheṇa ca / vimalagarbheṇa ca / vicitrapratibhānālaṃkāragarbheṇa ca / mahāraśmijālāvabhāsagarbheṇa ca / vimalaprabhāsaśrītejorājagarbheṇa ca / sarvalakṣaṇapratimaṇḍitaviśuddhiśrīgarbheṇa
ca / vajrārciḥśrīvatsālaṃkāragarbheṇa ca / jyotirjvalanārciḥśrīgarbheṇa ca / nakṣatrarājaprabhāvabhāsagarbheṇa ca / gaganakośānāvaraṇajñānagarbheṇa ca / anāvaraṇasvaramaṇḍalamadhuranirghoṣagarbheṇa ca / dhāraṇīmukhasarvajagatpraṇidhisaṃdhāraṇagarbheṇa ca / sāgaravyūhagarbheṇa ca /
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling in the divine realms of the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, having recently attained perfect awakening, in the second week, in the palace of <s>Vaśavartin</s>, the king of gods, in the jewel-treasury, the radiant mansion, together with a great assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, all non-retrogressing, bound by a single birth—that is, those who had assembled from various world-realms for unsurpassed perfect awakening. All had attained and abided in the domain of the sphere of all <s>Bodhisattva</s> knowledge; all had unceasing activity in entering the sphere of all <s>Tathāgata</s> knowledge; all were skilled in displaying all activities of empowerment at the proper time and occasion for ripening and disciplining all beings; all had unceasing activity in accomplishing the vows of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; all dwelt in the activities of fields [serving] the purposes of aeons; all had undertaken inexhaustible service to all beings through the perfect fulfillment of the accumulations of merit, knowledge, and supernatural power of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; all had attained the supreme perfection of the wisdom and skillful means of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; all were skilled in displaying the gates of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>; all had uninterrupted engagement in <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct; all were skilled in displaying all activities of sport in the <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, <s>samādhis</s>, attainments, superknowledges, and knowledges of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; all, having attained the supernatural powers, strengths, and masteries of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, were foremost speakers who, without mental fabrication and in a single mind-moment, were preceded by approaching the assembly-circles of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; all had arisen through sustaining the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> and through vast <s>Buddha</s>-worship and attendance; all had attained the reflection of their bodies in all world-realms through the practice of equanimity in undertaking the activities of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; all pervaded the sphere of unobstructed knowledge of mind throughout all three times with the unobstructed voices, sounds, and reverberations of all <s>dharmadhātu</s>; all were speakers who described the inexhaustible qualities, perfectly fulfilling the practice of all <s>Bodhisattva</s> virtues, illuminating the empowerment of inexpressible aeons. Namely: the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s>, <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, <s>Padmagarbha</s>, <s>Śrīgarbha</s>, <s>Padmaśrīgarbha</s>, <s>Ādityagarbha</s>, <s>Sūryagarbha</s>, <s>Kṣitigarbha</s>, <s>Śaśivimalagarbha</s>, <s>Sarvavyūhālaṃkārapratibhāsasaṃdarśanagarbha</s>, <s>Jñānavairocanagarbha</s>, <s>Ruciraśrīgarbha</s>, <s>Candanaśrīgarbha</s>, <s>Puṣpaśrīgarbha</s>, <s>Kusumaśrīgarbha</s>, <s>Utpalaśrīgarbha</s>, <s>Devaśrīgarbha</s>, <s>Puṇyaśrīgarbha</s>, <s>Anāvaraṇajñānaviśuddhigarbha</s>, <s>Guṇaśrīgarbha</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇaśrīgarbha</s>, <s>Amalagarbha</s>, <s>Vimalagarbha</s>, <s>Vicitrapratibhānālaṃkāragarbha</s>, <s>Mahāraśmijālāvabhāsagarbha</s>, <s>Vimalaprabhāsaśrītejorājagarbha</s>, <s>Sarvalakṣaṇapratimaṇḍitaviśuddhiśrīgarbha</s>, <s>Vajrārciḥśrīvatsālaṃkāragarbha</s>, <s>Jyotirjvalanārciḥśrīgarbha</s>, <s>Nakṣatrarājaprabhāvabhāsagarbha</s>, <s>Gaganakośānāvaraṇajñānagarbha</s>, <s>Anāvaraṇasvaramaṇḍalamadhuranirghoṣagarbha</s>, <s>Dhāraṇīmukhasarvajagatpraṇidhisaṃdhāraṇagarbha</s>, <s>Sāgaravyūhagarbha</s>,

body.text:
meruśrīgarbheṇa ca / sarvaguṇaviśuddhigarbheṇa ca / tathāgataśrīgarbheṇa ca / buddhaśrīgarbheṇa ca / vimukticandreṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / evaṃpramukhair
aparimāṇāprameyāsaṃkhyeyācintyātulyāmāpyānantāparyantāsīmāprāptānabhilāpyānabhilāpyairbodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ nānābuddhakṣetrasaṃnipatitairvajragarbhabodhisattvapūrvaṃgamaiḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Meruśrīgarbha</s>, <s>Sarvaguṇaviśuddhigarbha</s>, <s>Tathāgataśrīgarbha</s>, <s>Buddhaśrīgarbha</s>, and the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Vimukticandra</s>—together with these and other immeasurable, incalculable, innumerable, inconceivable, incomparable, unfathomable, infinite, boundless, limitless, and inexpressible <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who had assembled from various <s>Buddha</s>-fields, led by <s>Vajragarbha Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: atha khalu vajragarbho bodhisattvayāṃ velāyāṃ buddhānubhāvena mahāyānaprabhāsaṃ nāma bodhisattvasamādhiṃ samāpadyate sma / samanantarasamāpannaśca vajragarbho bodhisattva imaṃ mahāyānaprabhāsaṃ nāma bodhisattvasamādhim,atha tāvadeva daśasu dikṣu daśabuddhakṣetrakoṭiparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ lokadhātūnāmapareṇa daśabuddhakṣetrakoṭiparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatā mukhānyupardaṣayāmāsuṃ yadidaṃ vajragarbhasamanāmakā eva / te cainaṃ buddhā bhagavanta evamūcuḥ - sādhu sādhu bho jinaputra, yastvamimaṃ mahāyānaprabhāsaṃ bodhisattvasamādhiṃ samāpadyase / api tu khalu punastvaṃ kulaputra, amī daśasu dikṣu daśabuddhakṣetrakoṭiparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ lokadhātūnāmapareṇa daśabuddhakṣetrakoṭiparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatā adhitiṣṭhanti sarve vajragarbhasamanāmānaḥ asyaiva bhagavato vairocanasya pūrvapraṇidhānādhiṣṭhānena tava ca puṇyajñānaviśeṣeṇa sarvabodhisattvānāṃ ca acintyabuddhadharmālokaprabhāvanājñānabhūmyavatāraṇāya / sarvakuśalamūlasaṃgrahaṇāya / sarvabuddhadharmanirdeśāya / asaṃbhinnajñānavyavadānāya / sarvalokadharmānupalepāya / lokottarakuśalamūlapariśodhanāya / acintyajñānaviṣayādhigamāya / yāvatsarvajñānaviṣayādhigamāya / yadidaṃ daśānāṃ bodhisattvabhūmīnāmārambhapratilambhāya / yathāvadbodhisattvabhūmivyavasthānanirdeśāya / sarvabuddhadharmādhyālambanāya / anāsravadharmapravibhāgavibhāvanāya / suvicitavicayamahāprajñālokakauśalyāya / sunistīritakauśalyajñānamukhāvatāraṇāya / yathārhasthānāntaraprabhāvanāmandapratibhānālokāya / mahāpratisaṃvidbhūministīraṇāya / bodhicittasmṛtyasaṃpramoṣāya / sarvasattvadhātuparipācanāya / sarvatrānugataviniścayakauśalyapratilambhāya / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra pratibhātu te 'yaṃ dharmālokamukhaprabhedakauśalyadharmaparyāyo buddhānubhāvena tathāgatajñānālokādhiṣṭhānena svakuśalamūlapariśodhanāya dharmadhātusuparyavadāpanāya sattvadhātvanugrahāya dharmakāyajñānaśārīrāya sarvabuddhābhiṣekasaṃpratīcchanāya sarvalokābhyudgatātmabhāvasaṃdarśanāya sarvalokagatisamatikramāya lokottadharmagatipariśodhanāya sarvajñajñānaparipūraṇāya //
body.translated_text: Then at that time, <s>Vajragarbha Bodhisattva</s>, through the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, entered into the <s>Bodhisattva samādhi</s> called <s>Mahāyānaprabhāsa</s> (Radiance of the Great Vehicle). Immediately upon <s>Vajragarbha Bodhisattva</s>'s entering this <s>Bodhisattva samādhi</s> called <s>Mahāyānaprabhāsa</s>, at that very moment, from beyond world-realms equal in number to the atoms in ten billion <s>Buddha</s>-fields in each of the ten directions, <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal in number to the atoms in ten billion <s>Buddha</s>-fields manifested their faces—all bearing the very same name <s>Vajragarbha</s>. And those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, spoke to him thus: 'Well done, well done, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>! You have entered this <s>Bodhisattva samādhi</s> called <s>Mahāyānaprabhāsa</s>. Moreover, son of good family, these <s>Tathāgatas</s> from beyond world-realms equal in number to the atoms in ten billion <s>Buddha</s>-fields in each of the ten directions, all bearing the name <s>Vajragarbha</s>, empower you—through the power of the prior vows of this Blessed One <s>Vairocana</s>, through the distinction of your own merit and knowledge, and for the sake of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: for entry into the stages of the inconceivable illumination of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> and knowledge; for the gathering of all wholesome roots; for the exposition of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>; for the purification of undivided knowledge; for non-defilement by all worldly <s>dharmas</s>; for the purification of supramundane wholesome roots; for the attainment of the sphere of inconceivable knowledge; up to the attainment of the sphere of omniscient knowledge—namely, for the obtaining and commencement of the ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages; for the proper exposition of the establishment of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages; for reliance upon all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>; for the elucidation of the classification of undefiled <s>dharmas</s>; for the skill of the great light of wisdom through well-investigated discernment; for entry into the gates of well-articulated skill and knowledge; for the light of unfailing eloquence illuminating the stages of proper station; for the resolution of the stages of great analytical knowledge; for the non-forgetfulness of <s>bodhicitta</s>; for the ripening of the entire realm of beings; for the attainment of skill in definitive judgment that follows everywhere. Moreover, son of good family, let this <s>dharma</s>-discourse on the skill in the classification of the gates of <s>Dharma</s>-illumination be proclaimed by you, through the power of the <s>Buddhas</s>, through the empowerment of the light of <s>Tathāgata</s> knowledge, for the purification of your own wholesome roots, for the thorough purification of <s>dharmadhātu</s>, for the benefiting of the realm of beings, for the knowledge-body of the <s>Dharma</s>-body, for the acceptance of the consecration of all <s>Buddhas</s>, for the display of a self that has risen above all worlds, for transcending the courses of all worldly destinies, for the purification of the path of supramundane <s>dharma</s> destinies, and for the fulfillment of omniscient knowledge.'

body.text: atha khalu te buddhā bhagavanto vajragarbhasya bodhisattvasya anabhibhūtātmabhāvatāṃ copasaṃharanti sma / asaṅgapratibhānanirdeśatāṃ ca suviśobhitajñānavibhaktipraveśatāṃ ca smṛtyasaṃprabhoṣādhiṣṭhānatāṃ ca suviniścitamatikauśalyatāṃ ca sarvatrānugatabuddhyanutsargatāṃ ca samyaksaṃbuddhabalānavamṛdyatāṃ ca tathāgatavaiśāradyānavalīnatāṃ ca sarvajñajñānapratisaṃvidvibhāgadharmanayanistīraṇatāṃ ca sarvatathāgatasuvibhaktakāyavākcittālaṃkārābhinirhāratāṃ copasaṃharanti sma / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? yathāpi nāma asyaiva samādherdharmatāpratilambhena pūrvaṃ praṇidhānābhirhāreṇa ca supariśodhitādhyāśayatayā ca svavadātajñānamaṇḍalatayā ca susaṃbhṛtasaṃbhāratayā ca sukṛtaparikarmatayā
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, conferred upon <s>Vajragarbha Bodhisattva</s>: the state of an unconquerable self; the state of unobstructed eloquent exposition; the state of entry into the well-adorned divisions of knowledge; the state of empowerment of non-forgetfulness and mindfulness; the state of skill in well-determined understanding; the state of intelligence that follows everywhere and is never abandoned; the state of not being crushed by the powers of the Perfectly Awakened One; the state of not shrinking from the fearlessnesses of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; the state of resolution through the method of the <s>dharma</s> of analyzing the analytical knowledges of omniscient knowledge; and the state of accomplishing the adornment of body, speech, and mind of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> as well distributed. For what reason? Because, by virtue of having obtained the <s>dharmatā</s> of this very <s>samādhi</s>, through the prior accomplishment of vows, through the thorough purification of higher intention,

body.text: ca apramāṇasmṛtibhājanatayā ca prabhāsvarādhimuktiviśodhanatayā ca supratividvadhāraṇīmukhāsaṃbhedanatayā ca dharmadhātujñānamudrāsumudritatayā ca //
body.translated_text: through the clarity of one's own purified knowledge-maṇḍala, through the thorough gathering of accumulations, through the well-performed preparatory work, through being a vessel of immeasurable mindfulness, through the purification of luminous aspiration, through the unconfused well-analyzed gates of <s>dhāraṇī</s>, and through being well-sealed with the seal of <s>dharmadhātu</s> knowledge.

body.text: atha khalu te buddhā bhagavantastatrasthā eva ṛddhyanubhāvena dakṣiṇān pāṇīn prasārya vajragarbhasya bodhisattvasya śīrṣaṃ saṃpramārjayanti sma / samanantaraspṛṣṭaśca vajragarbho bodhisattvastairbuddhairbhagavadbhiḥ, atha tāvadeva samādhestasmād vyutthāya tān bodhisattvānāmantrayate sma - suviniścitamidaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvapraṇidhānamasaṃbhinnamanavalokyaṃ dharmadhātuvipulaṃ ākāśadhātuparyavasānamaparāntakoṭiniṣṭhaṃ sarvasattvadhātuparitrāṇam / yatra hi nāma bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvā atītānāmapi buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ jñānabhūmimavataranti, anāgatānāmapi buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ jñānabhūmimavataranti pratyutpannānāmapi buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ jñānabhūmimavataranti, tatra bhavanto jinaputrā daśa bodhisattvabhūmayo buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ jñānabhūmimavataranti, tatra bhavanto jinaputrāśca daśa bodhisattvabhūmayo 'tītānāgatapratyutpannairbuddhairbhagadbhirbhāṣitāśca bhāṣiṣyante ca bhāṣyante ca, yāḥ saṃdhāya ahaṃ evaṃ vadāmi / katamā daśa? yaduta pramuditā ca nāma bodhisattvabhūmiḥ / vimalā ca nāma / prabhākarī ca nāma / arciṣmatī ca nāma / sudurjayā ca nāma / abhimukhī ca nāma / dūraṃgamā ca nāma / acalā ca nāma / sādhumatī ca nāma / dharmameghā ca nāma bodhisattvabhūmiḥ / imā bhavanto jinaputrā daśa bodhisattvānāṃ bodhisattvabhūmayaḥ, yā atītānāgatapratyutpannaīrbuddhairbhagavadbhirbhāṣitāśca bhāṣiṣyante ca bhāṣyante ca / nāhaṃ bhavanto jinaputrāstaṃ buddhakṣetraprasaraṃ samanupaśyāmi, yatra tathāgatā imā daśa bodhisattvabhūmīrna prakāśayanti / tatkasya hetoḥ? sāmutkarṣiko 'yaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ bodhi(sattva)mārgapariśodhanadharmamukhāloko yadidaṃ daśabhūmiprabhedavyavasthānam / acintyamidaṃ bhavanto jinaputrāḥ sthānaṃ yadidaṃ bhūmijñānamiti //
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, remaining right there, extended their right hands through supernatural power and touched the head of <s>Vajragarbha Bodhisattva</s>. Immediately upon being touched by those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, <s>Vajragarbha Bodhisattva</s> arose from that <s>samādhi</s> and addressed those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: 'O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, this vow of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is well-determined, unbroken, unalterable, vast as <s>dharmadhātu</s>, extending to the boundary of the space-element, reaching to the final limit, protecting the entire realm of beings. For indeed, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> enter into the knowledge-stages of the <s>Buddhas</s> of the past, enter into the knowledge-stages of the <s>Buddhas</s> of the future, and enter into the knowledge-stages of the <s>Buddhas</s> of the present. There are, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages that enter into the knowledge-stages of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones. These ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages have been spoken, will be spoken, and are being spoken by the <s>Buddhas</s> of the past, future, and present. It is with reference to these that I speak thus. What are these ten? Namely: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage called <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful), that called <s>Vimalā</s> (Stainless), <s>Prabhākarī</s> (Luminous), <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (Radiant), <s>Sudurjayā</s> (Difficult to Conquer), <s>Abhimukhī</s> (Facing Forward), <s>Dūraṃgamā</s> (Far-reaching), <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable), <s>Sādhumatī</s> (Good Intelligence), and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage called <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of <s>Dharma</s>). These, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, are the ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, which have been spoken, will be spoken, and are being spoken by the <s>Buddhas</s> of the past, future, and present. I do not see, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, any range of <s>Buddha</s>-fields where the <s>Tathāgatas</s> do not illuminate these ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages. For what reason? This, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, is the supreme illumination of the <s>dharma</s>-gate for purifying the path of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>—namely, the establishment of the classification of the ten stages. This is inconceivable, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>—this matter, namely, the knowledge of the stages.'

body.text: atha khalu vajragarbho bodhisattva āsāṃ daśānāṃ bodhisattvabhūmīnāṃ nāmadheyamātraṃ parikīrtya tūṣṇīṃ babhūva, na bhūyaḥ prabhedaśo nirdiśati sma / atha khalu sā sarvāvatī bodhisattvaparṣat paritṛṣitā babhūva āsāṃ daśānāṃ bodhisattvabhūmīnāṃ nāmadheyamātraśravaṇena bhūmivibhāgānudīraṇena ca / tasyā etadabhavat - ko nu khalvatra hetuḥ kaśca pratyayaḥ, yadvajragarbho bodhisattva āsāṃ bodhisattvabhūmīnāṃ nāmadheyamātraṃ parikīrtya tūṣṇīṃbhāvena atināmayati, na bhūyaḥ prabhedaśo nirdiśatīti?
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajragarbha Bodhisattva</s>, having proclaimed only the names of these ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages, fell silent and did not explain them in detail. Then that entire assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> became eager, having heard only the names of these ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages without the detailed elucidation of the divisions of the stages. They thought: 'What is the reason, what is the cause, that <s>Vajragarbha Bodhisattva</s>, having proclaimed only the names of these <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages, passes the time in silence and does not explain them in detail?'

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena tasminneva bodhisattvaparṣatsaṃnipāte vimukticandro nāma bodhisattvastasyā bodhisattvaparṣadaścittāśayavicāramājñāya vajragarbhaṃ bodhisattvaṃ gāthābhigītena parigṛcchati sma-
body.translated_text: At that time, in that very assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Vimukticandra</s>, knowing the thoughts of that <s>Bodhisattva</s> assembly, addressed <s>Vajragarbha Bodhisattva</s> in verse—

children.text: kimarthaṃ śuddhasaṃkalpasmṛtijñānaguṇānvita /
children.translated_text: Why do you, endowed with the qualities of pure intention, mindfulness, and knowledge,

children.text: samudīryottamā bhūmīrna prakāśayase vibho // 1 //
children.translated_text: having announced the supreme stages, not illuminate them, O mighty one? (1)

children.text: viniścitā ime sarve bodhisattvā mahāyaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: All these <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are resolute, O greatly renowned one;

children.text: kasmādudīrya bhūmīśca(stvaṃ) pravibhāgaṃ na bhāṣase // 2 //
children.translated_text: why, having announced the stages, do you not expound their classification? (2)

children.text: śrotukāmā ime sarve jinaputrā viśāradāḥ /
children.translated_text: All these sons of the <s>Jinas</s> are confident and wish to hear;

children.text: vibhajyārthagatiṃ samyaragbhūmīnāṃ samudāhara // 3 //
children.translated_text: having properly analyzed the meaning and course of the stages, proclaim them! (3)

children.text: parṣadvi viprasanneyaṃ kausīdyāpagatā śubhā /
children.translated_text: This assembly is well-disposed, free from indolence, auspicious,

children.text: śuddhā pratiṣṭhitā sāre guṇajñānasamanvitā // 4 //
children.translated_text: pure, established in the essence, endowed with qualities and knowledge; (4)

children.text: nirīkṣamāṇā anyonyaṃ sthitāḥ sarve sagauravāḥ /
children.translated_text: gazing upon one another, all standing with reverence,

children.text: kṣaudraṃ hyaneḍakaṃ yadvatkāṅkṣanti tvamṛtopamam // 5 //
children.translated_text: like bees seeking honey, they desire [your words] that are like nectar. (5)

children.text: tasya śrutvā mahāprajño vajragarbho viśāradaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard him, <s>Vajragarbha</s>, the greatly wise and confident one,

children.text: parṣatsaṃtoṣaṇārthaṃ hi bhāṣate sma jinātmajaḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text: son of the <s>Jinas</s>, spoke for the purpose of satisfying the assembly— (6)

children.text: duṣkaraṃ paramametadadbhutaṃ bodhisattvacaritapradarśanam /
children.translated_text: This is supremely difficult and wondrous—the display of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct,

children.text: bhūmikāraṇavibhāga uttamo buddhabhāvasamudāgamo yataḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: the supreme classification of the causes of the stages, from which the attainment of Buddhahood [proceeds]. (7)

children.text: sūkṣma durdṛśa vikalpavarjitaḥścittabhūmivigato durāsadaḥ /
children.translated_text: Subtle, hard to see, free from conceptualization, transcending the ground of mind, difficult to reach—

children.text: gocaro hi viduṣāmanāsravo yatra muhyati jagacchave sati // 8 //
children.translated_text: for this is the undefiled domain of the wise, where the world is bewildered when it exists. (8)

children.text: vajropamaṃ hṛdayaṃ sthāpayitvā buddhajñānaṃ paramaṃ cādhimucya /
children.translated_text: Having established a heart like a diamond, and having aspired to the supreme <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge,

children.text: anātmānaṃ cittabhūmiṃ viditvā śakyaṃ śrotuṃ jñānametatsusūkṣmam // 9 //
children.translated_text: Having understood the self-less ground of mind, it is possible to hear this exceedingly subtle knowledge. // 9 //

children.text: antarīkṣa iva raṅgacitraṇā mārutaḥ khagapathāśrito yathā /
children.translated_text: Like a painting in the sky, like the wind resting on the path of birds,

children.text: jñānamevamiha bhāgaśaḥ kṛtaṃ durdṛśaṃ bhagavatāmanāsravam // 10 //
children.translated_text: Just so is this knowledge, divided into parts, hard to perceive, undefiled, [taught] by the <s>Bhagavats</s>. // 10 //

children.text: tasya me bhavati buddhirīdṛśī durlabho jagati yo 'sya vedakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Such is my understanding: rare in the world is one who knows this;

children.text: śraddhadhīta ca ya etaduttamaṃ na prakāśayitumutsahe yataḥ // 11 //
children.translated_text: And one who would have faith in this supreme [teaching]—since I dare not reveal it. // 11 //

body.text: evamukte vimukticandro bodhisattvo vajragarbhaṃ bodhisattvametadavocat - supariśuddho batāyaṃ bho jinaputra parṣatsaṃnipātaḥ supariśodhitādhyāśayānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ supariśodhitasaṃkalpānāṃ sucaritacaraṇānāṃ suparyupāsitabahubuddhakoṭiśatasahasrāṇāṃ susaṃbhṛtasaṃbhārāṇāmaparimitaguṇajñānasamanvāgatānāmapagatavimatisaṃdehānāmanaṅgaṇānāṃ supratiṣṭhitādhyāśayādhimuktīnāmaparapratyayānāmeṣu buddhadharmeṣu / tatsādhu bho jinaputra, prabhāṣasva / pratyakṣavihāriṇo hyate bodhisattvā atra sthāne //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vimukticandra</s> spoke thus to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s>: "How well-purified indeed, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, is this assembly gathering—of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> whose aspirations are well-purified, whose intentions are well-purified, whose conduct is well-practiced, who have attended upon many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, who have well-accumulated the provisions [of merit and knowledge], who are endowed with immeasurable qualities and knowledge, who are free from doubt and uncertainty, who are without blemish, whose aspirations and resolves are well-established, and who are independent in these <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. Therefore, O noble son of the <s>Jinas</s>, please speak! For these <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are directly dwelling in this state."

body.text: vajragarbha āha - kiṃcāpi bho jinaputra ayaṃ bodhisattvaparṣatsaṃnipātaḥ supariśuddhaḥ / peyālaṃ / atha ca punarye 'nye imānyevaṃrūpāṇyacintyāni sthānāni śṛṇuyuḥ, śrutvā ca vimatisaṃdehamutpādayeyuḥ, teṣāṃ tatsyāddīrgharātramanarthāya ahitāya duḥkhāya / iyaṃ me kāruṇyacittatā, yena tūṣṇīṃbhāvamevābhirocayāmi //
body.translated_text: <s>Vajragarbha</s> said: "Although, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, this <s>Bodhisattva</s> assembly gathering is well-purified—[as described above]—nevertheless, there may be others who, hearing these inconceivable topics of such a nature, might generate doubt and uncertainty; for them that would be for their harm, detriment, and suffering for a long time. It is out of this compassionate mind-state of mine that I prefer to remain silent."

body.text: atha khalu vimukticandro bodhisattvaḥ punareva vajragarbhaṃ bodhisattvametamevārthamadhyeṣate sma - tatsādhu bho jinaputra, prabhāṣasva / tathāgatasyaivānubhāvena imānyevaṃrūpāṇyacintyāni sthānāni svārakṣitāni śraddheyāni bhaviṣyanti / taskasya hetoḥ? tathā hi bho jinaputra asmin bhūminirdeśe bhāṣyamāṇe dharmatāpratilambha eṣa yatsarvabuddhasamanvāhāro bhavati / sarve bodhisattvāśca asyā eva jñānabhūmerārakṣārthamautsukyamāpadyante / tatkasya hetoḥ? eṣā hyādicaryā / eṣa samudāgamo buddhadharmāṇām / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra sarvalipyakṣarasaṃkhyānirdeśo mātṛkāpūrvaṃgamo mātṛkāparyavasānaḥ nāsti sa lipyakṣarasaṃkhyānirdeśo yo vinā mātṛkānirdeśam, evameva bho jinaputra sarve buddhadharmā bhūmipūrvaṃgamāśca caryāpariniṣpattito bhūmiparyavasānāḥ svayaṃbhūjñānādhigamatayā / tasmāttarhi bho jinaputra, prabhāṣasva / tathāgatā eva arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā ārakṣāmadhiṣṭhāsyanti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vimukticandra</s> once again entreated the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s> on this very matter: "Therefore, O noble son of the <s>Jinas</s>, please speak! Through the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, these inconceivable topics of such a nature will be well-protected and worthy of faith. For what reason? For, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, when this exposition of the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages) is being taught, it is the very nature of things that there is the sustaining power of all <s>Buddhas</s>. And all <s>Bodhisattvas</s> become eager to protect this very ground of knowledge. For what reason? Because this is the foundational practice; this is the arising of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. Just as, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, all exposition of letters, numbers, and script has the alphabet as its beginning and the alphabet as its culmination—there is no exposition of letters, numbers, and script apart from the exposition of the alphabet—even so, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> have the <s>bhūmis</s> as their beginning, and through the completion of practice they culminate in the <s>bhūmis</s>, by way of the realization of self-arisen knowledge. Therefore, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, please speak! The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the Perfectly Awakened Ones themselves will bestow their protective power."

body.text: atha khalu te sarve bodhisattvā ekasvarasaṃgītena tasyāṃ velāyāṃ vajragarbhaṃ bodhisattvaṃ gāthābhigītenaiva tamarthamadhyeṣante sma-
body.translated_text: Then all those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, in unison with a single voice, at that very moment entreated the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s> through verses sung in praise—

children.text: pravaravaravimalabuddhe svabhidhānānantaghaṭitapratibha /
children.translated_text: O one of supreme, excellent, and stainless wisdom, whose eloquence is joined with the infinite [power] of your own teaching,

children.text: pravyāhara madhuravarāṃ vācaṃ paramārthasaṃyuktām // 12 //
children.translated_text: Utter the sweetest and most excellent speech, connected with the ultimate truth! // 12 //

children.text: smṛtidhṛtiviśuddhabuddhe daśabalabalalābhamāśayaviśuddhim /
children.translated_text: O one of purified wisdom through mindfulness and retention, [describe] the attainment of the strength of the ten powers and the purity of aspiration,

children.text: pratisaṃviddaśavicayaṃ bhāṣasva daśottamā bhūmīḥ // 13 //
children.translated_text: The analysis of the tenfold <s>pratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledges)—speak of the ten supreme <s>bhūmis</s>! // 13 //

children.text: śamaniyamanibhṛtasumanāḥ prahīṇamadamānadṛṣṭisaṃkleśā /
children.translated_text: With minds calmed by <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) and <s>niyama</s> (restraint), having abandoned the defilements of pride, conceit, and wrong views,

children.text: niṣkāṅkṣā parṣadiyaṃ prārthayate bhāṣitāni tava // 14 //
children.translated_text: This assembly, free from doubt, entreats your words. // 14 //

children.text: tṛṣita iva śītamudakaṃ bubhukṣito 'nnaṃ subheṣajamivārtaḥ /
children.translated_text: As a thirsty person [desires] cool water, a hungry person food, a sick person excellent medicine,

children.text: kṣaudramiva sa madhukaragaṇastava vācamudīkṣate parṣat // 15 //
children.translated_text: As a swarm of bees [desires] honey—so does this assembly look eagerly for your speech. // 15 //

children.text: tatsādhu vimalabuddhe bhūmiviśeṣān vadasva virajaskān /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O one of stainless wisdom, speak of the distinctions of the <s>bhūmis</s>, free from dust,

children.text: daśabalayuktāsaṅgāṃ sugatagatimudīrayannikhilām // 16 //
children.translated_text: Proclaiming in full the path of the <s>Sugatas</s>, endowed with the unobstructed [knowledge of] the ten powers! // 16 //

body.text: atha khalu tasyāṃ velāyāṃ bhagavataḥ śākyamunerūrṇākośād bodhisattvabalāloko nāma raśmirniścacāra asaṃkhyeyāsaṃkhyeyaraśmiparivārā / sā sarvāsu daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuprasarānavabhāsya sarvāpāyaduḥkhāni pratiprasrabhya sarvamārabhavanāni dhyāmīkṛtya aparimitāni buddhaparṣanmaṇḍalānyavabhāsya acintyaṃ buddhaviṣayākāraprabhāvaṃ nidarśya sarvāsu daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuprasareṣu sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu dharmadeśanādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitān bodhisattvānavabhāsya acintyaṃ buddhavikurvaṇaṃ saṃdarśya uparyantarīkṣe mahāraśmighanābhrajālakūṭāgāraṃ kṛtvā tasthau / teṣāmapi buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmūrṇākośebhya evameva bodhisattvabalālokā nāma raśmayo niśceruḥ / niścarya asaṃkhyeyāsaṃkhyeyaraśmiparivārāstāḥ sarvāsu....pe...buddhavikurvaṇamādarśya idaṃ bhagavataḥ śākyamuneḥ parṣanmaṇḍalaṃ vajragarbhasya bodhisattvasyātmabhāvamavabhāsya uparyantarīkṣe evameva mahāraśmighanābhrajālakūṭāgāraṃ kṛtvā tasthuḥ / iti hi ābhiśca bhagavataḥ śākyamunerūrṇākośaprasṛtābhī raśmibhiste lokadhātavastāni ca buddhaparṣanmaṇḍalāni teṣāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ kāyā āsanāni ca sphuṭānyavabhāsitāni saṃdṛśyante sma / teṣāṃ ca aparimāṇeṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmūrṇākośaprasṛtābhī raśmibhirayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhāturidaṃ ca bhagavataḥ śākyamuneḥ parṣanmaṇḍalaṃ vajragarbhasya ca bodhisattvasya kāya āsanaṃ sphuṭamavabhāsitaṃ saṃdṛśyante sma / atha khalu tato mahāraśmighanābhrajālakūṭāgārādvuddhānubhāvena ayamevaṃrūpaḥ śabdo niścarati sma-
body.translated_text: Then, at that very moment, from the <s>ūrṇākośa</s> (hair-tuft between the brows) of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, there issued forth a light-ray called <s>Bodhisattvabalāloka</s> (Illumination of the Bodhisattva's Power), accompanied by innumerable and immeasurable rays. That [light], having illuminated all world-realms in all ten directions, having allayed all sufferings of the lower realms, having dimmed all the abodes of <s>Māra</s>, having illuminated immeasurable assembly-circles of <s>Buddhas</s>, having displayed the inconceivable power and form of the <s>Buddha</s>-domain, having illuminated in all ten directions in all world-realms the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> empowered with the sustaining power of <s>Dharma</s>-teaching in all <s>Tathāgata</s> assembly-circles, and having displayed the inconceivable miraculous transformation of the <s>Buddhas</s>—remained above in the sky, having formed a great pavilion of a mass of radiant cloud-nets. From the <s>ūrṇākośas</s> of those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones as well, light-rays called <s>Bodhisattvabalāloka</s> issued forth in the same way. Having issued forth, accompanied by innumerable rays, they [performed the same functions as described]... and having displayed the miraculous transformation of the <s>Buddhas</s>, they illuminated the assembly-circle of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> and the body of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s>, and remained above in the sky having formed just such a great pavilion of a mass of radiant cloud-nets. Thus, by the rays issued from the <s>ūrṇākośa</s> of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, those world-realms, those <s>Buddha</s> assembly-circles, and the bodies and seats of those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> were seen clearly illuminated. And by the rays issued from the <s>ūrṇākośas</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones in those immeasurable world-realms, this tri-thousand great-thousand world-system, this assembly-circle of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, and the body and seat of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s> were seen clearly illuminated. Then, from that great pavilion of the mass of radiant cloud-nets, by the power of the <s>Buddhas</s>, this sound issued forth—

children.text: asamasamākāśamairdaśabalavṛṣabhairanantamukhyaguṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: By the incomparable, space-like, ten-powered bulls, endowed with infinite and foremost qualities,

children.text: śākyakulajasya dharmairdevamanuṣyottamaiḥ kṛtamadhiṣṭhānam // 17 //
children.translated_text: The empowerment has been bestowed by the <s>dharmas</s> of the one born in the <s>Śākya</s> clan, supreme among gods and humans. // 17 //

children.text: anubhāvātsugatānāṃ kośaṃ vivṛṇuṣva dharmarājānām /
children.translated_text: By the power of the <s>Sugatas</s>, open the treasury of the <s>Dharma</s>-kings,

children.text: caryāvarāmudārāṃ prabhedaśo jñānabhūmiṃ ca // 18 //
children.translated_text: The excellent and noble practice, and the ground of knowledge in its divisions! // 18 //

children.text: adhiṣṭhitāste sugatairdhāritā bodhisattvaiśca /
children.translated_text: You are empowered by the <s>Sugatas</s> and upheld by the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>,

children.text: yeṣāṃ śrotrapathāgataḥ śreṣṭho yo dharmaparyāyaḥ // 19 //
children.translated_text: By those into whose ears has come the supreme <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. // 19 //

children.text: daśa bhūmīrvirajasaḥ pūrayitvānupūrveṇa /
children.translated_text: Having fulfilled in proper sequence the ten <s>bhūmis</s>, free from dust,

children.text: balāni daśa ca prāpya jinatāmarpayiṣyanti // 20 //
children.translated_text: And having attained the ten powers, they will reach <s>Jinahood</s> (Buddhahood). // 20 //

children.text: sāgarajale nimagnāḥ kalpoddāheṣu prakṣiptāḥ /
children.translated_text: Even those submerged in the waters of the ocean, even those cast into the conflagrations of the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age),

children.text: bhavyāste dharmaparyāyamimaṃ śrotumasaṃdigdhāḥ // 21 //
children.translated_text: They are capable of hearing this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse without doubt. // 21 //

children.text: ye tu vimatisaktāḥ saṃśayaiścābhyupetāḥ /
children.translated_text: But those who are attached to doubt and beset by uncertainties—

children.text: sarvaśo na hi teṣāṃ prāpsyate śrotrametat // 22 //
children.translated_text: For them, this [teaching] will in no way reach their ears. // 22 //

children.text: bhūmijñānapathaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ praveśasthānasaṃkramam /
children.translated_text: The supreme path of knowledge of the <s>bhūmis</s>, the entry-points and transitions,

children.text: anupūrveṇa bhāṣasva caryāviṣayameva ca // 23 //
children.translated_text: Speak of in proper sequence, along with the domain of practice! // 23 //

body.text: atha khalu vajragarbho bodhisattvo daśa diśo vyavalokya bhūyasyā mātrayā tasyāḥ parṣadaḥ saṃprasādarnārthaṃ tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata-
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s>, surveying the ten directions, in order to further gladden that assembly, at that moment spoke these verses—

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ durājñeyapadaṃ maharṣiṇāmakalpakalpāpagataṃ suduḥspṛśam /
children.translated_text: The subtle state of the great sages, hard to comprehend, gone beyond the reckoning of eons, extremely difficult to attain,

children.text: anāvilaṃ paṇḍitavijñaveditaṃ svabhāvaśāntaṃ hyanirodhasaṃbhavam // 24 //
children.translated_text: Undefiled, known by the wise and learned, quiescent by nature, without cessation or arising. // 24 //

children.text: svabhāvaśūnyaṃ praśamādvayakṣayaṃ gatyā vimuktaṃ samatāptinirvṛtam /
children.translated_text: Empty by nature, tranquil, non-dual, exhausted [of defilements], liberated from [all] destinies, having attained the bliss of equanimity,

children.text: anantamadhyaṃ vacasānudīritaṃ triyaghvavimuktaṃ nabhasā samānakam // 25 //
children.translated_text: Without end or middle, inexpressible by words, freed from the three times, equal to space. // 25 //

children.text: śāntaṃ praśāntaṃ sugatapraveditaṃ sarvairudāhārapadaiḥ sudurvacam /
children.translated_text: Peaceful, utterly pacified, realized by the <s>Sugatas</s>, extremely difficult to express by any illustrative terms—

children.text: bhūmiśca caryāpi ca tasya tādṛśī vaktuṃ suduḥkhaḥ kuta eva śrotum // 26 //
children.translated_text: Such are the <s>bhūmis</s> and the practice thereof: extremely difficult to speak of, how much more to hear! // 26 //

children.text: taccintayā cittapathaiśca varjitaṃ jñānābhinirhāramunīndraveditam /
children.translated_text: That which is beyond thought and the paths of mind, the production of knowledge understood by the lords of sages,

children.text: na skandhadhātvāyatanaprabhāvitaṃ na cittagamyaṃ na manovicintitam // 27 //
children.translated_text: Not produced from the aggregates, elements, or sense-bases, not accessible to thought, not conceivable by mind. // 27 //

children.text: yathāntarīkṣe śakuneḥ padaṃ budhairvaktuṃ na śakyaṃ na ca darśanopagam /
children.translated_text: Just as the footprint of a bird in the sky cannot be spoken of by the wise nor apprehended by sight,

children.text: tathaiva sarvā jinaputra bhūmayo vaktuṃ na śakyāḥ kuta eva śrotum // 28 //
children.translated_text: Even so, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, all the <s>bhūmis</s> cannot be spoken of—how much less heard! // 28 //

children.text: pradeśamātraṃ tu tato 'bhidhāsye maitrīkṛpābhyāṃ praṇidhānataśca /
children.translated_text: Yet I shall speak a fraction thereof, through loving-kindness and compassion, and through aspiration,

children.text: yathānupūrvaṃ na ca cittagocaraṃ jñānena tāḥ pūrayatāṃ yathāśayam // 29 //
children.translated_text: In proper sequence—though not within the range of thought—for those who fulfill them through knowledge, according to their dispositions. // 29 //

children.text: etādṛśo gocara durdṛśo 'sya vaktuṃ na śakyaḥ sa hi svāśayasthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Such is this domain, hard to perceive, impossible to express, for it abides in one's own inner experience;

children.text: kiṃ tu pravakṣyāmi jinānubhāvataḥ śṛṇvantu sarve sahitāḥ sagauravāḥ // 30 //
children.translated_text: Yet I shall speak through the power of the <s>Jinas</s>—let all listen together with reverence! // 30 //

children.text: jñānapraveśaḥ sa hi tādṛśo 'sya vaktuṃ na kalpairapi śakyate yat /
children.translated_text: For the entry into knowledge thereof is such that it cannot be expressed even in [many] eons;

children.text: samāsatastacchṛṇuta bravīmyahaṃ dharmārthatattvaṃ nikhilaṃ yathāsthitam // 31 //
children.translated_text: Hear it in brief—I shall speak the complete truth of the <s>Dharma</s>'s meaning as it really is. // 31 //

children.text: sagauravāḥ santa(ḥ) sajjā bhavanto vakṣyāmyahaṃ sādhu jinānubhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: With reverence, being ready and prepared—I shall speak well through the power of the <s>Jinas</s>;

children.text: udīrayiṣye varadharmaghoṣaṃ dṛṣṭāntayuktaṃ sahitaṃ samākṣaram // 32 //
children.translated_text: I shall utter the excellent sound of the <s>Dharma</s>, furnished with examples, coherent, and with proper syllables. // 32 //

children.text: suduṣkaraṃ tadvacasāpi vaktuṃ yaścāprameyaḥ sugatānubhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Extremely difficult to express even in words, and immeasurable is the power of the <s>Sugatas</s>;

children.text: mayi praviṣṭaḥ sa ca raśmimūrtiryasyānubhāvena mamāsti śaktiḥ // 33 //
children.translated_text: That radiant form has entered into me, by whose power I have the ability [to speak]. // 33 //

body.text: tatra bhavanto jinaputrāḥ sūpacitakuśalamūlānāṃ sucaritacaraṇānāṃ susaṃbhṛtasaṃbhārāṇāṃ suparyupāsitabuddhotpādānāṃ suparipiṇḍitaśukladharmāṇāṃ suparigṛhītakalyāṇamitrāṇāṃ suviśuddhāśayānāṃ vipulāghyāśayopagatānāṃ udārādhimuktisamanvāgatānāṃ kṛpākaruṇābhimukhānāṃ (bodhi)sattvānāṃ bodhāya cittamutpādyate / buddhajñānābhilāṣāya daśabalabalādhigamāya mahāvaiśāradyādhigamāya samatābuddhadharmapratilambhāya sarvajagatparitrāṇāya mahākṛpākaruṇāviśodhanāya daśadigaśeṣajñānādhigamāya sarvabuddhakṣetrāsaṅgapariśodhanāya tryadhvaikakṣaṇavibodhāya mahādharmacakrapravartanavaiśāradyāya ca taccittamutpadyate bodhisattvānāṃ mahākaruṇāpūrvaṃgamaṃ prajñājñānādhipateyamupāyakauśalyaparigṛhītamāśayādhyāśayopastabdhaṃ tathāgatabalāprameyaṃ sattvabalabuddhibalasuvicitavicayamasaṃbhinnajñānābhimukhaṃ svayaṃbhūjñānānukūlaṃ sarvabuddhadharmaprajñājñānāvavādasaṃpratyeṣakaṃ dharmadhātuparamamākāśadhātusthitakamaparāntakoṭiniṣṭham / yena cittotpādena sahotpannena bodhisattvo 'tikrānto bhavati, pṛthagjñānabhūmīmavakrānto bhavati, bodhisattvaniyāmaṃ jāto bhavati, tathāgatakule 'navadyo bhavati, sarvajātivādena vyāvṛtto bhavati, sarvalokagatibhyo 'vakrānto bhavati, lokottarāṃ gatiṃ sthito bhavati, bodhisattvadharmatāyāṃ suvyavasthito bhavati, bodhisattvāvasthānena samatānugato bhavati, tryaghvatathāgatavaṃśaniyato bhavati saṃbodhiparāyaṇaḥ / evaṃrūpadharmavyavasthito bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvaḥ pramuditāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau vyavasthito bhavatyacalanayogena //
body.translated_text: There, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, for those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have well-accumulated roots of merit, whose conduct is well-practiced, who have well-gathered the provisions [of merit and knowledge], who have well-attended upon the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, who have well-amassed wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, who have well-taken hold of spiritual friends, whose aspirations are well-purified, who have attained vast higher aspirations, who are endowed with noble resolves, and who face toward compassion and great compassion—the mind is generated toward awakening. That mind arises for the sake of desire for <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, for the attainment of the strength of the ten powers, for the attainment of the great fearlessnesses, for the acquisition of the equal <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, for the protection of all beings, for the purification of great compassion, for the attainment of knowledge that is unlimited in the ten directions, for the unobstructed purification of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, for the awakening to all three times in a single moment, and for the confidence of turning the great <s>Dharma</s>-wheel. That mind arises for the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, preceded by great compassion, governed by <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), embraced by skillful means, supported by aspiration and higher aspiration, immeasurable with the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, well-discerning the power of beings and the power of intelligence, in accord with unconfused knowledge, in conformity with self-arisen knowledge, seeking the instruction of the <s>prajñā</s>-knowledge of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, supreme in the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), abiding in the <s>ākāśadhātu</s> (realm of space), and culminating at the final limit. By this generation of the mind, as soon as it arises, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> transcends the ground of ordinary beings' knowledge, enters the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s fixed course, is born into the family of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> without fault, is turned away from all claims of birth [in lower states], has descended from all worldly destinies, stands upon the supramundane path, is well-established in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s nature of <s>dharmas</s>, follows equanimity through the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s abiding, and is destined for the lineage of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the three times, heading toward perfect awakening. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in such a nature of <s>dharmas</s>, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, is established on the first <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>, <s>Pramuditā</s> (the Joyful), through an unshakable application.

body.text: atra bhavanto jinaputrāḥ pramuditāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito bodhisattvaḥ prāmodyabahulo bhavati prasādabahulaḥ prītibahula utplāvanābahula udagrībahula utsībahula utsāhabahulo 'saṃrambhabahulo 'vihiṃsābahulo 'krodhabahulo bhavati / iti hi bhavanto jinaputrāḥ pramuditāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito bodhisattvan pramudito bhavati, buddhān bhagavato 'nusmaran buddhadharmān bodhisattvān bodhisattvacaryāḥ pāramitāviśuddhiṃ bodhisattvabhūmiviśeṣān bodhisattvāsaṃhāryatāṃ
body.translated_text: Here, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Pramuditā</s> (the Joyful) is full of joy, full of serene faith, full of delight, full of elation, full of exuberance, full of rapture, full of zeal, free from contention, free from harming, and free from anger. Thus, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Pramuditā</s> is joyful—recollecting the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones, the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practices, the purification of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), the distinctions of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmis</s>, the invincibility of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>—

body.text: tathāgatāvavādānuśāsanīṃ sattvārthasaṃprāpaṇam / pramudito bhavati sarvatathāgatajñānapraveśaprayogamanusmaran / bhūyaḥ prāmodyavān bhavati - vyāvṛtto 'smi sarvajagadviṣayāt, avatīrṇo 'smi buddhabhūmisamīpam, dūrībhūto 'smi bālapṛthagjanabhūmeḥ, āsanno 'smi jñānabhūmeḥ, vyavacchinno 'smi sarvāpāyadurgativinipātāt, pratiśaraṇabhūto 'smi sarvasattvānām, āsannadarśano 'smi sarvatathāgatānām, saṃbhūto 'smi sarvabuddhaviṣaye, sarvabodhisattvasamatāmupagato 'smi / vigatāni me sarvabhayatrāsacchambhitatvānīti prāmodyamutpādayati / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasya asyāḥ pramuditāyā bodhisattvabhūmeḥ sahapratilambhena yānīmāni bhayāni bhavanti - yadidamājīvikābhayaṃ vā aślokabhayaṃ vā maraṇabhayaṃ vā durgatibhayaṃ vā parṣacchāradyabhayaṃ vā, tāni sarvāṇi vyapagatāni bhavanti / tatkasya hetoḥ? yathāpi idamātmasaṃjñāpagamādātmasneho 'sya na bhavati, kutaḥ punaḥ sarvopakaraṇasnehaḥ? ato 'sya ājīvikābhayaṃ na bhavati / na ca kaṃcitsatkāraṃ kasyacitsakāśātpratikāṅkṣati, anyatra mayaiva teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvopakaraṇabāhulyamupanāmayitavyamiti, ato 'sya aślokabhayaṃ na bhavati / ātmadṛṣṭivigamācca asyātmasaṃjñā na bhavati, ato 'sya maraṇabhayaṃ na bhavati / mṛtasyaiva me niyataṃ buddhabodhisattvairna virahito bhaviṣyāmīti, ato 'sya durgatibhayaṃ na bhavati / nāsti me kaścidāśayena sarvaloke samasamaḥ, kutaḥ punaruttara ityato 'sya parṣacchāradyabhayaṃ na bhavati / evaṃ sarvabhayatrāsacchambhitatvaromaharṣāpagataḥ //
body.translated_text: the instruction and admonition of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> for accomplishing the welfare of beings. He becomes joyful, recollecting the effort of entering into the knowledge of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. He becomes even more joyful [thinking]: 'I have turned away from the domain of the entire world; I have descended near the stage of <s>Buddhahood</s>; I have become far removed from the stage of foolish ordinary beings; I have drawn near to the stage of knowledge; I have cut off all states of misery, evil destinies, and perdition; I have become a refuge for all beings; I am near to seeing all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; I have arisen in the domain of all <s>Buddhas</s>; I have attained equality with all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; all my fears, terrors, and tremblings have departed'—thus he generates joy. For what reason? For indeed, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s attainment of this <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, whatever fears there may be—namely, fear regarding livelihood, fear of ill-repute, fear of death, fear of evil destinies, or fear of timidity before assemblies—all of these are departed. For what reason? Since the notion of self has departed, he has no attachment to self; how then could there be attachment to any possessions? Therefore he has no fear regarding livelihood. And he does not expect any honor from anyone anywhere, [thinking] rather 'I myself must provide abundant provisions to those beings'—therefore he has no fear of ill-repute. And due to the departure of the view of self, he has no notion of self—therefore he has no fear of death. [Thinking] 'Even after dying, I will certainly not be separated from the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>'—therefore he has no fear of evil destinies. [Thinking] 'There is no one in all the world equal to me in aspiration, how much less superior'—therefore he has no fear of timidity before assemblies. Thus all fears, terrors, tremblings, and horripilation have departed.

body.text: atha khalu punarbhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvo mahākaruṇāpuraskṛtatvādanupahatena aprākṛtenādhyāśayena bhūyasyā mātrayā prayujyate sarvakuśalamūlamudāgamāya / sa śraddhādhipateyatayā prasādabahulatayā adhimuktiviśuddhyā avakalpanābahulatayā kṛpākaruṇābhinirhāratayā mahāmaitryupetatayā aparikhinnamānasatayā hryapatrāpyālaṃkāratayā kṣāntisauratyopetatayā tathāgatārhatsamyaksaṃbuddhaśāsanagauravacitrīkaraṇatayā rātriṃdivātṛptakuśalamūlopacayatayā kalyāṇamitraniṣevaṇatayā dharmārāmābhiratatayā atṛptabāhuśrutyaparyeṣaṇatayā yathāśrutadharmayoniśaḥpratyavekṣaṇatayā aniketamānasatayā anadhyavasitalābhasatkāraślokatayā anabhinanditopakaraṇasnehatayā ratnopamacittotpādātṛptābhinirhāratayā sarvajñabhūmyabhilāṣaṇatayā tathāgatabalavaiśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmādhyālambanatayā pāramitāsaṅgaparyeṣaṇatayā māyāśāṭhyaparivarjanatayā yathāvāditathākāritayā satatasamitaṃ satyavacanānurakṣaṇatayā tathāgatakulabhūṣaṇatayā bodhisattvaśikṣānutsarjanatayā mahāśailendrarājopamasarvajñatācittāprakampanatayā sarvalokakriyānabhilakṣaṇatayā utsargalokottarapathopetatayā atṛptabodhyaṅgasaṃbhāropacayatayā satatasamitamuttarottaraviśeṣaparimārgaṇatayā / evaṃrūpairbhavanto jinaputrā bhūmipariśodhakairdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ supratiṣṭhito bhavati pramuditāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, being led by great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), with an unimpaired and extraordinary intention, engages to an even greater degree in the accumulation of all wholesome roots. Through predominance of faith, abundance of serene confidence, purity of aspiration, abundance of resolve, arising of compassion and <s>karuṇā</s>, endowment with great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), unwearied mind, adornment of moral shame and modesty, endowment with patience and gentleness, reverence and esteem for the teaching of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones, day-and-night insatiable accumulation of wholesome roots, attendance upon spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), delight in the garden of the <s>Dharma</s>, insatiable pursuit of extensive learning, examination of the <s>Dharma</s> as heard according to its true meaning, mind free from attachment to any abode, non-attachment to gain, honor, and fame, non-delight in attachment to possessions, insatiable generation of the aspiration-mind like a jewel, aspiration for the stage of omniscience, reliance upon the powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the fearlessnesses, and the unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, unimpeded pursuit of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), abandoning of deceit and craft, acting as one speaks, constant guarding of truthful speech, adorning the family of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, not abandoning the training of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, unshakeable mind toward omniscient wisdom like the great king of mountains, not attending to all worldly activities, endowment with the supramundane path of renunciation, insatiable accumulation of the factors of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), and constantly seeking ever higher distinctions—by such qualities that purify the stage, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> becomes well-established on the <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage.

body.text: so 'syāṃ pramuditāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitaḥ san imānyevaṃrūpāṇi mahāpraṇidhānāni mahāvyavasāyān mahābhinirhārānabhinirharati - yaduta aśeṣaniḥśeṣānavaśeṣasarvabuddhapūjopasthāpanāya sarvākāravaropetamudārādhimuktiviśuddhaṃ dharmadhātuvipulamākāśadhātuparyavasānamaparāntakoṭiniṣṭhaṃ
body.translated_text: Standing on this <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, he generates great vows (<s>mahāpraṇidhāna</s>) of this kind, great resolves, and great undertakings—namely, a first great vow for the worship and service of all <s>Buddhas</s> without remainder, without exception, without residue, endowed with all excellent aspects, with purified noble aspiration, vast as the <s>Dharma</s>-realm, extending to the limit of the space-realm, reaching to the ultimate end,

body.text:
sarvakalpasaṃkhyābuddhotpādaṃsaṃkhyāpratiprasrabdhaṃ mahāpūjopasthānāya prathamaṃ mahāpraṇidhānamabhinirharati / yaduta sarvatathāgatabhāṣitadharmanetrīsaṃdhāraṇāya sarvabuddhabodhisattvasuparigrahāya sarvasamyaksaṃbuddhaśāsanaparirakṣaṇāya .... buddhotpādasaddharmaparigrahāya dvitīyam / yaduta sarvabuddhotpādaniravaśeṣasarvalokadhātuprasareṣu tuṣitabhavanavāsamādiṃ kṛtvā cyavanāsaṃkramaṇagarbhasthitijanmakumārakrīḍāntaḥpuravāsābhiniṣkramaṇaduṣkaracaryābodhimaṇḍopasaṃkramaṇamāragharṣaṇābhisaṃbodhyadhyeṣaṇamahādharmacakrapravartanamahāparinirvāṇopasaṃkramaṇāya pūjādharmasaṃgrahaprayogapūrvaṃgamaṃ kṛtvā sarvatraikakālavivartanāya ... buddhotpāda .... yāvanmahāparinirvāṇopasaṃkramaṇāya tṛtīyam / yaduta sarvabodhisattvacaryāvipulamahadgatāpramāṇāsaṃbhinnasarvapāramitāsaṃgṛhītasarvabhūmipariśodhanaṃ sāṅgopāṅganirhārasalakṣaṇasaṃvartavivartasarvabodhisattvacaryābhūtayathāvadbhūmipathopadeśapāramitāparikarmāvavādānuśāsanyanupradānopastabdhacittotpādābhinirhārāya ... caryā ... cittotpādābhinirhārāya caturtham / yaduta niravaśeṣasarvasattvadhāturūpyarūpisaṃjñāsaṃjñinaivasaṃjñināsaṃjñāṇḍajajarāyujasaṃsvedajaupapāduka- ... traidhātukaparyāpannaṣaḍgatisamavasṛtasarvopapattiparyāpannanāmarūpasaṃgṛhītāśeṣasarvasattvadhātuparipācanāya sarvabuddhadharmāvatāraṇāya sarvagatisaṃkhyāvyavacchedanāya sarvajñajñānapratiṣṭhāpanāya ... sattvadhātu ... sarvasattvadhātuparipācanāya pañcamam / yaduta niravaśeṣasarvalokadhātuvipulasaṃkṣiptamahadgatāpramāṇasūkṣmaudārikavyatyastāvamūrdhasamatalapraveśasamavarasaraṇānugatendrajālavibhāgadaśadigaśeṣavimātratāvibhāgapraveśajñānānugamapratyakṣatāyai ... lokadhātu ... lokadhātuvaimātryāvatāraṇāya ṣaṣṭham / yaduta sarvakṣetraikakṣetraikakṣetrasarvakṣetrasamavasaraṇapariśodhanamapramāṇabuddhakṣetraprabhāvyūhālaṃkārapratimaṇḍitaṃ
sarvakleśāpanayanapariśuddhapathopetamapramāṇajñānākarasattvaparipūrṇamudārabuddhaviṣayasamavasaraṇaṃ yathāśayasarvasattvasaṃdarśanasaṃtoṣaṇāya ... buddhakṣetra ... sarvabuddhakṣetrapariśodhanāya saptamam / yaduta sarvabodhisattvaikāśayaprayogatāyai niḥsapatnakuśalamūlopacayāya ekālambanasarvabodhisattvasamatāyai avirahitasatatasamitabuddhabodhisattvasamavadhānāya yatheṣṭabuddhotpādasaṃdarśanāya svacittotpādatathāgataprabhāvajñānānugamāya acyutānugāminyabhijñāpratilambhāya sarvalokadhātvanuvicaraṇāya sarvabuddhaparṣanmaṇḍalapratibhāsaprāptaye sarvopapattisvaśarīrānugamāya acintyamahāyānopetatāyai bodhisattvacaryācaraṇāvyavacchedāya ... caryā ... mahāyānāvatāraṇāya aṣṭamam / yaduta avivartyacakrasamārūḍhabodhisattvacaryācaraṇāya amoghakāyavāṅmanaskarmaṇe sahadarśananiyatabuddhadharmatvāya sahaghoṣodāhārajñānānugamāya sahaprasādakleśavinivartanāya mahābhaiṣajyarājopamāśrayapratilambhāya cintāmaṇivatkāyapratilambhāya sarvabodhisattvacaryācaraṇāya ... caryā ... amoghasarvaceṣṭatāyai navamam / yaduta sarvalokadhātuṣvanuttarasamyaksaṃbodhyabhisaṃbodhāya ekavālapathāvyativṛttasarvabālapṛthagjanajanmopapatyabhiniṣkramaṇavikurvaṇabodhimaṇḍadharmacakrapravartanamahāparinirvāṇopadarśanāya mahābuddhaviṣayaprabhāvajñānānugamāya sarvasattvadhātuyathāśayabuddhotpādakṣaṇakṣaṇavibhaṅgavibodhapraśamaprāpaṇasaṃdarśanāya ekābhisaṃbodhisarvadharmanirmāṇaspharaṇāya ekaghoṣodāhārasarvasattvacittāśayasaṃtoṣaṇāya mahāparinirvāṇopadarśanacaryābalāvyavacchedāya mahājñānabhūmisarvadharmavyavasthāpanasaṃdarśanāya
body.translated_text: unceasing through the number of <s>kalpas</s> in which <s>Buddhas</s> arise, for the great worship and service [of all <s>Buddhas</s>]. A second [great vow] for the preservation of the <s>Dharma</s>-treasury spoken by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, for the complete reception of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Bodhisattva</s> [teachings], for the protection of the teaching of all Perfectly Enlightened Ones, ... for the preservation of the true <s>Dharma</s> upon the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>. A third, for visiting all <s>Buddha</s>-arisings in all world-realms without remainder—beginning from dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, descent, conception, birth, youthful play, life in the inner palace, renunciation, austere practices, approaching the seat of awakening, vanquishing <s>Māra</s>, perfect awakening, being requested [to teach], turning the great wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, and the approach to the great <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>—preceded by worship and <s>Dharma</s>-collection, for the simultaneous unfolding [of all these] everywhere. A fourth, for the instruction and admonition regarding the path of all <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct—vast, exalted, immeasurable, undivided—encompassed by all <s>pāramitās</s>, purifying all stages, with complete detailed elaboration, teaching the true path of all <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct at each stage with its <s>pāramitā</s> preparation, and for the generation of the sustained aspiration-mind. A fifth, for the maturing of the entire realm of beings without remainder—form and formless, with perception, without perception, neither with nor without perception, egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, spontaneously born—included in the triple world, situated in the six destinies, encompassed by all modes of birth, included in name-and-form—for their entry into all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, for cutting off the numbers of all destinies, and for establishing them in omniscient knowledge. A sixth, for the direct knowledge of the entry into the variety of all world-realms without remainder—vast, contracted, exalted, immeasurable, subtle, gross, inverted, upside-down, level, entering into equality, following <s>Indra</s>'s net in its divisions, entering the immeasurability of all world-realms in the ten directions. A seventh, for the purification of all fields where one field is all fields and all fields are one field—adorned with the splendor and array of immeasurable <s>Buddha</s>-fields, endowed with the pure path of removing all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), filled with beings who are treasuries of immeasurable knowledge, a gathering-place of the exalted domain of the <s>Buddha</s>—for showing and satisfying all beings according to their aspirations, for the purification of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields. An eighth, for the unity of aspiration and effort of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, for the accumulation of wholesome roots without adversary, for the equality of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s> with one object, for the constant and continuous attendance upon <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, for seeing <s>Buddha</s>-arisings as desired, for the attainment of <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) following the power and knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s> through one's own aspiration-mind, for traversing all world-realms, for appearing in all <s>Buddha</s>-assembly circles, for following one's own body in all modes of birth, endowed with the inconceivable <s>Mahāyāna</s>—for entry into the <s>Mahāyāna</s> without interruption of <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct. A ninth, for the practice of <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct mounted on the irreversible wheel, for unfailing action of body, speech, and mind, for certainty of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities upon mere seeing, for knowledge following the mere utterance of a word, for the removal of <s>kleśas</s> upon mere gaining of faith, for the attainment of a body like the great Medicine King, for a body like the wish-fulfilling gem—for unfailing effectiveness of all activities in <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct. A tenth, for the attainment of <s>anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) in all world-realms,

body.text: dharmajñānarddhimāyābhijñāsarvalokadhātuspharaṇāya abhisaṃbodhimahājñānābhijñābhinirhārāya daśamam / iti hi bhavanto jinaputrā imānyevaṃrūpāṇi mahāpraṇidhānāni mahāvyavasāyān mahābhinirhārān daśa praṇidhānamukhāni pramukhaṃ kṛtvā paripūrṇāni daśapraṇidhānāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇi yāni bodhisattvaḥ pramuditāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito 'bhinirharati pratilabhate ca //
body.translated_text: for the entry into the knowledge, power, and magical display of the <s>Dharma</s>, pervading all world-realms, and for the great undertaking of <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) and supreme awakening. Thus, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, these ten headings of vows, led by such great vows, great resolves, and great undertakings, are fulfilled—innumerable hundreds of thousands of vows, which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> standing on the <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage generates and attains.

body.text: tāni ca mahāpraṇidhānāni daśabhirniṣṭhāpadairabhinirharati / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta sattvadhātuniṣṭhayā ca lokadhātuniṣṭhayā ca ākāśadhātuniṣṭhayā ca dharmadhātuniṣṭhayā ca nirvāṇadhātuniṣṭhayā ca buddhotpādadhātuniṣṭhayā ca tathāgatajñānadhātuniṣṭhayā ca cittālambanadhātuniṣṭhayā ca buddhaviṣayajñānapraveśadhātuniṣṭhayāḥ ca lokavartanīdharmavartanījñānavartanīdhātuniṣṭhayā ca / iti hi yā niṣṭhā sattvadhātuniṣṭhāyāḥ, sā me niṣṭhā eṣāṃ mahāpraṇidhānānāṃ bhavatu / yā niṣṭhā yāvajjñānavartanīdhātuniṣṭhāyāḥ, sā me niṣṭhā eṣāṃ mahāpraṇidhānānāṃ bhavatu / iti hyaniṣṭhā sattvadhātuniṣṭhā / aniṣṭhānīmāni me kuśalamūlāni bhavantu / aniṣṭhā yāvajjñānavartanīdhātuniṣṭhā / aniṣṭhānīmāni me kuśalamūlāni bhavantviti //
body.translated_text: And he generates those great vows through ten culmination-points (<s>niṣṭhāpada</s>). What are these ten? Namely, through the culmination of the realm of beings, the culmination of the realm of worlds, the culmination of the realm of space, the culmination of the <s>Dharma</s>-realm, the culmination of the realm of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the culmination of the realm of <s>Buddha</s>-arising, the culmination of the realm of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge, the culmination of the realm of mental objects, the culmination of the realm of entry into the domain of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, and the culmination of the realm of the turning of the world, the turning of <s>Dharma</s>, and the turning of knowledge. Thus, whatever is the culmination of the culmination of the realm of beings, may that be the culmination of these great vows of mine. Whatever is the culmination up to the culmination of the realm of the turning of knowledge, may that be the culmination of these great vows of mine. Thus the culmination of the realm of beings has no culmination; may these wholesome roots of mine have no culmination. The culmination up to the realm of the turning of knowledge has no culmination; may these wholesome roots of mine have no culmination.

body.text: sa evaṃ svabhinirhṛtapraṇidhānaḥ karmaṇyacitto mṛducitto 'saṃhāryaśraddho bhavati / so 'bhiśraddadhāti tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ pūrvāntacaryābhinirhārapraveśaṃ pāramitāsamudāgamaṃ bhūmipariniṣpattiṃ vaiśeṣikatāṃ balapariniṣpattiṃ vaiśāradyaparipūrimāveṇikabuddhadharmāsaṃhāryatāmacintyāṃ buddhadharmatāmanantamadhyaṃ tathāgataviṣayābhinirhāramaparimāṇajñānānugataṃ tathāgatagocarānupraveśaṃ phalapariniṣpattimabhiśraddadhāti / samāsataḥ sarvabodhisattvacaryāṃ yāvattathāgatabhūmijñānanirdeśādhiṣṭhānamabhiśraddadhāti //
body.translated_text: Having thus generated his vows, his mind becomes workable, soft, and his faith unshakeable. He has faith in the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones—their entry into the undertaking of conduct in former lives, their accomplishment of the <s>pāramitās</s>, the completion of the stages, their special distinction, the completion of the powers, the fulfillment of the fearlessnesses, the indestructibility of the unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, the inconceivable nature of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, the infinite and middleless undertaking of the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the entry into the sphere of the <s>Tathāgata</s> accompanied by immeasurable knowledge, and the completion of the fruit. In brief, he has faith in all <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct up to the foundation of the instruction in the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s> stage.

body.text: tasyaivaṃ bhavati - evaṃ gambhīrāḥ khalu punarime buddhadharmāḥ evaṃ viviktāḥ evaṃ śāntāḥ evaṃ śūnyāḥ evamānimittāḥ evamapraṇihitāḥ evaṃ nirupalepāḥ evaṃ vipulāḥ evamaparimāṇāḥ evamudārāḥ evaṃ durāsadāśceme buddhadharmāḥ / atha ca punarime bālapṛthagjanāḥ kudṛṣṭipatitayā saṃtatyā avidyāndhakāraparyavanaddhamānasena mānadhvajasamucchritaiḥ saṃkalpaistṛṣṇājālābhilaṣitairmanasikārairmāyāśāṭhyagahanānucaritaiścittāśayairīrṣyāmātsaryasaṃprayuktairgatyupapattiprayogai rāgadveṣamohaparicitaiḥ karmopacayaiḥ krodhopanāhasaṃdhukṣitābhiścittajvālābhirviparyāsasaṃprayuktaiḥ karmakriyābhinirhāraiḥ kāmabhavāvidyāsravānubaddhaiścittamanovijñānabījaistraidhātuke punarbhavāṅkuramabhinirvartayanti yadidaṃ nāmarūpasahajāvinirbhāgagatam / tenaiva ca nāmarūpeṇa vivardhitena eṣāṃ ṣaḍāyatanagrāmaḥ saṃbhavati / saṃbhūteṣvāyataneṣvanyonyasparśanipātato vedanā saṃbhavati / tāmeva vedanāṃ bhūyo bhūyo 'bhinandatāṃ tṛṣṇopādānaṃ vivardhate / vivṛddhe tṛṣṇopādāne bhavaḥ saṃbhavati / saṃbhūte ca bhave jātijarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ prādurbhavanti / evameteṣāṃ sattvānāṃ duḥkhaskandho 'bhinirvartate ātmātmīyavigato riktastucchaḥ śūnyo nirīho niśceṣṭo jaḍastṛṇakāṣṭhakuḍyavartmapratibhāsopamaḥ / na caivamavabudhyanta iti / teṣāmevaṃrūpeṇa sattvānāṃ duḥkhaskandhāvipramokṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā sattveṣu mahākaruṇonmiñjaḥ saṃbhavati - ete 'smābhiḥ sattvāḥ paritrātavyāḥ parimocayitavyā
body.translated_text: This thought arises in him: 'These <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> are indeed so profound, so isolated, so peaceful, so empty, so signless, so without aspiration, so undefiled, so vast, so immeasurable, so exalted, so difficult to reach—these <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>! And yet these foolish ordinary beings, with their continuum fallen into wrong views, with minds enveloped by the darkness of ignorance, with intentions raised up by the banner of pride, with mental engagements longing in the net of craving, with mental dispositions wandering in the thicket of deceit and hypocrisy, with pursuits of destiny and rebirth conjoined with envy and miserliness, with accumulations of <s>karma</s> imbued with passion, aversion, and delusion, with flames of mind kindled by anger and resentment, with accomplishments of <s>karmic</s> actions conjoined with the perversions, and with seeds of mind, intellect, and consciousness bound by the outflows of desire, existence, and ignorance—they produce the sprout of renewed existence in the three realms, namely, that which arises undifferentiated and conjoined with name-and-form. And with that very name-and-form growing, the village of their six sense-bases comes into being. When the sense-bases have come into being, from the contact of mutual impingement, feeling arises. For those who again and again delight in that very feeling, the clinging of craving grows. When the clinging of craving has grown, existence comes into being. And when existence has come into being, birth, old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and agitation arise. Thus the mass of suffering of these beings is produced—devoid of self and what belongs to self, empty, hollow, void, inactive, motionless, inert, comparable to the appearance of grass, wood, walls, and paths. Yet they do not understand it thus.' Having seen such beings unable to free themselves from the mass of suffering, there arises in him the welling up of great compassion toward beings: 'These beings must be protected by us, must be liberated

body.text: ato mahāsaṃmohāt, atyantasukhe ca nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpayitavyāḥ iti / ato 'sya mahāmaitryunmiñjaḥ saṃbhavati //
body.translated_text: from this great delusion, and must be established in the ultimate bliss of <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' From this, the welling up of great friendliness arises in him.

body.text: evaṃ kṛpāmaitryanugatena khalu punarbhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvo 'dhyāśayena prathamāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau vartamānaḥ sarvavastuṣu sāpekṣacittaṃ parivarjya buddhajñāne ca udāraspṛhābhilāṣabuddhirmahātyāgeṣu prayuñjate / sa ya ime tyāgāḥ - yaduta dhanadhānyakośakoṣṭhāgāraparityāgo vā hiraṇyasuvarṇamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajataparityāgo vā ratnābharaṇavibhūṣaṇaparityāgo vā hayarathagajapativāhanaparityāgo vā udyānatapovanavihāraparityāgo vā dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaparityāgo vā grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīparityāgo vā bhāryāputraduhitṛparityāgo vā sarvapriyamanāpavastuparityāgo vā śiraḥkarṇanāsākaracaraṇanayanasvamāṃsaśoṇitāsthimajjāmedaśchavicarmahṛdayasarvātmabhāvaparityāgo vā, teṣvanapekṣo bhūtvā sarvavastuṣu buddhajñāne ca udāraspṛhābhilāṣabuddhiḥ parityajati / evaṃ hyasya prathamāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya mahātyāgaḥ saṃbhavati //
body.translated_text: Thus, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding on the first <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>, with a higher intention accompanied by compassion and friendliness, abandoning the mind attached to all possessions, and with an intellect of noble aspiration and longing for <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, engages in great giving (<s>tyāga</s>). These are the acts of giving: the relinquishing of wealth, grain, treasuries, and storehouses; the relinquishing of gold, silver, jewels, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch, crystal, coral, natural gold, and refined silver; the relinquishing of ornamental jewelry and adornments; the relinquishing of horses, chariots, elephants, chief vehicles, and mounts; the relinquishing of parks, groves, and monasteries; the relinquishing of female servants, male servants, workers, and attendants; the relinquishing of villages, towns, markets, districts, kingdoms, and capital cities; the relinquishing of wife, sons, and daughters; the relinquishing of all beloved and pleasing possessions; and the relinquishing of head, ears, nose, hands, feet, eyes, one's own flesh, blood, bones, marrow, fat, skin, hide, heart, and the entire self. Having become indifferent to all these possessions, with an intellect of noble aspiration and longing for <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, he relinquishes them. Thus, for one established on the first <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>, great giving arises.

body.text: sa evaṃ karuṇāmaitrītyāgāśayo bhūtvā sarvasattvaparitrāṇārthaṃ bhūyo bhūyo laukikalokottarānarthān parimārgate parigaveṣate / parimārgamāṇaḥ parigaveṣamāṇaśca aparikhedacittamutpādayati / evamasyāparikhedaḥ saṃbhavati / aparikhinnaśca sarvaśāstraviśārado bhavati / ato 'sya śāstrajñatā saṃbhavati / sa evaṃ śāstropetaḥ kriyākriyāvicāritayā buddhyā hīnamadhyapraṇīteṣu sattveṣu tathatvāya pratipadyate yathābalaṃ yathābhajamānam / ato 'sya lokajñatā saṃbhavati / lokajñaśca kālavelāmātracārī hryapatrāpyavibhūṣitayā saṃtatyā ātmārthaparārtheṣu prayujyate / ato 'sya hryapatrāpyaṃ saṃbhavati / teṣu ca prayogeṣu naiṣkramyacārī avivartyāpratyudāvartyabalādhānaprāpto bhavati / evamasya dhṛtibalādhānamājataṃ bhavati / dhṛtibalādhānaprāptaśca tathāgatapūjopasthāneṣu prayujyate, śāsane ca pratipadyate / evaṃ hyasyeme daśa bhūmipariśodhakā dharmā ājātā bhavanti / tadyathā - śraddhā karuṇā maitrī tyāgaḥ khedasahiṣṇutā śāstrajñatā lokajñatā hryapatrāpyaṃ dhṛtibalādhānaṃ tathāgatapūjopasthānamiti //
body.translated_text: Having such a disposition of compassion, friendliness, and giving, for the sake of protecting all beings, he seeks and searches again and again for worldly and supramundane meanings. While seeking and searching, he generates a mind free from weariness. Thus his freedom from weariness arises. Being unwearied, he becomes learned in all scriptures. From this, his knowledge of scriptures arises. Being thus equipped with scriptural knowledge, with an intellect that examines what should and should not be done, he conducts himself appropriately among beings of low, middling, and excellent [disposition], according to his ability and share. From this, his knowledge of the world arises. Being knowledgeable of the world, conducting himself at the proper time and occasion, with a continuum adorned by modesty and conscience, he applies himself to purposes for himself and others. From this, his modesty and conscience arise. In those endeavors, conducting himself in renunciation, he attains the endowment of irreversible, unshakable strength. Thus his endowment of the strength of fortitude arises. Having attained the endowment of the strength of fortitude, he applies himself to worship and attendance upon the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and practices according to the teaching. Thus these ten <s>dharmas</s> that purify the <s>bhūmi</s> arise for him. Namely: faith, compassion, friendliness, giving, patience in hardship, knowledge of scriptures, knowledge of the world, modesty and conscience, the endowment of the strength of fortitude, and worship and attendance upon the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

body.text: tasya asyāṃ pramuditāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya bahavo buddhā ābhāsamāgacchanti audārikadarśanena praṇidhānabalena ca / bahūni buddhaśatāni bahūni buddhasahasrāṇi bahūni buddhaśatasahasrāṇi bahūni buddhanayutaśatasahasrāṇi bahavo buddhakoṭyo bahūni buddhakoṭīśatāni bahūni buddhakoṭīsahasrāṇi bahūni buddhakoṭīśatasahasrāṇi bahūni buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyābhāsamāgacchanti audārikadarśanena praṇidhānabalena ca / sa tāṃstathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān dṛṣṭvā udārādhyāśayena satkaroti gurukaroti mānayati pūjayati, cīvarapiṇḍapātraśayānāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiśca pratipādayati / bodhisattvasukhopadhānaṃ copasaṃharati / saṃghagaṇasaṃmānatāṃ ca karoti / tāni ca kuśalamūlānyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayati / tāṃśca asya buddhān bhagavataḥ pūjayataḥ sattvaparipāka ājāto bhavati / sa sattvāṃśca paripācayati
body.translated_text: For this <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Pramuditā</s>, many <s>Buddhas</s> come into [his] presence through direct vision and through the power of vows: many hundreds of <s>Buddhas</s>, many thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, many hundreds of thousands of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, many hundreds of <s>koṭis</s>, many thousands of <s>koṭis</s>, many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s>, many hundreds of thousands of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> come into [his] presence through direct vision and through the power of vows. Having seen those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, with noble higher intention he honors, reveres, esteems, and worships them, and provides them with robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines for the sick and other requisites. He also provides for the comfort of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and shows respect to the community of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. He dedicates those wholesome roots to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Through his worship of those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones, the ripening of beings arises for him. He ripens beings

body.text: dānena priyavadyena ca adhimuktibalena ca / asyopari dve arthasaṃgrahavastūnyājāyete na tu khalvaśeṣajñānaprativedhapratilambhena / tasya daśabhyaḥ pāramitābhyo dānapāramitā atiriktatamā bhavati, na ca pariśeṣāsu na samudāgacchati yathābalaṃ yathābhajamānam / sa yathā yathā buddhāṃśca bhagavataḥ pūjayati, sattvaparipākāya ca prayujya tānimān daśa bhūmipariśodhakān dharmān samādāya vartate, tathā tathāsya tāni kuśalamūlāni sarvajñatāpariṇāmitāni bhūyasyā mātrayottapyante, pariśuddhyanti, karmaṇyāni ca bhavanti yathākāmatayā / tadyathāpi nāma bhavanto jinaputrā jātarūpaṃ kuśalena karmāreṇa yathā yathāgnau prakṣipyate, tathā tathā pariśuddhyati karmaṇyaṃ ca bhavati vibhūṣaṇālaṃkāravidhiṣu yathākāmatayā, evameva bhavanto jinaputrā yathā yathā bodhisattvo ... peyālaṃ ... yathākāmatayā //
body.translated_text: through giving, through kind speech, and through the power of aspiration. Two further means of gathering [beings] arise for him above, but not through the attainment of the penetration of complete knowledge. Among the ten <s>pāramitās</s>, <s>dānapāramitā</s> (the perfection of giving) becomes the most prominent for him, though he does not fail to practice the remaining [<s>pāramitās</s>] according to his ability and share. As he worships the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones, as he applies himself to the ripening of beings, and as he undertakes and practices these ten <s>dharmas</s> that purify the <s>bhūmi</s>—to that extent his wholesome roots, dedicated to <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge), become ever more refined, purified, and workable at will. Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, natural gold, the more it is cast into fire by a skilled goldsmith, the more it is purified and becomes workable at will for the purposes of ornamental jewelry—even so, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the more the <s>Bodhisattva</s> ... [abbreviated passage] ... [his wholesome roots become purified and workable] at will.

body.text:
