punaraparaṃ bhavanto jinaputra bodhisattvena asyāṃ prathamāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitena asyā eva prathamāyā bodhisattvabhūmerākārapratilambhaniṣyandāḥ parimārgitavyāḥ parigaveṣitavyāḥ paripraṣṭavyāḥ / buddhabodhisattvānāṃ kalyāṇamitrāṇāṃ ca sakāśādatṛptena ca bhavitavyaṃ bhūmyaṅgapariniṣpādanāya / evaṃ yāvaddaśamyā bodhisattvabhūmeraṅgapariniṣpādanāya / tena bhūmipakṣapratipakṣakuśalena ca bhavitavyaṃ bhūmisaṃvartavivartakuśalena ca bhūmyākāraniṣyandakuśalena ca bhūmipratilambhavibhāvanākuśalena ca bhūmyaṅgapariśodhanakuśalena ca bhūmerbhūmisaṃkramaṇakuśalena ca bhūmibhūmivyavasthānakuśalena ca bhūmibhūmiviśeṣajñānakuśalena ca bhūmibhūmipratilambhāpratyudāvartyakuśalena ca sarvabodhisattvabhūmipariśodhanatayā tathāgatajñānabhūmyākramaṇakuśalena ca bhavitavyam / evaṃ bhūmyākārābhinirhārakuśalasya hi bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasya prathamāyā bodhisattvabhūmerucchalitasya niṣṭhānaṃ na saṃbhavati yāvaddaśabhūmibhūmyākramaṇamiti / mārgādhiṣṭhānāgamena ca bhūmejñānālokena ca buddhajñānālokaṃ prāpnoti / tadyathāpi nāma bhavanto jinaputrāḥ kuśalaḥ sārthavāho mahāsārthaparikarṣaṇābhiprāyo mahānagaramanuprāpayitukāmaḥ ādāveva mārgaguṇāṃśca mārgavivartadoṣāṃśca mārgasthānāntaraviśeṣāṃśca mārgasthānāntaravivartadoṣāṃśca mārgakriyāpathyodanakāryatāṃ ca parimārgayati parigaveṣayate / sa yāvanmahānagarānuprāptaye kuśalo bhavatyanuccalita eva prathamānmārgāntarasthānāt / sa evaṃ jñānavicāritayā buddhyā mahāpathyodanasamṛddhyā anupūrveṇa mahāsārthena sārdhaṃ yāvanmahānagaramanuprāpnoti, na cāṭavīkāntāradoṣaiḥ sārthasya vā ātmano vāsyopaghātaḥ saṃpadyate / evameva bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvaḥ kuśalo mahāsārthavāho yadā prathamāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito bhavati, tadā bhūmipakṣapratipakṣakuśalo bhavati, bhūmisaṃvartavivartakuśalo bhavati, bhūmyākāraniṣyandakuśalo bhavati, bhūmipratilambhavibhāvanākuśalo bhavati, bhūmyaṅgapariśodhanakuśalo bhavati, bhūmerbhūmisaṃkramaṇakuśalo bhavati, bhūmibhūmivyavasthānakuśalo bhavati, bhūmibhūmiviśeṣajñānakuśalo bhavati,
bhūmibhūmipratilambhāpratyudāvartyakuśalo bhavati, sarvabodhisattvabhūmipariśodhanatayā tathāgatajñānabhūmyākramaṇakuśalaśca bhavati / tadā bodhisattvo mahāpuṇyasaṃbhārapathyodanasusaṃgṛhito
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this first <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> should seek, search for, and inquire about the aspects, attainments, and outflows of this very first <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>—from the <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and spiritual friends—and should be insatiable in perfecting the factors of the <s>bhūmi</s>. Likewise up to perfecting the factors of the tenth <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>. He should become skilled in the allies and adversaries of the <s>bhūmis</s>, skilled in the arising and decline of the <s>bhūmis</s>, skilled in the aspects and outflows of the <s>bhūmis</s>, skilled in the elucidation of attaining the <s>bhūmis</s>, skilled in the purification of the factors of the <s>bhūmis</s>, skilled in the transition from <s>bhūmi</s> to <s>bhūmi</s>, skilled in the establishment of each <s>bhūmi</s>, skilled in the distinctive knowledge of each <s>bhūmi</s>, skilled in the irreversibility of attaining each <s>bhūmi</s>, and through the purification of all <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmis</s>, skilled in ascending to the knowledge-stage of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is thus skilled in accomplishing the aspects of the <s>bhūmis</s>, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, having set forth from the first <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>, there is no stopping until the ascending of the ten <s>bhūmis</s>. Through the approach of the path-empowerment and the light of knowledge of the <s>bhūmis</s>, he attains the light of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, a skilled caravan-leader, intending to guide a great caravan and wishing to bring it to a great city, at the very outset seeks and searches for the virtues of the road, the faults of detours from the road, the special features of intermediate stations on the road, the faults of the intermediate detours, and the provisions and nourishing food needed for the road-journey. He becomes skilled in reaching the great city without [having to] depart even from the first intermediate station on the road. With such knowledge-guided intellect, with abundance of provisions and nourishing food, he gradually brings the great caravan all the way to the great city, without any harm befalling the caravan or himself from the dangers of the wilderness. Even so, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the skilled great caravan-leader, is established on the first <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>, he becomes skilled in the allies and adversaries of the <s>bhūmis</s>, skilled in the arising and decline of the <s>bhūmis</s>, skilled in the aspects and outflows, skilled in the elucidation of attainments, skilled in the purification of factors, skilled in the transition from <s>bhūmi</s> to <s>bhūmi</s>, skilled in the establishment of each <s>bhūmi</s>, skilled in the distinctive knowledge of each <s>bhūmi</s>, skilled in the irreversibility of attaining each <s>bhūmi</s>, and through the purification of all <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmis</s>, skilled in ascending to the knowledge-stage of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, well-sustained by the provisions and nourishing food of the great accumulation of merit,

body.text: jñānasaṃbhārasukṛtavicayo mahāsattvasārthaparikarṣaṇābhiprāyaḥ sarvajñatāmahānagaramanuprāpayitukāmaḥ ādāveva bhūmimārgaguṇāṃśca bhūmimārgavivartadoṣāṃśca bhūmimārgasthānāntaraviśeṣāṃśca bhūmimārgasthānāntaravivartadoṣāṃśca mahāpuṇyajñānasaṃbhārapathyadanakriyākāryatāṃ ca parimārgate parigaveṣate buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ kalyāṇamitrāṇāṃ ca sakāśāt / sa yāvatsarvajñatāmahānagarānuprāptikuśalo bhavatyanuccalita eva prathamānmārgāntarasthānāt / sa evaṃ jñānavicāritayā buddhyā mahāpuṇyajñānasaṃbhārapathyadanasaṃruddhayā mahāntaṃ sattvasārthaṃ yathāparipācitaṃ saṃsārāṭavīkāntāradurgādatikramya yāvatsarvajñatāmahānagaramanuprāpayati / na saṃsāraṭavīkāntāradoṣaiḥ sattvasārthasya vā ātmano vā asyopaghātaḥ saṃpadyate / tasmāttarhi bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvena aparikhinnena bhūmiparikarmaparikarmaviśeṣābhiyuktena bhavitavyam / ayaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasya prathamāyāḥ pramuditāyā bodhisattvabhūmermukhapraveśaḥ samāsato nirdiśyate //
body.translated_text: with discernment well-exercised through the accumulation of knowledge, intending to guide the great caravan of beings, wishing to bring them to the great city of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge)—at the very outset, from the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and spiritual friends, he seeks and searches for the virtues of the path of the <s>bhūmis</s>, the faults of detours from the path of the <s>bhūmis</s>, the special features of intermediate stations on the path of the <s>bhūmis</s>, the faults of intermediate detours from the path of the <s>bhūmis</s>, and the provisions and nourishing food of the great accumulations of merit and knowledge needed for the journey. He becomes skilled in reaching the great city of <s>sarvajñatā</s> without [having to] depart even from the first intermediate station on the path. With such knowledge-guided intellect, with the abundance of provisions and nourishing food of the great accumulations of merit and knowledge, having crossed the great wilderness dangers of <s>saṃsāra</s> together with the great caravan of beings according to their ripening, he brings them all the way to the great city of <s>sarvajñatā</s>. No harm befalls the caravan of beings or himself from the dangers of the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therefore, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should apply himself unwearied to the specific preparatory work of purifying the <s>bhūmis</s>. This, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, is the introductory entry to the first <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>, <s>Pramuditā</s>, described in brief.

body.text: yo 'syāṃ pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo bhūyastvena jambūdvīpeśvaro bhavati mahaiśvaryādhipatyapratilabdho dharmānurakṣī kṛtī prabhuḥ sattvān mahātyāgena saṃgrahītukuśalaḥ sattvānāṃ mātsaryamalavinivṛttaye 'paryanto mahātyāgārambhaiḥ / yacca kiṃcitkarmārabhate dānena vā priyavadyatayā vā arthakriyayā vā samānārthatayā vā, tatsarvamavirahitaṃ buddhamanasikārairdharmamanasikāraiḥ saṃghamanasikārairbodhisattvamanasikārairbodhisattvacaryāmanasikāraiḥ pāramitāmanasikārairbhūmimanasikārairbalamanasikārairvaiśāradyamanasikārairāveṇikabuddhadharmamanasikārairyāvatsarvākāravaropetasarvajñajñānamanasikaraiḥ / kimiti? sarvasattvānāmagryo bhaveyaṃ śreṣṭho jyeṣṭho varaḥ pravara uttamo 'nuttamo nāyako vināyakaḥ pariṇāyako yāvatsarvajñajñānapratiśaraṇo bhaveyam iti / ākāṅkṣaṃśca tathārūpaṃ vīryamārabhate yathārūpeṇa vīryārambheṇa sarvagṛhakalatrabhogānutsṛjya tathāgataśāsane pravrajati / pravrajitaśca san ekakṣaṇalavamuhūrtena samādhiśataṃ ca pratilabhate samāpadyate ca / buddhaśataṃ ca paśyati, teṣāṃ cādhiṣṭhānaṃ saṃjānīte / lokadhātuśataṃ ca kampayati / kṣetraśataṃ cākramati / lokadhātuśataṃ cāvabhāsayati / sattvaśataṃ ca paripācayati / kalpaśataṃ ca tiṣṭhati / kalpaśataṃ ca pūrvāntāparāntataḥ praviśati / dharmamukhaśataṃ ca pravicinoti / kāyaśataṃ cādarśayati / kāyaṃ kāyaṃ ca bodhisattvaśataparivāramādarśayati / tathā uttare praṇidhānabalikā bodhisattvāḥ praṇidhānaviśeṣikatayā vikurvanti yeṣāṃ na sukarā saṃkhyā kurtuṃ kāyasya vā prabhāyā vā ṛdvervā cakṣuṣo vā gocarasya vā svarasya vā caryāyā vā vyūhasya vā adhiṣṭhānasya vā adhimuktervā abhisaṃskāraṇāṃ vā yāvadevatāvadbhirapi kalpakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrairiti //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this [first <s>bhūmi</s>] mostly becomes a sovereign lord of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, having attained great sovereignty and dominion, a protector of <s>Dharma</s>, capable, powerful, skilled in embracing beings through great generosity, and boundless in undertakings of great generosity for the removal of the stain of miserliness from beings. Whatever action he undertakes—whether through giving, through kindly speech, through beneficial conduct, or through joint endeavor—all of it is never separated from mental attention to the <s>Buddha</s>, mental attention to the <s>Dharma</s>, mental attention to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, mental attention to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, mental attention to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practices, mental attention to the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), mental attention to the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages), mental attention to the powers, mental attention to the fearlessnesses, mental attention to the distinctive <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, up to mental attention to the omniscient knowledge endowed with all excellent aspects. [Thinking:] 'How may I become the foremost among all beings, the best, the eldest, the excellent, the most excellent, the supreme, the unsurpassed, the leader, the guide, the chief guide—up to: how may I become one who takes refuge in omniscient knowledge!' And desiring thus, he undertakes such exertion that, by that undertaking of exertion, he renounces all household, wife, and enjoyments and goes forth in the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having gone forth, in a single instant, moment, or <s>muhūrta</s>, he attains a hundred <s>samādhis</s> and enters them; he sees a hundred <s>Buddhas</s> and recognizes their empowerment; he causes a hundred world-realms to tremble; he traverses a hundred fields; he illuminates a hundred world-realms; he ripens a hundred beings; he endures for a hundred <s>kalpas</s>; he enters a hundred <s>kalpas</s> of past and future; he investigates a hundred <s>Dharma</s>-doors; he displays a hundred bodies; and for each body he displays an entourage of a hundred <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Moreover, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are strong in aspiration, through the distinction of their aspirations, perform transformations that are not easy to reckon—whether of body, radiance, supernatural power, vision, domain, voice, practice, array, empowerment, resolve, or volitions—even in hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>.

body.text: pramuditā nāma prathamā bhūmiḥ //
body.translated_text: The first <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Pramuditā</s> (the Joyful).

body.text: 2 vimalā nāma dvitīyā bhūmiḥ /
body.translated_text: 2. The second <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Vimalā</s> (the Stainless).

body.text: vajragarbho bodhisattva āha - yo 'yaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvaḥ prathamāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau suparikarmakṛto dvitīyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmimabhilaṣati, tasya daśa cittāśayāḥ pravartante / katame daśa? yaduta ṛjvāśayatā ca mṛdvāśayatā ca karmaṇyāśayatā ca damāśayatā ca śamāśayatā ca kalyāṇāśayatā ca asaṃsṛṣṭāśayatā ca anapekṣāśayatā ca udārāśayatā ca māhātmyāśayatā ca / ime daśa cittāśayāḥ pravartante / tato dvitīyāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau vimalāyāṃ pratiṣṭhito bhavati //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s> said: "That <s>Bodhisattva</s>, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, who has been well-prepared on the first <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> and aspires to the second <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>—for him ten mental dispositions become active. Which ten? Namely: straightforward disposition, gentle disposition, capable disposition, tamed disposition, tranquil disposition, virtuous disposition, unentangled disposition, unattached disposition, noble disposition, and magnanimous disposition. These ten mental dispositions become active. Thereupon he becomes established on the second <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>, <s>Vimalā</s> (the Stainless)."

body.text: tatra bhavanto jinaputrā vimalāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito bodhisattvaḥ prakṛtyaiva daśabhiḥ kuśalaiḥ karmapathaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta prāṇātipātātprativirato bhavati / nihatadaṇḍo nihataśastro nihatavairo lajjāvān dayāpannaḥ sarvaprāṇibhūteṣu hitasukhānukampī maitracittaḥ / sa saṃkalpairapi prāṇivihiṃsāṃ na karoti, kaḥ punarvādaḥ parasattveṣu sattvasaṃjñinaḥ saṃcintyaudārikakāyaviheṭhanayā //
body.translated_text: There, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Vimalā</s> is by nature endowed with the ten wholesome courses of action. Which ten? Namely: he is abstinent from taking life. He has laid down the rod, laid down the sword, laid down enmity; he is modest, compassionate, intent on the welfare and happiness of all living beings, with a mind of loving-kindness. He does not commit harm to living beings even in thought—how much less through deliberately inflicting gross bodily injury on other beings.

body.text: adattādānātprativirataḥ khalu punarbhavati svabhogasaṃtuṣṭaḥ parabhogānabhilāṣī anukampakaḥ / sa paraparigṛhītebhyo vastubhyaḥ paraparigṛhītasaṃjñī steyacittamupasthāpya antaśastṛṇaparṇamapi nādattamādātā bhavati, kaḥ punarvādo 'nyebhyo jīvitopakaraṇebhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Moreover, he is abstinent from taking what is not given; he is content with his own possessions, not covetous of others' possessions, and compassionate. From objects belonging to others, having the perception that they belong to others, he does not even conceive a thought of theft to take even a blade of grass or a leaf—how much less other necessities of life.

body.text: kāmamithyācārātprativirataḥ khalu punarbhavati svadārasaṃtuṣṭaḥ paradārānabhilāṣī / sa paraparigṛhītāsu strīṣu parabhāryāsu gotradhvajadharmarakṣitāsu abhidhyāmapi notpādayati, kaḥ punarvādo dvīndriyasamāpatyā vā anaṅgavijñaptyā vā //
body.translated_text: Moreover, he is abstinent from sexual misconduct; he is content with his own wife and not covetous of others' wives. Toward women who belong to others, who are others' wives, who are protected by family, flag [of marriage], or <s>Dharma</s>, he does not even generate desire—how much less [engage in] the union of the two organs or other forms of sensual expression.

body.text: anṛtavacanātprativirataḥ khalu punarbhavati satyavādī bhūtavādī kālavādī, yathāvādī tathākārī / so 'ntaśaḥ svapnāntaragato 'pi vinidhāya dṛṣṭiṃ kṣāntiṃ ruciṃ matiṃ prekṣāṃ visaṃvādanābhiprāyo nānṛtāṃ vācaṃ niścārayati, kaḥ punarvādaḥ samanvāhṛtya /
body.translated_text: Moreover, he is abstinent from false speech; he speaks truth, speaks what is real, speaks timely, practices what he preaches. He, even when dreaming, having set aside his views, acceptance, inclination, understanding, and judgment, does not utter a false word with the intention to deceive—how much less deliberately.

body.text: piśunavacanātprativirataḥ khalu punarbhavati abhedāviheṭhāpratipannaḥ sattvānām / sa netaḥ śrutvā amutrākhyātā bhavatyamīṣāṃ bhedāya / na amutaḥ śrutvā ihākhyātā bhavatyeṣāṃ bhedāya / na saṃhitān bhinatti, na bhinnānāmanupradānaṃ karoti / na vyagrārāmo bhavati na vyagrarato na vyagrakaraṇīṃ vācaṃ bhāṣate sadbhūtāmasadbhūtāṃ vā //
body.translated_text: Moreover, he is abstinent from divisive speech; he is disposed toward non-division and non-injury of beings. Having heard something here, he does not report it there for the sake of dividing those [people]; having heard something there, he does not report it here for the sake of dividing these [people]. He does not break those who are united, nor does he give encouragement to those who are divided. He does not delight in conflict, does not rejoice in conflict, and does not speak words that create conflict—whether true or false.

body.text: paruṣavacanātprativirataḥ khalu punarbhavati / sa yeyaṃ vāgadeśā karkaśā parakaṭukā parābhisaṃjananī anvakṣānvakṣaprāgbhārā grāmyā pārthagjanakī anelā akarṇasukhā krodharoṣaniścāritā hṛdayaparidahanī manaḥsaṃtāpakarī apriyā amanaāpā amanojñā svasaṃtānaparasaṃtānavināśinī / tathārūpāṃ vācaṃ prahāya yeyaṃ vāk snigdhā mṛdvī manojñā madhurā priyakaraṇī manaāpakaraṇī hitakaraṇī nelā karṇasukhā hṛdayaṃgamā premaṇīyā paurī varṇavispaṣṭā vijñeyā śravaṇīyā niśritā bahujaneṣṭā bahujanakāntā bahujanapriyā bahujanamanaāpā vijñāpannā
body.translated_text: Moreover, he is abstinent from harsh speech. That speech which is repulsive, rough, bitter to others, offensive to others, inciting anger step by step, vulgar, fit for ordinary people, unpleasant, unpleasant to the ear, produced by anger and rage, burning the heart, causing mental torment, disagreeable, displeasing, unlovely, destructive of one's own and others' [mental] continuity—having abandoned such speech, that speech which is smooth, gentle, pleasing, sweet, endearing, agreeable, beneficial, pleasant, pleasant to the ear, heartfelt, lovable, urbane, clear in sound, intelligible, worth hearing, well-founded, desired by many, loved by many, dear to many, pleasing to many, informing,

body.text: sarvasattvahitasukhāvahā samāhitā manautplāvanakarī manaḥprahlādanakarī svasaṃtānaparasaṃtānaprasādanakarī tathārūpāṃ vācaṃ niścārayati //
body.translated_text: conducive to the welfare and happiness of all beings, collected, causing mental elation, causing mental delight, gladdening one's own and others' [mental] continuity—such speech he utters.

body.text: saṃbhinnapralāpātprativirataḥ khalu punarbhavati suparihāryavacanaḥ kālavādī bhūtavādī arthavādī dharmavādī nyāyavādī vinayavādī / sa nidānavatīṃ vācaṃ bhāṣate kālena sāvadānam / sa cāntaśa itihāsapūrvakamapi vacanaṃ parihārya pariharati, kaḥ punarvādo vāgvikṣepeṇa //
body.translated_text: Moreover, he is abstinent from idle chatter; he is careful in speech, speaks timely, speaks what is real, speaks what is meaningful, speaks the <s>Dharma</s>, speaks what is reasonable, speaks what is disciplined. He speaks words that have a basis, at the proper time, with due consideration. He avoids even speech in the form of historical tales with careful avoidance—how much more [does he avoid] throwing words about carelessly.

body.text: anabhidhyāluḥ khalu punarbhavati parasveṣu parakāmeṣu parabhogeṣu paravittopakaraṇeṣu / paraparigṛhīteṣu spṛhāmapi notpādayati, kimiti yatpareṣāṃ tannāma syāditi nābhidhyāmutpādayati, na prārthayate na praṇidadhāti, na lobhacittamutpādayati //
body.translated_text: Moreover, he is free from covetousness toward others' properties, others' pleasures, others' enjoyments, and others' wealth and resources. He does not even generate longing for what belongs to others, [thinking] 'May what belongs to others become mine'—he does not generate covetousness, does not wish for it, does not aspire to it, does not produce a greedy mind.

body.text: avyāpannacittaḥ khalu punarbhavati / sarvasattveṣu maitracitto hitacitto dayācittaḥ sukhacittaḥ snigdhacittaḥ sarvajagadanugrahacittaḥ sarvabhūtahitānukampācittaḥ / sa yānīmāni krodhopanāhakhilamalavyāpādaparidāhasaṃdhukṣitapratighādyāni tāni prahāya yānīmāni hitopasaṃhitāni maitryupasaṃhitāni sarvasattvahitasukhāya vitarkitavicāritāni, tānyanuvitarkayitā bhavati //
body.translated_text: Moreover, his mind is free from malice. Toward all beings he has a mind of loving-kindness, a mind of benevolence, a mind of compassion, a mind of happiness, a mind of affection, a mind of grace toward all the world, a mind of sympathy for the welfare of all beings. Having abandoned those states kindled by anger, resentment, malice, corruption, ill-will, vexation, and hostility, he cultivates those thoughts that are connected with benevolence, connected with loving-kindness, deliberated and considered for the welfare and happiness of all beings.

body.text: samyagdṛṣṭiḥ khalu punarbhavati samyakpathagataḥ kautukamaṅgalanānāprakārakuśīladṛṣṭivigata-ṛjudṛṣṭiraśaṭho 'māyāvī buddhadharmasaṃghaniyatāśayaḥ / sa imān daśa kuśalān karmapathān satatasamitamanurakṣan evaṃ cittāśayamabhinirharati - yā kācitsattvānāmapāyadurgativinipātaprajñaptiḥ sarvā sā eṣāṃ daśānāmakuśalānāṃ karmapathānāṃ samādānahetoḥ / hanta ahamātmanaiva samyakpratipattisthitaḥ parān samyakpratipattau sthāpayiṣyāmi / tatkasya hetoḥ? asthānametadanavakāśo yadātmā vipratipattisthitaḥ parān samyakpratipattau sthāpayet, naitasthānaṃ vidyata iti / sa evaṃ pravicinoti - eṣāṃ daśānāṃ akuśalānāṃ karmapathānāṃ samādānahetornirayatiryagyoniyamalokagatayaḥ prajñāyante / punaḥ kuśalānāṃ karmapathānāṃ samādānahetormanuṣyopapattimādiṃ kṛtvā yāvadbhavāgramityupapattayaḥ prajñāyante / tata uttaṃra ta eva daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathāṃ prajñākāreṇa paribhāvyamānāḥ prādeśikacittatayā traidhātukottrastamānasatayā mahākaruṇāvikalatayā parataḥ śravaṇānugamena ghoṣānugamena ca śrāvakayānaṃ saṃvartayanti / tata uttarataraṃ pariśodhitā aparapraṇeyatayā svayaṃbhūtvānukūlatayā svayamabhisaṃbodhanatayā parato 'parimārgaṇatayā mahākaruṇopāyavikalatayā gambhīredaṃpratyayānubodhanena pratyekabuddhayānaṃ saṃvartayati / tata uttarataraṃ pariśodhitāvipulāpramāṇatayā mahākaruṇopetatayā upāyakauśalasaṃgṛhītatayā saṃbaddhamahāpraṇidhānatayā sarvasattvāparityāgatayā buddhajñānavipuladhyālambanatayā bodhisattvabhūmipariśuddhyai pāramitāpariśuddhyai caryāvipulatvāya saṃvartante / tata uttarataraṃ pariśodhitāḥ sarvākārapariśodhitatvādyāvaddaśabalabalatvāya sarvabuddhadharmāḥ samudāgamāya saṃvartante / tasmāt tarhyasmābhiḥ samābhinirhāre sarvākārapariśodhanābhinirhāra eva yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Moreover, he possesses right view; he follows the right path, is free from various kinds of superstitious observances, lucky signs, and wrong views of many sorts; he has a straight view, is without deceit or fraud, and has firm conviction in the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>. Constantly guarding these ten wholesome courses of action, he generates this mental resolve: 'Whatever designation of lower realms, evil destinies, and downfall there is for beings—all that is due to the adoption of these ten unwholesome courses of action. Come, let me myself, established in right practice, establish others in right practice! For what reason? It is impossible and inconceivable that one who is himself established in wrong practice could establish others in right practice—that situation does not exist.' He reflects thus: 'Due to the adoption of these ten unwholesome courses of action, there arise the realms of hell, animal birth, and the world of <s>Yama</s>. Furthermore, due to the adoption of wholesome courses of action, there arise births beginning from human birth up to the summit of existence. Moreover, those same ten wholesome courses of action, when cultivated with the quality of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), with a limited mind, with a mind that recoils from the three realms, with deficiency in great compassion, following the hearing from others and following their voice—lead to the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle. Still further refined, through not being led by others, through conformity with self-arisen [knowledge], through self-awakening, through not seeking from others, through deficiency in the skillful means of great compassion, and through the awakening of profound dependent origination—they lead to the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle. Still further refined, through being vast and immeasurable, through being endowed with great compassion, through being embraced by skillful means, through being bound to great aspirations, through not abandoning any being, through having the vast field of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge as their object, they lead to the purification of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmis</s>, the purification of the <s>pāramitās</s>, and the vastness of practice. Still further refined, through being purified in all aspects, up to the strength of the ten powers, they lead to the arising of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. Therefore, we should apply ourselves to the complete purification in all aspects in our complete development.'

body.text: sa bhūyasyā mātrayā evaṃ pratisaṃśikṣate - ime khalu punardaśākuśalāḥ karmapathā adhimātratvādāsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā nirayaheturmadhyatvāt tiryagyoniheturmṛdutvādyamalokahetuḥ / tatra
body.translated_text: He trains further thus: 'These ten unwholesome courses of action, when intensely pursued, cultivated, and made habitual, are causes for hell-birth; when middling, causes for animal-birth; when mild, causes for the world of <s>Yama</s>.' Among these,

body.text:
prāṇātipāto nirayamupanayati tiryagyonimupanayati, yamalokamupanayati / atha cetpunarmanuṣyeṣu upapadyate, dvau vipākāvabhinirvartayati alpāyuṣkatāṃ ca bahuglānyatāṃ ca / adattādanaṃ ... peyālaṃ ... parīttabhogatāṃ ca sādhāraṇabhogatāṃ ca / kāmamithyācāro ... anājāneyaparivāratāṃ ca sasapatnadāratāṃ ca / mṛṣāvādo ... abhyākhyānabahulatāṃ ca parairvisaṃvādanatāṃ ca / paiśunyaṃ ... bhinnaparivāratāṃ ca hīnaparivāratāṃ ca / pāruṣyaṃ ... amanāpaśravaṇatāṃ ca kalahavacanatāṃ ca / saṃbhinnapralāpo ... anādeyavacanatāṃ ca aniścitapratibhānatāṃ ca / abhidhyā ... asaṃtuṣṭitāṃ ca mahecchatāṃ ca / vyāpādo ... ahitaiṣitāṃ ca parotpīḍanatāṃ ca / mityādṛṣṭiḥ ... kudṛṣṭipatitaśca bhavati śaṭhaśca māyāvī / evaṃ khalu mahato 'parimāṇasya duḥkhaskandhasya ime daśākuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ samudāgamāya saṃvartante / hanta vayaṃ imān daśākuśalān karmapathān vivarjya dharmārāmaratiratā viharāma / sa imān daśākuśalān karmapathān prahāya daśakuśalakarmapathapratiṣṭhitaḥ parāṃsteṣveva pratiṣṭhāpayati / sa bhūyasyā mātrayā sarvasattvānāmantike hitacittatāmutpādayati / sukhacittatāṃ maitracittatāṃ kṛpācittatāṃ dayācittatāmanugrahacittatāmārakṣācittatāṃ samacittatāmacāryacittatāṃ śāstṛcittatāmutpādayati / tasyaivaṃ bhavati - kudṛṣṭipatitā bateme sattvā viṣamamatayo viṣamāśayā utpathagahanacāriṇaḥ / te 'smābhirbhūtapathasamyagdṛṣṭimārgayāthātathye pratiṣṭhāpayitavyāḥ / bhinnavigṛhītacittavivādopapannā bateme sattvāḥ satatasamitaṃ krodhopanāhasaṃdhukṣitāḥ / te 'smābhiranuttare mahāmaitryupasaṃhāre pratiṣṭhāpayitavyāḥ / atṛptā bateme sattvāḥ paravittābhilāṣiṇo viṣamājīvānucaritāḥ
/ te 'smābhiḥ pariśuddhakāyavāṅmanaskarmāntājīvikāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayitavyāḥ / rāgadveṣamohatrinidānānugatā bateme sattvā vividhakleśāgnijvālābhiḥsatatasamitaṃ pradīptāḥ / na ca tato 'tyantaniḥsaraṇopāyaṃ parimārgayanti / te 'smābhiḥ sarvakleśapraśame nirupadrave nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpayitavyāḥ / mahāmohatamastimirapaṭalāvidyāndhakārāvṛtā bateme sattvā mahāndhakāragahanānupraviṣṭāḥ prajñālokasudūrībhūtā mahāndhakārapraskannāḥ kudṛṣṭikāntārasamavasṛtāḥ / teṣāmasmābhiranāvaraṇaṃ prajñācakṣurviśodhayitavyaṃ yathā sarvadharmayāthātathyāparapraṇayatāṃ pratilapsyante / mahāsaṃsārāṭavīkāntāramārgaprapannā bateme sattvā ayogakṣemiṇo 'nāśvāsaprāptā mahāprapātapatitā nirayatiryagyoniyamalokagatiprapātābhimukhāḥ kudṛṣṭiviṣamajālānuparyavanaddhā mohagahanasaṃchannā mithyāmārgavipathaprayātā jātyandhībhūtāḥ pariṇāyakavikalā aniḥsaraṇe niḥsaraṇasaṃjñino namucipāśabaddhā viṣayataskaropagṛhītāḥ kuśalapariṇāyakavirahitā mārāśayagahanānupraviṣṭā buddhāśayadūrībhūtāḥ / te 'smābhirevaṃvidhāt saṃsārāṭavīkāntāradurgāduttārayitavyā abhayapure ca sarvajñatānagare nirupadrave nirupatāpe pratiṣṭhāpayitavyāḥ / mahaughormyāmathairnimagnā bateme sattvāḥ kāmabhavāvidyādṛṣṭyoghasamavasṛṣṭāḥ saṃsārasrotonuvāhinastṛṣṇānadīprapannā mahāvegagrastā avilokanasamarthāḥ kāmavyāpādavihiṃsāvitarkapratānānucaritāḥ satkāyadṛṣṭyudakarākṣasagṛhītāḥ kāmagahanāvartānupraviṣṭā nandīrāgamadhyasaṃchannā asmimānasthalotsannā dauḥśīlyaviṣamācārāntaḥpuṭībhūtāḥ ṣaḍāyatanagrāmabhayatīramanuccalitāḥ kuśalasaṃtārakavirahitā anāthā
body.translated_text: Taking life leads to hell, leads to the animal realm, leads to the world of <s>Yama</s>. And if one is then reborn among humans, it produces two ripened results: short lifespan and frequent illness. Taking what is not given ... [abbreviated] ... meager possessions and shared possessions. Sexual misconduct ... an ignoble retinue and a co-wife. False speech ... prevalence of false accusations and being deceived by others. Divisive speech ... a divided retinue and a lowly retinue. Harsh speech ... hearing disagreeable things and quarrelsome speech. Idle chatter ... words that are not heeded and confused eloquence. Covetousness ... dissatisfaction and great craving. Ill will ... desire for others' harm and oppressing others. Wrong views ... one falls into wrong views and becomes deceitful and fraudulent. Thus indeed these ten unwholesome courses of action (<s>akuśala karmapatha</s>) conduce to the arising of a great, immeasurable mass of suffering. 'Come, let us abandon these ten unwholesome courses of action and dwell delighting in the garden of the <s>Dharma</s>!' He abandons these ten unwholesome courses of action, establishes himself in the ten wholesome courses of action, and establishes others in them as well. He generates to an even greater degree, toward all beings, a mind of benevolence, a mind of happiness, a mind of friendliness, a mind of compassion, a mind of pity, a mind of helpfulness, a mind of protection, an impartial mind, a mind [regarding all beings] as teacher, a mind [regarding them] as master. This thought occurs to him: 'Alas, these beings have fallen into wrong views, with distorted ideas, distorted dispositions, wandering in the jungle of wrong paths. They are to be established by us on the true path of right views in accordance with reality. Alas, these beings are broken, quarrelsome, constantly inflamed by anger and enmity. They are to be established by us in the supreme embrace of great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>). Alas, these beings are unsatisfied, covetous of others' wealth, following dishonest livelihoods. They are to be established by us in the livelihood of purified bodily, verbal, and mental action. Alas, these beings, followed by the three causes of passion, hatred, and delusion, are constantly ablaze with the flames of manifold afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), and they do not seek the means of final escape from them. They are to be established by us in the pacification of all afflictions, in <s>Nirvāṇa</s> free from calamity. Alas, these beings are enveloped in the great darkness of the film of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), plunged into the thicket of great darkness, far from the light of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), fallen into great darkness, sunk in the wilderness of wrong views. For them, we must purify the unobstructed eye of wisdom, so that they may attain the knowledge of the true nature of all <s>dharmas</s>. Alas, these beings have set out on the path through the wilderness of the great forest of <s>saṃsāra</s>, without safety, without comfort, fallen into a great precipice, facing the precipices of the destinations of hell, the animal realm, and the world of <s>Yama</s>, entangled in the crooked net of wrong views, hidden in the thicket of delusion, gone astray on the wrong path, blinded from birth, lacking a guide, perceiving escape where there is no escape, bound by the snares of <s>Namucī</s> (Māra), seized by the robbers of sense-objects, bereft of a good guide, plunged into the thicket of <s>Māra</s>'s dispositions, far from the disposition of the <s>Buddhas</s>. They are to be rescued by us from such a difficult passage through the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s> and established in the fearless city, the city of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>), free from calamity and affliction. Alas, these beings are submerged by the waves and turbulence of the great flood, fallen into the floods of desire, existence, ignorance, and views, carried along by the current of <s>saṃsāra</s>, swept into the river of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), seized by the great current, unable to look around, following the proliferations of thoughts of desire, malice, and harm, seized by the water-demon of the view of a self-entity (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), plunged into the whirlpool of the thicket of desires, hidden in the midst of delight and passion (<s>nandīrāga</s>), stranded on the sandbank of the conceit 'I am' (<s>asmimāna</s>), caught in the hollow of immoral and unwholesome conduct, not departing from the fearful shore of the village of the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>), bereft of a good ferryman, protectorless,

body.text:
aparāyaṇā aśaraṇāḥ / te 'smābhirmahākaruṇākuśalamūlabalenoddhṛtya nirupadrave 'rajasi kṣeme śive 'bhaye sarvabhayatrāsāpagate sarvajñatāratnadvīpe pratiṣṭhāpayitavyāḥ / ruddhā bateme sattvā bahuduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsabahule 'nunayapratighapriyāpriyavinibandhane saśokaparidevānucarite tṛṣṇānigaḍabandhane māyāśāṭhyāvidyāgahanasaṃchanne traidhātukacārake / te 'smābhiḥ sarvatraidhātukaviveke sarvaduḥkhopaśame 'nāvaraṇanirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpayitavyāḥ / ātmātmīyābhiniviṣṭā bateme sattvāḥ skandhālayānuccalitāścaturviparyāsānuprayātāḥ ṣaḍāyatanaśūnyagrāmasaṃniśritāścaturmahābhūtoragābhidrutāḥ skandhavadhakataskarābhighātitā aparimāṇaduḥkhapratisaṃvedinaḥ / te 'smābhiḥ paramasukhe sarvaniketavigame pratiṣṭhāpayitavyā yaduta sarvāvaraṇaprahāṇanirvāṇe
/ hīnalīnadīnādhimuktā bateme sattvā agryasarvajñajñānacittavikalāḥ sati niḥsaraṇe mahāyāne śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānāvatīrṇamatayaḥ / te 'smābhirudārabuddhadharmamativipulādhyālambena sarvajñajñānalocanatayā anuttare mahāyāne pratiṣṭhāpayitavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: without refuge, without shelter. They are to be rescued by us through the power of the wholesome roots of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) and established on the jewel-island of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>), free from calamity, free from dust, secure, auspicious, fearless, free from all fear and terror. Alas, these beings are imprisoned in [a state] abundant with suffering, grief, and distress, bound by the fetters of attraction and aversion toward the pleasant and unpleasant, accompanied by sorrow and lamentation, bound in the shackles of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), hidden in the thicket of deceit, dishonesty, and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), wandering in the three realms. They are to be established by us in the complete separation from all three realms, in the pacification of all suffering, in unobstructed <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Alas, these beings are attached to self and what belongs to self, not departing from the abode of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), following the four distortions (<s>viparyāsa</s>), dwelling in the empty village of the six sense-bases, pursued by the serpents of the four great elements, assailed by the murderous robbers of the aggregates, experiencing immeasurable suffering. They are to be established by us in supreme happiness, in the complete departure from all abodes, namely in <s>Nirvāṇa</s> through the abandonment of all obstructions. Alas, these beings have inferior, timid, and lowly aspirations, lacking the mind of supreme omniscient knowledge; though the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) is the means of escape, they have descended into the opinions of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles. They are to be established by us in the supreme <s>Mahāyāna</s>, through the exalted aspiration for the vast <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> and through the eye of omniscient knowledge.'

body.text: iti hi bhavanto jinaputrā evaṃ śīlabalādhānānugatasya bodhisattvasya kṛpākaruṇāmaitryabhinirhārakuśalasya sarvasattvānavadhīṣṭakalyāṇamitrasyāparityaktasarvasattvasya kriyākriyābhinirhārakuśalasya vimalāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhitasya bahavo buddhā ābhāsabhāgacchānti ... audārika ... peyālaṃ ... pariṇāmayati / tāṃśca tathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān paryupāsate, teṣāṃ ca sakāśebhyo gauraveṇemāneva daśa kuśalān karmapathān pratigṛhṇāti, yathāpratigṛhītāṃśca nāntarā praṇāśayati / so 'nekān kalpānanekāni kalpaśatāni anekāni kalpasahasrāṇi anekāni kalpaśatasahasrāṇi anekāni kalpaniyutaśatasahasrāni anekakalpakoṭīranekānikalpakoṭiśatāni anekāni kalpakoṭiśatasahasrāni anekāni kalpakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi mātsaryadauḥśīlyamalāpanītatayā tyāgaśīlaviśuddhau samudāgacchati / tadyathāpi nāma bhavanto jinaputrāstadeva jātarūpaṃ kāsīsaprakṣiptaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā sarvamalāpagataṃ bhavati, evameva bhavanto jinaputrāstadeva jātarūpaṃ kāsīsaprakṣiptaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā sarvamalāpagataṃ bhavati, evameva bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvo 'syāṃ vimalāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito 'nekān kalpān yāvadanekāni kalpakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi mātsaryadauḥśīlyamalāpanītatayā tyāgaśīlaviśudvau samudāgacchati / tasya caturbhyaḥ saṃgrahavastubhyaḥ priyavadyatā atiriktatamā bhavati / daśabhyaḥ pāramitābhyaḥ śīlapāramitā atiriktatamā bhavati / na ca pariśeṣāsu na samudāgacchati yathābalaṃ yathābhajamānam //
body.translated_text: Thus, O sons of the Conqueror, when this <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who follows the force of morality, who is skilled in bringing forth compassion and loving-kindness, who is a spiritual friend that has not abandoned any being, who has not forsaken any being, who is skilled in accomplishing both action and non-action, and who is established on the Stainless (<s>Vimalā</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage—many <s>Buddhas</s> appear to him in their reflected forms ... [extensive] ... [abbreviated] ... he dedicates. And he attends those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, and from them he receives with reverence these very ten wholesome courses of action, and having received them he does not let them perish. For many <s>kalpas</s>, many hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>, many thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, many hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, many <s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, many hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, many <s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, through the removal of the stains of miserliness and immorality, he attains purity of generosity and morality. Just as, O sons of the Conqueror, that very gold, when placed in acid, becomes to a greater degree free from all impurities—just so, O sons of the Conqueror, that very gold, when placed in acid, becomes to a greater degree free from all impurities—even so, O sons of the Conqueror, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this Stainless (<s>Vimalā</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, for many <s>kalpas</s> up to many <s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, through the removal of the stains of miserliness and immorality, attains purity of generosity and morality. Of the four means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>), affectionate speech becomes most predominant for him. Of the ten perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>), the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) becomes most predominant. And it is not that he does not attain the rest, but according to his strength and capacity.

body.text: iyaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasya vimalā nāma dvitīyā bodhisattvabhūmiḥ samāsanirdeśataḥ, yasyāṃ pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo bhūyastvena rājā bhavati cakravartī caturdvīpādhipatidharmādhipatyapratilabdhaḥ saptaratnasamanvāgataḥ kṛtī prabhuḥ sattvānāṃ dauḥśīlyamalavinivartanāya kuśalaḥ sattvān daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpayitum / yacca kiṃcit karmārabhate ... peyālam //
body.translated_text: This, O sons of the Conqueror, is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s second <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage called Stainless (<s>Vimalā</s>), described in summary. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this stage becomes for the most part a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), lord of the four continents, having obtained sovereignty of the <s>Dharma</s>, endowed with the seven treasures, capable, powerful, skilled in turning beings away from the stain of immorality, skilled in establishing beings in the ten wholesome courses of action. And whatever action he undertakes ... [abbreviated].

body.text: vimalā nāma dvitīyā bhūmiḥ //
body.translated_text: The second stage, called Stainless (<s>Vimalā</s>).

body.text: 3 prabhākarī nāma tṛtīyā bhūmiḥ /
body.translated_text: 3. The third stage, called Luminous (<s>Prabhākarī</s>).

body.text: vajragarbho bodhisattva āha - yo 'yaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvo dvitīyāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau supariśodhitādhyāśayastṛtīyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmimākramati, sa daśabhiścittāśayamanaskārairākramati / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta śuddhacittāśayamanaskāreṇa ca sthiracittāśayamanaskāreṇa ca nirviccittāśayamanaskāreṇa ca avirāgacittāśayamanaskāreṇa ca avinivartacittāśayamanaskāreṇa ca dṛḍhacittāśayamanaskāreṇa ca uttaptacittāśayamanaskāreṇa ca atṛptacittāśayamanaskāreṇa ca udāracittāśayamanaskāreṇa ca māhātmyacittāśayamanaskāreṇa ca / ebhirdaśabhiścittāśayamanaskārairākramati / sa khalu punarbhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvastṛtīyāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito 'nityatāṃ ca sarvasaṃskāragatasya yathābhūtaṃ pratyavekṣate, duḥkhatāṃ ca aśubhatāṃ ca anāśvāsikatāṃ ca vipralopatāṃ ca acirasthitikatāṃ ca kṣaṇikotpādanirodhatāṃ ca pūrvantāsaṃbhavatāṃ ca aparāntāsaṃkrāntitāṃ ca pratyutpannāvyavasthitatāṃ ca sarvasaṃskāragatasya pratyavekṣate / sa evaṃbhūtaṃ sarvasaṃskāragataṃ saṃpaśyannanabhisaraṃ nirākrandaṃ saśokaṃ saparidevaṃ sopāyāsaṃ priyāpriyavinibaddha duḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsābahulamasaṃnicayabhūtaṃ rāgadveṣamohāgnisaṃpradīptamanekavyādhivivardhitaṃ ca ātmabhāvaṃ saṃpaśyan bhūyasyā mātrayā sarvasaṃskārebhyaścittamuccālayati, tathāgatajñāne ca saṃpreṣayati / sa tathāgatajñānasyācintyatāṃ ca samanupaśyati, atulyatāṃ ca aprameyatāṃ ca durāsadatāṃ ca asaṃspṛṣṭatāṃ ca nirupadravatāṃ ca nirupāyāsatāṃ ca abhayapuragamanīyatāṃ ca apunarāvṛttitāṃ ca bahujanaparitrāṇatāṃ ca samanupaśyati / sa evamapramāṇatāṃ ca tathāgatajñānasya samanupaśyan evaṃ bahūpadravatāṃ ca sarvasaṃskāragatasya vyupaparīkṣamāṇo bhūyasyā mātrayā sattvānāmantike daśa cittāśayānupasthāpayati / katamān daśa? yaduta anāthātrāṇāpratiśaraṇacittāśayatāṃ ca nityadaridrapratiśaraṇacittāśayatāṃ ca rāgadveṣamohāgnisaṃpradīptapratiśaraṇacittāśayatāṃ ca bhavacārakāvaruddhapratiśaraṇacittāśayatāṃ ca satatasamitaklaśagahenāvṛtaprasuptapratiśaraṇacittāśayatāṃ ca vilokanasamarthapratiśaraṇacittāśayatāṃ ca kuśaladharmacchandarahitapratiśaraṇacittāśayatāṃ ca buddhadharmapramuṣitapratiśaraṇacittāśayatāṃ ca saṃsārasrotonuvāhipratiśaraṇacittāśayatāṃ ca mokṣopāyapraṇaṣṭapratiśaraṇacittāśayatāṃ ca / imān daśa cittāśayanupasthāpayati //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s> said: 'That <s>Bodhisattva</s>, O sons of the Conqueror, who has well-purified his aspirations on the second <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage and enters the third <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage—he enters with ten mental dispositions and attentions. Which ten? Namely, the attention of a pure mental disposition, the attention of a stable mental disposition, the attention of a disenchanted mental disposition, the attention of a dispassionate mental disposition, the attention of an irreversible mental disposition, the attention of a firm mental disposition, the attention of a refined mental disposition, the attention of an insatiable mental disposition, the attention of an exalted mental disposition, and the attention of a great mental disposition. With these ten mental dispositions and attentions he enters. Now, O sons of the Conqueror, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the third <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage contemplates as it truly is the impermanence of all conditioned things (<s>saṃskāra</s>), their suffering, their impurity, their unreliability, their dissolution, their impermanence, their momentary arising and cessation, their non-origination in the past, their non-passing-on in the future, their non-abiding in the present—all this pertaining to conditioned things he contemplates. He, seeing the conditioned state of all things thus—without refuge, without appeal, full of sorrow and lamentation, full of distress, bound by the fetters of the pleasant and unpleasant, abundant in suffering, grief, and distress, without accumulation, ablaze with the fires of passion, hatred, and delusion, growing with manifold diseases—seeing this embodied existence, he to a greater degree turns his mind away from all conditioned things and directs it toward the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. He contemplates the inconceivability of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge, its incomparability, its immeasurability, its inaccessibility, its untouchability, its freedom from calamity, its freedom from distress, its leading to the city of safety, its irreversibility, its capacity to rescue many beings. Seeing thus the immeasurability of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge and investigating the great calamity of all conditioned things, he to a greater degree generates ten mental dispositions toward beings. Which ten? Namely, a mental disposition of refuge for the shelterless, protectorless, and refugeless; a mental disposition of refuge for those always destitute; a mental disposition of refuge for those ablaze with the fires of passion, hatred, and delusion; a mental disposition of refuge for those imprisoned in the wandering through existence; a mental disposition of refuge for those constantly enveloped and asleep in the thicket of afflictions; a mental disposition of refuge for those unable to look around; a mental disposition of refuge for those lacking the desire for wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; a mental disposition of refuge for those who have lost the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>; a mental disposition of refuge for those carried along by the current of <s>saṃsāra</s>; a mental disposition of refuge for those who have lost the means of liberation. These ten mental dispositions he generates.'

body.text: sa evaṃ bahūpadravaṃ sattvadhātuṃ samanupaśyan evaṃ vīryamārabhate - mayaivaite sattvāḥ paritrātavyāḥ parimocayitavyāḥ paritoṣayitavyāḥ saṃropayitavyā vinetavyāḥ parinirvāpayitavyā iti / sa evaṃ nirvidanugataśca sarvasaṃskāragatyā upekṣānugataśca sarvasattveṣu anuśaṃsānugataśca sarvajñajñāne tathāgatajñānapratiśaraṇaḥ sarvasattvaparitrāṇāyābhiyuktaḥ evaṃ vyupaparīkṣate - katamena khalu upāyamārgeṇa śakyā ime sattvā evaṃ bahuduḥkhopakleśaprapatitā abhyuddhartum, atyantasukhe ca nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpayitum, sarvadharmaniḥsaṃśayatāṃ cānuprāpayitumiti?
body.translated_text: Seeing thus the greatly afflicted realm of beings, he arouses vigor thus: 'These very beings are to be rescued by me, liberated, gratified, planted [in wholesome roots], trained, and led to complete <s>Nirvāṇa</s>!' He, thus accompanied by disenchantment regarding all conditioned things, accompanied by equanimity toward all beings, accompanied by the benefit of omniscient knowledge, taking the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge as his refuge, devoted to the rescue of all beings, investigates thus: 'By what skillful path can these beings, who have fallen into such great suffering and affliction, be rescued, established in the ultimate happiness of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, and caused to attain freedom from doubt regarding all <s>dharmas</s>?'

body.text: tasya bodhisattvasyaivaṃ bhavati - nānyatra anāvaraṇavimokṣajñānasthānāt / tacca anāvaraṇajñānavimokṣasthānam nānyatra sarvadharmayathāvadavabodhāt / sa ca sarvadharmayathāvadavabodho nānyatra apracārānutpādacāriṇyāḥ prajñāyāḥ / sa ca prajñāloko nānyatra dhyānakauśalyaviniścayabuddhipratyavekṣaṇāt / tacca dhyānakauśalyaviniścayabuddhipratyavekṣaṇaṃ nānyatra śrutakauśalyāditi //
body.translated_text: That <s>Bodhisattva</s> thinks thus: 'There is nothing apart from the abode of unobstructed liberation-knowledge. And that abode of unobstructed knowledge-liberation is nothing apart from the understanding of all <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are. And that understanding of all <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are is nothing apart from the wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) that operates through non-activity and non-arising. And that light of wisdom is nothing apart from the investigation through the discernment of skill in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). And that investigation through the discernment of skill in <s>dhyāna</s> is nothing apart from skill in learning.'

body.text:
sa evaṃ pratyavekṣitajñāno bhūyasyā mātrayā saddharmaparyeṣaṇābhiyukto viharati / rātridivaṃ dharmaśravaṇārthiko dharmakāmātṛptāpratiprasrabdho buddhardharmaparyeṣṭihetoḥ / dharmārāmo dharmarato dharmapratiśaraṇo dharmanimno dharmapravaṇo dharmaprāgbhāro dharmaparāyaṇo dharmalayano dharmatrāṇo dharmānudharmacārī / sa evaṃ buddhadharmaparyeṣaṇābhiyukto nāsti tatkiṃcid dravyavittajātaṃ vā dhanadhānyakośakoṣṭhāgārajātaṃ vā hiraṇyasuvarṇamaṇimuktāvajravaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajatajātaṃ vā yāvatsarvāṅgapratyaṅgaparityāgo vā yanna parityajati tayā dharmakāmatayā / na ca tasmādduṣkarasaṃjñī bhavati anyatra tasminneva dharmabhāṇakapudgale duṣkarasaṃjñī bhavati yo 'syaikadharmapadamapi deśayati / sa dharmahetornāsti tatkiṃcidupātaṃ bāhyaṃ vastu yanna parityajati / nāsti tatkiciṃdādhyātmikaṃ vastu yanna parityajati / nāsti tatkiṃcidguruparicaryopasthānaṃ yannopādatte / nāsti sā kācid mānābhimānotsarganirmāṇopacāratā yāṃ nopādatte / nāsti sā kācitkāyikī pīḍā yāṃ nopādatte / sa citro bhavatyaśrutadharmapada śravaṇena, na tveva trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātupratimena ratnarāśipratilambhena / sa citro bhavatyekasubhāṣitagāthāśravaṇena na tveva cakravartirājyapratilambhena / sa citro bhavatyaśrutadharmapadaśravaṇena bodhisattvacaryāpariśodhanena na tveva śakratvabrahmatvapratilambhena bahukalpaśatasahasraparyavasānena / sacedidaṃ kaścidevaṃ brūyāt - evamahaṃ tulyamidaṃ dharmapadaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhopanītaṃ bodhisattvacaryāpariśodhanaṃ saṃśrāvayeyam, sacettvaṃ mahatyāmagnikhadāyāṃ saṃprajvalitāyāmekajvālībhūtāyāmātmānaṃ prapātayeḥ, mahāntaṃ ca duḥkhavedanopakramaṃ svaśarīreṇopādadyā iti / tasyaivaṃ bhavati - utsahe 'hamekasyāpi dharmapadasya samyaksaṃbuddhopanītasya bodhisattvacaryāpariśodhanasyārthāya trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātāvagniparipūrṇe brahmalokādātmānamutsraṣṭum, kiṃ punaḥ prākṛtāyāṃ agnikhadāyām / api tu khalu punaḥ sarvairnirayāpāyaduḥkhasaṃvāsairapyasmābhirbuddhadharmāḥ paryeṣitavyāḥ, kiṃ punarmanuṣyaduḥkhasaṃvāsairiti / sa evaṃrūpeṇa vīryārambheṇa dharmān paryeṣate / yathāśruteṣu dharmeṣu ca yoniśaḥ pratyavakṣeṇajātīyo bhavati / tāṃśca dharmān śrutvā svacittanidhyaptyā eko rahogata evaṃ mīmāṃsate - dharmānudharmapratipattyā ime buddhadharmā anugantavyā na kevalaṃ vākkarmapariśuddhyeti / so 'syāṃ prabhākaryāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito bodhisattvo dharmānudharmapratipattihetorviviktaṃ kāmairviviktaṃ pāpakairakuśaladharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ
savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati / sa vitarkavicārāṇāṃ vyupaśamādadhyātmasaṃprasādāccetasa ekotībhāvādavitarkamavicāraṃ samādhijaṃ prītisukhaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati / sa prītervirāgādupekṣako viharati smṛtimān saṃprajānan / sukhaṃ ca kāyena pratisaṃvedayati yattadāryā ācakṣante - upekṣakaḥ smṛtimān / sukhavihārī niṣprītikaṃ tṛtīyaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati / sa sukhasya ca prahāṇādduḥkhasya ca prahāṇātpūrvameva ca saumanasyadaurmanasyayorastaṃgamādaduḥkhāsukhamupekṣāsmṛtipariśuddhaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati / sa sarvaśo rūpasaṃjñānāṃ samatikramāt pratighasaṃjñānāmastaṃgamānnānātvasaṃjñānāmamanasikārādanantakamākāśamityākāśānantyāyatanamupasaṃpadya
body.translated_text: Having thus examined knowledge, he dwells even more devoted to the pursuit of the true <s>Dharma</s>. Day and night he seeks to hear the <s>Dharma</s>, insatiable in his desire for the <s>Dharma</s>, unceasing in the pursuit of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. He delights in the <s>Dharma</s>, rejoices in the <s>Dharma</s>, takes refuge in the <s>Dharma</s>, inclines toward the <s>Dharma</s>, tends toward the <s>Dharma</s>, is drawn toward the <s>Dharma</s>, is devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>, rests in the <s>Dharma</s>, is protected by the <s>Dharma</s>, and practices the <s>Dharma</s> in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>. Being thus devoted to the pursuit of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, there is no material possession or wealth, no treasure of grain, storehouse or granary, no gold, silver, gems, pearls, diamonds, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch, crystal, coral, refined gold or silver, and even the sacrifice of all his limbs and members—nothing that he would not give up out of that desire for the <s>Dharma</s>. And he does not regard this as difficult, except that he regards as difficult the person of the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher who teaches him even a single word of <s>Dharma</s>. For the sake of the <s>Dharma</s>, there is no external thing that he would not give up; there is no internal thing that he would not give up; there is no service and attendance upon a teacher that he would not undertake; there is no abandonment of pride and conceit that he would not undertake; there is no bodily hardship that he would not endure. He is delighted by hearing an unheard word of <s>Dharma</s>, but not even by obtaining a heap of jewels equal to the three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system. He is delighted by hearing a single well-spoken verse, but not even by obtaining the kingdom of a <s>Cakravartin</s>. He is delighted by hearing an unheard word of <s>Dharma</s> that purifies <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct, but not even by obtaining the status of <s>Śakra</s> or <s>Brahmā</s> for many hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>. If someone were to say to him: 'I shall teach you this word of <s>Dharma</s> brought forth by a Perfectly Enlightened One that purifies <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct, if you would throw yourself into a great blazing fire-pit that has become a single mass of flame, and endure great painful sensations with your own body,' he would think thus: 'I am able, for the sake of even a single word of <s>Dharma</s> brought forth by a Perfectly Enlightened One that purifies <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct, to cast myself from the <s>Brahma</s>-world into a three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system filled with fire—how much more so into an ordinary fire-pit! Moreover, all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities should be pursued by us even through dwelling in the sufferings of hells and evil destinies—how much more so through the sufferings of human existence!' With such heroic effort he seeks the <s>Dharma</s>. And regarding the <s>dharmas</s> as heard, he becomes one who examines them thoroughly. Having heard those <s>dharmas</s>, he reflects upon them alone in solitude through his own mental discernment, thinking: 'These <s>Buddha</s>-qualities are to be followed through practice in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, not merely through purification of verbal action.' Standing on this <s>Prabhākarī</s> (Radiant) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for the sake of practice in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome qualities, with initial and sustained thought, with joy and happiness born of seclusion, enters and dwells in the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Through the calming of initial and sustained thought, with inner serenity, with one-pointedness of mind, without initial or sustained thought, with joy and happiness born of concentration, he enters and dwells in the second <s>dhyāna</s>. Through the fading of joy, he dwells equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending. He experiences happiness with the body—that which the Noble Ones declare: 'Equanimous, mindful, dwelling in happiness'—and enters and dwells in the third <s>dhyāna</s> without joy. Through the abandonment of happiness and suffering, and through the prior disappearance of mental pleasure and displeasure, he enters and dwells in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, which is neither painful nor pleasant, purified by equanimity and mindfulness. Through completely transcending perceptions of form, through the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, through non-attention to perceptions of diversity, [thinking] 'Space is infinite,' he enters and dwells in the base of infinite space.

body.text: viharati / sa sarvaśa ākāśānantyāyatanasamatikramādanantaṃ vijñānamiti vijñānānantyāyatanamupasaṃpadya viharati / sa sarvaśo vijñānānantyāyatanasamatikramānnāsti kiṃcidityākiṃcanyāyatanamupasaṃpadya viharati / sa sarvaśa ākiṃcanyāyatanasamatikramānnaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanamupasaṃpadya viharati tenānabhiratipadasthānena nānyatra dharmānudharmapratipattimupādāya //
body.translated_text: He dwells [therein]. Through completely transcending the base of infinite space, [thinking] 'Consciousness is infinite,' he enters and dwells in the base of infinite consciousness. Through completely transcending the base of infinite consciousness, [thinking] 'There is nothing,' he enters and dwells in the base of nothingness. Through completely transcending the base of nothingness, he enters and dwells in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception—yet without taking a stance in that state of non-delight, except through the practice in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: sa maitrīsahagatena cittena vipulena mahadgatenādvayenāpramāṇenāvaireṇāsapatnenānāvaraṇenāvyābādhena sarvatrānugatena dharmadhātuparame loke ākāśadhātuparyavasāne sarvāvantaṃ lokaṃ spharitvopasaṃpadya viharati / evaṃ karuṇāsahagatena cittena / muditāsahagatena cittena / upekṣāsahagatena cittena viharati //
body.translated_text: With a mind accompanied by <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness)—vast, exalted, non-dual, immeasurable, free from enmity, free from hostility, unobstructed, unafflicting, all-pervading, supreme in the <s>Dharma</s>-realm, extending to the limit of the space-realm—he pervades the entire world and enters and dwells therein. Likewise with a mind accompanied by <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), with a mind accompanied by <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), and with a mind accompanied by <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), he dwells.

body.text: so 'nekavidhāṃ ṛddhividhiṃ pratyanubhavati / pṛthivīmapi kampayati / eko 'pi bhūtvā bahudhā bhavati / bahudhāpi bhūtvaiko bhavati / āvirbhāvaṃ tirobhāvamapi pratyanubhavati / tiraḥkuḍyaṃ tiraḥprākāraṃ parvatamapyasajjan gacchati tadyathāpi nāma ākāśe / ākāśe 'pi paryaṅkena krāmati tadyathāpi nāma pakṣiśakuniḥ / pṛthivyāmapyunmajjananimajjanaṃ karoti tadyathāpi nāma udake / udake 'pyamañjan gacchati tadyathāpi pṛthivyām / dhūmayati prajvalati, tadyathāpi nāma mahānagniskandhaḥ / svakāyādapi mahāvāridhārā utsṛjati tadyathāpi nāma mahāmeghaḥ / yābhirvāridhārābhirayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhāturādīptaḥ pradīptaḥ saṃprajvalito 'gninā ekajvālībhūto nirvāpyate / imāvapi candrasūryāvevaṃmaharddhikau evaṃmahānubhāvau pāṇinā parāmṛśati parimārṣṭi yāvadbrahmalokamapi kāyena vaśaṃ vartayati //
body.translated_text: He experiences manifold forms of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>). He causes the earth to tremble. Having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one. He experiences appearing and disappearing. He passes unobstructed through walls, through ramparts, through mountains, as if through space. He travels cross-legged through space, just as a bird. He dives in and out of the earth, as if in water. He walks upon water without sinking, as if on earth. He smokes and blazes, just like a great mass of fire. From his own body he releases great streams of water, just like a great cloud. With those streams of water, this three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system, ablaze, burning, and flaming, having become a single mass of fire, is extinguished. He touches and handles with his hand even the moon and sun, of such great power and such great might. He exerts mastery with his body as far as the <s>Brahma</s>-world.

body.text: sa divyena śrotradhātunā [viśuddhenā]tikrāntamānuṣyakena ubhayān śabdān śṛṇoti divyān mānuṣyākān, sūkṣmānaudārikāṃśca / ye dūre 'ntike vā antaśo daṃśamaśakakīṭamakṣikāṇāmapi śabdān śṛṇoti / [eṣā divyaśrotrābhijñā] //
body.translated_text: With the divine ear-element, purified and surpassing the human, he hears both kinds of sounds—divine and human, subtle and gross—those that are far and near, down to the sounds of gadflies, mosquitoes, insects, and flies. [This is the divine ear superknowledge.]

body.text: sa parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāṃ cetasaiva cittaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sarāgaṃ cittaṃ sarāgacittamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / virāgaṃ cittaṃ virāgacittamiti prajānāti / sadoṣaṃ ... vigatadoṣaṃ ... samohaṃ ... vigatamohaṃ ... sakleśaṃ ... niḥkleśaṃ ... parīttaṃ ... vipulaṃ ... mahadgataṃ ... apramāṇaṃ ... saṃkṣiptaṃ ... [vistīrṇaṃ] ... samāhitaṃ ... asamāhitaṃ ... vimuktaṃ ... avimuktaṃ ... sāṅganam ... anaṅganam ... audārikaṃ cittamaudārikacittamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / anaudārikaṃ cittamanaudārikaṃ cittamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / iti parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāṃ cetasaiva cittaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / [ityeṣā paracittajñānāmijñā] //
body.translated_text: He knows with his mind, as it truly is, the minds of other beings and other persons. He knows a mind with passion as a mind with passion, as it truly is. He knows a mind free from passion as a mind free from passion. A mind with aversion... free from aversion... a mind with delusion... free from delusion... a mind with <s>kleśa</s> (defilement)... free from <s>kleśa</s>... a contracted mind... an expansive mind... an exalted mind... an immeasurable mind... a concentrated mind... a distracted mind... a composed mind... an uncomposed mind... a liberated mind... an unliberated mind... a mind with blemish... a mind without blemish... a gross mind, he knows as a gross mind, as it truly is. A non-gross mind, he knows as a non-gross mind, as it truly is. Thus he knows with his mind, as it truly is, the minds of other beings and other persons. [This is the superknowledge of knowing the minds of others.]

body.text: so 'nekavidhaṃ pūrvanivāsamanusmarati / ekāmapi jātimanusmarati / dve tisraścatasraḥ pañca daśa viṃśatiḥ triṃśataṃ catvāriṃśataṃ pañcāśataṃ jātiśatamanusmarati / anekānyapi jātiśatāni /
body.translated_text: He recollects manifold former abodes. He recollects one birth; two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty births; a hundred births; many hundreds of births;

body.text: anekānyapi jātiśatasahasrāṇi / saṃvartakalpamapi vivartakalpamapi / anekānapi saṃvartavivartakalpānapyanusmarati / kalpaśatamapi kalpasahasramapi kalpakoṭīmapi kalpakoṭīśatamapi kalpakoṭīsahasramapi kalpakoṭīśatasahasramapi yāvadanekānyapi kalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyanusmarati - amutrāhamāsaṃ evaṃnāmā / evaṃgotraḥ evaṃjātiḥ evamāhāra evamāyuḥpramāṇaḥ evaṃ cirasthitikaḥ evaṃ sukhaduḥkhapratisaṃvedī / so 'haṃ tataścyuto 'tropapannaḥ / tataścyuta ihopapannaḥ / iti sākāraṃ soddeśaṃ sanimittamanekavidhaṃ pūrvanivāsamanusmarati / [eṣā pūrvanivāsānusmṛtyabhijñā] //
body.translated_text: many hundreds of thousands of births; a <s>kalpa</s> of dissolution, a <s>kalpa</s> of evolution; many <s>kalpas</s> of dissolution and evolution. He recollects a hundred <s>kalpas</s>, a thousand <s>kalpas</s>, a <s>koṭi</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, a thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, up to many <s>koṭi-niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>: 'There I was, of such a name, such a clan, such a birth, such a diet, of such a lifespan, of such long duration, experiencing such happiness and suffering. Having passed away from there, I was reborn here; having passed away from there, I was reborn here.' Thus with its aspects, its details, and its signs, he recollects manifold former abodes. [This is the superknowledge of recollecting former abodes.]

body.text: sa divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣyakeṇa sattvān paśyati cyavamānānupapadyamānān suvarṇān durvarṇān sugatān durgatān praṇītān hīnān / yathākarmopagān sattvān yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti - ime bhavantaḥ sattvāḥ kāyaduścaritena samanvāgatā vāgduścaritena samanvāgatā [manoduścaritena samanvāgatāḥ] / āryāṇāmapavādakā mithyādṛṣṭayaḥ mithyādṛṣṭikarmasamādānahetostaddhetuṃ tatpratyayaṃ kāyasya bhadātparaṃ maraṇādapāyadurgativinipātanirayeṣūpapadyante / ime punarbhavantaḥ sattvāḥ kāyasucaritena samanvāgatā [vāksucaritena samanvāgatā manaḥsucaritena samanvāgatā] āryāṇāmanapavādakāḥ / samyagdṛṣṭikarmasamādānahetostaddhetuṃ tatpratyayaṃ kāyasya bhedāt paraṃ maraṇātsugatau svarge devalokeṣūpapadyanta iti / [prajānāti / evaṃ] divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamanuṣyeṇa sākāraṃ soddeśaṃ sanimittaṃ sattvān paśyati / cyavamānānupapadyamānān ... yathābhūtaṃ paśyati //
body.translated_text: With the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, he sees beings dying and being reborn—fair and ugly, in good destinies and bad destinies, exalted and lowly. He knows, as it truly is, beings as proceeding according to their <s>karma</s>: 'These beings, endowed with bodily misconduct, endowed with verbal misconduct, [endowed with mental misconduct], slanderers of the Noble Ones, holding wrong views—by reason of undertaking the actions of wrong view, from that cause, from that condition, upon the breaking up of the body, after death, they are reborn in states of misery, evil destinies, perdition, and hells. But these beings, endowed with good bodily conduct, [endowed with good verbal conduct, endowed with good mental conduct], not slanderers of the Noble Ones, holding right views—by reason of undertaking the actions of right view, from that cause, from that condition, upon the breaking up of the body, after death, they are reborn in good destinies, in heaven, among the gods.' [He knows this.] Thus with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, with its aspects, its details, and its signs, he sees beings dying and being reborn... he sees them as they truly are.

body.text: sa imāni dhyānāni vimokṣān samādhīn samāpattīśca samāpadyate, vyuttiṣṭhete / na ca teṣāṃ vaśenopapadyate 'nyatra yatra bodhyaṅgaparipūriṃ paśyati tatra saṃcintya praṇidhānavaśenopapadyate / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi tasya bodhisattvasyopāyakauśalyābhinirhatā cittasaṃtatiḥ //
body.translated_text: He enters and arises from these <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, <s>samādhis</s>, and attainments. Yet he is not reborn under their power; rather, wherever he sees the fulfillment of the factors of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), there he is reborn intentionally, through the power of his vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>). For what reason? Because the mental continuum of that <s>Bodhisattva</s> is produced through skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>).

body.text: tasya asyāṃ prabhākaryāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya bahavo buddhā ābhāsamāgacchanti / peyālaṃ / pariṇāmayati / tāṃśca tathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān paryupāste / teṣāṃ ca dharmadeśanāṃ satkṛtya śṛṇoti udgṛhṇāti dhārayati / śrutvā ca yathābhajamānaṃ pratipattyā samādayati / sa sarvadharmāṇāmasaṃkrāntitāṃ ca avināśitāṃ ca pratītya pratyayatayā vyavalokayati //
body.translated_text: For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> standing on this <s>Prabhākarī</s> (Radiant) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, many <s>Buddhas</s> come into his presence. [Abbreviation.] He dedicates [the merit]. He attends upon those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones. He reverently hears, grasps, and retains their <s>Dharma</s>-teaching. Having heard it, he undertakes it through practice as appropriate. He observes, through dependent origination, the non-transference and non-destruction of all <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: tasya bhūyasyā mātrayā sarvāṇi kāmabandhanāni tanūni bhavanti / sarvāṇi rūpabandhanāni sarvāṇi bhavabandhanāni sarvāṇyavidyābandhanāni tanūni bhavanti / dṛṣṭikṛtabandhanāni ca pūrvameva prahīṇāni bhavanti / tasya asyāṃ prabhākaryāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya ... peyālaṃ ... anupacayaṃ mithyārāgaḥ prahāṇaṃ gacchati anupacayaṃ mithyādoṣaḥ prahāṇaṃ gacchati, anupacayaṃ mithyāmohaḥ prahāṇaṃ gacchati / tāni cāsya kuśalamūlānyuttapyante pariśuddhyanti karmaṇyāni
body.translated_text: To an even greater degree, all his bonds of desire become attenuated; all bonds of form, all bonds of existence, and all bonds of ignorance become attenuated. Bonds created by [wrong] views have already been abandoned previously. For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> standing on this <s>Prabhākarī</s> (Radiant) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage... [abbreviation]... wrong passion goes toward abandonment without accumulation, wrong aversion goes toward abandonment without accumulation, wrong delusion goes toward abandonment without accumulation. And those wholesome roots of his become refined, purified, and workable.

body.text: ca bhavanti / tadyathāpi nāma bhavanto jinaputrāstadeva jātarūpaṃ kuśalasya karmārasya hastagataṃ tulyadharaṇameva pramāṇenāvatiṣṭhate, evameva bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasya asyāṃ prabhākaryāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya anekān kalpān yāvadanekāni kalpakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi ... .prahāṇaṃ gacchanti / tasya bhūyasyā mātrayā kṣāntisauratyāśayatā ca pariśuddhyati, sākhilyamādhuryāśayatā ca akopyāśayatā ca akṣubhitāśayatā ca alubhitāśayatā ca anunnāmavanāmāśayatā ca sarvakṛtapratikṛtānāṃ niḥkāṅkṣāśayatā ca sattvakṛtapratikṛtānāṃ kāṅkṣāśayatā ca aśāṭhyamāyāvitāśayatā ca agahanāśayatā ca pariśuddhyati / tasya caturbhyaḥ saṃgrahavastubhyo 'rthacaryā atiriktatamā bhavati / daśabhyaḥ pāramitābhyaḥ kṣāntipāramitā atiriktatamā bhavati / na ca pariśeṣāsu na samudāgacchati yathābalaṃ yathābhajamānam / iyaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasya prabhākarī nāma tṛtīyā bodhisattvabhūmiḥ samāsanirdeśataḥ, yasyāṃ pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo bhūyastvena indro bhavati devarājastridaśādhipatiḥ kṛtī prabhuḥ sattvānāṃ kāmarāgavinivartanopāyopasaṃhārāya kuśalaḥ sattvān kāmapaṅkādabhyuddhartum, yacca kiṃcit ... peyālaṃ ... yathārūpeṇa vīryārambheṇa ekakṣaṇalavamuhūrtena samādhiśatasahasraṃ ca pratilabhate ... //
body.translated_text: Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the very same gold, when in the hands of a skillful goldsmith, remains equal in weight and measure—even so, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> called <s>Prabhākarī</s> (the Luminous), for many <s>kalpas</s>, up to many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>... [defilements] are eliminated. For him, to a greater degree, his disposition of patience and gentleness is purified, as well as his disposition of graciousness and sweetness, his immovable disposition, his undisturbed disposition, his uncovetous disposition, his disposition free from elation and depression, his disposition of certainty regarding all actions and their results, his disposition of longing for the actions and results of beings, his disposition free from deceit and guile, and his straightforward disposition are purified. Among the four means of attraction, beneficial conduct is most preeminent for him. Among the ten <s>pāramitās</s>, the <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience) is most preeminent for him; yet he does not fail to develop the remaining ones according to his ability and engagement. This, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s third <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> called <s>Prabhākarī</s> (the Luminous), in brief exposition. Established on it, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> mostly becomes <s>Indra</s>, the king of the gods, the lord of the <s>Trayastriṃśa</s> [heaven], capable, powerful, skilled in the means for turning beings away from sensual desire, able to lift beings from the mire of sensual pleasure. Whatever [action he undertakes]... [as before]... by such exertion, in a single instant, moment, or <s>muhūrta</s>, he attains a hundred thousand <s>samādhis</s>...

body.text: prabhākarī nāma tṛtiyā bhūmiḥ //
body.translated_text: The third <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Prabhākarī</s> (the Luminous).

body.text: 4 arciṣmatī nāma caturthī bhūmiḥ /
body.translated_text: 4. The fourth <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (the Radiant).

body.text: vajragarbha āha - yo 'yaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvastṛtīyāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau supariśuddhālokaścaturthī bodhisattvabhūmimākramati, sa daśabhirdharmālokapraveśairākramati / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta sattvadhātuvicāraṇālokapraveśena ca lokadhātuvicaraṇālokapraveśena ca dharmadhātuvicāraṇālokapraveśena ākāśadhātuvicāraṇālokapraveśena ca vijñānadhātuvicāraṇā lokapraveśena ca kāmadhātuvicaraṇālokapraveśena ca rūpadhātuvicaraṇālokapraveśena ca ārūpyadhātuvicaraṇālokapraveśena udārāśayādhimuktidhātuvicaraṇālokapraveśena ca māhātmyāśayādhimuktidhātuvicaraṇālokapraveśena / ebhirdaśabhirdharmālokapraveśairākramati //
body.translated_text: <s>Vajragarbha</s> said: "That <s>Bodhisattva</s>, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, who, having well-purified his illumination on the third <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>, ascends to the fourth <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>—he ascends through ten entries into the illumination of <s>Dharma</s>. Which ten? Namely: through the entry into the illumination of investigating the realm of beings, through the entry into the illumination of investigating the realm of world-systems, through the entry into the illumination of investigating the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), through the entry into the illumination of investigating the realm of space, through the entry into the illumination of investigating the realm of consciousness, through the entry into the illumination of investigating the desire realm, through the entry into the illumination of investigating the form realm, through the entry into the illumination of investigating the formless realm, through the entry into the illumination of investigating the realm of noble aspirations and resolves, and through the entry into the illumination of investigating the realm of magnanimous aspirations and resolves. Through these ten entries into the illumination of <s>Dharma</s> he ascends."

body.text:
tatra bhavanto jinaputrā arciṣmatyā bodhisattvabhūmeḥ sahapratilambhena bodhisattvaḥ saṃvṛtto bhavati tathāgatakule tadātmakadharmapratilambhāya daśabhirjñānaparipācakairdharmaiḥ / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta apratyudāvartyāśayatayā ca triratnābhedyaprasādaniṣṭhāgamanatayā ca saṃskārodayavyayavibhāvanatayā ca svabhāvānutpattyāśayatayā ca lokapravṛttinivṛttyāśayatayā ca karmabhavopapattyāśayatayā ca saṃsāranirvāṇāśayatayā ca sattvakṣetrakarmāśayatayā ca pūrvāntāparāntāśayatayā abhāvakṣayāśayatayā ca / ebhirbhavanto jinaputrā daśabhirjñānaparipācakairdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ saṃvṛtto bhavati tathāgatakule tadātmakadharmapratilambhāya / sa khalu punarbhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvo 'syāmarciṣmatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhito 'dhyātmaṃ kāye kāyānudarśī viharati ātāpī saṃprajānan smṛtimān vinīya loke 'bhidhyādaurmanasye bahirdhā kāye ... adhyātmaṃ bahirdhā kāye / evamevādhyātmaṃ vedanāsu bahirdhā vedanāsu adhyātmaṃ bahirdhā vedanāsu / evamadhyātmaṃ citte bahirdhā citte 'dhyātmaṃ citte / adhyātmaṃ dharmeṣu dharmānudarśī ... bahirdhā dharmeṣu dharmānudarśī ... evamadhyātmaṃ bahirdhā dharmeṣu ... / so 'nutpannānāṃ pāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpādāya cchandaṃ janayati vyāyacchate vīryamārabhate cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti samyakpraṇidadhāti / utpannānāṃ pāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇāya ... / anutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmutpādāya ... / utpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ sthitaye 'saṃpramoṣāya vaipulyāya bhūyobhāvāya bhāvanāya paripūraye ... / chandasamādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgataṃ ṛddhipādaṃ bhāvayati vivekaniśritaṃ virāganiśritaṃ nirodhaniśritaṃ vyavasargapariṇataṃ vīryapariṇataṃ cittapariṇataṃ mīmāṃsāpariṇatam / sa śraddhendriyaṃ bhāvayati vivekaniśritaṃ ... vīryendriyaṃ ... smṛtīndriyaṃ ... samādhīndriyaṃ ... prajñendriyaṃ ... sa / śraddhābalaṃ bhāvayati ... vīryabalaṃ ... smṛtibalaṃ
... samādhibalaṃ ... prajñābalaṃ ... / smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ bhāvayati dharmapravicaya ... vīrya ... prīti ... prasrabdhi ... samādhi ... upekṣā ... / samyakdṛṣṭiṃ bhāvayati ... samyaksaṃkalpaṃ ... samyagvācaṃ ... samyakkarmāntaṃ ... samyagājīvaṃ ... samyagvyāyāmaṃ ... samyaksmṛtiṃ ... samyaksamādhiṃ ... //
body.translated_text: There, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, simultaneously with attaining the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (the Radiant), the <s>Bodhisattva</s> becomes oriented toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s family for the attainment of the <s>dharmas</s> inherent to it, through ten <s>dharmas</s> that ripen knowledge. Which ten? Namely: through having an irreversible disposition, through arriving at unshakable faith in the Three Jewels, through discerning the arising and passing away of <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations), through having a disposition toward the non-arising of own-nature, through having a disposition toward the cessation and arising of the world, through having a disposition toward <s>karma</s>, existence, and rebirth, through having a disposition toward <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, through having a disposition toward beings, fields, and <s>karma</s>, through having a disposition toward past and future, and through having a disposition toward non-existence and exhaustion. Endowed with these ten <s>dharmas</s> that ripen knowledge, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> becomes oriented toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s family for the attainment of the <s>dharmas</s> inherent to it. Moreover, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Arciṣmatī</s> dwells internally contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief regarding the world; [and] externally in the body... internally and externally in the body. Likewise, internally in feelings, externally in feelings, internally and externally in feelings. Likewise, internally in the mind, externally in the mind, internally and externally in the mind. Internally contemplating <s>dharmas</s> in <s>dharmas</s>... externally in <s>dharmas</s>... internally and externally in <s>dharmas</s>... He generates desire for the non-arising of unarisen evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, makes effort, exerts energy, applies his mind, and rightly resolves. For the abandonment of arisen evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>... For the arising of unarisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>... For the maintenance, non-loss, increase, abundance, cultivation, and fulfillment of arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>... He cultivates the base of supernatural power endowed with concentration of desire, abandonment, and volition, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, ripening in relinquishment, ripening in energy, ripening in mind, ripening in investigation. He cultivates the faculty of faith based on seclusion... the faculty of energy... the faculty of mindfulness... the faculty of concentration... the faculty of wisdom... He cultivates the power of faith... the power of energy... the power of mindfulness... the power of concentration... the power of wisdom...
