He cultivates the awakening-factor of mindfulness, of investigation of <s>dharmas</s>... of energy... of joy... of tranquility... of concentration... of equanimity... He cultivates right view... right intention... right speech... right action... right livelihood... right effort... right mindfulness... right concentration...

body.text: tacca sarvasattvasāpekṣatayā ca pūrvapraṇidhānābhinirhāropastabdhatayā ca mahākaruṇāpūrvaṃgamatayā ca mahāmaitryupetatayā ca sarvajñajñānādhyālambanatayā ca buddhakṣetraviṭhapanālaṃkārābhinirhāratayā ca tathāgatabalavaiśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmalakṣaṇānuvyañjanasvaraghoṣasaṃpadabhinirhāratayā ca uttarottaravaiśeṣikadharmaparimārgaṇatayā ca gambhīrabuddhadharmavimokṣaśravaṇānugamanatayā ca
body.translated_text: And all this [is done] with regard for all beings, supported by the development of former aspirations, preceded by great compassion, endowed with great loving-kindness, with omniscient knowledge as its object, for the purpose of developing the adornment and establishment of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, for the purpose of developing the marks of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s powers, fearlessnesses, distinctive <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, major and minor marks, and the perfection of voice, for the purpose of seeking ever-higher distinctive <s>dharmas</s>, and for the purpose of following and hearing the profound <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> of liberation,

body.text:
mahopāyakauśalyabalavicāraṇatayā ca / tasya khalu punarbhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasya asyāmarciṣmatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya yānīmāni satkāyadṛṣṭipūrvaṃgamāni ātmasattvajīvapoṣapudgalaskandhadhātvāyatanābhiniveśasamucchritāni unmiñjitāni nimiñjitāni vicintitāni vitarkitāni kelāyitāni mamāyitāni dhanāyitāni niketasthānāni, tāni sarvāṇi vigatāni bhavanti sma / sa yānīmāni karmāṇyakaraṇīyāni samyaksaṃbuddhavivarṇitāni saṃkleśopasaṃhitāni, tāni sarveṇa sarvaṃ prajahāti / yāni cemāni karmāṇi karaṇīyāni samyaksaṃbuddhapraśastāni bodhimārgasaṃbhārānukūlāni, tāni samādāya vartate / sa bhūyasyā mātrayā yathā yathopāyaprajñābhinirhṛtāni mārgasamudāgamāya mārgāṅgāni bhāvayati, tathā tathā snigdhacittaśca bhavati, maducittaśca karmaṇyacittaśca hitasukhāvahacittaśca aparikliṣṭacittaśca uttarottaraviśeṣaparimārgaṇacittaśca jñānaviśeṣaṇābhilāṣacittaśca sarvajagatparitrāṇacittaśca gurugauravānukūlacittaśca yathāśrutadharmapratipatticittaśca bhavati / sa kṛtajñaśca bhavati, kṛtavedī ca sūrataśca sukhasaṃvāsaśca ṛjuśca mṛduśca agahanacārī ca nirmāyanirmāṇaśca suvacāśca pradakṣiṇagrāhī ca bhavati / sa evaṃ kṣamopeta evaṃ damopeta evaṃ śamopeta evaṃ kṣamadamaśamopeta uttarāṇi bhūmipariśodhakāni mārgāṅgāni manasi kurvāṇaḥ samudācaran aprasrabdhavīryaśca bhavati aparikliṣṭaḥ / apratyudāvartyavīryaśca vipulavīryaśca anantavīryaśca uttaptavīryaśca asamavīryaśca asaṃhāryavīryaśca sarvasattvaparipācanavīryaśca nayānayavibhaktavīryaśca bhavati / tasya bhūyasyā mātrayā āśayadhātuśca viśuddhyati,
adhyāśayadhātuśca na vipravasati, adhimuktidhātuścottapyate, kuśalamūlavivṛddhiścopajāyate, lokamalakaṣāyatā cāpagacchati, sarvasaṃśayavimatisaṃdehāścāsyocchidyante, niṣkāṅkṣābhimukhatā ca paripūryate, prītiprasabdhī ca samudāgacchati, tathāgatādhiṣṭhānaṃ cābhimukhībhavati, apramāṇacittāśayatā ca samudāgacchāti //
body.translated_text: and for the purpose of investigating the power of great skillful means. Moreover, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, for this <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Arciṣmatī</s>, all those dwelling-places preceded by the view of the self-existent body—the clinging to self, being, life, sustainer, person, aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, with their rising and falling, deliberating, reflecting, playing, possessing, owning, and settling—all these are gone. He completely abandons whatever actions are not to be done, censured by the Perfectly Awakened Ones, connected with defilement; and he undertakes and practices whatever actions are to be done, praised by the Perfectly Awakened Ones, conducive to the provisions of the path to awakening. To the greater degree that he cultivates the path-factors for the arising of the path, developed through skillful means and wisdom, to that degree his mind becomes gentle, soft, workable, conducive to welfare and happiness, unafflicted, seeking ever-higher distinction, desirous of distinguished knowledge, intent on the protection of all the world, devoted to the reverence of teachers, and practicing according to the <s>Dharma</s> as heard. He is grateful, acknowledges kindness, is agreeable, easy to live with, straightforward, gentle, of uncomplicated conduct, free from deceit and pretense, tractable, and favorable. Thus endowed with patience, tamed, tranquil, and equipped with patience-taming-tranquility, applying his mind to and practicing the path-factors that purify the higher <s>bhūmis</s>, his energy is unrelaxed and unafflicted. His energy is irreversible, vast, infinite, ardent, unequaled, invincible, [directed toward] the ripening of all beings, and discerning what is proper and improper. To a greater degree, the realm of his disposition is purified, the realm of his higher aspiration does not depart, the realm of his resolve is heated, the growth of his wholesome roots arises, the stain and corruption of the world departs, all his doubts, uncertainties, and hesitations are cut off, his orientation toward freedom from doubt is fulfilled, joy and tranquility arise, his orientation toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s empowerment comes about, and an immeasurable mental disposition arises.

body.text: tasya asyāmarciṣmatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya ... peyālaṃ ... / bhūyastvena ca teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ śāsane pravrajati / tasya bhūyasyā mātrayā āśayādhyāśayādhimuktisamatā viśudhyati / tasya asyāmarciṣmatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya ... āśayādhyāśayādhimuktisamatāviśuddhistiṣṭhati, tāni cāsya kuśalamūlāni sūttaptāni prabhāsvaratarāṇi ca bhavanti / tadyathāpi nāma bhavanto jinaputrāstadeva jātarūpaṃ kuśalena karmāreṇābharaṇīkṛtamasaṃhāryaṃ bhavati tadanyairakṛtābharaṇairjātarūpaiḥ, evameva bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasya asyāmarciṣmatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya tāni kuśalamūlānyasaṃhāryāṇi bhavanti tadanyeṣāmadharabhūmisthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ kuśalamūlaiḥ / tadyathāpi nāma bhavanto jinaputrā maṇiratnaṃ jātaprabhaṃ
body.translated_text: For this <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Arciṣmatī</s>... [as before]... mostly he goes forth in the teaching of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>. To a greater degree, the equality of his disposition, higher aspiration, and resolve is purified. For this <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Arciṣmatī</s>... the purification of the equality of his disposition, higher aspiration, and resolve remains stable, and his wholesome roots become well-heated and ever more radiant. Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the very same gold, when fashioned into an ornament by a skillful goldsmith, becomes unmatched by other unfashioned gold pieces—even so, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the wholesome roots of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Arciṣmatī</s> become unmatched by the wholesome roots of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established on lower <s>bhūmis</s>. Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, a jewel-gem with natural radiance,

body.text: pariśuddharaśmimaṇḍalamālokapramuktamasaṃhāryaṃ bhavati tadanyairapi śuddhaprabhai ratnajātaiḥ, anācchedyaprabhaṃ ca bhavati sarvamārutodakapravarṣaiḥ, evameva bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvo 'syāmarciṣmatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitaḥ sannasaṃhāryo bhavati tadanyairadharabhūmisthitairbodhisattvaiḥ, anācchedyajñānaśca bhavati sarvamārakleśasamudācāraiḥ / tasya caturbhyaḥ saṃgrahavastubhyaḥ samānārthatā atiriktatamā bhavati / daśabhyaḥ pāramitābhyo vīryapāramitā atiriktatamā bhavati, na ca pariśeṣāsu na samudāgacchati yathābalaṃ yathābhajamānam / iyaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasyārciṣmatī nāma caturthī bhūmiḥ samāsanirdeśataḥ, yasyāṃ pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo bhūyastvena suyāmo bhavati devarājaḥ kṛtī prabhuḥ sattvānāṃ satkāyadṛṣṭisamuddhātāya kuśalaḥ sattvān samyagdarśane pratiṣṭhāpayitum / yacca kiṃcit ... ..... //
body.translated_text: with a pure circle of rays emitting light, is unmatched by other gems of pure luster, and its radiance cannot be cut off by all winds and rains—even so, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Arciṣmatī</s> is unmatched by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established on lower <s>bhūmis</s>, and his knowledge cannot be cut off by any activity of <s>Māra</s> or defilements. Among the four means of attraction, joint endeavor is most preeminent for him. Among the ten <s>pāramitās</s>, the <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of energy) is most preeminent for him; yet he does not fail to develop the remaining ones according to his ability and engagement. This, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s fourth <s>bhūmi</s> called <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (the Radiant), in brief exposition. Established on it, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> mostly becomes <s>Suyāma</s>, the king of the gods, capable, powerful, skilled in rooting out the view of the self-existent body in beings, able to establish beings in right view. Whatever [action he undertakes]...

body.text: arciṣmatī nāma caturthī bhūmiḥ //
body.translated_text: The fourth <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (the Radiant).

body.text:
5 sudurjayā nāma pañcamī bhūmiḥ /
vajragarbha āha - yo 'yaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvaścaturthyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau suparipūrṇamārgaḥ pañcamīṃ bodhisattvabhūmimavatarati, sa daśabhiścittāśayaviśuddhisamatābhiravatarati / katamābhirdaśabhiḥ? yaduta atītabuddhadharmaviśuddhyāśayasamatayā ca anāgatabuddhadharmaviśuddhyāśayasamatayā ca pratyutpannabuddhadharmaviśuddhyāśayasamatayā ca śīlaviśuddhyāśayasamatayā ca cittaviśuddhyāśayasamatayā ca dṛṣṭikāṅkṣāvimativilekhāpanayanaviśuddhyāśayasamatayā ca mārgāmārgajñānaviśuddhyāśayasamatayā ca pratipatprahāṇājñānaviśuddhyāśayasamatayā ca sarvabodhipakṣyadharmottarottaravibhāvanaviśuddhyāśayasamatayā ca sarvasattvaparipācanaviśuddhyāśayasamatayā ca / ābhirdaśabhiścittāśayaviśuddhisamatābhiravatarati / sa khalu punarbhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvaḥ pañcamīṃ bodhisattvabhūmimanuprāptaḥ eṣāmeva bodhipakṣyāṇāṃ mārgāṅgānāṃ suparikarmakṛtatvātsupariśodhitādhyāśayatvācca bhūya uttarakālamārgaviśeṣamabhiprārthayamānastathatvānupratipannaśca praṇidhānabalādhānataśca kṛpāmaitrībhyāṃ sarvasattvāparityāgataśca puṇyavijñānasaṃbhāropacayataśca apratiprasrabdhitaśca upāyakauśalyābhinirhārataśca uttarottarabhūmyavabhāsālocanataśca tathāgatādhiṣṭhānasaṃpratyeṣaṇataśca smṛtimatigatibuddhibalādhānataśca apratyudāvartanīyamanasikāro bhūtvā idaṃ duḥkhamāryasatyamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / ayaṃ duḥkhasamudayaḥ āryasatyamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / ayaṃ duḥkhanirodhaḥ āryasatyamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / iyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipadāryasatyamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sa saṃvṛtisatyakuśalaśca bhavati / paramārthasatyakuśalaśca bhavati / lakṣaṇasatyakuśalaśca bhavati / vibhāgasatyakuśalaśca bhavati / nistīraṇasatyakuśalaśca bhavati / vastusatyakuśalaśca bhavati / prabhavasatyakuśalaśca bhavati / kṣayānutpādasatyakuśalaśca bhavati / mārgajñānāvatārasatyakuśalaśca bhavati / sarvabodhisattvabhūmikramānusaṃdhiniṣpādanatayā yāvattathāgatajñānasamudayasatyakuśalaśca bhavati / sa parasattvānāṃ yathāśayasaṃtoṣaṇātsaṃvṛtisatyaṃ prajānāti / ekanayasamavasaraṇātparamārthasatyaṃ prajānāti / svasāmanyalakṣaṇānubodhāllakṣaṇasatyaṃ prajānāti / dharmavibhāgavyavasthānānubodhādvibhāgasatyaṃ prajānāti / skandhadhātvāyatanavyavasthānānubodhānnistīraṇasatyaṃ prajānāti / cittaśarīraprapīḍanopanipātitatvādvastusatyam, gatisaṃdhisaṃbandhanatvātprabhavasatyam,
sarvajvaraparidāhātyantopaśamātkṣayānutpādasatyam, advayānutpādasatyam, advayābhinirhāranmārgajñānāvatārasatyam, sarvākārābhisaṃbodhitsarvabodhisattvabhūmikramānusaṃdhiniṣpādanatayā yāvattathāgatajñānasamudayasatyaṃ prajānāti adhimuktijñānabalādhānānna khalu punarniravaśeṣajñānāt //
body.translated_text: 5. The fifth stage, called <s>Sudurjayā</s> (Difficult to Conquer). <s>Vajragarbha</s> said: O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has completed the path on the fourth <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> enters the fifth <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> through ten equalities of purified intention. Which ten? Namely: through equality of purified intention regarding the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> of the past, through equality of purified intention regarding the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> of the future, through equality of purified intention regarding the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> of the present, through equality of purified intention regarding morality, through equality of purified intention regarding the mind, through equality of purified intention in removing views, doubts, uncertainties, and hesitations, through equality of purified intention regarding knowledge of what is and is not the path, through equality of purified intention regarding knowledge of practice and abandonment, through equality of purified intention in the progressive elucidation of all <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening, and through equality of purified intention in ripening all beings. Through these ten equalities of purified intention, one enters [the fifth <s>bhūmi</s>]. Moreover, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has arrived at the fifth <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>, because of having well-performed the preparatory work for these very path-factors conducive to awakening and because of well-purified higher intention, further seeking a distinction of the path for the time ahead—being one who practices in accordance with <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), through the endowment of the power of vows, through non-abandonment of all beings out of compassion and friendliness, through the accumulation of the stores of merit and knowledge, through unceasing [effort], through the accomplishment of skillful means, through surveying the illumination of progressively higher <s>bhūmis</s>, through seeking the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and through the endowment of the power of mindfulness, intelligence, progress, and understanding—having become one whose mental engagement is irreversible, he knows as it truly is: 'This is the noble truth of suffering.' He knows as it truly is: 'This is the noble truth of the origin of suffering.' He knows as it truly is: 'This is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering.' He knows as it truly is: 'This is the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering.' He becomes skilled in conventional truth, skilled in ultimate truth, skilled in the truth of characteristics, skilled in the truth of distinctions, skilled in the truth of resolution, skilled in the truth of objects, skilled in the truth of origination, skilled in the truth of destruction and non-arising, skilled in the truth of entry into path-knowledge, and skilled in the truth of accomplishing the progressive connection of all <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmis</s>

body.text: sa evaṃ satyakauśalyajñānābhinirhṛtayā buddhyā sarvasaṃskṛtaṃ riktaṃ tucchaṃ mṛṣā moṣadharma avisaṃvādakaṃ bālālāpanamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / tasya bhūyasyā mātrayā sattveṣu mahākaruṇā abhimukhībhavati, mahāmaitryālokaśca prādurbhavati //
body.translated_text: through to the truth of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge). He, with an intellect produced by skill in truths, knows as it truly is that all conditioned [things] are empty, hollow, false, of deceiving nature, not misleading, and mere prattle of fools. In him, to an even greater degree, great compassion turns toward beings, and the light of great friendliness appears.

body.text: sa evaṃ jñānabalādhanaprāptaḥ sarvasattvasāpekṣo buddhajñānābhilāṣī pūrvāntāparāntaṃ sarvasaṃskāragatasya pratyavekṣate yathā pūrvāntato 'vidyābhavatṛṣṇāprasṛtānāṃ sattvānāṃ saṃsārasroto
body.translated_text: He, having thus attained the endowment of the power of knowledge, caring for all beings, aspiring for <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, examines all conditioned formations from their past to their future limits: how, from the past, the stream of <s>saṃsāra</s> carries beings impelled by ignorance, existence, and craving,

body.text: 'nuvāhināṃ skandhālayānucchalitānāṃ duḥkhaskandho vivardhate, nirātmā niḥsattvo nirjīvo niṣpoṣo niṣpudgala ātmātmīyavigataḥ, taṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / yathā ca anāgatasyaiva asatsaṃmohābhilāṣasya vyavacchedaḥ paryanto niḥsaraṇaṃ nāstyasti ca, tacca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti //
body.translated_text: who are unable to depart from the shelter of the aggregates, and whose mass of suffering grows—devoid of self, devoid of a being, devoid of a life-force, devoid of a nourisher, devoid of a person, devoid of self and what belongs to self—he knows this as it truly is. And he knows as it truly is the cutting off, the limit, and the escape from the longing of one deluded in what does not yet exist in the future, and that it both exists and does not exist.

body.text: tasyaivaṃ bhavati - āścaryaṃ yāvadajñānasamūḍhā bateme bālapṛthagjanāḥ, yeṣāmasaṃkhyeyā ātmabhāvā niruddhāḥ, nirudhyante nirotsyante ca / evaṃ ca kṣīyamāṇāḥ kāye na nirvidamutpādayanti / bhūyasyā mātrayā duḥkhayantraṃ vivardhayanti / saṃsārasrotasaśca mahābhayānna nivartante / skandhālayaṃ ca notsṛjanti / dhātūragebhyaśca ga nirvidyante / nandīrāgataścārakaṃ ca nāvabudhyante / ṣaḍāyatanaśūnyagrāmaṃ ca na vyavalokayanti / ahaṃkāramamakārābhiniveśānuśayaṃ ca na prajahanti / mānadṛṣṭiśalyaṃ ca noddharanti / rāgadveṣamohajvalanaṃ ca na praśamayanti / avidyāmohāndhakāraṃ ca na vidhamayanti / tṛṣṇārṇavaṃ ca nocchoṣayanti / daśabalasārthavāhaṃ ca na paryeṣante / mārāśayagahanānugataśca saṃsārasāgare vividhākuśalavitarkagrāhākule pariplavante / apratiśaraṇāstathā saṃvegamāpadyante, bahūni duḥkhāni pratyanubhavanti yaduta jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsān / hanta ahameṣāṃ sattvānāṃ duḥkhārtānāmanāthānāmatrāṇānāmaśaraṇānāmalayanānāmaparāyaṇānāmandhānāmavidyāṇḍakośapaṭalaparyavanaddhānāṃ tamobhibhūtānāmarthāya eko 'dvitīyo bhūtvā tathārūpaṃ puṇyajñānasaṃbhāropacayaṃ bibharmi, yathārūpeṇa puṇyajñānasaṃbhāropacayena saṃbhṛtena ime sarvasattvā atyantaviśuddhimanuprāpnuyuḥ, yāvaddaśabalabalatāmasaṅgajñānaniṣṭhāmanuprāpnuyuriti //
body.translated_text: This thought arises in him: 'How astonishing! These foolish ordinary beings are so deluded by ignorance that innumerable self-existences of theirs have ceased, are ceasing, and will cease. And even while perishing thus, they do not generate disenchantment with the body. They increasingly augment the machinery of suffering. They do not turn back from the great danger of the stream of <s>saṃsāra</s>. They do not relinquish the shelter of the aggregates. They do not become disenchanted with the burning of the elements. They do not understand the prison-house of delight and passion. They do not survey the empty village of the six sense-bases. They do not abandon the latent tendency of the clinging to "I" and "mine." They do not extract the arrow of pride and views. They do not pacify the burning of passion, aversion, and delusion. They do not dispel the darkness of the blindness of ignorance. They do not dry up the ocean of craving. They do not seek the caravan-leader of the ten powers. And, following the thicket of <s>Māra</s>'s dispositions, they drift about in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, teeming with fearsome crocodiles of manifold unwholesome thoughts. Without refuge, they fall into such distress and experience many sufferings—namely, birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and agitation. Alas! Let me become one, alone and without a second, for the sake of these beings who are afflicted by suffering, without a protector, without a shelter, without a refuge, without a resting place, without recourse, blind, enveloped by the egg-shell covering of the darkness of ignorance, overcome by darkness. Let me bear such an accumulation of the stores of merit and knowledge that, when gathered, all these beings may attain ultimate purity, up to the culmination of unobstructed knowledge of the power of the ten powers.'

body.text: sa evaṃ suvilokitajñānābhinirhṛtayā buddhyā yatkiṃcit kuśalamūlabhārabhate, tatsarvasattvaparitrāṇāyārabhate / sarvasattvahitāya sarvasattvasukhāya sarvasattvānukampāyai sarvasattvānupadravāya sarvasattvaparimocanāya sarvasattvānukarṣāya sarvasattvaprasādanāya sarvasattvavinayāya sarvasattvaparinirvāṇāyārabhate //
body.translated_text: He, with an intellect produced by such well-examined knowledge, whatever wholesome roots he undertakes, he undertakes them for the protection of all beings, for the welfare of all beings, for the happiness of all beings, for compassion toward all beings, for the non-harm of all beings, for the liberation of all beings, for the attraction of all beings, for the inspiring of all beings, for the disciplining of all beings, and for the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of all beings.

body.text: sa bhūyasyā mātrayā asyāṃ pañcamyāṃ sudurjayāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito bodhisattvaḥ smṛtimāṃśca bhavati, asaṃpramoṣadharmatayā matimāṃśca bhavati, suviniścitajñānatayā gatimāṃśca bhavati, sūtrārthagatisaṃdhāyabhāṣitāvabodhatayā hrīmāṃśca bhavati, ātmaparānurakṣaṇatayā dhṛtimāṃśca bhavati, saṃvaracāritrānutsargatayā buddhimāṃśca bhavati, sthānāsthānakauśalyasuvicāritatayā jñānānugataśca bhavati, aparapraṇeyatayā prajñānugataśca bhavati, arthānarthasaṃbhedapadakuśalatayā abhijñānirhāraprāptaśca bhavati, bhāvanābhinirhārakuśalatayā upāyakuśalaśca bhavati lokānuvartanatayā / atṛptaśca bhavati puṇyasaṃbhāropacayatayā / apratiprasrabdhavīryaśca bhavati jñānasaṃbhāraparyeṣaṇatayā / aparikhinnāśayaśca bhavati mahāmaitrīkṛpāsaṃbhārasaṃbhṛtatayā / aśithilaparyeṣaṇābhiyuktaśca bhavati tathāgatabalavaiśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmaparyeṣaṇatayā / svabhinirhṛtamanasikārānugataśca bhavati buddhakṣetraviṭhapanālaṃkārābhinirhṛtatayā / vicitrakuśalakriyābhiyuktaśca bhavati lakṣaṇānuvyañjanasamudānayanatayā / satatasamitaṃ svabhiyuktaśca bhavati tathāgatakāyavākcittālaṃkāraparyeṣaṇatayā / mahāgauravopasthānaśīlaśca bhavati sarvabodhisattvadharmabhaṇākaśuśrūṣaṇatayā /
body.translated_text: This <s>Bodhisattva</s>, established to an even greater degree on this fifth <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Sudurjayā</s>, becomes endowed with mindfulness through the nature of non-forgetfulness; endowed with intelligence through well-determined knowledge; endowed with progress through understanding the meaning, progress, and intentional speech of the <s>sūtras</s>; endowed with modesty through guarding oneself and others; endowed with fortitude through non-abandonment of the conduct of restraint; endowed with understanding through well-examined skill in what is and is not appropriate; endowed with following knowledge through not being led by others; endowed with following wisdom through skill in distinguishing the words of meaning and non-meaning; endowed with the accomplishment of superknowledges through skill in accomplishing cultivation; and endowed with skillful means through conformity with the world. He becomes insatiable through the accumulation of the stores of merit; unrelenting in vigor through seeking the accumulation of knowledge; unflagging in intention through being furnished with the stores of great friendliness and compassion; untiring in search, being devoted to seeking the powers, fearlessnesses, and exclusive <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; following the mental engagements produced by himself through the accomplishment of adorning and establishing <s>Buddha</s>-fields; devoted to varied skillful activities through accumulating the marks and minor signs; constantly and continually self-devoted through seeking the adornment of body, speech, and mind of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; disposed to great reverence and attendance through eagerness to listen to all <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Dharma</s>-preachers;

body.text: apratihatacittaśca bhavati bodhicittamahopāyakauśalyasaṃdhyupasaṃhitalokapracāratayā / rātriṃdivamanyacittaparivarjitaśca bhavati sarvasattvaparipācanābhiyogatayā //
body.translated_text: and one of unobstructed mind through worldly conduct connected with the great skillful means of <s>bodhicitta</s>. Day and night, he is one who has abandoned all other thoughts through devotion to the ripening of all beings.

body.text: sa evamabhiyukto dānenāpi sattvān paripācayati, priyavadyatayāpi, arthakriyayāpi, samānārthatayāpi, rūpakāyasaṃdarśanenāpi, dharmadeśanayāpi, bodhisattvacaryāprabhāvanayāpi, tathāgatamāhātmyaprakāśanatayāpi, saṃsāradoṣasaṃdarśanenāpi, buddhajñānānuśaṃsāparikīrtanenāpi, maharddhivikurvaṇābhinirhāraṇānopacārakriyāprayogairapi sattvān paripācayati / sa evaṃ sattvaparipācanābhiyukto buddhajñānānugatacittasaṃtāno 'pratyudāvartanīyakuśalamūlaprayogo vaiśeṣikadharmaparimārgaṇābhiyuktaḥ yānīmāni sattvahitāni loke pracaranti, tadyathā - lipiśāstramudrāsaṃkhyāgaṇanānikṣepādīni nānādhātutantracikitsātantrāṇi śoṣāpasmārabhūtagrahapratiṣedhakāni viṣavetālaprayogapratighātakāni kāvyanāṭakākhyānagāndharvetihāsasaṃpraharṣaṇāni grāmanagarodyānanadīsarastaḍāgapuṣkariṇīpuṣpaphalauṣadhivanaṣaṇḍābhinirhārāṇi suvarṇarūpyamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālaratnākaranidarśanāni candrasūryagrahajyotirnakṣatrabhūmicālamṛgaśakunisvapnanimittāni pradeśapraveśāni sarvāṅgapratyaṅgalakṣaṇāni cārānucāraprayoganimittāni saṃvaracāritrasthānadhyānābhijñāpramāṇārūpyasthānāni, yāni cānyānyapi aviheṭhanāvihiṃsāsaṃprayuktāni sarvasattvahitasukhāvahāni, tānyapyabhinirharati kāruṇikatayā anupūrvabuddhadharmapratiṣṭhāpanāya //
body.translated_text: Thus devoted, he ripens beings through giving, through speaking kindly, through beneficial action, through shared purpose, through displaying a material body, through teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, through illuminating <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct, through revealing the greatness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, through displaying the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>, through proclaiming the benefits of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, and through the application and practice of the accomplishment of great supernatural transformations. Thus devoted to the ripening of beings, with a mind-continuum that follows <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, with irreversible application of wholesome roots, and devoted to seeking distinctive <s>dharmas</s>—whatever things that bring welfare to beings are current in the world, such as: writing, the sciences, seals, mathematics, enumeration, assaying, and the rest; the various treatises on substances and treatises on medicine; those that counteract consumption, epilepsy, and spirit-possession; those that counteract poison, <s>vetāla</s> sorcery, and magical practices; poetry, drama, narratives, music, and history that bring delight; the production of villages, towns, parks, rivers, lakes, ponds, pools, flowers, fruits, medicinal herbs, and forest groves; the display of mines of gold, silver, jewels, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch, crystal, coral, and gems; [knowledge of] the moon, sun, planets, luminaries, constellations, earthquakes, and the omens of animals, birds, and dreams; the entry into regions; the marks of all limbs and parts of the body; the signs of practice in espionage and intelligence; [and skill in] restraint, conduct, stations, <s>dhyānas</s>, superknowledges, the immeasurables, and the formless stations—whatever other things are connected with non-harming and non-injury and bring welfare and happiness to all beings, those too he accomplishes, out of compassion, for the purpose of gradually establishing [beings] in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: tasya asyāṃ sudurjayāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya ... .peyālaṃ ... pariṇāmayati / tāṃśca tathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān paryupāsate, teṣāṃ ca sakāśād gauravacitrīkāreṇa satkṛtya dharmadeśanāṃ śṛṇoti udgṛhṇāti dhārayati / śrutvā ca yathābalaṃ yathābhajamānaṃ pratipatyā saṃpādayati / bhūyastvena ca teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ śāsane pravrajati / pravrajitaśca śrutadhārī dharmabhāṇako bhavati / sa bhūyasyā mātrayā śrutācāradhāraṇīpratilabdho dharmabhāṇako bhavati anekeṣāṃ ca buddhakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇāmantike anekakalpakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇyasaṃpramoṣatayā / tasya asyāṃ sudurjayāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya anekān kalpāṃstāni kuśalamūlānyuttapyante pariśudhyanti prabhāsvaratarāṇi ca bhavanti, anekāni kalpaśatāni ... / tasya tāni kuśalamūlānyuttapyante pariśuddhyanti prabhāsvaratarāṇi ca bhavanti / tadyathāpi nāma bhavanto jinaputrāstadeva jātarūpaṃ musārgalvasṛṣṭaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayottapyate pariśudhyati prabhāsvarataraṃ bhavati, evameva bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasya asyāṃ sudurjayāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya tāni kuśalamūlānyupāyaprajñāvicāritāni bhūyasyā mātrayottapyante pariśuddhyanti, prabhāsvaratarāṇi ca bhavanti, jñānaprayogaguṇābhinirhārādasaṃhāryavicāritatamāni ca bhavanti / tadyathāpi nāma bhavanto jinaputrāścandrasūryagrahajyotirnakṣatrāṇāṃ vimānālokaprabhavātamaṇḍalībhirasaṃhāryā bhavati mārutāsādhāraṇā ca, evameva bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasya asyāṃ sudurjayāyāṃ
body.translated_text: For this <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Sudurjayā</s> ... [abbreviated passage] ... he dedicates [his wholesome roots]. He attends upon those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, and from their presence, having honored them with reverence and esteem, he hears, grasps, and retains the <s>Dharma</s> teaching. Having heard, he fulfills it through practice according to his ability and share. To an even greater extent, he goes forth in the teaching of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Having gone forth, he becomes a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher who retains what he has heard. To an even greater degree, having attained the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of learning, conduct, and retention, he becomes a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, and in the presence of many hundreds of thousands of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, for many hundreds of thousands of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>koṭis</s> of aeons, through non-forgetfulness. For this <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Sudurjayā</s>, over many aeons those wholesome roots become refined, purified, and ever more radiant; over many hundreds of aeons... his wholesome roots become refined, purified, and ever more radiant. Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, that same natural gold, released from the crucible, becomes to an even greater degree refined, purified, and more radiant—even so, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the wholesome roots of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Sudurjayā</s>, examined by skillful means and wisdom, become to an even greater degree refined, purified, and more radiant, and become the most unassailable through the accomplishment of qualities by the application of knowledge. Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the radiant sphere of the light emanating from the palaces of the moon, sun, planets, luminaries, and constellations is unassailable and incomparable to the wind—even so, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> on this <s>Sudurjayā</s>

body.text:
bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya tāni kuśalamūlānyupāyaprajñājñānacittavicāraṇānugatānyasaṃhāryāṇi bhavanti, sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhairlaukikāsādhāraṇāni ca bhavanti / tasya daśabhyaḥ pāramitābhyo dhyānapāramitā atiriktatamā bhavati, na ca pariśeṣāsu na samudāgacchati yathābalaṃ yathābhajamānam / iyaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasya sudurjayā nāma pañcamī bodhisattvabhūmiḥ samāsanirdeśataḥ, yasyāṃ pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo bhūyastvena saṃtuṣito bhavati, devarājaḥ kṛtī prabhuḥ sattvānāṃ sarvatīrthyāyatanavinivartanāya kuśalaḥ sattvān satyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpayitum / yatkiṃcit
... .. //
body.translated_text: For one established in [the fifth] <s>bodhisattva</s> stage, those roots of merit become accompanied by the investigation of mind through skillful means, wisdom, and knowledge, and become indestructible, and they become uncommon to all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> and worldly beings. Of the ten <s>pāramitās</s>, <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation) becomes most predominant for him, though he does not fail to accomplish the remaining ones according to his strength and capacity. This, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, is the fifth <s>bodhisattva</s> stage called <s>Sudurjayā</s> (Extremely Difficult to Conquer), described in summary. A <s>bodhisattva</s> established in it becomes for the most part <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> (a Contented One), a king of <s>devas</s>, accomplished and powerful, skillful in turning beings away from the abodes of all heretical doctrines, and capable of establishing beings in the [four noble] truths. Whatever

body.text: sudurjayā nām pañcamī bhūmiḥ //
body.translated_text: [This is] the fifth stage called <s>Sudurjayā</s>.

body.text: 6 abhimukhī nāma ṣaṣṭhī bhūmiḥ /
body.translated_text: 6. The sixth stage called <s>Abhimukhī</s> (Facing Forward).

body.text: vajragarmo bodhisattva āha - yo 'yaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvaḥ pañcamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau suparipūrṇamārgaḥ ṣaṣṭhīṃ bodhisattvabhūmimavatarati / sa daśabhirdharmasamatābhiravatarati / katamābhirdaśabhiḥ? yaduta sarvadharmānimittasamatayā ca sarvadharmālakṣaṇasamatayā ca sarvadharmānutpādasamatayā ca sarvadharmājātatayā ca sarvadharmaviviktasamatayā ca sarvadharmādiviśuddhisamatayā ca sarvadharmaniṣprapañcasamatayā ca sarvadharmānāvyūhānirvyūhasamatayā ca sarvadharmamāyāsvapnapratibhāsapratiśrutkodakacandrapratibimbanirmāṇasamatayā ca sarvadharmabhāvābhāvādvayasamatayā ca / ābhirdaśabhirdharmasamatābhiravatarati //
body.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s> said: O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who has fully perfected the path on the fifth <s>bodhisattva</s> stage enters the sixth <s>bodhisattva</s> stage. He enters through ten equalities of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmasamatā</s>). Which ten? Namely: through the equality of signlessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, the equality of characteristiclessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, the equality of non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s>, the equality of unbornness of all <s>dharmas</s>, the equality of isolation of all <s>dharmas</s>, the equality of primordial purity of all <s>dharmas</s>, the equality of non-elaboration of all <s>dharmas</s>, the equality of non-construction and non-deconstruction of all <s>dharmas</s>, the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> being like illusions, dreams, reflections, echoes, water-moons, mirror-images, and magical creations, and the equality of non-duality of existence and non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s>. Through these ten equalities of <s>dharmas</s> he enters [the sixth stage].

body.text: sa evaṃsvabhāvān sarvadharmān pratyavakṣemāṇo 'nusṛjan anulomayan avilomayan śraddadhan abhiyan pratiyan avikalpayan anusaran vyavalokayan pratipadyamānaḥ ṣaṣṭhīmabhimukhīṃ bodhisattvabhūmimanuprāpnoti tīkṣṇayā ānulomikyā kṣāntyā / na ca tāvadanutpattikadharmakṣāntimukhamanuprāpnoti //
body.translated_text: Examining, following, conforming to, not opposing, having faith in, approaching, responding to, not conceptualizing, pursuing, observing, and realizing all <s>dharmas</s> of such a nature, he attains the sixth <s>bodhisattva</s> stage called <s>Abhimukhī</s> through sharp conforming patience (<s>ānulomikī kṣānti</s>). Yet he does not yet attain the gateway of patience regarding the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>).

body.text: sa evaṃsvabhāvān sarvadharmānanugacchan bhūyasyā mātrayā mahākaruṇāpūrvaṃgamatvena mahākaruṇādhipateyatayā mahākaruṇāparipūrṇārthaṃ lokasya saṃbhavaṃ ca vibhavaṃ ca vyavalokayate / tasya lokasya saṃbhavaṃ ca vibhavaṃ ca vyavalokayata evaṃ bhavati - yāvatyo lokasamudācāropapattayaḥ sarvāḥ, tā ātmābhiniveśato bhavanti / ātmābhiniveśavigamato na bhavanti lokasamudācāropapattaya iti / tasyaivaṃ bhavati - tena khalu punarime bālabuddhya ātmābhiniviṣṭā ajñānatimirāvṛtā bhāvābhāvābhilāṣiṇo 'yoniśomanasikāraprasṛtā vipathaprayātā mithyānucāriṇaḥ puṇyāpuṇyāneñjyānabhisaṃskārānupacinvanti / teṣāṃ taiḥ saṃskārairavaropitaṃ cittabījaṃ sāsravaṃ sopādānamāyatyāṃ jātijarāmaraṇapunarbhavābhinirvṛttisaṃbhavopagataṃ bhavati / karmakṣetrālayamavidyāndhakāraṃ tṛṣṇāsnehamasmimānapariṣyandanataḥ / dṛṣṭikṛtajālapravṛddhyā ca nāmarūpāṅkuraḥ prādurbhavati / prādurbhūto vivardhate / vivṛddhe nāmarūpe pañcānāmindriyāṇāṃ pravṛttirbhavati / pravṛttānāmindriyāṇāmanyonya(saṃ)nipātataḥ sparśaḥ / sparśasya saṃnipātato vedanā prādurbhavati / vedanāyāstata uttare 'bhinandanā bhavati / tṛṣṇābhinandanata upādānaṃ vivardhate / upādāne vivṛddhe bhavaḥ saṃbhavati / bhave saṃbhūte skandhapañcakamunmajjati / unmagnaṃ skandhapañcakaṃ gatipañcake 'nupūrvaṃ mlāyati / mlānaṃ vigacchati / mlānavigamājjvaraparidāhaḥ / jvaraparidāhanidānāḥ sarvaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ samudāgacchanti / teṣāṃ na kaścitsamudānetā / svabhāvānābhogābhyāṃ ca vigacchanti / na caiṣāṃ kaścidvigamayitā / evaṃ bodhisattvo 'nulomākāraṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ pratyavekṣate //
body.translated_text: Following all <s>dharmas</s> of such a nature, to a greater degree, with great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) as his forerunner, under the sovereignty of great compassion, for the purpose of fulfilling great compassion, he contemplates the arising and passing away of the world. As he contemplates the arising and passing away of the world, it occurs to him thus: All the modes of worldly origination and existence arise dependent on self-grasping.

body.text: tasyaivaṃ bhavati - satyeṣvanabhijñānaṃ paramārthato 'vidyā / avidyāprakṛtasya karmaṇo vipākaḥ saṃskārāḥ / saṃskārasaṃniśritaṃ prathamaṃ cittaṃ vijñānam / vijñānasahajāścatvāra upādānaskandhā
body.translated_text: It occurs to him thus: Non-comprehension of the [four noble] truths is, in the ultimate sense, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). The fruition of action rooted in <s>avidyā</s> constitutes the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations). The initial consciousness dependent on the <s>saṃskāras</s> is <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). The four aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandhas</s>) co-arising with consciousness are

body.text: nāmarūpam / nāmarūpavivṛddhiḥ ṣaḍāyatanam / indriyaviṣayavijñāgatrayasamavadhānaṃ sāsravaṃ sparśaḥ / sparśasahajā vedanā / vedanādhyavasānaṃ tṛṣṇā / tṛṣṇāvivṛddhirupādānam / upādānaprasṛtaṃ sāsravaṃ karma bhavaḥ / karmaniṣyando jātiḥ skandhonmajjanam / skandhaparipāko jarā / jīrṇasya skandhabhedo maraṇam / mriyamāṇasya vigacchataḥ saṃmūḍhasya sābhiṣvaṅgasya hṛdayasaṃtāpaḥ śokaḥ / śokasamutthitā vākpralāpāḥ paridevaḥ / pañcendriyanipāto duḥkham / manodṛṣṭinipāto daurmanasyam / duḥkhadaurmanasyabahulatvasaṃbhūtā upāyāsāḥ / evamayaṃ kevalo duḥkhaskandho duḥkhavṛkṣo 'bhinirvartate kārakavedakavirahita iti //
body.translated_text: <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form). The development of <s>nāmarūpa</s> is the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>). The convergence of the triad of sense faculty, sense object, and consciousness that is tainted (<s>sāsrava</s>) is contact (<s>sparśa</s>). Feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) co-arises with contact. The fixation upon feeling is craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). The intensification of craving is clinging (<s>upādāna</s>). Tainted action issuing from clinging is becoming (<s>bhava</s>). The result flowing from action is birth (<s>jāti</s>)—the emergence of the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>). The maturation of the aggregates is aging (<s>jarā</s>). The disintegration of the aggregates of one who has aged is

body.text: tasyaivaṃ bhavati - kārakābhiniveśataḥ kriyāḥ prajñāyante / yatra kārako nāsti, kriyāpi tatra paramārthato nopalabhyate / tasyaivaṃ bhavati - cittamātramidaṃ yadidaṃ traidhātukam / yānyapīmāni dvādaśa bhavāṅgāni tathāgatena prabhedaśo vyākhyātāni, api sarvāṇyeva tāni cittasamāśritāni / tatkasya hetoḥ? yasmin vastuni hi rāgasaṃyuktaṃ cittamutpadyate tadvijñānam / vastusaṃskāre 'smimoho 'vidyā / avidyācittasahajaṃ nāmarūpam / nāmarūpavivṛddhiḥ ṣaḍāyatanam / ṣaḍāyatanabhāgīyaḥ sparśaḥ / sparśasahajā vedanā / vedayato 'vitṛptistṛṣṇā / tṛṣṇārtasya saṃgraho 'parityāga upādānam / eṣāṃ bhavāṅgānāṃ saṃbhavo bhavaḥ / bhavonmajjanaṃ jātiḥ / jātiparipāko jarā / jarāpagamo maraṇamiti //
body.translated_text: It occurs to him thus: Due to the clinging to a doer, actions are perceived. Where there is no doer, action too is ultimately not found. It occurs to him thus: This triple world (<s>traidhātuka</s>) is mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>). These twelve links of existence (<s>bhavāṅgas</s>), which the <s>Tathāgata</s> has explained in detail, are all entirely dependent on mind. For what reason?

body.text: tatra avidyā dvividhakāryapratyupasthānā bhavati / ālambanataḥ sattvān saṃmohayati, hetuṃ ca dadāti saṃskārābhinirvṛttaye / saṃskārā api dvividhakāryapratyupasthānā bhavanti / anāgatavipākābhinirvṛtti ca kurvanti, hetuṃ ca dadati vijñānābhinirvṛttaye / vijñānamapi dvividhakāryapratyupasthānaṃ bhavati / bhavapratisaṃdhiṃ ca karoti, hetuṃ ca dadāti nāmarūpābhinirvṛttaye / nāmarūpamapi dvividhakāryapratyupasthānaṃ bhavati / anyonyopastambhanaṃ ca karoti, hetuṃ ca dadāti ṣaḍāyatanābhinirvṛttaye / ṣaḍāyatanamapi dvividhakāryapratyupasthānaṃ bhavati / svaviṣayavibhaktitāṃ cādarśayati, hetuṃ ca dadāti sparśābhinirvṛttaye / sparśo 'pi dvividhakāryapratyupasthāno bhavati / ālambanasparśanaṃ ca karoti, hetuṃ ca dadāti vedanābhinirvṛttaye / vedanāpi dvividhakāryapratyupasthānā bhavati / iṣṭāniṣṭobhayavimuktānubhavanaṃ ca karoti, hetuṃ ca dadāti tṛṣṇābhinirvṛttaye / tṛṣṇāpi dvividhakāryapratyupasthānā bhavati / saṃrajanīyavastusaṃrāgaṃ ca karoti, hetuṃ ca dadātyupādānābhinirvṛttaye / upādānamapi dvividhakāryapratyupasthānaṃ bhavati / saṃkleśabandhanaṃ ca karoti, hetuṃ ca dadāti bhavābhinirvṛttaye / bhavo 'pi dvividhakāryapratyupasthāno bhavati / anyabhavagatipratyadhiṣṭhānaṃ ca karoti, hetuṃ ca dadāti jātyabhinirvṛttaye / jātirapi dvividhakāryapratyupasthānā bhavati / skandhonmajjanaṃ ca karoti, hetuṃ ca dadāti jarābhiniṃvṛttaye / jarāpi dvividhakāryapratyupasthānā bhavati / indriyapariṇāmaṃ ca karoti, hetuṃ ca dadāti maraṇasamavadhānābhinirvṛttaye / maraṇamapi dvividhakāryapratyupasthānaṃ bhavati - saṃskāravidhvaṃsanaṃ ca karoti, aparijñānānucchedaṃ ceti //
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) presents itself in a twofold function: it deludes beings with respect to objects, and it serves as the cause for the production of <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations). The <s>saṃskāras</s> too present themselves in a twofold function: they bring about the production of future fruition, and they serve as the cause for the production of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). <s>Vijñāna</s> too presents itself in a twofold function:

body.text: tatra avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā ityavidyāpratyayatā saṃskārāṇāmanucchedo 'nupastambhaśca / saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānamiti saṃskārapratyayatā vijñānānāmanucchedo 'nupastambhaśca / peyālaṃ ... jātipratyayatā jarāmaraṇasyānucchedo 'nupastambhaśca / avidyānirodhātsaṃskāranirodha ityavidyāpratyayatābhāvātsaṃskārāṇāṃ vyupaśamo 'nupastambhaśca / peyālaṃ ... jātipratyayatābhāvājjarāmaraṇasya vyupaśamo 'nupastambhaśca //
body.translated_text: Therein, '<s>saṃskāras</s> are conditioned by <s>avidyā</s>' means that the conditionality of the <s>saṃskāras</s> by <s>avidyā</s> is [their] non-interruption and non-support. '<s>Vijñāna</s> is conditioned by <s>saṃskāras</s>' means that the conditionality of <s>vijñāna</s> by <s>saṃskāras</s> is [their] non-interruption and non-support. [And so on for the rest...] The conditionality of old age and death by birth is [their] non-interruption and non-support. 'From the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> comes the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s>' means that from the absence of the conditionality of <s>avidyā</s>,

body.text: tatra avidyā tṛṣṇopādānaṃ ca kleśavartmano 'vyavacchedaḥ / saṃskārā bhavaśca karmavartmano 'vyavacchedaḥ / pariśeṣaṃ duḥkhavartmano 'vyavacchedaḥ / pravibhāgataḥ pūrvāntāparāntanirodhavartmano vyavacchedaḥ / evameva trivartma nirātmakamātmātmīyarahitaṃ saṃbhavati ca asaṃbhavayogena, vibhavati ca avibhavayogena svabhāvato naḍakalāpasadṛśam //
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>avidyā</s>, <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), and <s>upādāna</s> (clinging) constitute the non-interruption of the path of afflictions (<s>kleśavartman</s>). <s>Saṃskāras</s> and <s>bhava</s> (becoming) constitute the non-interruption of the path of action (<s>karmavartman</s>). The remainder constitutes the non-interruption of the path of suffering (<s>duḥkhavartman</s>). In terms of analysis, the path of cessation of the prior and subsequent limits is interrupted. Thus this triple path, devoid of self, free from self and what belongs to self, arises through the mode of non-arising and ceases through the mode of

body.text: api tu khalu punaryaducyate - avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā ityeṣā paurvāntikyapekṣā / vijñānaṃ yāvadvedanetyeṣā pratyutpannāpekṣā / tṛṣṇa yāvadbhava ityeṣā aparāntikyapekṣā / ata urdhvamasya pravṛttiriti / avidyānirodhātsaṃskāranirodha ityapekṣāvyavaccheda eṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Moreover, when it is said '<s>saṃskāras</s> are conditioned by <s>avidyā</s>'—this is with reference to the past. '<s>Vijñāna</s> up to <s>vedanā</s>'—this is with reference to the present. '<s>Tṛṣṇā</s> up to <s>bhava</s>'—this is with reference to the future. Beyond this is its continuation. 'From the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> comes the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s>'—this is the interruption of that reference.

body.text: api tu khalu punastriduḥkhatā dvādaśa bhavāṅgānyupādāya / tatra avidyā saṃskārā yāvatṣaḍāyatanamityeṣā saṃskāraduḥkhatā / sparśo vedanā caiṣā duḥkhaduḥkhatā / pariśeṣāṇi bhavāṅgānyeṣā pariṇāmaduḥkhatā / avidyānirodhātsaṃskāranirodha iti triduḥkhatāvyavaccheda eṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Moreover, the three kinds of suffering (<s>triduḥkhatā</s>) are understood in terms of the twelve links of existence. Therein, <s>avidyā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, up to the six sense-bases—this is the suffering of formations (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>). Contact and feeling—this is the suffering of suffering (<s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s>). The remaining links of existence—this is the suffering of change (<s>pariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s>). 'From the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> comes the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s>'—this is the interruption of the three kinds of suffering.

body.text: avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā iti hetupratyayaprabhavatvaṃ saṃskārāṇām / evaṃ pariśeṣāṇām / avidyānirodhātsaṃskāranirodha ityabhāvaḥ saṃskārāṇām / evaṃ pariśeṣāṇām //
body.translated_text: '<s>Saṃskāras</s> are conditioned by <s>avidyā</s>'—this is the arising of <s>saṃskāras</s> from the cause-condition (<s>hetupratyaya</s>). Likewise for the remainder. 'From the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> comes the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s>'—this is the non-existence of <s>saṃskāras</s> [without their cause]. Likewise for the remainder.

body.text: avidyāpratyāḥ saṃskārā ityutpādavinibandha eṣaḥ / evaṃ pariśeṣāṇām / avidyānirodhātsaṃskāranirodha iti vyayavinibandha eṣaḥ / evaṃ pariśeṣāṇām //
body.translated_text: '<s>Saṃskāras</s> are conditioned by <s>avidyā</s>'—this is the binding to arising. Likewise for the remainder. 'From the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> comes the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s>'—this is the binding to cessation. Likewise for the remainder.

body.text: avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā iti bhāvānulomaparīkṣā / evaṃ pariśeṣāṇām / avidyānirodhātsaṃskāranirodha iti kṣayavyayāvinivandha eṣaḥ / evaṃ pariśeṣāṇām //
body.translated_text: '<s>Saṃskāras</s> are conditioned by <s>avidyā</s>'—this is the examination in conformity with existence. Likewise for the remainder. 'From the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> comes the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s>'—this is the binding to diminution and cessation. Likewise for the remainder.

body.text: sa evaṃ dvādaśākāraṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ pratyavekṣate 'nulomapratilomaṃ yaduta bhavāṅgānusaṃdhitaśca ekacittasamavasaraṇataśca svakarmāsaṃbhedataśca avinirbhāgataśca trivartmānuvartanataśca pūrvāntapratyutpannāparāntāvekṣaṇataśca triduḥkhatāsamudayataśca hetupratyayaprabhavataśca utpādavyayavinibandhanataśca abhāvākṣayatāpratyavekṣaṇataśca //
body.translated_text: Thus he contemplates dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) in its twelve aspects, in forward and reverse order: namely, in terms of the connection of the links of existence, the convergence in a single moment of consciousness, the non-confusion of one's own <s>karma</s>, the non-differentiation, the following of the triple path, the examination of the prior limit, the present, and the subsequent limit, the arising of the three kinds of suffering, the origination from cause and condition, and the binding to arising and cessation.

body.text: tasyaivaṃ dvādaśākāraṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ pratyavekṣamāṇasya nirātmato niḥsattvato nirjīvato niṣpudgalataḥ kārakavedakarahitato 'svāmikato hetupratyayādhīnataḥ svabhāvaśūnyato viviktato 'svabhāvataśca prakṛtyā pratyavekṣamāṇasya śūnyatāvimokṣamukhamājātaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: As he thus contemplates the twelve aspects of dependent origination—examining them as devoid of self, devoid of a being, devoid of a life-force, devoid of a person, free from doer and experiencer, ownerless, dependent on causes and conditions, empty of inherent nature, isolated, and without self-nature by their very nature—the gateway of liberation through emptiness (<s>śūnyatāvimokṣamukha</s>) arises for him.

body.text: tasyaivaṃ bhavāṅgānāṃ svabhāvanirodhātyantavimokṣapratyupasthānato na kiṃciddharmanimittamutpadyate / ato 'sya ānimittavimokṣamukhamājātaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: It occurs to him thus: Because of the presentation of the ultimate cessation of the intrinsic nature of the links of existence, no sign of any <s>dharma</s> arises. Therefore the gateway of liberation through signlessness (<s>ānimittavimokṣamukha</s>) arises for him.

body.text: tasyaivaṃ śūnyatānimittamavatīrṇasya na kaścidabhilāṣa utpadyate anyatra mahākaruṇāpūrvakātsattvaparipācanāt / evamasya apraṇihitavimokṣamukhamājātaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: For him who has thus entered emptiness and signlessness, no aspiration whatsoever arises, except for the ripening of beings preceded by great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>). Thus the gateway of liberation through wishlessness (<s>apraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>) arises for him.

body.text: ya imāni trīṇi vimokṣamukhāni bhāvayan ātmaparasaṃjñāpagato kārakavedakasaṃjñāpagato bhāvābhāvasaṃjñāpagato bhūyasyā mātrayā mahākaruṇāpuraskṛtaḥ prayujyate 'pariniṣpannānāṃ bodhyaṅgānāṃ pariniṣpattaye, tasyaivaṃ bhavati - saṃyogātsaṃskṛtaṃ pravartate / visaṃyogānna pravartate / sāmagryā saṃskṛtaṃ pravartate / visāmagryā na pravartate / hanta vayamevaṃ bahudoṣaduṣṭaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ viditvā asya saṃyogasya asyāḥ sāmagryā vyavacchedaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ, na cātyantopaśamaṃ sarvasaṃskārāṇāmavirāgayiṣyāmaḥ sattvaparipācanatāyai //
body.translated_text: One who, cultivating these three gates of liberation (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>), free from the perception of self and other, free from the perception of agent and experiencer, free from the perception of existence and non-existence, preceded to a greater degree by great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), strives for the perfection of the as-yet-unperfected factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>). This thought occurs to him: 'Through conjunction, the conditioned arises; through disjunction, it does not arise. Through the coming together of conditions, the conditioned arises; through the absence of conditions, it does not arise. Come, let us, having understood the conditioned as beset with many faults, bring about the cessation of this conjunction, of this assemblage of conditions—yet we shall not bring about the ultimate pacification of all conditioned things, for the sake of maturing beings.'

body.text: evamasya bhavanto jinaputrāḥ saṃskāragataṃ bahudoṣaduṣṭaṃ svabhāvarahitamanutpannāniruddhaṃ prakṛtyā pratyavekṣamāṇasya mahākaruṇābhinirhārataśca sattvakāryānutsargataśca saṅgajñānābhimukho nāma prajñāpāramitāvihāro 'bhimukhībhavatyavabhāsayogena / sa evaṃ jñānasamanvāgataḥ prajñāpāramitāvihārāvabhāsito bodhyaṅgāhārakāṃśca pratyayānupasaṃharati / na ca saṃskṛtasaṃvāsena saṃvasati / svabhāvopaśamaṃ ca saṃskārāṇāṃ pratyavekṣate / na ca tatrāvatiṣṭhate bodhyaṅgāparityaktatvāt //
body.translated_text: Thus, O sons of the Conqueror, for this one who contemplates the conditioned as beset with many faults, devoid of own-nature, unproduced and unceased by nature, and who brings forth great compassion and does not abandon the welfare of beings—the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> abiding called 'Facing Non-Attached Knowledge' (<s>saṅgajñānābhimukha</s>) becomes manifest through the application of illumination. He, thus endowed with knowledge and illuminated by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> abiding, brings together the conditions that nourish the factors of awakening, yet does not dwell in association with the conditioned. He contemplates the natural pacification of conditioned things, yet does not rest there, because of not having abandoned the factors of awakening.

body.text: tasya asyāmabhimukhyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya avatāraśūnyatā ca nāma samādhirājāyate / svabhāvaśūnyatā ... paramārthaśūnyatā ... paramaśūnyatā ... mahāśūnyatā ... saṃprayogaśūnyatā ... abhinirhāraśūnyatā yathāvadavikalpaśūnyatā sāpekṣaśūnyatā vinirbhāgāvinirbhāgaśūnyatā nāma samādhirājāyate / tasyaivaṃpramukhāni daśa śūnyatāsamādhimukhaśatasahasrāṇyāmukhībhavanti / evamānimittasamādhimukhaśataśahasrāṇi apraṇihitasamādhimukhaśatasahasrāṇyāmukhībhavanti / tasya bhūyasyā mātrayā asyāmabhimukhyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasyabhedyāśayatā ca paripūryate / niyatāśayatā ... kalyāṇāśayatā ... gambhīrāśayatā ... apratyudāvartyāśayatā ... apratiprastrabdhāśayatā ... vimalāśayatā ... anantāśayatā ... jñānābhilāṣāśayatā ... upāyaprajñāsaṃprayogāśayatā ca paripūryate //
body.translated_text: For this <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this Facing (<s>Abhimukhī</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) called 'Emptiness of Entry' (<s>avatāraśūnyatā</s>) arises; 'Emptiness of Own-Nature' (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) ... 'Emptiness of Ultimate Reality' (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>) ... 'Supreme Emptiness' (<s>paramaśūnyatā</s>) ... 'Great Emptiness' (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>) ... 'Emptiness of Association' (<s>saṃprayogaśūnyatā</s>) ... 'Emptiness of Accomplishment' (<s>abhinirhāraśūnyatā</s>), 'Emptiness of Non-Conceptualization as It Truly Is' (<s>yathāvadavikalpaśūnyatā</s>), 'Relative Emptiness' (<s>sāpekṣaśūnyatā</s>), and the <s>samādhi</s> called 'Emptiness of Differentiation and Non-Differentiation' (<s>vinirbhāgāvinirbhāgaśūnyatā</s>) arises. Beginning with these, a hundred thousand gates of emptiness <s>samādhi</s> become manifest for him. Likewise, a hundred thousand gates of signless (<s>ānimitta</s>) <s>samādhi</s> and a hundred thousand gates of wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>) <s>samādhi</s> become manifest. For this <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this Facing (<s>Abhimukhī</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, to a greater degree, the indestructible aspiration is perfected, the determinate aspiration ... the wholesome aspiration ... the profound aspiration ... the irreversible aspiration ... the unrelinquished aspiration ... the stainless aspiration ... the boundless aspiration ... the aspiration for knowledge ... and the aspiration for the union of skillful means and wisdom is perfected.

body.text: tasyaite daśa bodhisattvāśayāḥ svanugatā bhavanti tathāgatabodhau / apratyudāvartanīyavīryaśca bhavati sarvaparapravādibhiḥ / samavasṛtaśca bhavati jñānabhūmau / vinivṛttaśca bhavati śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmibhyaḥ / ekāntikaśca bhavati buddhajñānābhimukhatāyām / asaṃhāryaśca bhavati sarvamārakleśasamudācāraiḥ / supratiṣṭhitaśca bhavati bodhisattvajñānālokatāyām / suparibhāvitaśca bhavati śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitadharmasamudācāraiḥ / saṃprayuktaśca bhavatyupāyaprajñāvicāraiḥ / vyavakīrṇaśca bhavati bodhipākṣikadharmābhinirhāraiḥ / tasya asyāmabhimukhyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya prajñāpāramitāvihāro 'tiriktatara ājāto bhavati, tīkṣṇā cānulomikī tṛtīyā kṣāntireṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ yathāvadanulomatayā na vilomatayā //
body.translated_text: These ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> aspirations of his become conformed to the awakening of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And he becomes one of irreversible vigor against all opposing doctrines. And he becomes established on the stage of knowledge. And he becomes turned away from the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> stages. And he becomes exclusively oriented toward <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. And he becomes unshakable by all the activities of <s>Māra</s> and afflictions. And he becomes well-established in the light of <s>Bodhisattva</s> knowledge. And he becomes well-cultivated in the practices of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. And he becomes engaged in the investigations of skillful means and wisdom. And he becomes permeated with the accomplishment of the factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣika dharma</s>). For this <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this Facing (<s>Abhimukhī</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> abiding becomes most predominant, and the third acute, concordant patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) with respect to these <s>dharmas</s> [arises] in conformity and not in opposition to their true nature.

body.text: tasya asyāmabhimukhyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya yathāvatsamāpattiprajñājñānālokatayā prayujyate, pratipattitaścādhārayati / sa bhūyasyā mātrayā tathāgatadharmakośaprāpto bhavati / tasya asyāmabhimukhyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya anekān kalpāṃstāni kuśalamūlāni bhūyasyā mātrayā uttaptaprabhāsvaratarāṇi bhavanti / anekāni kalpaśatāni ... . / tāni kuśalamūlāni bhūyasyā mātrayottaptaprabhāsvaratarāṇi bhavanti / tadyathāpi nāma bhavanto jinaputrāstadeva jātarūpaṃ vaiḍūryaparisṛṣṭaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayottaptaprabhāsvarataraṃ bhavati, evameva bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasya asyāmabhimukhyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya tāni kuśalamūlānyupāyaprajñājñānavicāritāni bhūyasyā mātrayottaptaprabhāsvaratarāṇi bhavanti, bhūyo bhūyaśca praśamāsaṃhāryatāṃ gacchanti / tadyathāpi nāma bhavanto jinaputrāścandrābhā sattvāśrayāṃśca prahlādayati asaṃhāryā ca bhavati catasṛbhirvātamaṇḍalībhiḥ, evameva bhavanto jinaputra bodhisattvasya asyāmabhimukhyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya tāni kuśalamūlānyanekeṣāṃ sattvakoṭinayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ kleśajvālāḥ praśamayanti, prahlādayanti, asaṃhāryāṇi ca bhavanti caturbhirmārāvacaraiḥ / tasya daśabhyaḥ pāramitābhyaḥ prajñāpāramitā atiriktatamā bhavati, na ca pariśeṣā na samudāgacchati yathābalaṃ yathābhajamānam / iyaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasya abhimukhī nāma ṣaṣṭhī bodhisattvabhūmiḥ samāsanirdeśataḥ, yasyāṃ pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo bhūyastvena sunirmito bhavati devarājaṃ kṛtī prabhuḥ sattvānāmabhimānapratiprasrabdhaye kuśalaḥ sattvānyābhimānikadharmebhyo vinivartayitum / asaṃhāryaśca bhavati sarvaśrāvakaparipṛcchāyāṃ kuśalaḥ sattvān pratītyasamutpāde 'vatārayitum / yacca kiṃcit ... . //
body.translated_text: For this <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this Facing (<s>Abhimukhī</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, he strives through the light of wisdom-knowledge of proper attainment, and maintains it in practice. He to a greater degree becomes one who has obtained the treasury of <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. For this <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this Facing (<s>Abhimukhī</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, for many <s>kalpas</s>, for many hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> ... those wholesome roots become to a greater degree refined and more luminous. Just as, O sons of the Conqueror, that very gold, when placed in contact with <s>vaidūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), becomes to a greater degree refined and more luminous—even so, O sons of the Conqueror, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this Facing (<s>Abhimukhī</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, those wholesome roots, examined by the knowledge of skillful means and wisdom, become to a greater degree refined and more luminous, and go ever more toward pacification and unshakability. Just as, O sons of the Conqueror, the light of the moon both refreshes beings and is unshakable by the four circles of wind—even so, O sons of the Conqueror, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this Facing (<s>Abhimukhī</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, those wholesome roots pacify and refresh the flames of affliction of many <s>koṭī-niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of beings, and become unshakable by the four domains of <s>Māra</s>. Of the ten perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>), the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) becomes most predominant for him, and it is not that the rest are not attained, but according to his strength and capacity. This, O sons of the Conqueror, is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s sixth <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage called Facing (<s>Abhimukhī</s>), described in summary. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this stage becomes for the most part a <s>Sunirmita</s> (Well-Created) king of the gods, capable, powerful, skilled in turning beings away from the conceit regarding <s>dharmas</s>, skilled in causing beings to turn away from conceited <s>dharmas</s>. And he becomes unshakable in all inquiries of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, skilled in causing beings to enter dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). And whatever action [he undertakes] ... [abbreviated].

body.text: abhimukhī nāma ṣaṣṭī bhūmiḥ //
body.translated_text: The sixth stage, called Facing (<s>Abhimukhī</s>).

body.text: 7 duraṃgamā nāma saptamī bhūmiḥ /
body.translated_text: 7. The seventh stage, called Far-Going (<s>Dūraṃgamā</s>).

body.text: vajragarbha āha - yo 'yaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvaḥ ṣaṣṭyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau suparipūrṇabodhisattvamārgaḥ saptamīṃ bodhisattvabhūmimākramati, sa daśabhirupāyaprajñājñānābhinirhṛtairmārgāntarārambhaviśeṣairākramati / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitasamādhisuparibhāvitamānasaśca bhavati, mahāpuṇyajñānasambhāropacayaṃ ca saṃbibharti / nairātmyaniḥsattvanirjīvaniṣpudgalatāṃ ca sarvadharmāṇāmavatarati, caturapramāṇābhinirhāraṃ ca notsṛjati / puṇyadharmocchrayapāramitābhisaṃskāraṃ cābhisaṃskaroti, na ca kiṃciddharmamabhiniviśate / sarvatraidhātukavivekaprāptaśca bhavati, traidhātukaviṭhapanālaṃkārābhinirhāraṃ cābhinirharati / atyantaśāntopaśāntaśca sarvakleśajvālāpagamādbhavati, sarvasattvarāgadveṣakleśajvālāpraśamābhinirhāraṃ cābhinirharati / māyāmarīcisvapnapratibhāsapratiśrutkodakacandrapratibimbanirmāṇabhāvābhāvasvabhāvādvayānugataśca bhavati, karmakriyāvibhaktyapramāṇāśayatāṃ cābhinirharati / ākāśasamakṣetrapathasubhāvitamanāśca bhavati, buddhakṣetraviṭhapanālaṃkārābhinirhāraṃ cābhinirharati / prakṛtidharmakāyatāṃ ca sarvabuddhanāmavatarati, rūpakāyalakṣaṇānuvyañjanaviṭhapanālaṃkārābhinirhāraṃ cābhinirharati / anabhilāpyarutaghoṣāpagataṃ ca prakṛtiśāntaṃ tathāgataghoṣamadhimucyate, sarvasvarāṅgavibhaktiviśuddhyalaṃkārābhinirhāraṃ cābhinirharati / ekakṣaṇatryadhvānubodhaṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmavatarati, nānālakṣaṇākalpasaṃkhyāvibhāvanāṃ cānupraviśati sattvāśayavibhāvanāya / evirbhavanto jinaputrā daśabhirupāyaprajñājñānābhinirhṛtibhirmārgāntarārambhaviśeṣairbodhisattvaḥ ṣaṣṭhyā bodhisattvabhūmeḥ saptamīṃ bodhisattvabhūmimākrānta ityucyate //
body.translated_text: <s>Vajragarbha</s> said: 'That <s>Bodhisattva</s>, O sons of the Conqueror, whose <s>Bodhisattva</s> path is well-perfected on the sixth <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, and who enters the seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage—he enters with ten special path-initiations accomplished through the knowledge of skillful means and wisdom. Which ten? Namely, he is one whose mind is well-cultivated in the <s>samādhi</s> of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, and he accumulates a great store of merit and knowledge. He enters into the selflessness, beinglessness, lifelessness, and personlessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, yet does not abandon the accomplishment of the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>). He perfects the conditioning of the perfections through the exaltation of meritorious <s>dharmas</s>, yet does not cling to any <s>dharma</s>. He attains complete separation from the three realms, yet accomplishes the adornment of the three-realm display. He becomes utterly peaceful and pacified through the departure of all flames of affliction, yet accomplishes the pacification of the flames of affliction of passion, hatred, and affliction of all beings. He follows the non-dual nature of illusion, mirage, dream, reflection, echo, moon-in-water, magical emanation, existence, non-existence, and own-nature, yet accomplishes immeasurable aspiration for the differentiation of action and its results. His mind is well-cultivated as equal to space in its path, yet he accomplishes the adornment of the <s>Buddha</s>-field display. He enters into the natural <s>Dharmakāya</s> of all <s>Buddhas</s>, yet accomplishes the adornment of the display of the marks and minor marks of the <s>Rūpakāya</s> (form body). He is devoted to the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s voice, which is naturally peaceful and free from inexpressible sound and cry, yet accomplishes the adornment of the purity of all varieties of voice and limbs of speech. He enters into the awakening of the <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones to the three times in a single instant, yet enters into the display of various marks, <s>kalpas</s>, and numbers for the sake of displaying beings' dispositions. With these ten special path-initiations accomplished through the knowledge of skillful means and wisdom, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is said to have entered the seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage from the sixth <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage.'

body.text: sa saptamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito bodhisattvo 'pramāṇāsattvadhātumavatarati / apramāṇaṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sattvaparipācanavinayakarmāvatarati / apramāṇaṃ lokadhātumavatarati / apramāṇaṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ kṣetrapariśuddhimavatarati / apramāṇaṃ ca dharmanānātvamavatarati / apramāṇaṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ jñānābhisaṃbodhimavatarati / apramāṇaṃ ca kalpasaṃkhyāpraveśamavatarati / apramāṇaṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ tryadhvānubodhamavatarati / apramāṇaṃ ca sattvānāmadhimuktinānātvaviśeṣamavatarati / apramāṇaṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ rūpakāyanānātvadarśanamavatarati / apramāṇaṃ ca sattvānāmāśayendriyanānātvamavatarati / apramāṇaṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ ghoṣodāhārasattvasaṃtoṣaṇamavatarati / apramāṇaṃ sattvānāṃ cittacaritanānātvamavatarati / apramāṇaṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ jñānaprasarānugamamavatarati / apramāṇaṃ śrāvakayānaniryāṇā-adhimuktinānātvamavatarati / apramāṇaṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mārgadeśanāvatāramavatarati / apramāṇaṃ pratyekabuddhayānasamudāgamaniṣpattimavatarati / apramāṇaṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ jñānamukhapraveśanirdeśamavatarati / bodhisattvānāṃ bodhisattvacaryāprayogamavatarati / apramāṇaṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahāyānasamudayāvatāranirdeśanāmavatarati //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage enters the immeasurable realm of beings. He enters the immeasurable work of maturing and disciplining beings by the <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones. He enters immeasurable world-realms. He enters the immeasurable purification of the fields of the <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones. He enters the immeasurable diversity of <s>Dharma</s>. He enters the immeasurable awakening to knowledge of the <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones. He enters the immeasurable entry into the enumeration of <s>kalpas</s>. He enters the immeasurable awakening of the <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones to the three times. He enters the immeasurable diversity and distinction of beings' aspirations. He enters the immeasurable display of the diversity of the form-bodies of the <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones. He enters the immeasurable diversity of beings' dispositions and faculties. He enters the immeasurable satisfaction of beings through the utterance of the voice of the <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones. He enters the immeasurable diversity of beings' mind-conduct. He enters the immeasurable following of the extent of the knowledge of the <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones. He enters the immeasurable diversity of aspirations for the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle. He enters the immeasurable entry into the path-teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones. He enters the immeasurable attainment and accomplishment of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle. He enters the immeasurable instruction on the entry into the gate of knowledge of the <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones. He enters the practice and application of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct. He enters the immeasurable instruction of the <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones on the entry into the arising of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

body.text: tasyaivaṃ bhavati - evamapramāṇaḥ khalu punastathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ viṣayo yasya na sukarā saṃkhyā kartuṃ kalpakoṭiśatasahasrairyāvadetāvadbhirapi kalpakoṭiniyutaśatasahasraiḥ / sarva ... viṣayo 'smābhiḥ samupasthāpayitavyo 'nābhogato 'kalpāvikalpataśca paripūrayitavya iti / sa evaṃ supratyavekṣitajñānābhijñaḥ satatasamitamabhiyuktopāyaprajñāparibhāviteṣu mārgāntarārambhaviśeṣeṣu supratiṣṭhito bhavatyavicālyayogena //
body.translated_text: This thought occurs to him: 'So immeasurable indeed is the domain of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, that it is not easy to enumerate even in hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, nor even in that many <s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. This entire ... domain is to be served by us, and is to be fulfilled effortlessly and without conceptualization.'  He, thus endowed with well-examined knowledge and superknowledges, constantly devoted, becomes well-established in the special path-initiations cultivated by skillful means and wisdom, through the practice of unshakability.

body.text: sa ekakṣaṇamapi mārgābhinirhārānna vyuttiṣṭhate / sa gacchanneva jñānābhinirhārayukto bhavati / tiṣṭhannapi niṣaṇṇo 'pi śayāno 'pi svapnāntaragato 'pyapagatanīvaraṇaḥ sarveryāpathe sthito 'virahito bhavati ebhirevaṃrūpaiḥ saṃjñāmanasikāraiḥ / tasya sarvacittotpāde daśānāṃ bodhisattvapāramitānāṃ samudāgamaparipūriḥ samudāgacchati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi sa bodhisattvaḥ sarvāṃścittotpādānutpannotpannān mahākaruṇāpūrvakān buddhadharmasamudāgamāya tathāgatajñānāya pariṇāmayati / tatra yaḥ kuśalamūlasya sattvebhya utsargo buddhajñānaṃ paryeṣamāṇasya, iyamasya dānapāramitā / yaḥ praśamaḥ sarvakleśaparidāhānām, iyamasya śīlapāramitā / yā kṛpāmaitrīpūrvagamā sarvasattveṣu kṣāntiḥ, iyamasya kṣāntipāramitā / ya uttarottarakuśaladharmātṛptatayārambhaḥ parākramaḥ, iyamasya vīryapāramitā / yā vipratisāryavisṛtamārgatā sarvajñajñānābhimukhatā, iyamasya dhyānapāramitā / yā sarvadharmāṇāṃ prakṛtyanutpādābhimukhī kṣāntiḥ, iyamasya prajñāpāramitā / yo 'pramāṇājñānābhinirhāraḥ, iyamasyopāyakauśalapāramitā / yā sarvaparapravādimārasaṃghairmārgānācchedyatā, iyamasya balapāramitā / yadyathāvatsarvadharmajñānanitīraṇam, iyamasya jñānapāramitā / evamasya bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasya dūraṃgamāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya imā daśa pāramitāḥ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe paripūryante / evaṃ catvāri saṃgrahavastūni paripūryante, catvāri ca adhiṣṭhānāni, saptatriṃśad bodhipakṣyāśca dharmāḥ, trīṇi ca vimokṣamukhāni, samāsataḥ sarvabodhyaṅgikā dharmāḥ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe paripūryante //
body.translated_text: He does not depart from the accomplishment of the path even for a single instant. Whether going, standing, sitting, lying down, or even entered into a dream, free from hindrances, established in all postures, he is never separated from such perceptions and mental attentions. In every production of his thought, the attainment and fulfillment of the ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>) is accomplished. Why is that? For that <s>Bodhisattva</s> dedicates all his produced and unproduced thoughts, preceded by great compassion, to the attainment of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> and the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therein, the giving up of wholesome roots to beings while seeking <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge—this is his perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>). The pacification of all the burning of afflictions—this is his perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>). The patience preceded by compassion and loving-kindness toward all beings—this is his perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>). The effort and exertion through insatiability for ever-higher wholesome <s>dharmas</s>—this is his perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>). The orientation toward omniscient knowledge through the path free from regret and distraction—this is his perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>). The patience oriented toward the natural non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s>—this is his perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>). The accomplishment of immeasurable knowledge—this is his perfection of skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalapāramitā</s>). The indestructibility of the path by all opposing doctrines and hosts of <s>Māra</s>—this is his perfection of power (<s>balapāramitā</s>). The ascertainment of the knowledge of all <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are—this is his perfection of knowledge (<s>jñānapāramitā</s>). Thus, O sons of the Conqueror, for this <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the Far-Going (<s>Dūraṃgamā</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, these ten perfections are fulfilled at every moment. Likewise, the four means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>) are fulfilled, the four foundations (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>), the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya dharma</s>), the three gates of liberation (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>)—in short, all factors of awakening are fulfilled at every moment.

body.text: evamukte vimukticandro bodhisattvo vajragarbhaṃ bodhisattvametadavocat - kiṃ punarbho jinaputrā asyāmeva saptamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya sarvabodhyaṅgikā dharmāḥ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe paripūryante, āhosvitsarvāsu daśasu bodhisattvabhūmiṣu? vajragarbha āha - sarvāsu bho jinaputrā daśasu bodhisattvabhūmiṣu bodhisattvasya sarvabodhyaṅgāni kṣaṇe kṣaṇe paripūryante, tadatirekeṇa punarasyāmeva saptamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau / tatkasya hetoḥ? iyaṃ bho jinaputrā bodhisattvabhūmiḥ prāyogikacaryāparipūraṇī ca jñānābhijñānacaryākramaṇī ca / api tu khalu punarbho jinaputrāḥ prathamāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sarvapraṇidhānādhyālambena bodhisattvasya sarvabodhyaṅgāni kṣaṇe kṣaṇe paripūryante / dvitīyāyāṃ cittamalāpanayanena / tṛtīyāyāṃ praṇidhānavivardhanatayā dharmāvabhāsapratilambhena ca / caturthyāṃ mārgāvatāreṇa / pañcamyāṃ lokatrayānuvṛtyā / ṣaṣṭyāṃ gambhīradharmamukhapraveśena / asyāṃ tu saptamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sarvabuddhadharmasamutthāpanatayā kṣaṇe kṣaṇe sarvabodhyāṅgāni paripūryante /
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vimukticandra</s> said this to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s>: 'Do all the qualities constituting the factors of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) become fulfilled moment by moment for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> standing on just this seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, or on all ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages?' <s>Vajragarbha</s> said: 'On all ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, the factors of <s>bodhi</s> of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> become fulfilled moment by moment, but to a surpassing degree on just this seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage. For what reason? Because this <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, is the one that fulfills the applied practice and enters upon the course of knowledge and superknowledge. Moreover, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, on the first <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, the factors of <s>bodhi</s> of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> become fulfilled moment by moment through reliance upon all vows. On the second, through the removal of mental impurities. On the third, through the increase of vows and the attainment of the radiance of the <s>Dharma</s>. On the fourth, through entering the path. On the fifth, through conforming to the three worlds. On the sixth, through entering the gateway of the profound <s>dharmas</s>. But on this seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, the factors of <s>bodhi</s> become fulfilled moment by moment through the arousing of all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities.

body.text:
tatkasya hetoḥ? yāni bodhisattvena prathamāṃ bodhisattvabhūmimupādāya yāvatsaptamī bodhisattvabhūmirityabhinirhṛtāni jñānābhinirhāraprayogāṅgāni, imānyaṣṭamī bodhisattvabhūmimārabhya yāvadatyantaparyavasānamityanābhogena pariniṣpadyante / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputrā dvayorlokadhātvoḥ saṃkliṣṭaviśuddhāśayaśca lokadhātorekāntapariśuddhāśayaśca lokadhātorlokāntarikā duratikramā na śakyā yathātathātikramitumanyatra mahābhijñābalādhānāt, evameva bho jinaputra vyāmiśrapariśuddhā bodhisattvacaryāntarikā duratikramā na śakyā yathātathātikramitumanyatra mahāpraṇidhānopāyaprajñābhijñābalādhānāt / vimukticandra āha - kiṃ punarbho jinaputra saptasu bodhisattvabhūmiṣu kleśacaryāsaṃkliṣṭā bodhisattvacaryā pratyetavyā? vajragarbha āha - prathamāmeva bho jinaputra bodhisattvabhūmimupādāya sarvābodhisattvacaryāpagatakleśakalmāṣā bodhipariṇāmanādhipatyena pratyetavyā / yathābhāgimārgasamatayā, (na ca) tāvatsaptasu bodhisattvabhūmiṣu samatikrāntā kleśacaryetyavācanīyā / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra rājā cakravartī divyaṃ hastiratnamabhirūḍhaścaturo dvīpānākramati, manuṣyaduḥkhadāridryasaṃkleśadoṣāṃśca prajānāti, na ca tairdoṣairlipyate
/ na ca tāvatsamatikrānto manuṣyabhāvaṃ bhavati / yadā punarmanuṣyāśrayaṃ hitvā brahmalokopapanno bhavati brāhmyavimānamabhirūḍhaḥ, sahasralokadhātumalpakṛcchreṇa paśyatyanuvicarati, brahmapratibhāsaṃ cādarśayati, na ca manuṣya iti prabhāvyate, evameva bhoḥ prathamāṃ bhūmimupādāya bodhisattvaḥ pāramitāyānābhirūḍhaḥ sarvajagadanuvicaran saṃkleśadoṣān prajānāti, na ca tairdoṣairlipyate samyagmārgābhirūḍhatvāt / na ca tāvatsamatikrāntaḥ sarvajagatsaṃkleśadoṣān vaktavyaḥ / saptasu bhūmiṣu sarvaprāyogikacaryāṃ vihāya saptamyā bhūmeraṣṭamīṃ bodhisattvabhūmimavakrānto bhavati, tadā pariśuddhaṃ bodhisattvayānamabhirūḍhaḥ sarvajagadanuvicaran sarvajagatsaṃkleśadoṣān prajānāti, na ca tairdoṣairlipyate samatikrāntatvād lokatriyābhyaḥ / asyāṃ punarbho jinaputra sapyamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito bodhisattvo bhūyastvena rāgādipramukhaṃ sarvakleśagaṇaṃ samatikrānto bhavati / so 'syāṃ dūraṃgamāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau caran bodhisattvo 'saṃkleśāniṣkleśa iti vaktavyaḥ / tatkasmāt? asamudācārātsarvakleśānāṃ na saṃkleśa iti vaktavyaḥ / tathāgatajñānābhilāṣādaparipūrṇābhiprāyatvācca na niṣkleśa iti vaktavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: For what reason? Those constituents of the application of knowledge-generation that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has produced from the first <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage up to the seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage—these are accomplished effortlessly (<s>anābhogena</s>) from the eighth <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage onward to the ultimate end. Just as, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, between two world-realms—one with defiled aspirations and the other entirely pure in aspiration—the intermediate space is exceedingly difficult to cross and cannot be crossed as it truly is except through the attainment of the power of great superknowledge, even so, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the intermediate space of mixed and pure <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct is exceedingly difficult to cross and cannot be crossed as it truly is except through the attainment of the power of great vows, skillful means, wisdom, and superknowledge. <s>Vimukticandra</s> said: 'Should the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct on the seven <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages be regarded as defiled by the activity of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)?' <s>Vajragarbha</s> said: 'From the very first <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage onward, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, all <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct should be regarded as free from the stain of <s>kleśas</s>, through the sovereignty of dedication to <s>bodhi</s>.
