Through equality with the path of respective aspects, it is not to be said that the <s>kleśa</s>-activity has been transcended on the seven <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages. Just as, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, a <s>Cakravartin</s> king, having mounted the divine elephant-jewel, traverses the four continents and knows the sufferings, poverty, defilements, and faults of humans, yet is not stained by those faults—he has not yet transcended the state of being human. But when, having abandoned the human condition, he is reborn in the <s>Brahma</s>-world and, having mounted the <s>Brahma</s>-palace, sees and traverses a thousand world-systems with little effort, and shows the appearance of <s>Brahmā</s>, he is no longer called human—even so, from the first stage onward, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having mounted the vehicle of the <s>pāramitās</s>, traversing all the world, knows the faults of defilement, yet is not stained by those faults because he has mounted the correct path. But he is not yet to be said to have transcended the defilement-faults of all the world. Leaving behind all applied practice on the seven stages and having crossed from the seventh stage to the eighth <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, then, having mounted the purified <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle, traversing all the world, he knows the defilement-faults of all the world, yet is not stained by those faults because he has transcended the three worlds. But on this seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> standing here has for the most part transcended the entire host of <s>kleśas</s> headed by passion. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who walks on this <s>Dūraṅgamā</s> (Far-reaching) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage is to be called neither defiled nor undefiled. Why? Because all <s>kleśas</s> do not manifest, he is not to be called defiled. Because his aspiration for <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge is not yet fulfilled, he is not to be called undefiled.

body.text: so 'syāṃ saptamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito bodhisattvo 'dhyāśayapariśuddhena kāyakarmaṇā samanvāgato bhavati / adhyāśayapariśuddhena vākkarmaṇā adhyāśayapariśuddhena manaskarmaṇā samanvāgato bhavati / ye ceme daśākuśalāḥ karmapathāstathāgatavivarṇitāḥ, tān sarveṇa sarvaṃ samatikrānto bhavati / ye ceme daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ samyaksaṃbuddhānubhāvitāḥ, tān satatasamitamanuvartate / yāni laukikāni śilpasthānakarmasthānāni yānyabhinirhṛtāni pañcamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau, tānyasya sarvāṇyanābhogata evaṃ pravartante / sa ācāryaḥ saṃmato bhavati trisāhasra mahāsāhasralokadhātau, sthāpayitvā tathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksambuddhān, aṣṭamīṃ bhūmimupādāya ca bodhisattvān / nāsya kaścitsamo bhavatyāśayena vā prayogeṇa vā / yāni cemāni dhyānāni
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> standing on this seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage is endowed with bodily action purified through noble aspiration, with verbal action purified through noble aspiration, and with mental action purified through noble aspiration. He has completely transcended the ten unwholesome courses of action disparaged by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. He constantly follows the ten wholesome courses of action praised by the Perfectly Enlightened Ones. The worldly arts and crafts and occupational sciences that were produced on the fifth <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage—all of these operate for him effortlessly. He is regarded as a teacher in the three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system, except for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> from the eighth stage onward. No one is equal to him in aspiration or application. And as for these <s>dhyānas</s>,

body.text: samādhayaḥ samapattayo 'bhijñā vimokṣāśca, tānyasya sarveṇa sarvamāmukhībhavanti bhāvanābhinirhārākāreṇa / na ca tāvadvipākataḥ pariniṣpannāni bhavanti tadyathāpi nāma aṣṭamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya / asyāṃ saptamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya sarvacittotpādeṣu prajñopāyabhāvanābalaṃ paripūryate / bhūyasyā mātrayā sarvabodhyaṅgaparipūriṃ pratilabhate //
body.translated_text: <s>samādhis</s>, attainments, superknowledges, and liberations—all of these become present to him in the mode of cultivation and generation. Yet they are not yet accomplished through the ripening of fruition as they are for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> standing on the eighth <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage. For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> standing on this seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, in every arising of mind, the power of the cultivation of wisdom and skillful means becomes fulfilled. To an even greater degree, he attains the fulfillment of all the factors of <s>bodhi</s>.

body.text: so 'syāṃ saptamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitaḥ san suvicitavicayaṃ ca nāma bodhisattvasamādhi samāpadyate / suvicintitārthaṃ ca nāma ... / viśeṣamatiṃ ca nāma ... / prabhedārthakośaṃ ca ... / sarvārthavicayaṃ ca ... / supratiṣṭhitadṛḍhamūlaṃ ca ... / jñānābhijñāmukhaṃ ca ... / dharmadhātu(pari)karmaṃ ca ... / tathāgatānuśaṃsaṃ ca ... / vicitrārthakośasaṃsāranirvāṇamukhaṃ ca bodhisattvasamādhiṃ samāpadyate / sa evaṃpramukhāni mahābhijñājñānamukhāni paripūrṇāni daśa samādhiśatasahasrāṇi bhūmipariśodhikāni samāpadyate //
body.translated_text: Standing on this seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, he enters the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called 'Well-Investigated Examination,' and [the <s>samādhi</s>] called 'Well-Considered Meaning,' and that called 'Distinguished Intelligence,' and 'Treasury of Analyzed Meaning,' and 'Examination of All Meanings,' and 'Well-Established and Firm-Rooted,' and 'Gateway of Knowledge and Superknowledge,' and 'Preparation of the <s>Dharma</s>-realm,' and 'Commendation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>,' and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called 'Gateway of <s>Saṃsāra</s> and <s>Nirvāṇa</s> with Treasury of Various Meanings.' He enters such principal gateways of great superknowledge and knowledge—a full ten hundred thousand <s>samādhis</s> that purify the stage.

body.text: sa eṣāṃ samādhīnāmupāyaprajñāsupariśodhitānāṃ pratilambhānmahākaruṇābalena cātikrānto bhavati śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmim, abhimukhaśca bhavati prajñājñānavicāraṇābhūmeḥ //
body.translated_text: Through the attainment of these <s>samādhis</s>, well-purified through skillful means and wisdom, and through the power of great compassion, he transcends the stages of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and stands face to face with the stage of the investigation of wisdom-knowledge.

body.text: tasya asyāṃ saptamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya apramāṇaṃ kāyakarma nimittāpagataṃ pravartate / apramāṇaṃ vākkarma ... manaskarma nimittāpagataṃ pravartate suviśodhitamanutpattikadharmakṣāntyavabhāsitam / vimukticandra āha - nanu bho jinaputra, prathamāyāmeva bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya apramāṇaṃ kāyavāṅmanaskarma sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhacaryāṃ samatikrāntaṃ bhavati? vajragarbha āha - bhavati bho jinaputra / tatpunarbuddhadharmādhyālambanamāhātmyena, na punaḥ svabuddhivicāreṇa / asyāṃ tu punaḥ saptamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau svabuddhigocaravicārapratilambhādasaṃhāryaṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhairbhavati / tadyathāpi nāma bhavanto jinaputrā rājakulaprasūto rājaputro rājalakṣaṇasamanvāgato jātamātra eva sarvāmātyagaṇamabhibhavati rājādhipatyena, na punaḥ svabuddhivicāreṇa / yadā punaḥ sa saṃvṛddho bhavati tadā svabuddhibalādhānataḥ sarvāmātyakriyāsamatikrānto bhavati, evameva bho jinaputrā bodhisattvaḥ sahacittotpādena sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānabhibhavatyadhyāśayamāhātmyena, na punaḥ svabuddhivicāreṇa / asyāṃ tu saptamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito bodhisattvaḥ svaviṣayajñānaviśeṣamāhātmyāvasthitatvātsarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhakriyāmatikrānto bhavati //
body.translated_text: For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> standing on this seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, immeasurable bodily action operates, free from characteristics; immeasurable verbal action and mental action operate, free from characteristics, well-purified and illuminated by the patient acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>). <s>Vimukticandra</s> said: 'Is it not the case, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, that even for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> standing on the first <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, immeasurable bodily, verbal, and mental action has transcended all <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> conduct?' <s>Vajragarbha</s> said: 'Indeed it is so, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>. But that is through the greatness of reliance upon <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, not through the investigation of one's own intelligence. But on this seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, through the attainment of the investigation in the domain of one's own intelligence, it becomes indestructible by <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. Just as, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, a prince born in the royal family, endowed with the marks of a king, from birth itself overpowers the entire assembly of ministers through the sovereignty of kingship, not through the investigation of his own intelligence. But when he has grown up, through the attainment of the power of his own intelligence, he transcends all ministerial activities. Even so, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, from the moment of generating the aspiration-mind, overpowers all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> through the greatness of his noble aspiration, not through the investigation of his own intelligence. But the <s>Bodhisattva</s> standing on this seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, through being established in the greatness of the distinction of knowledge in his own domain, transcends all <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> activities.'

body.text: sa khalu punarbho bodhisattvo 'syāṃ saptamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito gambhīrasya vivittasyāpracārasya kāyavāṅmanaskarmaṇo lābhī bhavati / na cottaraṃ viśeṣaparimārgaṇābhiyogamavasṛjati / [yena parimārgaṇābhiyogena nirodhaprāptaśca bhavati, na ca nirodhaṃ sākṣātkaroti //]
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> standing on this seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage indeed attains deep, secluded, non-operating bodily, verbal, and mental action. Yet he does not abandon the effort of seeking higher distinction. [Through that effort of seeking, he attains cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), yet does not directly realize cessation.]

body.text: vimukticandra āha - katamāṃ bhūmimupādāya bodhisattvo nirodhaṃ samāpadyate? vajragarbha āha - ṣaṣṭhīṃ bho jinaputra bodhisattvabhūmimupādāya bodhisattvo nirodhaṃ samāpadyate / asyāṃ
body.translated_text: <s>Vimukticandra</s> said: 'From which stage onward does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> enter cessation (<s>nirodha</s>)?' <s>Vajragarbha</s> said: 'From the sixth <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage onward, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> enters cessation. On this

body.text: punaḥ saptamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvaścittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe nirodhaṃ samāpadyate ca vyuttiṣṭhate ca / na ca nirodhaḥ sākṣātkṛta iti vaktavyaḥ / tena so 'cintyena kāyavāṅmana skarmaṇā samanvāgata ityucyate / āścaryaṃ bho yatra hi nāma bodhisattvo bhūtakoṭivihāreṇa ca viharati, na ca nirodhaṃ sākṣātkaroti / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra puruṣaḥ kuśalo mahāsāgare vārilakṣaṇābhijñaḥ paṇḍito vyakto medhāvī tatropagatayā mīmāṃsayā samanvāgato mahāsāgare mahāyānapātrābhirūḍho vahanakuśalaśca bhavati, vārikuśalaśca bhavati, na ca mahāsamudre vāridoṣairlipyate, evameva bho jinaputra asyāṃ saptamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvaḥ sarvajñajñānamahāsāgarāvatīrṇaḥ pāramitāmahāyānapātrābhirūḍho bhūtakoṭivihāreṇa ca viharati, na ca nirodhaṃ sākṣātkaroti, (na ca sasṃkṛtātyantavyupaśamavitarkadoṣairlipyate) //
body.translated_text: seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, the established <s>Bodhisattva</s> enters and arises from cessation moment by moment. Yet cessation is not to be said to be directly realized. Therefore he is said to be endowed with inconceivable bodily, verbal, and mental action. It is wonderful, indeed, that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> dwells in the abiding of the ultimate reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>), yet does not directly realize cessation. Just as, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, a man skilled in the ocean, knowledgeable in the characteristics of water, wise, intelligent, and discerning, endowed with the examination appropriate thereto, having mounted a great <s>Mahāyāna</s> vessel in the great ocean, is skilled in navigation and skilled in [reading] the waters, and is not affected by the faults of the waters in the great ocean—even so, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, having descended into the great ocean of omniscient knowledge, having mounted the great <s>Mahāyāna</s> vessel of the <s>pāramitās</s>, dwells in the abiding of the ultimate reality, yet does not directly realize cessation (and is not affected by the faults of the discursive thought of the utter pacification of the conditioned).

body.text: sa evaṃ jñānabalādhānaprāptaḥ samādhijñānabalabhāvanābhinirhṛtayā buddhyā mahatopāyaprajñābalādhānena saṃsāramukhaṃ cādarśayati / nirvāṇasatatāśayaśca bhavati / mahāparivāraparivṛtaśca bhavati / satatasamitaṃ ca cittavivekapratilabdho bhavati / traidhātukopapattiṃ ca praṇidhānavaśenābhinirharati sattvaparipācanārtham / na ca lokadoṣairlipyate / śāntapraśāntopaśāntaśca bhavati / upāyena ca jvalati / jvalaṃśca na dahate / saṃvartate ca buddhajñānena / vivartate ca śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmibhyām / buddhajñānaviṣayakośaprāptaśca bhavati / māraviṣayagataśca dṛśyate / caturmārapathasamatikrāntaśca bhavati / māraviṣayagocaraṃ cādarśayati / sarvatīrthyāyatanopagataśca dṛśyate / buddhatīrthyāyatanānutsṛṣṭāśayaśca bhavati / sarvalokakriyānugataśca dṛśyate / lokottaradharmagatisamavasaraṇaśca bhavati / sarvadevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyaśakrabrahmalokapālātirekavyūhālaṃkāraviṭhapanāprāptaśca bhavati / sarvabuddhadharmatimanasikāraṃ ca na vijahāti //
body.translated_text: Having thus attained the foundation of the power of knowledge, through the intelligence produced by the cultivation of the power of <s>samādhi</s>-knowledge, through the great foundation of the power of skillful means and wisdom, he displays the gateway of <s>saṃsāra</s> and yet has a constant aspiration for <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. He is surrounded by a great retinue, yet has constantly and continuously attained mental seclusion. He brings about rebirth in the triple world through the power of his vow for the purpose of maturing beings, yet is not stained by worldly faults. He is peaceful, fully peaceful, and perfectly peaceful. Through skillful means he blazes, yet blazing, he does not burn. He evolves through <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge and revolves from the stages of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. He has attained the treasury of the domain of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, yet is seen as entering the domain of <s>Māra</s>. He has transcended the path of the four <s>Māras</s>, yet displays the sphere of action of <s>Māra</s>'s domain. He is seen as having arrived at the abode of all heretical schools, yet his aspiration never abandons the establishment of the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching. He is seen as following all worldly activities, yet he arrives at the abode of the supramundane <s>Dharma</s>-course. He has attained the array, adornment, and display surpassing all <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, non-humans, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the world-guardians, yet he does not abandon mental attention to all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities.

body.text: tasyaivaṃ jñānasamanvāgatasya asyāṃ saptasyāṃ dūraṃgamāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya bahavo buddhā ābhāsamāgacchanti ... / tāṃśca tathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān paryupāsate / teṣāṃ ca sakāśādgauravacitrīkāreṇa satkṛtya dharmadeśanāṃ śṛṇoti, udgṛhṇāti dhārayati / śrutvā ca yathāvatsamāpattiprajñājñānālokena prayujyate / pratipattitaścādhārayati / śāsanasaṃdhārakaśca bhavati teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ mahātmanām / asaṃhāryaśca sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhābhisamayaparipṛcchāsu / tasya bhūyasyā mātrayā sattvānugrahāya gambhīradharmakṣāntirviśuddhyati / tasya ... anekān kalpāṃstāni kuśalamūlānyuttapyante, pariśuddhyanti, karmaṇyāni ca bhavanti, paryavadānaṃ cāgacchanti / anekāni kalpaśatāni ... anekāni kalpakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi tāni kuśalamūlānyuttapyante, pariśuddhyanti, karmaṇyāni ca bhavanti, paryavadānaṃ cāgacchanti / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputrāḥ tadeva jātarūpaṃ sarvaratnapratyuptaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayottaptataraṃ bhavati, prabhāsvarataraṃ bhavati, asaṃhāryataraṃ ca bhavatyanyābhyo bhūṣaṇavikṛtibhyaḥ, evameva bho jinaputrāḥ ... tāni kuśalamūlānyupāyaprajñājñānābhinirhṛtāni bhūyasyā mātrayottaptatarāṇi
body.translated_text: For this <s>Bodhisattva</s>, thus endowed with knowledge, established on this seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>, <s>Dūraṃgamā</s> (the Far-reaching), many <s>Buddhas</s> come into his presence... He attends upon those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, and with reverence and honor he hears the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching from them, grasps it, and retains it. Having heard, he applies himself with the illumination of the wisdom-knowledge of attainment as it truly is. Having practiced, he retains it. He becomes a bearer of the teaching of those great-souled <s>Buddhas</s>. He is unshakable in all inquiries of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> regarding realization. To a greater degree, his patient acceptance of the profound <s>Dharma</s> for the benefit of beings is purified. For many <s>kalpas</s>... those wholesome roots are heated, purified, become workable, and reach complete purity. For many hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>... for many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, those wholesome roots are heated, purified, become workable, and reach complete purity. Just as, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the very same gold, when studded with all [kinds of] gems, becomes heated to a greater degree, more radiant, and more unmatched than other ornamental creations—even so, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>,... those wholesome roots, developed through skillful means, wisdom, and knowledge, become heated to a greater degree,

body.text:
bhavanti prabhāsvaratarāṇi, paryavadātatarāṇi asaṃhāryatarāṇi ca bhavanti sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputrāḥ sūryābhā asaṃhāryā bhavanti sarvajyotirgaṇacandrābhābhiścaturṣu mahādvīpeṣu, sarvasnehagatāni bhūyastvena pariśoṣayanti, sarvaśasyāni paripācayanti, evameva bho jinaputrā ... tāni kuśalamūlānyasaṃhāryāṇi bhavanti sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ, caturviparyāsagatāni ca sarvakleśasnehagatāni bhūyastvena pariśoṣayanti / kleṣāvilāni ca sarvasaṃtānāni paripācayanti / tasya daśabhyaḥ pāramitābhya upāyakauśalyapāramitā atiriktatamā bhavati, na ca pariśeṣā na samudāgacchati yathābalaṃ yathābhajamānam / iyaṃ bho jinaputrā bodhisattvasya dūraṃgamā nāma saptamī bodhisattvabhūmiḥ samāsanirdeśataḥ,
yasyāṃ pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo bhūyastvena vaśavartī bhavati devarājaḥ kṛtī prabhuḥ sattvānāmabhisamayajñānopasaṃhāreṣvaparyantaḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaparipṛcchāsu kuśalaḥ sattvānniyāmamavakrāmayitum / yacca kicit ... //
body.translated_text: more radiant, more purified, and more unmatched by all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. Just as, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the light of the sun is unmatched by all hosts of stars and the light of the moon on the four great continents, and mostly dries up all oily substances and ripens all crops—even so, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>,... those wholesome roots are unmatched by all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and mostly dry up all the oily substances of defilements connected with the four perversions, and ripen all mental continuities obscured by defilements. Among the ten <s>pāramitās</s>, the <s>upāyakauśalyapāramitā</s> (perfection of skillful means) is most preeminent for him; yet the remaining ones do not fail to arise, according to his ability and engagement. This, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> called <s>Dūraṃgamā</s> (the Far-reaching), in brief exposition. Established on it, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> mostly becomes <s>Vaśavartin</s>, the king of the gods, capable, powerful, boundless in presenting the knowledge of realization to beings, skilled in causing beings to enter the fixed course [of awakening]. Whatever [action he undertakes]...

body.text: dūraṃgamā nāma saptamī bhūmiḥ //
body.translated_text: The seventh <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Dūraṃgamā</s> (the Far-reaching).

body.text: 8 acalā nāma aṣṭamī bhūmiḥ /
body.translated_text: 8. The eighth <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Acalā</s> (the Immovable).

body.text: vajragarbho bodhisattva āha - yo 'yaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvaḥ saptasu bodhisattvabhūmiṣu sukṛtavicayaḥ prajñopāyābhyāṃ supariśodhitamārgaḥ susaṃbhṛtasaṃbhāraḥ suparibaddhamahāpraṇidhānaḥ adhiṣṭhitatathāgatādhiṣṭhānaḥ svakuśalamūlabalādhānaprāptaḥ tathāgatabalavaiśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmānugatasaṃjñāmanasikāraḥ supariśodhitādhyāśayasaṃkalpa puṇyajñānabalābhyudgataḥ mahākaruṇākṛpābhyāṃ sarvasattvānutsṛṣṭaprayogaḥ apramāṇajñānapathānugataḥ, sa sarvadharmāṇāmādyanutpannatāṃ ca yathābhūtamavatarati / ajātatāṃ ca alakṣaṇatāṃ ca asaṃbhūtatāṃ ca avināśitāṃ ca aniṣṭhitatāṃ ca apravṛttitāṃ ca anabhinivṛttitāṃ ca abhāvasvabhāvatāṃ ca ādimadhyaparyavasānasamatāṃ ca tathatāvikalpasarvajñajñānapraveśatāṃ ca sarvadharmāṇāṃ yathābhūtamavatarati / sa sarvaśaścittamanovijñānavikalpasaṃjñāpagato 'navagṛhītākāśasamo 'bhyavakāśaprakṛtito 'vatīrṇo 'nutpattikadharmakṣāntiprāpta ityucyate //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s> said: "That <s>Bodhisattva</s>, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, who on the seven <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmis</s> has well-investigated, whose path is well-purified through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), who has well-accumulated the provisions, who is firmly bound by great aspirations, who is empowered by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s empowerment, who has attained the strength of his own wholesome roots, whose perception and mental attention follow the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s powers, fearlessnesses, and distinctive <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, who has well-purified his higher aspirations and intentions, who has risen through the power of merit and knowledge, and who through great compassion has not abandoned the endeavor for all beings, who follows the path of immeasurable knowledge—he enters, as it truly is, the primordial non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s>. He enters, as it truly is, the unborn-ness, characteristicless-ness, non-production, indestructibility, non-establishment, non-activity, non-reversal, nature as non-existence, equality of beginning-middle-end, and the entry into omniscient knowledge through the non-conceptualization of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of all <s>dharmas</s>. He is completely free from all conceptualization of mind, thought, and consciousness—equal to ungraspable space, entered into the nature of openness—and is said to have attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>)."

body.text: tatra bhavanto jinaputrā evaṃ kṣāntisamanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ sahapratilambhādacalāyā bodhisattvabhūmergambhīraṃ bodhisattvavihāramanuprāpto bhavati durājñātamasaṃbhinnaṃ sarvanimittāpagataṃ sarvasaṃjñāgrahavyāvṛttamapramāṇamasaṃhāryaṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ sarvavivekābhimukhībhūtam / tadyathāpi nāma bhavanto jinaputrā bhikṣurṛddhimāṃścetovaśipāramitāprāpto 'nupūrveṇa navamaṃ nirodhaṃ samāpannaḥ sarveñjitamanyanāspanditavikalpāpagato bhavati, evameva bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvo 'syā aṣṭamyā acalāyā bodhisattvabhūmeḥ sahapratilambhātsarvābhogavigato 'nābhogadharmatāprāptaḥ kāyavākcittautsukyāpagataḥ sarveñjitamanyanāspanditavikalpāpagato vipākadharmatāvasthito bhavati / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputrāḥ puruṣaḥ suptaḥ svapnāntaragato mahaughaprāptamātmānaṃ saṃjānīte / sa tatra mahadvyāyāmautsukyamārabhetottaraṇāya / sa tenaiva mahatā vyāyāmautsukyena vibudhyeta / samanantaravibuddhaśca vyāyāmautsukyabhayāpagato bhavet / evameva bho jinaputrā bodhisattvaścaturmahaughaprāptaṃ sattvakāyaṃ saṃjānāna uttaraṇābhiprāyaḥ sarvajñajñānābhisaṃbodhāya mahadvyāyāmautsukyamārabhate / sa mahāvīryārambhaprāptaḥ samanantaramanuprāpta imāmacalāṃ bodhisattvabhūmiṃ sarvābhogavigato bhavati / tasya sarveṇa sarvaṃ dvayasamudācāro vā nimittasamudācāro vā nābhāsībhavati / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputrā brahmalokopapattisthitaḥ kāmāvacarān kleśān na samudācarati, evameva bho jinaputrā bodhisattvo 'calāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitaḥ sarvacittamanovijñānasamudācārānna samudācarati / sarvabuddhasamudācāramapi ... bodhisamudācāramapi ... bodhisattvasamudācāramapi ... pratyekabuddhasamudācāramapi ... śrāvakasamudācāramapi ... nirvāṇasamudācāramapi ... arhatsamudācāramapi ... anāgāmisamudācāramapi ... nirvāṇasamudācāramapi ... arhatsamudācāramapi ... anāgāmisamudācāramapi ... sakṛdāgāmisamudācāramapi ... srotaāpannasamudācāramapi na samudācarati / kaḥ punarvādo laukikān samudācārān samudācariṣyatīti //
body.translated_text: There, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thus endowed with this patience, simultaneously with the attainment of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Acalā</s> (the Immovable), enters a profound <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding—hard to comprehend, unbreakable, free from all signs, turned away from all grasping at perceptions, immeasurable, unmatched by all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, oriented toward complete seclusion. Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, a monk endowed with supernatural power who has attained mastery over mind, having entered the ninth cessation-attainment in due sequence, is free from all stirring, agitation, and conceptualization—even so, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, simultaneously with the attainment of this eighth <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Acalā</s>, is free from all deliberate effort, has attained the nature of effortlessness, is free from the eagerness of body, speech, and mind, is free from all stirring, agitation, and conceptualization, and abides in the nature of karmic fruition. Just as, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, a man who has fallen asleep and entered a dream perceives himself caught in a great flood; he would exert great effort and eagerness to cross over; by that very great effort and eagerness he would awaken; and having immediately awakened, he would be free from the effort, eagerness, and fear—even so, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, perceiving the mass of beings caught in the four great floods, with the intention to rescue them, undertakes great effort and eagerness for the awakening to omniscient knowledge. Having attained great exertion of energy, immediately upon reaching this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Acalā</s>, he becomes free from all deliberate effort. For him, there is absolutely no appearance of any duality or any sign-activity. Just as, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, one established in the <s>Brahmaloka</s> does not engage in the defilements of the desire realm—even so, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Acalā</s> does not engage in any activity of mind, thought, or consciousness. He does not engage in any <s>Buddha</s>-activity... nor awakening-activity... nor <s>Bodhisattva</s>-activity... nor <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-activity... nor <s>Śrāvaka</s>-activity... nor <s>nirvāṇa</s>-activity... nor <s>Arhat</s>-activity... nor non-returner-activity... nor <s>nirvāṇa</s>-activity... nor <s>Arhat</s>-activity... nor non-returner-activity... nor once-returner-activity... nor stream-enterer-activity. How much less would he engage in worldly activities!

body.text: tasya khalu bho jinaputra bodhisattvasya evamimāmacalāṃ bodhisattvabhūmimanugatasya pūrvapraṇidhānabalādhānasthitasya buddhā bhagavantastasmin dharmamukhasrotasi tathāgatajñānopasaṃhāraṃ kurvanti / evaṃ cainaṃ bruvanti - sādhu sādhu kulaputra / eṣā paramārthakṣāntirbuddhadharmānugamāya / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra yā asmākaṃ daśabalacaturvaiśāradyabuddhadharmasamṛddhiḥ, sā tava nāsti / tasyā buddhadharmasamṛddheḥ paryeṣaṇāya abhiyogaṃ kuru, vīryamārabhasva / etadeva kṣāntimukhaṃ monmokṣīḥ / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra kiṃcāpi tvayaivaṃ śāntavimokṣavihāro 'nuprāptaḥ, imān punaraśāntānapraśāntān bālapṛthagjanān nānākleśasamudācāraprāptān vividhavitarkopahatamānasān samanvāhara, apekṣasva / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra pūrvapraṇidhānamanusmara sattvārthasaṃprāpaṇaṃ jñānamukhācintyatāṃ ca / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra eṣā sarvadharmāṇāṃ dharmatā / utpādādvā tathāgatānāmanutpādādvā sthitaivaiṣā dharmatā dharmadhātusthitiḥ yadidaṃ sarvadharmaśūnyatā sarvadharmānupalabdhiḥ / naitayā tathāgatā eva kevalaṃ prabhāvyante, sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhā api hyetāmavikalpadharmatāmanuprāpnuvanti / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra prekṣasva tāvat tvamasmākaṃ kāyāpramāṇatāṃ ca jñānāpramāṇatāṃ ca buddhakṣetrāpramāṇatāṃ ca jñānābhinirhārāpramāṇatāṃ ca prabhāmaṇḍalāpramāṇatāṃ ca svarāṅgaviśuddhyapramāṇatāṃ ca / tathaiva tvamapyabhinirhāramutpādaya / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra ekastveṣa āloko yo 'yaṃ sarvadharmanirvikalpālokaḥ / īdṛśāstu kulaputra dharmālokāstathāgatānāmaparyantagatā aparyantakṛtā aparyantabaddhāḥ, yeṣāṃ saṃkhyā nāsti, gaṇanā pramāṇamupaniṣadaupamyaṃ nāsti, teṣāmadhigamāya abhinirhāramutpādaya / api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra prekṣasva tāvaddaśasu dikṣu apramāṇakṣetratāṃ ca apramāṇasattvatāṃ ca apramāṇadharmavibhaktitāṃ ca / tatsarvamanugaṇaya / yathāvattayā abhinirhāramutpādaya / iti hi bho jinaputra te buddhā bhagavanta evaṃbhūmyanugatasya bodhisattvasya evaṃ pramukhānyaprameyāṇyasaṃkhyeyāni jñānābhinirhāramukhānyupasaṃharanti, yairjñānābhinirhāramukhairbodhisattvo 'pramāṇajñānavibhaktito 'bhinirhārakarmābhiniṣpādayati //
body.translated_text: Now, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, for this <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has thus entered this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Acalā</s>, established through the power of his former aspirations, the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones present to him in that stream of the <s>Dharma</s>-door the instruction of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge. They speak to him thus: 'Well done, well done, O son of good family! This is the supreme patience that leads to the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. But, O son of good family, the achievement of our ten powers, four fearlessnesses, and <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>—that you do not yet possess. Strive for the attainment of that achievement of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, exert your energy! Do not abandon this door of patience! But, O son of good family, although you have attained this peaceful and liberated abiding, consider these unpeaceful, unquiet ordinary beings, afflicted by the manifold activities of defilements, minds assailed by various thoughts—regard them, look after them! Furthermore, O son of good family, remember your former aspirations for the accomplishment of the welfare of beings, and the inconceivable doors of knowledge! Furthermore, O son of good family, this is the <s>dharmatā</s> (nature) of all <s>dharmas</s>: whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise or do not arise, this <s>dharmatā</s> stands firm, this <s>dharmadhātu</s> abiding—namely, the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>, the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>. It is not by this alone that <s>Tathāgatas</s> are distinguished; all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> too attain this non-conceptual <s>dharmatā</s>. Furthermore, O son of good family, behold the immeasurability of our body, the immeasurability of our knowledge, the immeasurability of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, the immeasurability of the production of knowledge, the immeasurability of the radiance-circle, the immeasurability of the purity of voice and limbs—generate the development [to attain] likewise! Furthermore, O son of good family, this is but one illumination—namely, the illumination of non-conceptualization of all <s>dharmas</s>. But, O son of good family, the illuminations of <s>dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are boundless, endless, unlimited—for them there is no counting, no reckoning, no measure, no basis, no comparison—generate the development for their attainment! Furthermore, O son of good family, behold the immeasurable fields in the ten directions, the immeasurable beings, the immeasurable analysis of <s>Dharma</s>—take it all into account; generate the development accordingly.' Thus, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones present to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has entered such a <s>bhūmi</s> these and other immeasurable and innumerable foremost doors of the production of knowledge, by which doors the <s>Bodhisattva</s> accomplishes the work of producing immeasurable knowledge in its analysis.

body.text: ārocayāmi te bho jinaputra, prativedayāmi / te cedbuddhā bhagavantastaṃ bodhisattvamevaṃ sarvajñajñānābhinirhāramukheṣu nāvatārayeyuḥ, tadevāsya parinirvāṇaṃ bhavetsarvasattvakāryapratiprasrabdhiśca / tena khalu punarbuddhā bhagavantastasya bodhisattvasya tāvadapramāṇaṃ jñānābhinirhārakarmopasaṃharanti, yasyaikakṣaṇābhinirhṛtasya jñānābhinirhārakarmaṇaḥ sa pūrvakaḥ prathamacittotpādamupādāya yāvatsaptamīṃ bhūmipratiṣṭhāmupāgata ārambhaḥ śatatamīmapi kalāṃ nopeti, sahasratamīmapi, śatasahasratamīmapi ... peyālaṃ ... koṭīniyutaśatasahasratamīmapi kalāṃ nopeti, saṃkhyāmapi, gaṇanāmapi, upamāmapi, upanisāmapi, yāvadaupamyamapi na kṣamate / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi bho jinaputra pūrvamekakāyābhinirhāratayā caryābhinirhāro 'bhūt / imāṃ punarbhūmiṃ samārūḍhasya bodhisattvasya apramāṇakāyavibhaktito bodhisattvacaryābalaṃ samudāgacchati / apramāṇaghoṣābhinirhārataḥ apramāṇajñānābhinirhārataḥ apramāṇopapattyabhinirhārataḥ apramāṇakṣetrapariśodhanataḥ apramāṇasattvaparipācanataḥ
body.translated_text: I declare to you, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, I proclaim: if those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones did not cause that <s>Bodhisattva</s> to descend into these foremost doors for the production of omniscient knowledge, that would be his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, along with the cessation of all activity for beings. But those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones present to that <s>Bodhisattva</s> such immeasurable work of producing knowledge that, for the knowledge-production accomplished in a single moment, that prior effort from the first generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> up to the establishment on the seventh <s>bhūmi</s> does not reach even one hundredth part, nor one thousandth, nor one hundred-thousandth... nor one hundred-thousandth of a <s>koṭi-niyuta</s>—it does not bear comparison in number, reckoning, or analogy. For what reason? Because, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, previously the production of practice was through the development of a single body. But for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has ascended to this <s>bhūmi</s>, the power of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-practice arises through the analysis of immeasurable bodies, through the production of immeasurable voices, through the production of immeasurable knowledge, through the production of immeasurable rebirths, through the purification of immeasurable fields, through the ripening of immeasurable beings,

body.text: apramāṇabuddhapūjopasthānataḥ apramāṇadharmakāyānubodhataḥ apramāṇābhijñābalādhānābhinirhārataḥ apramāṇaparṣanmaṇḍalavibhaktyabhinirhārataśca apramāṇānugatena kāyavāṅmanaskarmābhinirhāreṇa sarvabodhisattvacaryābalaṃ samudāgacchatyavicālyayogena / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra mahāsamudragāmī poto 'prāpto mahāsamudraṃ sābhogavāhano bhavati / sa eva samanantaramanuprāpto mahāsamudramanābhogavāhano vātamaṇḍalīpraṇīto yadekadivasena mahāsamudre kramate, tatsarvasābhogavāhanatayā na śakyaṃ varṣaśatenāpi tāvadaprameyamanuprāptum / evameva bho jinaputra bodhisattvaḥ susaṃbhṛtamahākuśalamūlasaṃbhāro mahāyānasamudāgamābhirūḍho mahābodhisattvacaryāsāgaramanuprāpto yadekamuhūrtena jñānānābhogatayā sarvajñajñānenākramati, tanna śakyaṃ pūrvakeṇa sābhogakarmaṇā kalpaśatasahasreṇāpi tāvadaprameyamanuprāptum //
body.translated_text: through the immeasurable worship and attendance upon <s>Buddhas</s>, through the immeasurable awakening to the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, through the immeasurable production of the power of <s>abhijñā</s> (higher knowledges), and through the immeasurable production of the analysis of assembly-circles—through the production of body, speech, and mind activity followed by the immeasurable, the power of all <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice arises through unshakable application. Just as, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, a great ship bound for the ocean, before reaching the great ocean, moves with effort; but the very same ship, as soon as it reaches the great ocean, moves without effort, propelled by the circle of wind, and what it traverses in one day on the great ocean—that immeasurable [distance] could not be reached even in a hundred years through effortful movement. Even so, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has well-accumulated great wholesome roots as provisions, who has boarded the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, who has reached the ocean of the great <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice—what he traverses in one moment through effortless knowledge toward omniscient knowledge, that immeasurable [distance] could not be reached even in a hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s> through prior effortful activity.

body.text:
tatra bho jinaputra bodhisattvo 'ṣṭamīṃ bodhisattvabhūmimanuprāpto mahatyā upāyakauśalyajñānābhinirhārānābhogaprasṛtayā bodhisattvabuddhyā sarvajñajñānaṃ vicārayan lokadhātusaṃbhavaṃ ca vicārayati, lokadhātuvibhavaṃ ca vicārayati / sa yathā ca lokaḥ saṃvartate, taṃ ca prajānāti / yathā ca loko vivartate, ... / yena ca karmopacayena lokaḥ saṃvartate, ... / yena ca karmakṣayeṇa loko vivartate, ... / yāvatkālaṃ ca lokaḥ saṃvartate, ... / yāvatkālaṃ ca loko vivartate, ... / yāvatkālaṃ ca lokaṃ saṃvṛttastiṣṭhati, ... / yāvatkālaṃ ca loko vivṛttastiṣṭhati, taṃ ca prajānāti sarvatra cānavaśeṣataḥ / sa pṛthivīdhātuparīttatāṃ ca prajānāti mahadgatatāṃ ca ... apramāṇatāṃ ca ... vibhaktitāṃ ca prajānāti / abdhātu ... / tejodhātu ... / vāyudhātu ... / sa paramāṇurajaḥsūkṣmatāṃ ca prajānāti, mahadgatatāṃ ca apramāṇatāṃ ca vibhaktitāṃ ca prajānāti / apramāṇaparamāṇurajovibhaktikauśalyaṃ ca prajānāti / asyāṃ ca lokadhātau yāvanti pṛthivīdhātoḥ paramāṇurajāṃsi tāni prajānāti / yāvanti abdhātoḥ ... / tejodhātoḥ ... / vāyudhātoḥ ... / yāvantyo ratnavibhaktayo yāvanti ca ratnaparamāṇurajāṃsi tāni prajānāti / sattvakāya ... / kṣetrakāya ... / sa sattvānāṃ kāyaudārikatāṃ ca kāyasūkṣmatāṃ ca kāyavibhaktitāṃ ca prajānāti / yāvanti paramāṇurajāṃsi saṃbhūtāni nairayikakāyāśrayatastāni prajānāti / tiryagyonikāyāśrayataḥ ... / ... yamalokakāyāśrayataḥ ... / ... asuralokakāyāśrayataḥ
... . / devalokakāyāśrayataḥ ... . / manuṣyalokakāyāśrayataḥ ... . / sa evaṃ paramāṇurajaḥprabhedajñānāvatīrṇaḥ kāmadhātusaṃvartaṃ ca prajānāti / rūpadhātuvivartaṃ ... / ārūpyadhātuvivartaṃ ca prajānāti / rūpadhātuparīttatāṃ ... . ārūpyadhātuparīttatāṃ ... / āmadhātuparīttatāṃ ca mahadgatatāṃ ca apramāṇatāṃ ca vibhaktitāṃ ca prajānāti / rūpadhātuparīttatāṃ ... ārūpyadhātuparīttataṃ ... / kāmadhātuparīttatāṃ ca mahadgatatāṃ ca apramāṇatāṃ ca vibhaktitāṃ ca prajānāti / rūpadhātvārūpyadhātuparīttatāṃ ... / traidhātukavicārajñānānugame svabhinirhṛtajñānālokaḥ sattvakāyaprabhedajñānakuśalaḥ kṣetrakāyavibhāgajñānakuśalaśca sattvopapattyāyatanābhinirhāre buddhiṃ cārayati / sa yādṛśī sattvānāmupapattiśca kāyasamudāgamaśca, tādṛśameva svakāyamadhitiṣṭhati sattvaparipācanāya / sa ekāmapi trisāhasramahāsāhasrāṃ lokadhātuṃ
body.translated_text: There, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who has attained the eighth <s>bodhisattva</s> stage, investigating omniscient knowledge (<s>sarvajñajñāna</s>) with <s>bodhisattva</s> wisdom that proceeds effortlessly through the accomplishment of skillful means and knowledge (<s>upāyakauśalyajñānābhinirhāra</s>), contemplates the arising of world-systems and contemplates the dissolution of world-systems. He knows how the world contracts, and he knows how the world expands. He knows through what accumulation of <s>karma</s> the world contracts, and through what exhaustion of <s>karma</s> the world expands. He knows how long the world contracts, how long the world expands, how long the contracted world endures, and how long the expanded world endures—all this he knows completely without remainder. He knows the smallness, greatness, immeasurability, and differentiation of the earth element; of the water element; of the fire element; of the wind element. He knows the subtlety of atomic particles, their greatness, immeasurability, and differentiation. He knows the skill in differentiating immeasurable atomic particles. He knows how many atomic particles of the earth element exist in this world-system; how many of the water element; of the fire element; of the wind element. He knows the varieties of gems and their atomic particles; of beings' bodies; of fields. He knows the coarseness, subtlety, and differentiation of beings' bodies. He knows how many atomic particles are constituted from the physical basis of hell-beings; of animals; of the world of <s>Yama</s>; of the world of <s>asuras</s>; of the world of <s>devas</s>; of the world of humans. Having thus entered into the knowledge of the differentiation of atomic particles, he knows the contraction of the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>); the expansion of the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>); the expansion of the formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>). He knows the smallness, greatness, immeasurability, and differentiation of the form realm, the formless realm, and the desire realm.

body.text: spharitvā sattvānāṃ svakāyaṃ vibhaktyadhimuktiṣu tathatvāyopapattaye 'bhinirharati pratibhāsajñānānugamanatayā (yathā sattvāḥ paripākaṃ gacchantyanuttarasamyaksaṃbodhivimuktaye) / evaṃ dve vā tisro vā catasro vā pañca vā daśa vā viṃśatirvā triṃśadvā catvāriṃśadvā pañcāśadvā śataṃ vā yāvadanabhilāpyā api trisāhasramahāsāhasrā lokadhātūḥ spharitvā sattvānāṃ svakāyaṃ ... peyālaṃ ... pratibhāsajñānānugamanatayā / sa evaṃjñānasamanvāgato 'syāṃ bhūmau supratiṣṭhita ekabuddhakṣetrācca na calati, anabhilāpyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu tathāgataparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu ca pratibhāsaprāpto bhavati //
body.translated_text: Having pervaded [everywhere], he manifests his own body for beings according to their differentiated dispositions, for the purpose of arriving at suchness (<s>tathatā</s>), following the course of reflective knowledge. Just as beings ripen toward liberation in unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s>)—thus in two, three, or more

body.text: yādṛśī sattvānāṃ kāyavibhaktiśca varṇaliṅgasaṃsthānārohapariṇāhādhimuktyadhyāśayaśca teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu teṣu ca parṣanmaṇḍaleṣu tatra tatra tathā tathā svakāyamādarśayati / sa śramaṇaparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu śramaṇavarṇarūpamādarśayati / brāhmaṇaparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu brāhmaṇavarṇarūpamādarśayati / kṣatriya ... / vaiśya ... / śūdra ... / gṛhapati ... / cāturmahārājika ... / trāyastriṃśa ... / evaṃ yāma ... / tuṣita ... / nirmāṇarati ... / paranirmitavaśavarti ... / māra ... / brahma ... / yāvadakaniṣṭha ... / śrāvakavaineyikānāṃ sattvānāṃ śrāvakakāyavarṇarūpamādarśayati / pratyekabuddhavaineyikānāṃ sattvānāṃ pratyekabuddhakāyavarṇarūpamādarśayati / bodhisattva ... / tathāgata ... / iti hi bho jinaputra yāvanto 'nabhilāpyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu sattvānāmupapattyāyatanādhimuktiprasarāsteṣu tathatvāya svakāyavibhaktimādarśayati //
body.translated_text: According to whatever bodily differentiation beings possess—their color, marks, shape, height, girth, disposition, and inclination—in those <s>buddha</s>-fields and in those assembly-circles, in each place he displays his own body accordingly. He appears in assemblies of <s>śramaṇas</s>,

body.text: sa sarvakāyavikalpāpagataḥ kāyasamatāprāptaḥ (taccāsya kāyasaṃdarśanamakṣūṇamavandhyaṃ ca sattvaparipākavinayāya) sa sattvakāyaṃ ca prajānāti / kṣetrakāyaṃ ca ... / karmavipākakāyaṃ ca ... / śrāvakakāyaṃ ca ... / pratyekabuddhakāyaṃ ca ... / bodhisattvakāyaṃ ca ... / tathāgatakāyaṃ ca ... / jñānakāyaṃ ca ... / dharmakāyaṃ ca ... / ākāśakāyaṃ ca prajānāti / sa sattvānāṃ cittāśayābhinirhāramājñāya yathākālaparipākavinayānatikramādākāṅkṣan sattvakāyaṃ svakāyamadhitiṣṭhati / evaṃ kṣetrakāyaṃ karmavipākakāyaṃ ... ātmakāyamadhitiṣṭhati / sa sattvānāṃ cittāśayābhinirhāramājñāya yaṃ yameva kāyaṃ yasmin yasmin kāye ākāṅkṣati, taṃ tameva kāyaṃ tasmin tasmin kāye (svakāyaṃ) adhitiṣṭhati / sa sattvakāyānāṃ karmakāyatāṃ ca prajānāti / vipākakāyatāṃ ca ... / kleśakāyatāṃ ca ... / rūpakāyatāṃ ca ... / ārūpyakāyatāṃ ca prajānāti / kṣetrakāyānāṃ parīttatāṃ ca prajānāti, mahadgatatāṃ ca apramāṇatāṃ ca saṃkliṣṭatāṃ ca viśuddhatāṃ ca vyatyastatāṃ ca adhomūrdhatāṃ ca samatalatāṃ ca samavasaraṇatāṃ ca digjālavibhāgatāṃ ca prajānāti / karmavipākakāyānāṃ vibhaktisaṃketaṃ prajānāti / evaṃ śrāvakākāyānāṃ pratyekabuddhakāyānāṃ bodhisattvakāyānāṃ vibhaktisaṃketaṃ prajānāti / tathāgatakāyānāmabhisaṃbodhikāyatāṃ ca prajānāti / praṇidhānakāyatāṃ ca ... / nirmāṇakāyatāṃ ca / adhiṣṭhānakāyatāṃ ca / rūpalakṣaṇānuvyañjanavicitrālaṃkārakāyatāṃ ca / prabhākāyatāṃ ca / manomayakāyatāṃ ca / puṇyakāyatāṃ ca / jñānakāyatāṃ ca / dharmakāyatāṃ ca prajānāti / jñānakāyānāṃ suvicāritatāṃ ca prajānāti / yathāvannistīraṇatāṃ ca phalaprayogasaṃgṛhītatāṃ
body.translated_text: Having gone beyond all conceptualization of bodies and attained equality of body (<s>kāyasamatā</s>)—and that display of his body is undiminished and unfailing for the purpose of ripening and disciplining beings—he knows the body of beings, the body of fields, the body of <s>karma</s>-fruition, the body of <s>śrāvakas</s>,

body.text: ca laukikalokottaravibhāgatāṃ ca triyāṇavyavasthānatāṃ ca sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇatāṃ ca nairyāṇikānairyāṇikatāṃ ca śaikṣāśaikṣatāṃ ca prajānāti / dharmakāyānāṃ samatāṃ ca prajānāti / avikopanatāṃ ca avasthānasaṃketasaṃvṛttivyavasthānatāṃ ca sattvāsattvadharmavyavasthānatāṃ ca buddhadharmāryasaṃghavyavasthānatāṃ ca prajānāti / ākāśakāyānāmapramāṇatāṃ ca sarvatrānugatatāṃ ca aśarīratāṃ ca avitathānantatāṃ ca rūpakāyābhivyaktitāṃ ca prajānāti //
body.translated_text: He knows the distinction between worldly and supramundane, the establishment of the three vehicles (<s>triyāna</s>), what is common and uncommon, what leads to liberation and what does not, the states of learners and non-learners (<s>śaikṣa</s> and <s>aśaikṣa</s>). He knows the equality of <s>dharmakāyas</s>, their indestructibility, and their stability.

body.text: sa evaṃ kāyajñānābhinirhāraprāpto vaśavartī bhavati sarvasattveṣu / āyurvaśitāṃ ca pratilabhate 'nabhilāpyānabhilāpyakalpāyuḥpramāṇādhiṣṭhānatayā / cetovaśitāṃ ca pratilabhate 'pramāṇāsaṃkhyeyasamādhinidhyaptijñānapraveśatayā / pariṣkāravaśitāṃ ca sarvalokadhātvanekavyūhālaṃkārapratimaṇḍitādhiṣṭhānasaṃdarśanatayā / karmavaśitāṃ ca yathākālaṃ karmavipākādhiṣṭhānasaṃdarśanatayā / upapattivaśitāṃ ca sarvalokadhātūpapattisaṃdarśanatayā adhimuktisaṃdarśanatayā sarvalokadhātubuddhapratipūrṇasaṃdarśanatayā praṇidhānasaṃdarśanatayā yatheṣṭabuddhakṣetrakālābhisaṃbodhisaṃdarśanatayā ṛddhisaṃdarśanatayā sarvabuddhakṣetra-ṛddhivikurvaṇasaṃdarśanatayā dharmasaṃdarśanatayā anantamadhyadharmamukhālokasaṃdarśanatayā jñānasaṃdarśanatayā tathāgatabalavaiśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmalakṣaṇānuvyañjanābhisaṃbodhisaṃdarśanatayā //
body.translated_text: Having thus attained the accomplishment of body-knowledge, he becomes sovereign over all beings. He obtains mastery over lifespan (<s>āyurvaśitā</s>) through the ability to sustain a lifespan of inexpressibly inexpressible <s>kalpas</s>. He obtains mastery over mind (<s>cetovaśitā</s>) through immeasurable and innumerable <s>samādhis</s>.

body.text: sa āsāṃ daśānāṃ bodhisattvavaśitānāṃ sahapratilambhena acintyajñānī ca bhavati atulyajñānī ca aprameyajñānī ca vipulajñānī ca asaṃhāryajñānī ca bhavati / tasyaivaṃbhūmyanugatasya evaṃ jñānasamanvāgatasya atyantāgavadyaḥ kāyakarmasamudācāraḥ pravartate, atyantānavadyaśca vāk ... / atyantānavadyaśca manaḥsamudācāraḥ pravartate / jñānapūrvaṃgamo jñānānuparivartī prajñāpāramitādhipateyo mahākaruṇāpūrvaka upāyakauśalyasuvibhaktaḥ praṇidhānasvabhinirhṛtastathāgatādhiṣṭhānasvadhiṣṭhito 'pratiprasrabdhasattvārthaprayogo 'paryantalokadhātuvibhaktigataḥ / samāsato bho jinaputra bodhisattvasya imāmacalāṃ bodhisattvabhūmimanuprāptasya sarvabuddhadharmasamudānayanāya kāyavāṅmanaskarmasamudācāraḥ pravartate / sa evamimāmacalāṃ bodhisattvabhūmimanuprāptaḥ supratiṣṭhitāśayabalaśca bhavati sarvakleśasamudācārāpagatatvāt / supratiṣṭhitādhyāśayabalaśca bhavati mārgāvipravāsitatvāt / mahākaruṇābalasupratiṣṭhitaśca bhavati sattvārthānutsargatvāt / mahāmaitrībala ... sarvajagatparitrāṇatvāt / dhāraṇībala ... asaṃpramoṣadharmatvāt / pratibhānabala ... sarvabuddhadharmapravicayavibhāgakuśalatvāt / abhijñābala ... aparyantalokadhātucaryāvibhāgakuśalatvāt / praṇidhānabala ... sarvabodhisattvakriyānutsargatvāt / pāramitābala ... sarvabuddhadharmasamudānayanatvāt / tathāgatādhiṣṭhānabala ... sarvākārasarvajñānābhimukhatvāt / sa evaṃbalādhānaprāptaḥ sarvakriyāśca saṃdarśayati, sarvakriyāsu ca anavadyo bhavatyanupaliptaśca //
body.translated_text: Through the simultaneous attainment of these ten <s>bodhisattva</s> masteries (<s>vaśitā</s>), he becomes one of inconceivable knowledge, incomparable knowledge, immeasurable knowledge, vast knowledge, and indestructible knowledge. For one endowed with such knowledge, having followed such stages,

body.text: iyaṃ bho jinaputra bodhisattvasya aṣṭamī jñānabhūmiracaletyucyate 'saṃhāryatvāt / avivartyabhūmirityucyate jñānāvivartyatvāt / durāsadabhūmirityucyate sarvajagaddurjñānatvāt / kumārabhūmirityucyate
body.translated_text: This, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s eighth stage of knowledge, called <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable) because it cannot be shaken; called the irreversible stage (<s>avivartyabhūmi</s>) because of the irreversibility of knowledge; called the inaccessible stage (<s>durāsadabhūmi</s>) because it is difficult for all the world to comprehend; called the youthful stage (<s>kumārabhūmi</s>) because

body.text: anavadyatvāt / janmabhūmirityucyate yathābhiprāyavaśavartitvāt / pariniṣpannabhūmirityucyate apunaḥkāryatvāt / pariniṣṭhitabhūmirityucyate / sukṛtajñānavicayatvāt / nirmāṇabhūmirityucyate svabhinirhṛtapraṇidhānatvāt / adhiṣṭhānabhūmirityucyate / parāvikopanatvāt / anābhogabhūmirityucyate pūrvāntābhinirhṛtatvāt //
body.translated_text: it is faultless; called the birth stage (<s>janmabhūmi</s>) because of sovereignty according to one's intention; called the fully accomplished stage (<s>pariniṣpannabhūmi</s>) because nothing further remains to be done; called the firmly established stage (<s>pariniṣṭhitabhūmi</s>) because of well-accomplished investigation of knowledge; called the transformation stage (<s>nirmāṇabhūmi</s>) because of the accomplishment of one's own

body.text: evaṃ jñānasvabhinirhṛtaḥ khalu punarbho jinaputra bodhisattvo buddhagotrānugato buddhaguṇaprabhāvabhāsitastathāgateryāpathacaryācāritrānugato buddhaviṣayābhimukhaḥ satatasamitaṃ svadhiṣṭhitatathāgatādhiṣṭhānaśca bhavati śakrabrahmalokapālapratyudgataśca vajrapāṇisatatānubaddhaśca samādhibalānutsṛṣṭaśca ca apramāṇakāyavibhaktyabhinirhṛtaśca sarvakāyacaryābalopagataśca mahābhijñāvipākapariniṣpannaśca anantasamādhivaśavartī ca apramāṇavyākaraṇapratyeṣakaśca yathāparipavakkajagadabhisaṃbodhinidarśakaśca bhavati / sa evaṃ jñānabhūmyanugato mahāyānamaṇḍalānupraviṣṭaḥ suvicāritamahājñānābhijñaḥ satatasamitaṃ pramuktaprajñālokaraśmirasaṅgadharmadhātupathāvatīrṇo lokadhātupathavibhaktikovidaḥ sarvākāraguṇasaṃdarśakaḥ svacittotpādavaśavartī pūrvāntāparāntasuvicitajñānaḥ sarvamārapathāvartanavivartanajñānānugataḥ sarvatathāgataviṣayagocarānupraviṣṭo 'paryantalokadhātuprasareṣu bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratyapratyudāvartyayogena / tata ucyate bodhisattvo 'calāṃ bodhisattvabhūmimanuprāpta iti //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> thus self-produced through knowledge, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, follows the <s>Buddha</s>-lineage, is illuminated by the radiance of the <s>Buddha</s>'s qualities, follows the conduct and behavior of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s deportment, faces the <s>Buddha</s>'s domain, is constantly and continually empowered by his own empowerment and that of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, is welcomed by <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the world-guardians, is constantly attended by <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, is unsurpassed in the power of <s>samādhi</s>, has accomplished the production of immeasurable body-divisions, has attained the power of all bodily conduct, has completed the ripening of the great superknowledges, commands infinite <s>samādhis</s>, seeks immeasurable predictions, and displays the awakening of the world according to its ripening. He, thus following the stage of knowledge, having entered the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, possessed of well-examined great knowledge and superknowledges, constantly and continually emitting rays of the light of wisdom, having descended to the path of the unobstructed <s>dharmadhātu</s>, skilled in the divisions of the paths of world-realms, displaying qualities in all aspects, commanding his own arising of the mind, possessed of well-examined knowledge of past and future, following the knowledge of turning and diverting from all the paths of <s>Māra</s>, having entered the domain and sphere of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>—he practices the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct in the expanse of boundless world-realms with irreversible application. Therefore he is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has arrived at the <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable).

body.text: tatra bho jinaputra acalāṃ bodhisattvabhūmimanuprāpto bodhisattvaḥ satatasamitamaparyantatathāgatadarśanāvirahito bhavati samādhibalasvabhinirhṛtatvāt / audārikaṃ buddhadarśanapūjopasthānaṃ notsṛjati / sa ekaikasmin kalpe ekaikasmin lokadhātuprasare anekān buddhān, anekāni buddhaśatāni ... peyālaṃ ... anekāni buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi satkaroti gurukaroti mānayati pūjayati sarvākārapūjābhinirhāraṃ copasaṃharati / tāṃśca tathāgatān paryupāste, lokadhātuvibhaktipūrvakaṃ ca dharmālokopasaṃhāraṃ pratīcchati / sa bhūyasyā mātrayā tathāgatadharmakośaprāpto 'saṃhāryo bhavati lokadhātuparipṛcchānirdeśeṣu / tāni cāsya kuśalamūlānyanekān kalpānuttapyante ... / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra tadeva jātarūpaṃ supariniṣṭhitaṃ kuśalena karmāreṇa suparikarmakṛtaṃ jambūdvīpasvāminaḥ kaṇṭhe śirasi vā ābaddhamasaṃhāryaṃ bhavati sarvajambūdvīpakānāṃ sattvānāmābharaṇavikṛtaiḥ, evameva bho jinaputra asyāmacalāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya tāni kuśalamūlānyasaṃhāryāṇi bhavanti sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhairyāvatsaptamībhūmisthitaiśca bodhisattvaiḥ / imāṃ ca bhūmimanugatasya bodhisattvasya mahatī prajñājñānaprabhā sattvānāṃ kleśatamāṃsi praśamayati suvibhaktajñānamukhābhinirhāratayā / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra sāhasriko mahābrahmā sāhasralokadhātuṃ
body.translated_text: Here, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has arrived at the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Acalā</s> is constantly and continually never separated from seeing the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, through having self-produced the power of <s>samādhi</s>. He does not abandon the direct seeing, worship, and attendance upon the <s>Buddhas</s>. In each aeon, in each expanse of world-realms, he honors, reveres, esteems, and worships many <s>Buddhas</s>, many hundreds of <s>Buddhas</s>... [abbreviated passage]... many hundreds of thousands of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, and provides the accomplishment of worship in all aspects. He attends upon those <s>Tathāgatas</s> and receives the gathering of <s>Dharma</s>-illumination preceded by the division of world-realms. To an even greater degree, having attained the treasury of <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, he becomes unassailable in questions about the divisions of world-realms

sāhasrādhipatiḥ / abhibhūranabhibhūto 'nvarthadarśī vaśiprāptaḥ kṛtī prabhuḥ sattvānāṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvapāramitopadeśopasaṃhāreṣu asaṃhāryo lokadhātuvibhaktiparipṛcchānirdeśeṣu / yacca kiṃcit ... //
body.translated_text: having pervaded [them] with friendliness and illuminated [them] with radiance—even so, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Acalā</s>, having pervaded world-realms equal in number to the atoms in a hundred thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields with the great radiance of friendliness, gradually pacifies the burning of the defilements of beings and refreshes their supports. Among the ten <s>pāramitās</s>, <s>praṇidhānapāramitā</s> (the perfection of vows) becomes the most prominent for him, though he does not fail to practice the remaining [<s>pāramitās</s>] according to his ability and share. This, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, is the eighth <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> called <s>Acalā</s>, described in brief. In detail, however, it should be understood as extending to the end of innumerable aeons of exposition. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> established thereon

body.text: acalā nāma aṣṭamī bhūmiḥ //
body.translated_text: —the eighth <s>bhūmi</s> called <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable).

body.text: 9 sādhumatī nāma navamī bhūmiḥ /
body.translated_text: 9. The ninth stage, called <s>Sādhumatī</s> (Good Intelligence).

body.text: vajragarbho bodhisattva āha - yo 'yaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattva evamapramāṇajñeyavicāritayā buddhyā bhūyaścottarān śāntān vimokṣānadhyavasyan adhyālambamānaḥ bhūyaścottaraṃ tathāgatajñānaṃ susamāptaṃ vicārayan tathāgataguhyānupraveśaṃ cāvataran acintyajñānamāhātmyaṃ ca pravicinvan dhāraṇīsamādhipravicayaṃ ca pariśodhayan abhijñāvaipulyaṃ cābhinirharan lokadhātuvibhaktiṃ cānugacchan tathāgatabalavaiśādyāveṇikabuddhadharmāsaṃhāryatāṃ ca parikarmayan tathāgatadharmacakrapravartanavṛṣabhatāṃ cānukramamāṇaḥ mahākaruṇādhiṣṭhānapratilambhaṃ cānutsṛjan navamīṃ bodhisattvabhūmimākramati / so 'syāṃ sādhumatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitaḥ kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtadharmābhisaṃskāraṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sāsravānāsravadharmābhisaṃskāraṃ ca ... / laukikalokottaradharmābhisaṃskāraṃ ca ... / cintyācintyadharmābhisaṃskāraṃ ca ... / niyatāniyatadharmābhisaṃskāraṃ ca ... / śrāvakapratyekabuddhadharmābhisaṃskāraṃ ca ... / bodhisattvacaryādharmābhisaṃskāraṃ ca ... / tathāgatabhūmidharmābhisaṃskāraṃ ca ... / saṃskṛtadharmābhisaṃskāraṃ ca.. / asaṃskṛtadharmābhisaṃskāraṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti //
body.translated_text: <s>Vajragarbha Bodhisattva</s> said: O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, with an intellect that examines immeasurable objects of knowledge, further aspires to and takes hold of the higher peaceful liberations, further examines the well-completed <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge, enters the secrets of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, investigates the greatness of inconceivable knowledge, purifies the investigation of <s>dhāraṇīs</s> and <s>samādhis</s>, accomplishes the breadth of superknowledges, follows the divisions of world-realms, cultivates the unassailability of the powers, fearlessnesses, and exclusive <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, progressively follows the bull-like quality of turning the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and does not relinquish the attainment of the empowerment of great compassion—he ascends to the ninth <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>. Established on this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Sādhumatī</s>, he knows as it truly is the formations of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate <s>dharmas</s>; the formations of <s>dharmas</s> with and without outflows; worldly and supramundane <s>dharma</s>-formations; conceivable and inconceivable <s>dharma</s>-formations; determinate and indeterminate <s>dharma</s>-formations; <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> <s>dharma</s>-formations; <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct <s>dharma</s>-formations; <s>Tathāgata</s>-stage <s>dharma</s>-formations; conditioned <s>dharma</s>-formations; and unconditioned <s>dharma</s>-formations.

body.text: sa evaṃjñānānugatayā buddhyā sattvacittagahanopacāraṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / kleśagahanopacāraṃ ca ... / karmagahanopacāraṃ ca ... / indriyagahanopacāraṃ ca ... / adhimuktigahanopacāraṃ ca ... / dhātugahanopacāraṃ ca ... / āśayānuśayagahanopacāraṃ ca ... / upapattigahanopacāraṃ ca ... / vāsanānusaṃdhigahanopacāraṃ ca ... / trirāśivyavasthānagahanopacāraṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sa sattvānāṃ cittavaimātratāṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / cittavicitratāṃ ca cittakṣaṇalaghuparivartabhaṅgabhaṅgatāṃ ca cittaśarīratāṃ ca cittānantyasarvataḥprabhūtatāṃ ca cittaprabhāsvaratāṃ ca cittasaṃkleśaniḥkleśatāṃ ca cittabandhavimokṣatāṃ ca cittamāyāviṭhapanatāṃ ca cittayathāgatipratyupasthānatāṃ ca yāvadanekāni cittanānātvasahasrāṇi yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sa kleśānāṃ dūrānugatatāṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / prayogānantatāṃ ca ... / sahajāvinirbhāgatāṃ ca ... / anuśayaparyutthānaikārthatāṃ ca ... / cittasaṃprayogāsaṃprayogatāṃ ca ... / upapattisaṃdhiyathāgatipratyupasthānatāṃ ca ... / traidhātukavibhaktitāṃ ca ... / tṛṣṇāvidyādṛṣṭiśalyamānamahāsāvadyatāṃ ca ... / trividhakarmaṇi dānānupacchedatāṃ ca ... / samāsato yāvaccaturaśītikleśacaritanānātvasahasrānupraveśatāṃ
body.translated_text: He, with an intellect that follows knowledge, knows as it truly is the deep workings of beings' minds, the deep workings of defilements, the deep workings of <s>karma</s>, the deep workings of faculties, the deep workings of aspirations, the deep workings of dispositions, the deep workings of latent tendencies and inclinations, the deep workings of rebirths, the deep workings of the connections of habitual tendencies, and the deep workings of the establishment of the three groups. He knows as it truly is the diversity of beings' minds, the variegation of mind, the momentary lightness of the turning and breaking and crumbling of mind, the embodiedness of mind, the infinity and all-pervasiveness of mind, the luminosity of mind, the defilement and purification of mind, the bondage and liberation of mind, the illusory establishment of mind, the occurrence of mind according to its course, and up to many thousands of diversities of mind. He knows as it truly is the far-reaching [nature] of defilements, their infinite modes of application, their congenital undifferentiated [nature], the identity of purpose of latent tendencies and active manifestations, their conjunction and disjunction with mind, the occurrence of their connection according to rebirth-course, their division in the three realms, the great fault of the arrow of craving, ignorance, and views, together with pride, the non-interruption of the three kinds of <s>karma</s> through giving, and in brief, up to the entry into eighty-four thousand diversities of the course of defilements

ca ... / lokottaradharmavyavasthānatāṃ ca ... / (sopādānānupādānatāṃ ca ... / saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtatāṃ ca / ) dṛṣṭadharmopapadyāparaparyāyavedanīyatāṃ ca ... / yānāyānaniyatāniyatatāṃ ca ... / samāsato yāvaccaturaśītikarmanānātvasahasrapravibhaktivicayakauśalyaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sa indriyāṇāṃ mṛdumadhyādhimātratāṃ ca ... / pūrvāntāparāntasaṃbhedāsaṃbhedatāṃ ca ... / udāramadhyanikṛṣṭatāṃ ca ... / kleśasahajāvinirbhāgatāṃ ca ... / yānāyānaniyatāniyatatāṃ ca ... / yathāparipavkāparipakvavaineyikatāṃ ca ... / indriyajālānuparivartanalaghubhaṅganimittagrahaṇatāṃ ca ... / indriyādhipatyānavamardanīyatāṃ ca ... / vivartyāvivartyendriyapravibhāgatāṃ ca ... / dūrānugatasahajāvinirbhāganānātvavimātratāṃ ca, samāsato yāvadanekānīndriyanānātvasahasrāṇi prajānāti / so 'dhimuktīnāṃ mṛdumadhyādhimātratāṃ ca ... yāvadanekānyadhimuktinānātvasahasrāṇi prajānāti / sa dhātūnāṃ ... . / sa āśayānāṃ ... . / so 'nuśayānāmāśayasahajacittasahajatāṃ ca ... . / cittasaṃprayogatāṃ ca ... / viprayogavibhāgadūrānugatatāṃ ca ... / anādikālānuddhaṭitatāṃ ca ... / sarvadhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattyabhijñāprasahyatāṃ ca / traidhātukasaṃdhisunibaddhatāṃ ca / anādikālacittanibandhasamudācāratāṃ ca / āyatanadvārasamudayavijñaptitāṃ ca / pratipakṣālābhādravyabhūtatāṃ ca / bhūmyāyatanasamavadhānāsamavadhānatāṃ ca / ananyāryamārgasamuddhaṭanatāṃ ca prajānāti / sa upapattinānātvatāṃ ca / yathākarmopapattitāṃ ca / nirayatiryagyonipretāsuramanuṣyadevavyavasthānatāṃ ca / rūpārūpyopapattitāṃ ca / saṃjñāsaṃjñopapattitāṃ ca / karmakṣetratṛṣṇāsnehāvidyāndhakāravijñānabījapunarbhavaprarohaṇatāṃ
ca / nāmarūpasahajāvinirbhāgatāṃ ca / bhavasaṃmohatṛṣṇābhilāṣasaṃdhitāṃ ca / bhoktukāmabhavitukāmasattvaratyanavarāgratāṃ ca / traidhātukāvagrahaṇasaṃjñāniṣkarṣaṇatāṃ ca prajānāti / sa vāsanānāmupacārānupacāratāṃ ca ... / yathāgatisaṃbandhavāsanāvāsitatāṃ ca / yathāsattvacaryācaraṇavāsitatāṃ ca / yathākarmakleśābhyāsavāsitatāṃ ca / kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtadharmābhyāsavāsitatāṃ ca / punarbhavagamanādhivāsitatāṃ ca ... / anupūrvādhivāsitatāṃ ca / dūrānugatānupacchedakleśopakarṣaṇavikārānuddharaṇavāsitatāṃ ca / dravyabhūtādravyabhūtavāsitatāṃ ca / śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvatathāgatadarśanaśravaṇasaṃvāsavāsitatāṃ ca prajānāti / sa sattvarāśīnāṃ samyaktvaniyatatāṃ ca prajānāti mithyātvaniyatatāṃ ca / ubhayatvāniyatatāṃ ca ... / samyagdṛṣṭisamyagniyatatāṃ ca mithyādṛṣṭimithyā ... niyatatāṃ ca / tadubhayavigamādaniyatatāṃ ca pañcānantaryānyatamamithyādṛṣṭiniyatatāṃ ca ... / pañcendriyasamyagniyatatāṃ ca ... / aṣṭamithyātvamithyāniyatatāṃ ca ... / samyaktvasamyagniyatatāṃ ca ... / apunaḥkāritatāṃ ca ... / mātsaryerṣyāghṛṇopacārāvinivṛttyā mithyāniyatatāṃ ca ... / āryānuttaramārgabhāvanopasaṃhārasamyaktvaniyatatāṃ ca ... / tadubhayavigamādaniyatarāśyupadeśatāṃ ca prajānāti / iti hi bho jinaputra evaṃjñānānugato bodhisattvaḥ sādhumatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhita ityucyate //
body.translated_text: —he knows as it truly is. He [knows] the wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate nature of <s>karmas</s>; their informative and non-informative nature; their congenital undifferentiated nature conjoined with mind; the continuity of their fruit through the uninterrupted accumulation of momentary destruction by their own nature; their ripening and nature of ripening; the diversity of undertaking dark, bright, dark-and-bright, and partial <s>karmas</s>; the immeasurability of the field of <s>karma</s>; the distinction between noble and worldly [<s>karma</s>]; the establishment of supramundane <s>dharmas</s>; the nature with and without clinging; the conditioned and unconditioned nature; the nature of being experienced in the present life, at rebirth, or in subsequent lives; the determinate and indeterminate nature regarding vehicles and non-vehicles; and in brief, up to the skill in examining eighty-four thousand diversities of <s>karma</s>—he knows as it truly is. He [knows] the mild, middling, and intense nature of faculties; their distinction and non-distinction regarding past and future; their exalted, middling, and inferior nature; their congenital undifferentiated nature conjoined with defilements; their determinate and indeterminate nature regarding vehicles and non-vehicles; the mature and immature nature of those to be trained; the momentary lightness of the turning, breaking, and sign-grasping of the network of faculties; the uncrushability of the supremacy of faculties; the division of reversible and irreversible faculties; the far-reaching diversity of congenital undifferentiated nature; and in brief, up to many thousands of diversities of faculties—he knows. He [knows] the mild, middling, and intense nature of aspirations... up to many thousands of diversities of aspirations. He [knows those of] dispositions... He [knows those of] latent tendencies... He [knows] latent tendencies as congenital with inclination and congenital with mind; their conjunction [with mind]; their separation, division, and far-reaching [nature]; their non-uprooting from beginningless time; their overcoming of all <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, <s>samādhis</s>, attainments, and superknowledges; their being well-bound to the junctures of the three realms; their habitual occurrence bound to mind from beginningless time; their being known through the arising at the gates of the sense-bases; their reality as substantial [things] due to the absence of antidotes; their equal and unequal presence on the stages and sense-bases; and their being uprooted only by the noble, unsurpassed path—he knows. He [knows] the diversity of rebirths; rebirth according to <s>karma</s>; the establishment of hells, animal births, hungry ghosts, <s>asuras</s>, humans, and gods; rebirth in the form and formless [realms]; rebirth with and without perception; the sprouting of renewed existence through the seeds of consciousness in the darkness of ignorance, watered by the moisture of craving in the field of <s>karma</s>; the congenital undifferentiated nature of name-and-form; the continuity through the longing of craving and the delusion of existence; the unceasing attachment of beings who desire enjoyment, desire becoming, and delight; and the extraction from the perception of grasping in the three realms—he knows. He [knows] the frequented and unfrequented nature of habitual tendencies; the permeation by habitual tendencies according to the connection of their course; the permeation according to the conduct of beings; the permeation according to the practice of <s>karma</s> and defilements; the permeation through the practice of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate <s>dharmas</s>; the permeation through going to renewed existence; the gradual permeation; the permeation of the far-reaching, uninterrupted defilement-attraction, transformation, and non-uprooting; the substantial and insubstantial permeation; and the permeation through seeing, hearing, and living with <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>Tathāgatas</s>—he knows. He knows the determinate-rightness of the group of beings; the determinate-wrongness; the indeterminate nature of both; the determinate-rightness of right view; the determinate-wrongness of wrong view; the indeterminate nature due to the absence of both; the determinate-wrongness of any one of the five heinous acts and wrong views; the determinate-rightness of the five faculties; the determinate-wrongness of the eight wrong [factors]; the determinate-rightness of right [factors]; the non-returning [nature]; the determinate-wrongness through the non-ceasing of the workings of miserliness, envy, and cruelty; the determinate-rightness through the cultivation and gathering of the noble unsurpassed path; and the designation as the indeterminate group through the absence of both—he knows. Thus, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who follows knowledge in this way is said to be established on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Sādhumatī</s>.

body.text: so 'syāṃ sādhumatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthita evaṃ caryāvimātratāṃ sattvānāmajñāya tathaiva mokṣopasaṃhāramupasaṃharati / sa sattvaparipākaṃ prajānāti / sattvavinayaṃ ca ... / śrāvakayānadeśanāṃ ca / pratyekabuddhayānadeśanāṃ ca / bodhisattvayānadeśanāṃ ca / tathāgatabhūmideśanāṃ ca prajānāti / sa evaṃ jñātvā tathatvāya sattvebhyo dharmaṃ deśayati / yathāśayavibhaktito yathānuśayavibhaktito yathendriyavibhaktito
body.translated_text: Established on this <s>bodhisattva</s> stage called <s>Sādhumatī</s> (Good Intelligence), knowing the immeasurability of beings' conduct, he accordingly applies the means of liberation. He knows the ripening of beings, the discipline of beings, the teaching of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle, the teaching of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, the teaching of the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle, and the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s> stage. Having thus known, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings for the purpose of suchness (<s>tathatā</s>), according to their differentiated dispositions, according to their differentiated latent tendencies, according to their differentiated faculties,

body.text: yathādhimuktivibhaktito yathāgocaravibhāgajñānopasaṃhārataḥ sarvagocarajñānānugamanato yathādhātugahanopacārānugamanato yathāgatyupapattikleśakarmavāsanānuvartanato yathārāśivyavasthānānugamanato yathāyānādhimokṣavimuktiprāptito 'nantavarṇarūpakāyasaṃdarśanataḥ sarvalokadhātumanojñasvaravijñāpanataḥ sarvarutaravitaparijñānataḥ sarvapratisaṃvidviniścayakauśalyataśca dharmaṃ deśayati //
body.translated_text: according to their differentiated inclinations, according to the application of knowledge distinguishing their domains of activity, following the knowledge of all domains, following the approach to the depths of their elemental constitutions, following the tendencies of their destinies, births, afflictions, actions, and impressions, following their establishment according to class, according to their attainment of liberation through inclination toward [their respective] vehicles—he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> through displaying bodies of endless colors and forms, through making known with pleasing sounds throughout all world-systems, through complete understanding of all utterances and sounds, and through skill in the determination of all analytical knowledges.

body.text: so 'syāṃ sādhumatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitaḥ san bodhisattvo dharmabhāṇakatvaṃ kārayati, tathāgatadharmakośaṃ ca rakṣati / sa dharmābhāṇakagatimupagato 'pramāṇajñānānugatena kauśalyena catuḥpratisaṃvidabhinirhṛtayā bodhisattvavācā dharmaṃ deśayati / tasya satatasamitamasaṃbhinnāścatasro bodhisattvapratisaṃvido 'nupravartante / katamāścatasraḥ? yaduta dharmapratisaṃvit arthapratisaṃvit niruktipratisaṃvit pratibhānapratisaṃvit //
body.translated_text: Established on this <s>bodhisattva</s> stage called <s>Sādhumatī</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> acts as a preacher of the <s>Dharma</s> and guards the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s treasury of <s>Dharma</s>. Having entered the course of a <s>Dharma</s> preacher, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> with <s>bodhisattva</s> speech accomplished through the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), with skill followed by immeasurable knowledge. The four <s>bodhisattva</s> analytical knowledges operate for him constantly and uninterruptedly. Which four? Namely: analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmapratisaṃvid</s>), analytical knowledge of meaning (<s>arthapratisaṃvid</s>), analytical knowledge of etymology (<s>niruktipratisaṃvid</s>), and analytical knowledge of eloquence (<s>pratibhānapratisaṃvid</s>).

body.text: sa dharmapratisaṃvidā svalakṣaṇaṃ dharmāṇāṃ prajānāti / arthapratisaṃvidā vibhaktiṃ dharmāṇāṃ prajānāti / niruktipratisaṃvidā asaṃbhedadeśanāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prajānāti / pratibhānapratisaṃvidā anuprabandhānupacchedatāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prajānāti //
body.translated_text: Through analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>, he knows the individual characteristics of <s>dharmas</s>. Through analytical knowledge of meaning, he knows the differentiation of <s>dharmas</s>. Through analytical knowledge of etymology, he knows the non-confused teaching of <s>dharmas</s>. Through analytical knowledge of eloquence, he knows the unbroken continuity of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ dharmapratisaṃvidā abhāvaśarīraṃ dharmāṇāṃ prajānāti / arthapratisaṃvidā udayāstagamanaṃ dharmāṇāṃ prajānāti / niruktipratisaṃvidā sarvadharmaprajñaptyacchedanadharmaṃ deśayati / pratibhānapratisaṃvidā yathāprajñaptyavikopanatāparyantatayā dharmaṃ deśayati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, through analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>, he knows the non-existent body of <s>dharmas</s>. Through analytical knowledge of meaning, he knows the arising and passing away of <s>dharmas</s>. Through analytical knowledge of etymology, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> that cuts off all designations of <s>dharmas</s>. Through analytical knowledge of eloquence, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> with the limitlessness of non-disturbance according to designation.

body.text: punaraparaṃ dharmapratisaṃvidā pratyutpannavibhaktiṃ dharmāṇāṃ prajānāti / arthapratisaṃvidā atītānāgatavibhaktiṃ dharmāṇāṃ prajānāti / niruktipratisaṃvidā atītānāgapratyutpannāsaṃbhedato dharmaṃ deśayati / pratibhānapratisaṃvidā ekaikamadhvānamārabhya aparyantadharmālokatayā dharmaṃ deśayati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, through analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>, he knows the differentiation of <s>dharmas</s> in the present. Through analytical knowledge of meaning, he knows the differentiation of <s>dharmas</s> in the past and future. Through analytical knowledge of etymology,

body.text: punaraparaṃ dharmapratisaṃvidā dharmaprabhedaṃ prajānāti / arthapratisaṃvidā arthaprabhedaṃ prajānāti / niruktipratisaṃvidā yathārutadeśanatayā dharmaṃ deśayati / pratibhānapratisaṃvidā yathānuśayajñānaṃ deśayati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, through analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>, he knows the analysis of <s>dharmas</s>. Through analytical knowledge of meaning, he knows the analysis of meanings. Through analytical knowledge of etymology, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> according to the spoken words.

body.text: punaraparaṃ dharmapratisaṃvidā dharmajñānavibhaktyasaṃbhedakauśalyaṃ prajānāti / arthapratisaṃvidā anvayajñānatathātvavyavasthānaṃ prajānāti / niruktipratisaṃvidā saṃvṛtijñānasaṃdarśanāsaṃbhedatayā nirdiśati / pratibhānapratisaṃvidā paramārthajñānakauśalyena dharmaṃ deśayati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, through analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>, he knows the skill of non-confused differentiation of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge. Through analytical knowledge of meaning, he knows the establishment of the suchness of inferential knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>). Through analytical knowledge of etymology,

body.text: punaraparaṃ dharmapratisaṃvidā ekanayāvikopaṃ dharmāṇāṃ prajānāti / arthapratisaṃvidā skandhadhātvāyatanasatyapratītyasamutpādakauśalyānugamamavatarati / niruktipratisaṃvidā sarvajagadabhigamanīyasumadhuragirinirghoṣākṣarairnirdiśati / pratibhānapratisaṃvidā bhūyo bhūyo 'paryantadharmāvabhāsatayā nirdiśati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, through analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>, he knows the non-disturbance of the single method of <s>dharmas</s>. Through analytical knowledge of meaning, he enters the skill in <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, truths, and dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>).

body.text: punaraparaṃ dharmapratisaṃvidā ekayānasamavasaraṇanānātvaṃ prajānāti / arthapratisaṃvidā pravibhaktayānavimātratāṃ prajānāti / niruktipratisaṃvidā sarvayānānyabhedena nirdiśati / pratibhānapratisaṃvidā ekaikaṃ yānamaparyantadharmābhāsena deśayati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, through analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>, he knows the diversity within the convergence into the single vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>). Through analytical knowledge of meaning, he knows the immeasurability of the differentiated vehicles. Through analytical knowledge of etymology,

body.text: punaraparaṃ dharmapratisaṃvidā sarvabodhisattvacarijñānacaridharmacarijñānānugamamavatarati / arthapratisaṃvidā daśabhūmivyavasthānanirdeśapravibhaktimavatarati / niruktipratisaṃvidā yathābhūmimārgopasaṃhārasaṃbhedena nirdiśati / pratibhānapratisaṃvidā ekaikāṃ bhūmimaparyantākāreṇa nirdiśati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, through analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>, he enters the knowledge-following of all <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, <s>dharma</s>-conduct, and knowledge-conduct. Through analytical knowledge of meaning, he enters the detailed exposition of the establishment of the ten stages (<s>daśabhūmi</s>).

body.text: punaraparaṃ dharmapratisaṃvidā sarvatathāgataikalakṣaṇānubodhamavatarati / arthapratisaṃvidā nānākālavastulakṣaṇavibhaṅgānugamaṃ prajānāti / niruktipratisaṃvidā yathābhisaṃbodhiṃ vibhaktinirdeśena nirdiśati / pratibhānapratisaṃvidā ekaikaṃ dharmapadamaparyantakalpāvyavacchedena nirdiśati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, through analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>, he enters the awakening to the single characteristic of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>.
