Through analytical knowledge of meaning, he knows the following of the analysis of characteristics according to various times and objects. Through analytical knowledge of etymology,

body.text: punaraparaṃ dharmapratisaṃvidā sarvatathāgatavāgbalavaiśarādyabuddhadharmamahākaruṇāpratisaṃvitprayogadharmacakrānupravartamānasarvajñajñānānugamaṃ prajānāti / arthapratisaṃvidā caturaśītisattvacaritasahasrāṇāṃ yathāśayaṃ yathendriyaṃ yathādhimuktivibhaktitastathāgataghoṣaṃ prajānati / niruktipratisaṃvidā sarvasattvacaryāsaṃbhedatastathāgataghoṣānuraveṇa nirdiśati / pratibhānapratisaṃvidā tathāgatajñānaprabhācaryāmaṇḍalādhimukttyā dharmaṃ deśayati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, through analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>, he knows the application of the <s>Dharma</s> teaching of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>' powers of speech, confidences, <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, great compassion, analytical knowledges, and <s>Dharma</s>-wheel, following the path of omniscient knowledge (<s>sarvajñajñāna</s>).

body.text: sa evaṃ pratisaṃvidā jñānābhinirhārakuśalo bho jinaputra bodhisattvo navamīṃ bodhisattvabhūmimanuprāptastathāgatadharmakośaprāpto mahādharmabhāṇakatvaṃ ca kurvāṇaḥ arthavatīdhāraṇīpratilabdhaśca bhavati / dharmavatī ... / jñānābhinirhāravatī ... / avabhāsavatī ... / vasumatīdhāraṇī ... / sumatidhāraṇī ... / tejodhāraṇī ... / asaṅgamukhadhāraṇī ... / ananta ... / vicitrārthakośa ... / sa evamādīnāṃ dhāraṇīpadānāṃ paripūrṇāni daśadhāraṇīmukhāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇi pratilabhate / tathā asaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrānugatenaiva svarāṅgakauśalyena tāvadapramāṇānugatenaiva pratibhānavibhaktimukhena dharmaṃ deśayati / sa evamapramāṇairdhāraṇīmukhāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrairdaśasu dikṣu aprameyāṇāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sakāśāddharmaṃ śṛṇoti / śrutvā ca na vismārayati / yathāśrutaṃ ca apramāṇavibhaktita evaṃ nirdiśati //
body.translated_text: Skilled in the accomplishment of knowledge through analytical knowledges, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who has attained the ninth <s>bodhisattva</s> stage, having obtained the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s treasury of <s>Dharma</s> and performing the great preaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, obtains the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of meaning (<s>arthavatī</s>), the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmavatī</s>), the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of knowledge-accomplishment, the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of illumination (<s>avabhāsavatī</s>), the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of wealth (<s>vasumatī</s>), the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of good understanding (<s>sumatī</s>), the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of radiance (<s>tejas</s>), the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of the unobstructed gateway (<s>asaṅgamukha</s>), the infinite (<s>dhāraṇī</s>), and the treasury of varied meanings. He thus obtains a full ten times innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>dhāraṇī</s> gateways. With that same skill in voice and articulation followed by innumerable hundreds of thousands, and with that same immeasurably followed gateway of eloquent discourse, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>. With these immeasurable innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>dhāraṇī</s> gateways, he hears the <s>Dharma</s> from immeasurable <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavats</s> in the ten directions. Having heard it, he does not forget it. And as he has heard it, he expounds it with immeasurable analysis.

body.text: sa ekasya tathāgatasya sakāśāddaśabhirdhāraṇīmukhāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrairdharmān paryavāpnoti / yathā caikasya, evamaparyantānāṃ tathāgatānām / sa praṇidhānamātreṇa bahutaraṃ samyaksaṃbuddhasakāśāddharmamukhālokaṃ saṃpratīcchati, na tveva mahābāhuśrutyaprāptaḥ śrāvakaḥ śrutodgrahaṇadhāraṇīpratilabdhaḥ kalpaśatasahasrodgrahaṇādhiṣṭhānena / sa evaṃ dhāraṇīprāptaśca bhavati pratibhānaprāptaśca dharmasāṃkathyaṃ saṃniṣaṇṇaḥ sarvāvatīṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuṃ spharitvā yathāśayavibhaktitaḥ sattvebhyo dharmaṃ deśayati dharmāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ / dharmāsanaṃ cāsya tathāgatānabhiṣekabhūmiprāptān bodhisattvān sthāpayitvā sarvato viśiṣṭamapramāṇāvabhāsaprāptaṃ bhavati / sa dharmāsane niṣaṇṇa ākāṅkṣan ekaghoṣodāhāreṇa sarvaparṣadaṃ nānāghoṣarutavimātratayā saṃjñāpayati / ākāṅkṣan nānāghoṣanānāsvarāṅgavibhaktibhirājñāpayati / ākāṅkṣan raśmimukhopasaṃhārairdharmamukhāni niścārayati / ākāṅkṣan sarvaromakūpebhyo ghoṣānniścārayati / ākāṅkṣan yāvattrisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau rūpāvabhāsāstebhyaḥ sarvarūpāvabhāsebhyo dharmarutāni niścārayati / ākāṅkṣan ekasvararutena sarvadharmadhātuṃ vijñāpayati / ākāṅkṣan sarvarutanirghoṣeṣu dharmarutamadhitiṣṭhati / ākāṅkṣan
body.translated_text: From a single <s>Tathāgata</s>, he comprehends the <s>Dharma</s> through ten times innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>dhāraṇī</s> gateways. And as with one, so with boundless <s>Tathāgatas</s>. By the mere power of his vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), he receives a greater illumination of <s>Dharma</s> gateways from perfectly awakened ones than even a great learned <s>śrāvaka</s> who has obtained the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of hearing and retention could receive through the sustaining power of a hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s> of retention. Having thus attained <s>dhāraṇī</s> and eloquence, seated for <s>Dharma</s> discourse, pervading the entire great trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s>), he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings according to their differentiated dispositions, seated on the <s>Dharma</s> throne. His <s>Dharma</s> throne, except for <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have attained the stage of <s>Tathāgata</s> consecration, surpasses all others, having attained immeasurable illumination. Seated on the <s>Dharma</s> throne, if he wishes, with a single utterance he makes the entire assembly understand through the diversity of various sounds and utterances. If he wishes, he instructs through the differentiation of various sounds and voice-articulations. If he wishes, he brings forth <s>Dharma</s> gateways through the application of rays of light. If he wishes, he brings forth sounds from every pore. If he wishes, from all the visible illuminations throughout the great trichiliocosm, he brings forth <s>Dharma</s> sounds from all those visible illuminations. If he wishes, with a single vocal sound he makes known the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>. If he wishes, he sustains the <s>Dharma</s> sound in all utterances and resonances. If he wishes,

body.text:
sarvalokadhātuparyāpannebhyo gītāvādyatūryaśabdebhyo dharmarutaṃ niścārayati / ākāṅkṣan ekākṣararutātsarvadharmapadaprabhedarutaṃ niścārayati / ākāṅkṣan anabhilāpyānabhilāpyalokadhātvaparyantataḥ pṛthivyaptejovāyuskandhebhyaḥ sūkṣmaparamāṇurajaḥprabhedata ekaikaparamāṇurajonabhilāpyāni dharmamukhāni niścārayati / sacettaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuparyāpannaḥ sarvasattvā upasaṃkramya ekakṣaṇalavamuhūrtena praśnān paripṛccheyuḥ, ekaikaśca teṣāmapramāṇarutavimātratayā paripṛcchet, yaṃ caikaḥ sattvaḥ paripṛcchenna taṃ dvitīyaḥ, taṃ bodhisattvaḥ sarvasattvarutapadavyañjanamudgṛhṇiyāt / udgṛhya caikarutābhivyāhāreṇa teṣāṃ sarvasattvānāṃ cittāśayān paritoṣayet (yāvadanabhilāpyalokadhāturpayāpannā vā sattvā upasaṃkramya ekakṣaṇalavamuhūrtena praśnān paripṛccheyuḥ, ekaikaśca teṣāmapramāṇarutavimātratayā paripṛcchet, yaṃ caikaḥ paripṛcchenna taṃ dvitīyaḥ, taṃ bodhisattva ekakṣaṇalavamuhūrtenaiva sarvamudgṛhya ekodāhāreṇaiva sarvānājñāpayet / yāvadanabhilāpyānapi lokadhātūn spharitvā yathāśayendriyādhimuktitaḥ sattvebhyo dharmaṃ deśayati / dharmasāṃkathyaṃ niṣaṇṇaśca tathāgatādhiṣṭhānasaṃpratyeṣakaḥ sakalena buddhakāryeṇa sarvasattvānāṃ pratyupasthito bhavati / sa bhūyasyā mātrayā evaṃ jñānāvabhāsapragrahaṇamārabhate / sacedekasmin vālāgraprasare yāvantyanabhilāpyeṣu lokadhātuṣu paramāṇurajāṃsi tāvantastathāgatāstāvadapramāṇaprāpteṣveva parṣanmaṇḍaleṣu dharmaṃ deśayeyuḥ / ekaikaśca tathāgatastāvadapramāṇaprāptebhyaḥ sarvasattvebhyo nānātvato dharmaṃ deśayet,
ekaikasmiṃśca sattvāśayasaṃtāne tāvadapramāṇameva dharmopasaṃhāramupasaṃharet / yathā caikastathāgataḥ parṣanmaṇḍale tathā te sarve tathāgatāḥ / yathā caikasmin vālāgraprasare tathā sarvasmin dharmadhātau / tatrāsmābhistādṛśaṃ smṛtivaipulyamabhinirhartavyaṃ yathaikakṣaṇena sarvatathāgatānāṃ sakāśāddharmāvabhāsaṃ pratyeṣemahi ekarutāvyatirekāt / yāvanti ca tāni yathāparikīrtitāni parṣanmaṇḍalāni nānānikāyadharmapravaṇaikaparipūrṇāni, tatrāsmābhistādṛśaṃ prajñāvabhāsaviniścayapratibhānaṃ pariśodhyaṃ yadekakṣaṇena sarvasattvān paritoṣayet, kiṃ punariyatsu lokadhātuṣu sattvāni //
body.translated_text: from all the sounds of songs, music, and instruments throughout all world-systems, he brings forth the sound of <s>Dharma</s>. If he wishes, from a single syllable-sound he brings forth the sound of the analysis of all <s>Dharma</s> words. If he wishes, throughout inexpressibly inexpressible boundless world-systems, from the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, and the aggregates, through the analysis of subtle atomic particles, from each and every atomic particle he brings forth inexpressible <s>Dharma</s> gateways. If all the beings contained in this great trichiliocosm were to approach and ask questions in a single instant, moment, and <s>muhūrta</s>, and each of them were to ask with immeasurable diversity of speech, and what one being asks another does not ask—the <s>bodhisattva</s> would comprehend the words, syllables, and speech-sounds of all those beings, and having comprehended them, with a single utterance he would satisfy the mental dispositions of all those beings. Even if the beings contained in inexpressible world-systems were to approach and ask questions in a single instant—and each with immeasurable diversity of speech, and what one asks another does not—the <s>bodhisattva</s>, having comprehended everything in a single instant, would instruct them all with a single utterance. Pervading even inexpressible world-systems, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings according to their dispositions, faculties, and inclinations. Seated for <s>Dharma</s> discourse, sustained by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s blessing, he stands ready for all beings with the complete work of a <s>Buddha</s>. To a greater degree he undertakes the apprehension of such knowledge-illumination: if on the tip of a single hair, as many <s>Tathāgatas</s> as there are atomic particles in inexpressible world-systems were to teach the <s>Dharma</s> in equally immeasurable assemblies, and each <s>Tathāgata</s> were to teach the <s>Dharma</s> diversely to equally immeasurable beings, and upon each stream of a being's disposition were to apply equally immeasurable <s>Dharma</s>—as one <s>Tathāgata</s> in one assembly, so all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>; and as on one hair-tip, so throughout the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>—'We must accomplish such vastness of mindfulness that in a single instant we would receive the <s>Dharma</s>-illumination from all <s>Tathāgatas</s> without exception from a single utterance. And in however many assemblies as have been described, each filled with diverse <s>Dharma</s> teachings of various traditions, we must purify such illumination of wisdom, determination, and eloquence that in a single instant it would satisfy all beings—how much more so the beings in this many world-systems!'

body.text: sa imāṃ sādhumatīṃ bodhisattvabhūmimanuprāpto bodhisattvo bhūyasyā mātrayā rātriṃdivamananyamanasikāraprayukto bhūtvā buddhagocarānupraviṣṭastathāgatasamavadhānaprāpto gambhīrabodhisattvavimokṣānuprāpto bhavati / sa evaṃjñānānugato bodhisattvaḥ samāhitastathāgatadarśanaṃ na vijahāti / ekaikāsmiṃśca kalpe 'nekān buddhān, anekāni buddhaśatāni ... anekāni buddhakoṭinayutaśatasahasrāṇi ... / dṛṣṭvā ca satkaroti gurukaroti mānayati pūjayati / audārikena buddhadarśanena pūjopasthānaṃ notsṛjati / tāṃśca tathāgatān praśnān paripṛcchati / sa dharmadharaṇīnirdeśābhinirjāto bhavati / tasya bhūyasyā mātrayā tāni kuśalamūlānyuttaptatamānyasaṃhāryāṇi bhavanti / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputrāstadeva jātarūpamābharaṇīkṛtaṃ supariniṣṭhitaṃ kuśalena karmāreṇa rājñaścakravartina uttamāṅge kaṇṭhe vā ābaddhamasaṃhārya bhavati sarvakoṭṭarājānāṃ cāturdvipakānāṃ ca sattvānāmābharaṇavikṛtaiḥ, evameva bho jinaputrā bodhisattvasya asyāṃ sādhumatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya tāni kuśalamūlāni mahājñānālokasuvibhaktānyuttapyante,
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has reached this <s>Sādhumatī</s> (Good Intelligence) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, to an even greater degree, day and night engaged without any other mental attention, enters the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>, attains the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and reaches the profound <s>Bodhisattva</s> liberations. That <s>Bodhisattva</s>, thus following knowledge, while concentrated, does not abandon the vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. In each <s>kalpa</s>, he sees many <s>Buddhas</s>, many hundreds of <s>Buddhas</s>... many <s>koṭi-nayuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>... Having seen them, he honors, reveres, esteems, and worships them. Through the superior vision of the <s>Buddha</s>, he does not abandon worship and service. He questions those <s>Tathāgatas</s> with inquiries. He becomes one accomplished in the exposition of <s>dhāraṇīs</s> of the <s>Dharma</s>. To an even greater degree, those wholesome roots of his become most refined and indestructible. Just as, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, that same refined gold, fashioned into an ornament well-completed by a skilled goldsmith, when bound upon the head or neck of a <s>Cakravartin</s> king, becomes indestructible by the ornamental crafts of all subordinate kings and of beings on the four continents—even so, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the wholesome roots of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> standing on this <s>Sādhumatī</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage become refined, well-differentiated by the great light of knowledge,

body.text: asaṃhāryāṇi bhavanti sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhairadharabhūmisthitaiśca bodhisattvaiḥ / tasya sā kuśalamūlābhā sattvānāṃ kleśacittagahanānyavabhāsya tata eva vyāvartate / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputrā dvisāhasriko mahābrahmā sarvasmin dvisāhasrike lokadhātau gahananimnopacārānavabhāsayati, evameva bho jinaputrā bodhisattvasya asyāṃ sādhumatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya sā kuśalamūlābhā sattvānāṃ kleśacittagahanānyavabhāsya tata eva vyāvartate / tasya daśabhyaḥ pāramitābhyo balapāramitā atiriktatamā bhavati, na ca pariśeṣāsu na samudācarati yathābalaṃ yathābhajamānam / iyaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasya sādhumatī nāma navamī bodhisattvabhūmiḥ ... mahābrahmā bhavati mahābalasthāmaprāpto dvisāhasrādhipatirabhibhūḥ ... pāramitopadeśeṣvasaṃhāryaḥ sattvāśayaparipṛcchānirdeśaiḥ / yacca kiṃcit ... //
body.translated_text: indestructible by all <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> standing on lower stages. That radiance of his wholesome roots illuminates the dense thickets of the afflicted minds of beings, and then turns back from there. Just as, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the great <s>Brahmā</s> of the two-thousandfold [world-system] illuminates the dense and low-lying places in the entire two-thousandfold world-system—even so, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the radiance of the wholesome roots of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> standing on this <s>Sādhumatī</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage illuminates the dense thickets of the afflicted minds of beings, and then turns back from there. Of the ten <s>pāramitās</s>, the perfection of power (<s>balapāramitā</s>) is foremost for him, yet he does not cease to practice the remaining ones according to his ability and as appropriate. This, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s ninth <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage called <s>Sādhumatī</s>... He becomes a great <s>Brahmā</s>, endowed with great power and might, lord of the two-thousandfold [world-system], supreme... indestructible in the instructions of the <s>pāramitās</s>, through his expositions that inquire into the aspirations of beings. And whatever...

body.text: sādhumatī nāma navamī bhūmiḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth stage called <s>Sādhumatī</s>.

body.text: 10 dharmameghā nāma daśamī bhūmiḥ /
body.translated_text: 10. The tenth stage called <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of <s>Dharma</s>).

body.text: vajragarbho bodhisattva āha - yo 'yaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattva evamapramāṇajñeyavicāritayā buddhyā yāvannavamī bodhisattvabhūmiriti suvicitavicayaḥ suparipūrṇaśukladharmaḥ paryantasaṃbhāropacayopacitaḥ suparigṛhītamahāpuṇyajñānasaṃbhāraḥ mahākaruṇāvaipulyādhigataḥ lokadhātuvibhaktivaimātryakovidaḥ sattvadhātupraviṣṭagahanopacāraḥ tathāgatagocarapraveśānugatasaṃjñāmanasikāraḥ balavaiśāradyabuddhadharmādhyālambanānugataḥ sarvākārasarvajñajñānābhiṣekabhūmiprāpta ityucyate //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s> said: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, who has thus with intelligence that investigates immeasurable objects of knowledge, up to the ninth <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, well-investigated and well-examined, with well-fulfilled bright qualities, accumulated through the accumulation of the utmost provisions, with well-received great stores of merit and knowledge, endowed with the abundance of great compassion, skilled in the variety and immensity of world-realms, who has entered the dense thickets of the realm of beings, whose perception and mental attention follow entry into the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who follows reliance upon the powers, fearlessnesses, and <s>Buddha</s>-qualities—he is said to have reached the stage of consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) for the omniscient knowledge in all its aspects.'

body.text: tasya khalu punarbhavanto jinaputrā evaṃjñānānugatasya bodhisattvasya abhiṣekabhūmisamāpannasya vimalo nāma samādhirāmukhībhavati / dharmadhātuvibhaktipraveśaśca nāma / bodhimaṇḍālaṃkāravyūhaśca nāma / sarvākāraraśmikusumaśca nāma / sāgaragarbhaśca nāma / sāgarasamṛddhiśca nāma / ākāśadhātuvipulaśca nāma / sarvadharmasvabhāvavicayaśca nāma / sarvasattvacittacaritānugataśca nāma / pratyutpannasarvabuddhasaṃmukhāvasthitaśca nāma bodhisattvasamādhirāmukhībhavati / tasaivaṃpramukhāni daśa samādhyasaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇyāmukhībhavanti / sa tān sarvān samādhīn samāpadyate ca vyuttiṣṭhate ca, samādhikauśalyānugataśca yāvatsamādhikāryaṃ tatsarvaṃ pratyanubhavati / tasya yāvaddaśasamādhyasaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇāṃ paryante sarvajñajñānaviśeṣābhiṣekavānnāma bodhisattvasamādhirāmukhībhavati //
body.translated_text: For that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, thus following knowledge and having reached the stage of consecration, there appears the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called 'Stainless,' and [the <s>samādhi</s>] called 'Entry into the Analysis of the <s>Dharma</s>-realm,' and 'Array and Adornment of the Seat of Awakening,' and 'Flowers of Rays of All Aspects,' and 'Ocean-womb,' and 'Ocean-abundance,' and 'Vastness of the Space-realm,' and 'Examination of the Own-nature of All <s>Dharmas</s>,' and 'Following the Course of the Minds of All Beings,' and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called 'Standing in the Presence of All Present <s>Buddhas</s>.' Led by these, innumerable ten hundreds of thousands of <s>samādhis</s> appear to him. He enters and arises from all those <s>samādhis</s>, and following the skill in <s>samādhi</s>, he experiences whatever is the function of <s>samādhi</s>. At the end of those innumerable ten hundreds of thousands of <s>samādhis</s>, there appears the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called 'Consecration into the Distinction of Omniscient Knowledge.'

body.text: yasmin samanantarābhimukhībhūte daśatrisāhasraśatasahasrāparyantapramāṇaṃ mahāratnarājapadmaṃ prādurbhavati sarvākārararatnapratyarpitaṃ sarvalokaviṣayasamatikrāntaṃ lokottarakuśalamūlasaṃbhūtaṃ māyāsvabhāvagocarapariniṣpannaṃ dharmadhātusuvyavasthitāvabhāsaṃ divyaviṣayasamatikrāntaṃ mahāvaiḍūryamaṇiratnadaṇḍamatulyacandanarājakarṇikaṃ mahāśmagarbhakesaraṃ jāmbūnadasuvarṇāvabhāsapatramaparimitaraśmisaṃkusumitaśarīraṃ sarvapravararatnapratyuptagarbhamaparyantamahāratnajālasaṃchannaṃ paripūrṇadaśatrisāhasraśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamamahāratnapadmaparivāram / tadanugatastadanurūpaśca tasya bodhisattvasya kāyaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate / sa tasya sarvajñajñānaviśeṣābhiṣekavataḥ samādheḥ sahapratilambhāttasminmahāratnarājapadme niṣaṇṇaḥ saṃdṛśyate / samanantaraniṣaṇṇaśca sa bodhisattvastasmin mahāratnarājapadme, atha yāvanti tasya mahāratnarājapadmasya mahāpadmāni parivāraḥ prādurbhūtaḥ, tāvanto bodhisattvā daśadiglokadhātusaṃnipatitāstaṃ bodhisattvamanuparivārya teṣu mahāratnapadmeṣu niṣīdanti / ekaikaśca teṣāṃ daśa samādhiśatasahasrāṇi samāpadyate tameva bodhisattvaṃ nirīkṣamāṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: Immediately upon this [<s>samādhi</s>] appearing, a great jewel-king lotus arises, measuring ten times a hundred thousand three-thousandfold [world-systems], set with jewels of all aspects, transcending the domain of all worlds, born from supramundane wholesome roots, accomplished in the domain of the nature of illusion, illuminating the well-established <s>Dharma</s>-realm, transcending the divine domain, with a stem of great <s>vaiḍūrya</s> gem-jewel, an incomparable pericarp of the king of sandalwood, stamens of great emerald jewels, petals radiant with <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold, a body blossoming with immeasurable rays, a womb set with all the best jewels, covered with a boundless net of great jewels, with an attendant retinue of great jewel-lotuses equal in number to the atoms in ten times a hundred thousand three-thousandfold [world-systems]. The body of that <s>Bodhisattva</s> stands corresponding to and conforming with it. Upon that <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s simultaneous attainment of the <s>samādhi</s> called 'Consecration into the Distinction of Omniscient Knowledge,' he is seen seated on that great jewel-king lotus. As soon as that <s>Bodhisattva</s> is seated on that great jewel-king lotus, as many great lotuses as there are in the retinue of that great jewel-king lotus—that many <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have gathered from the world-realms of the ten directions sit down on those great jewel-lotuses, surrounding that <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Each of them enters ten hundred thousand <s>samādhis</s>, gazing upon that <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: samanantarasamāpanne ca tasmin bodhisattve teṣu ca bodhisattveṣu niravaśeṣam, atha sarvalokadhātusaṃprakampanaṃ bhavati / sarvāpāyapratiprasrambhaṇaṃ ca, sarvadharmadhātvavabhāsakaraṇaṃ ca, sarvalokadhātupariśodhanaṃ ca, sarvabuddhakṣetranāmadheyarutānanuravaṇaṃ ca, sarvasabhāgacaritabodhisattvasaṃnipātanaṃ
body.translated_text: As soon as that <s>Bodhisattva</s> and those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have completely entered [<s>samādhi</s>], there is a trembling of all world-realms, a pacification of all evil destinies, an illumination of the entire <s>Dharma</s>-realm, a purification of all world-realms, a resounding of the names of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, a gathering of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of similar conduct,

body.text:
ca sarvalokadhātudevamanuṣyatūryasaṃgītisaṃpravādanaṃ ca sarvasattvasukhasaṃjananaṃ ca sarvasamyaksaṃbuddhācintyapūjopasthānapravartanaṃ ca sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalavijñāpanaṃ ca bhavati / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi bho jinaputrāstasya bodhisattvasya samanantaraniṣaṇṇasya tasmin mahāratnarājapadme adhastāccaraṇatalābhyāṃ daśaraśmyasaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇi niścaranti / niścarya daśadiśamavīciparyantān mahānirayānavabhāsayanti / nairayikānāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvaduḥkhāni pratiprasrambhayati / jānumaṇḍalābhyāṃ daśa ... daśadiśaṃ sarvatiryagyonibhavanānyavabhāsayanti, sarvatiryagyoniduḥkhāni ca praśamayanti / nābhimaṇḍalād daśa ... sarvayamalokabhavanāni avabhāsayanti, sarvayamalaukikānāṃ sattvānāṃ duḥkhāni ca praśamayanti / vāmadakṣiṇābhyāṃ pārśvābhyāṃ ... manuṣyāśrayān ... manuṣya ... / ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ devāsurabhavanāni ... devāsura ... / aṃsābhyāṃ ... śrāvakayānīyāśrayānavabhāsayanti, dharmālokamukhaṃ copasaṃharanti / pṛṣṭhato grīvāyāśca ... pratyekabuddhāśrayānavabhāsayanti, śāntisamādhimukhanayaṃ copasaṃharanti / mukhadvārād ... prathamacittopādamupādāya yāvannavamīṃ bhūmimanuprāptān bodhisattvānavabhāsayanti, prajñopāyakauśalyanayaṃ copasaṃharanti / ūrṇākośāddaśaraśmyasaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇi niścaranti, niścarya daśasu dikṣu sarvamārabhavanānyavabhāsya dhyāmīkṛtya abhiṣekabhūmiprāptān bodhisattvān avabhāsya tatkāyeṣvevāstaṃ gacchanti / uparyuttamāṅgāt paripūrṇadaśatrisāhasrāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamā raśmayo niścaranti, niścarya daśasu dikṣu dharmadhātupramāṇānyākāśadhātuparyavasānāni sarvatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalānyavabhāsya daśākāraṃ lokaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya uparikhagapathe sthitvā mahāraśmijālamaṇḍalāni
kṛtvā uttaptaprabhāsaṃ nāma mahattathāgatapūjopasthānaṃ sarvatathāgatānāmanupravartayanti / tasya pūjopasthānasya prathamacittotpādamupādāya yāvannavamībhūmyanupravartitam tathāgatapūjopasthānaṃ ... / tataḥ khalvapi mahāraśmijālamaṇḍalādyāvatī daśasu dikṣu niravaśeṣasarvadharmadhātvantargatā puṣpaprajñaptirvā gandhadhūpamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāvastrābharaṇamaṇiratnaprajñaptirvā, tato 'tiriktatarāḥ sarvalokaviṣayasamatikrāntā lokottarakuśalamūlasaṃbhārādhipatyābhinirvṛttāḥ sarvākāraguṇasaṃpannā acintyanirvāṇādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitā nānāvyūhamahāratnavarṣā iva ekaikatathāgataparṣanmaṇḍale mahāmeghā ivābhipravarṣanti sma / tāṃ ca ye sattvāḥ pūjāṃ saṃjānante, te sarve niyatā bhavantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / evaṃrūpaṃ pūjopasthānaṃ pravartya tā raśmayaḥ punareva sarvāvanti tathāgataparṣanmaṇḍalānyavabhāsya daśākāraṃ lokaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya teṣāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmadhastātkramataleṣu astaṃ gacchanti / tatasteṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ teṣāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ viditaṃ bhavati - amuṣmin lokadhātuprasare evaṃcaryānugato bodhisattvo 'bhiṣekakālaprāpta iti / tatra bho jinaputrā daśabhyo digbhyo 'paryantebhyo lokadhātuprasarebhyo 'prameyāsaṃkhyeyāparyantā bodhisattvā yāvannavamībodhisattvabhūmipratiṣṭhitā āgatya taṃ bodhisattvamanuparivārya mahatīṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā tameva bodhisattvaṃ
body.translated_text: a playing and sounding of divine and human musical instruments in all world-realms, a generation of happiness for all beings, a setting in motion of the inconceivable worship and service of all Perfectly Enlightened Ones, and an announcement to all the assembly-circles of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. For what reason? For indeed, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, from the soles of the feet of that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as soon as he is seated on that great jewel-king lotus, innumerable ten hundreds of thousands of rays issue forth, and having issued forth, illuminate the great hells down to <s>Avīci</s> in the ten directions, and pacify all the sufferings of beings in the hells. From his kneecaps, ten [rays]... illuminate all the abodes of the animal realm in the ten directions and pacify all sufferings of the animal realm. From his navel-circle, ten... illuminate all the abodes of the world of <s>Yama</s> and pacify the sufferings of all beings in the world of <s>Yama</s>. From his left and right sides... illuminate human abodes... [pacify] human [sufferings]. From both his hands... illuminate the abodes of <s>devas</s> and <s>asuras</s>... [pacify <s>deva</s> and <s>asura</s> sufferings]. From his shoulders... illuminate the abodes of those following the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle and present the gateway of the radiance of the <s>Dharma</s>. From his back and neck... illuminate the abodes of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> and present the method of the <s>samādhi</s> of peace. From the opening of his mouth... illuminate <s>Bodhisattvas</s> from the first generation of the aspiration-mind up to those who have reached the ninth stage, and present the method of the skill in wisdom and means. From his <s>ūrṇā</s>-tuft, innumerable ten hundreds of thousands of rays issue forth, and having issued forth, illuminate all the abodes of <s>Māra</s> in the ten directions, obscuring them, illuminate the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have reached the stage of consecration, and disappear into those very bodies. From above, from his crown, rays equal to the atoms in ten times innumerable hundreds of thousands of three-thousandfold [world-systems] issue forth, and having issued forth, illuminate all the assembly-circles of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the ten directions, as far as the <s>Dharma</s>-realm and extending to the limit of the space-realm, circumambulate the world ten times, stand above in the sky-path, form great arrays of ray-nets, and set in motion the great worship and service of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> called 'Blazing Radiance.' That worship and service follows from the first generation of the aspiration-mind up to the ninth stage... the <s>Tathāgata</s> worship and service [of all previous stages]. From that great ray-net array, whatever offerings of flowers, incense, perfume, garlands, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, cloths, ornaments, gems, and jewels are found within the entire <s>Dharma</s>-realm in all directions without remainder—surpassing those, transcending the domain of all worlds, accomplished through the sovereignty of the accumulation of supramundane wholesome roots, endowed with qualities of all aspects, empowered by the inconceivable foundation of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>—they rain down like great clouds pouring various arrays of great jewel-rains upon each assembly-circle of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And all those beings who perceive that worship become destined for <s>anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). Having thus set in motion such worship and service, those rays again illuminate all the assembly-circles of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, circumambulate the world ten times, and disappear beneath the feet of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones. Then it becomes known to those <s>Tathāgatas</s> and those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: 'In such-and-such a world-realm, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> following such conduct has arrived at the time of consecration.' Thereupon, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, from the ten directions, from world-realms without limit, immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless <s>Bodhisattvas</s> up to those established on the ninth <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage come, surround that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, perform great worship, and gazing upon that very <s>Bodhisattva</s>,

body.text: nirīkṣamāṇā daśa samādhiśatasahasrāṇi samāpadyante / abhiṣekabhūmiprāptānāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ kāyebhyaḥ śrīvatsālaṃkārādvajrasvastikāt sarvamāraśatruvijayo nāmaikaikā mahāraśmirdaśaraśmyasaṃkhyeyaśatasahasraparivārā niścarati, niścarya daśadiśo 'vabhāsya aparyantāni prātihāryāṇi saṃdarśya tasya bodhisattvasya śrīvatsālaṃkāre vajrasvastika evāstaṃ gacchati / samanantarādastamitāyāśca tasyā raśmyāḥ śatasahasraguṇottarā tasya bodhisattvasya balasthāmābhivṛddhiḥ prajñāyate //
body.translated_text: enter ten hundred thousand <s>samādhis</s>. From the bodies of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have reached the stage of consecration, from the <s>śrīvatsa</s>-ornament, from the <s>vajra-svastika</s>, a single great ray called 'Victory Over All <s>Māra</s>-Enemies' issues forth, attended by innumerable ten hundreds of thousands of rays; having issued forth, it illuminates the ten directions, displays boundless miraculous transformations, and disappears into the <s>vajra-svastika</s> of the <s>śrīvatsa</s>-ornament of that <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Immediately upon the disappearance of that ray, the increase of that <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s power and might, a hundred-thousandfold greater, becomes evident.

body.text: atha khalu bho jinaputrāḥ sarvajñatābhijñāvatyo nāma raśmayasteṣāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmūrṇākośebhyo niścarantyasaṃkhyeyaparivārāḥ / tāḥ sarvāsu daśasu dikṣu aśeṣataḥ sarvalokadhātūnavabhāsya daśākāraṃ lokaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya mahānti tathāgatavikurvitāni saṃdarśya bahūni bodhisattvakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi saṃcodya sarvabuddhakṣetraprasarān ṣaḍvikāraṃ saṃprakampya sarvāpāyacyutigatyupapattīḥ praśamya sarvamārabhavanāni dhyāmīkṛtya sarvatathāgatābhisaṃbodhivibuddhabuddhāsanānyupasaṃdarśya sarvabuddhaparṣanmaṇḍalavyūhaprabhāvaṃ nidarśya dharmadhātuparamānākāśadhātuparyavasānān sarvalokadhātūnavabhāsya punarevāgatya taṃ sarvāvantaṃ bodhisattvaparṣatsaṃnipātamuparyuparipradakṣiṇīkṛtya mahāvyuhānnidarśya tā raśmayastasya bodhisattvasyottamāṅge 'staṃ gacchanti / tatparivāraraśmayaśca tathā saṃnipatitānāṃ teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ śirassvantardhīyante sma / samanantarasaṃnipatitābhiśca tābhī raśmibhiste bodhisattvā apratilabdhapūrvāṇi daśa samādhiśatasahasrāṇi pratilabhante / tāśca raśmayastulyakālaṃ tasya bodhisattvasyottamāṅge nipatitā bhavanti / sa ca bodhisattvo 'bhiṣikta ityucyate samyaksaṃbuddhaviṣaye / daśabalaparipūryā tu samyaksaṃbuddha iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputrā yo rājñaścakravartinaḥ putro jyeṣṭhaḥ kumāro 'gryamahiṣīprasūtaścakravartirājalakṣaṇasamanvāgato bhavati, taṃ rājā cakravartī divye hastisauvarṇe bhadrapīṭhe niṣādya, caturbhyo mahāsamudrebhyo vāryānīya, upariratnavimānena dhāryamāṇena mahatā puṣpadhūpagandhadīpamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākātūryatālāvacarasaṃgitivyūhena sauvarṇaṃ bhṛṅgāraṃ gṛhītvā tena vāriṇā taṃ kumāraṃ mūrdhanyabhiṣiñcati / samanantarābhiṣiktaśca rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhabhiṣikta iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati / daśakuśalakarmapathaparipūryā tu cakravartīti saṃjñāṃ pratilabhate / evameva bho jinaputrāḥ samanantarābhiṣikto bodhisattvastairbuddhairbhagavadbhirmahājñānābhiṣekābhiṣikta ityucyate / samyaksaṃbuddhābhiṣekeṇa daśabalaparipūryā tu samyaksaṃbuddha iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati / ayaṃ bho jinaputrā bodhisattvasya mahājñānābhiṣeko yasyārthe bodhisattvo 'nekāni duṣkaraśatasahasrāṇyārabhate / sa evamabhiṣikto 'prameyaguṇajñānavivardhito dharmameghāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhita ityucyate //
body.translated_text: Then indeed, O sons of the Conqueror, rays called 'Endowed with the Superknowledge of Omniscience' (<s>sarvajñatābhijñāvatyaḥ</s>) issue forth from the <s>ūrṇākośa</s> (hair-tuft) of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, accompanied by innumerable retinues. Those rays, illuminating completely all world-realms in all ten directions, circumambulating the ten-fold world, displaying the great miraculous transformations of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, inspiring many <s>koṭī-niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, causing all <s>Buddha</s>-field expanses to quake in six ways, pacifying all descents into the lower realms of rebirth, dimming all the abodes of <s>Māra</s>, revealing the awakening-seats of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> fully awakened to perfect awakening, displaying the splendor of the assembly-circles of all <s>Buddhas</s>, illuminating all world-realms extending to the ultimate limit of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> and the expanse of space—those rays return again, circumambulate above that entire assembled congregation of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, display great arrays, and then set upon the crown of that <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And the retinue-rays likewise disappear into the heads of those assembled <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Immediately upon those rays descending, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> attain a hundred thousand previously unattained <s>samādhis</s>. And those rays simultaneously descend upon the crown of that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and that <s>Bodhisattva</s> is then called 'consecrated' (<s>abhiṣikta</s>) in the domain of the Perfectly Awakened Ones. But through the fulfillment of the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>), he comes to be reckoned a Perfectly Awakened One (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>). Just as, O sons of the Conqueror, the eldest prince of a <s>Cakravartin</s> king, born of the chief queen, endowed with the marks of a <s>Cakravartin</s> king—the <s>Cakravartin</s> king seats him upon a divine golden elephant-throne, and having brought water from the four great oceans, beneath a canopy of jewels held aloft, with a great array of flowers, incense, perfumes, lamps, garlands, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, musical instruments, cymbals, and songs, takes a golden vessel and with that water consecrates the prince upon the crown. Immediately upon consecration, he comes to be reckoned a <s>Kṣatriya</s> king, anointed upon the crown. But through the fulfillment of the ten wholesome courses of action, he obtains the designation '<s>Cakravartin</s>.' Even so, O sons of the Conqueror, immediately upon that <s>Bodhisattva</s> being consecrated by those <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones with the great consecration of knowledge,

body.text: so 'syāṃ dharmameghāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo dharmadhātusamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / kāmadhātusamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / rūpadhātusamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / ārūpyadhātusamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / lokadhātusamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sarvasattvadhātusamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / vijñānadhātusamudāgamaṃ
body.translated_text: He, this <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of Dharma) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, knows as it truly is the origination of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena). He knows as it truly is the origination of the <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm). He knows as it truly is the origination of the <s>Rūpadhātu</s> (form realm). He knows as it truly is the origination of the <s>Ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm). He knows as it truly is the origination of the world-realm. He knows as it truly is the origination of the realm of all beings. He knows as it truly is the origination of the consciousness-realm (<s>vijñānadhātu</s>).

body.text:
ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtadhātusamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / ākāśadhātusamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / bhūtābhūtadeśanāṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / nirvāṇaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / dṛṣṭikleśasamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / lokadhātupravṛttinivṛttisamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / śrāvakacaryāsamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / pratyekabuddhacaryāsamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / bodhisattvacaryāsamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / tathāgatabalavaiśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmarūpakāyadharmakāyasamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sarvākārasarvajñajñānasamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / abhisaṃbodhidharmacakrapravṛttisaṃdarśanasamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / samāsataḥ sarvadharmapraveśavibhaktiniṣtīrṇasamudāgamaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sa evaṃjñānānugatayā buddhyā uttari sattvakāyanirmāṇaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / kleśakāyanirmāṇaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / dṛṣṭikṛtanirmāṇaṃ ca ... lokadhātunirmāṇaṃ ca ... dharmadhātunirmāṇaṃ ca ... śrāvakanirmāṇaṃ ca ... pratyekabuddhanirmāṇaṃ ca ... bodhisattvanirmāṇaṃ ca ... tathāgatanirmāṇaṃ ca ... sarvanirmāṇakalpākalpatāṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca ... dharmādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca ... saṃghādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca ... karmādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca kleśādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca ... kālādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca ... praṇidhānādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca ... pūjādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca ... caryādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca ... kalpādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca ... jñānādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca prajānāti / sa yānīmāni tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ sūkṣmapraveśajñānāni yaduta caryāsūkṣmapraveśajñānaṃ vā, cyutyupapattisukṣmapraveśajñānaṃ vā, janmasūkṣmapraveśajñānaṃ vā, abhiniṣkramaṇasūkṣmapraveśajñānaṃ vā, abhisaṃbodhisūkṣmapraveśajñānaṃ vā,
vikurvaṇasukṣmapraveśajñānaṃ vā, dharmacakrapravartanasūkṣmapraveśajñānaṃ vā, dharmadeśanāsukṣmapraveśajñāna vā, dharmavistarasūkṣmapraveśajñānaṃ vā, āyuḥpramāṇādhiṣṭhānajñānaṃ vā, varṇarūpakāyasaṃdarśanajñānaṃ vā, sarvasattvavinayātikramaṇajñānaṃ vā, sarvalokadhātuspharaṇajñānaṃ vā, sarvasattvacittacaritavyavalokanajñānaṃ vā, ekakṣaṇe tryadhvavyavalokanajñānaṃ vā, pūrvāntāparāntaniravaśeṣajñānaṃ vā, sarvasattvacittacaritanānātvasamantajñānaṃ vā, tathāgatabalavaiśāradyabuddhadharmācintyajñānaṃ vā, tathāgataparinirvāṇajñānaṃ vā, śāsanādhiṣṭhānasaddharmasthitijñānaṃ vā, evaṃpramukhānyaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāni tathāgatānāṃ sukṣmapraveśajñānāni, tāni sarvāṇi yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sa yānīmāni tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ guhyasthānāni yaduta kāyaguhyaṃ vā vāgguhyaṃ vā cittaguhyaṃ vā kālākālavicāraṇāguhyaṃ vā bodhisattvavyākaraṇaguhyaṃ vā sattvasaṃgrahanigrahaguhyaṃ vā vineyotsādanāvasānaguhyaṃ vā yathākālāvavādānuśāsanādhyupekṣaṇaṃ vā yānanānātvavyavasthāpanaguhyaṃ vā sattvacaryendriyavibhaktiguhyaṃ vā sattvakarmakriyāvatāraguhyaṃ vā bodhisattvacaryendriyavibhaktiguhyaṃ vā caryābhisaṃbodhisvabhāvaprabhāvānubodhiguhyaṃ vā svabhāvābhisaṃbodhyadhiṣṭhānaguhyaṃ vā avatārottāraṇaguhyaṃ vā ākarṣaṇasaṃpreṣaṇaguhyaṃ vā sthānacaṃkramaṇaniṣadyāśayyāsanasaṃdarśanaguhyaṃ vā āhāraparibhogakāyopakaraṇapratisevanaguhyaṃ vā bhāṣitatūṣṇīṃbhāvadhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattisaṃdarśanaguhyaṃ vā, evaṃpramukhānyaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāni tathāgatānāṃ
body.translated_text: He knows as it truly is the origination of the conditioned and unconditioned realm. He knows as it truly is the origination of the space-realm (<s>ākāśadhātu</s>). He knows as it truly is the teaching of what is real and unreal. He knows <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as it truly is. He knows as it truly is the origination of views and afflictions. He knows as it truly is the origination of the arising and cessation of world-realms. He knows as it truly is the origination of the conduct of <s>Śrāvakas</s>. He knows as it truly is the origination of the conduct of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. He knows as it truly is the origination of the conduct of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Likewise,

body.text:
guhyasthānāni, tāni sarvāṇi yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sa yānīmāni tathāgatānāṃ kalpapraveśasamavasaraṇajñānāni yaduta ekakalpāsaṃkhyeyakalpasamavasaraṇatā / asaṃkhyeyakalpaikakalpasamavasaraṇatā / saṃkhyeyakalpāsaṃkhyeyakalpasamavasaraṇatā / asaṃkhyeyakalpasaṃkhyeyakalpasamavasaraṇatā / cittakṣaṇakalpasamavasaraṇatā / kalpacittakṣaṇasamavasaraṇatā / kalpākalpasamavasaraṇatā / akalpakalpasamavasaraṇatā / sabuddhakakalpābuddhakakalpasamavasaraṇatā / abuddhakakalpasabuddhakakalpasamavasaraṇatā / atītānāgatakalpapratyutpannakalpasamavasaraṇatā / pratyutpannakalpātītānāgatakalpasamavasaraṇatā / atītakalpānāgatakalpasamavasaraṇatā / anāgatakalpātītakalpasamavasaraṇatā / dīrghakalpahrasvakalpasamavasaraṇatā / hrasvakalpadīrghakalpasamavasaraṇatā / sarvakalpeṣu saṃjñākṛtasamavasaraṇatā / sarvasaṃjñākṛteṣu kalpasamavasaraṇatā / evaṃ pramukhānyaprameyāṇyasaṃkhyeyāni kalpapraveśasamavasaraṇāni, tāni sarvāni yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sa yānīmāni tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmavatārajñānāni yaduta vālapathāvatārajñānaṃ vā paramāṇurajovatārajñānaṃ vā buddhakṣetrakāyābhisaṃbodhyavatārajñānaṃ vā sattvakāyacittābhisaṃbodhyavatārajñānaṃ vā sarvatrānugatābhisaṃbodhyavatārajñānaṃ vā vyatyastacarisaṃdarśanāvatārajñānaṃ vā anulomacarisaṃdarśanāvatārajñānaṃ
vā pratilomacarisaṃdarśanāvatārajñānaṃ cintyācintyalokavijñeyavijñeyaṃ carisaṃdarśanāvatārajñānaṃ vā śrāvakavijñeyapratyekabuddhavijñeyabodhisattvavijñeyatathāgatavijñeyacarisaṃdarśanāvatārajñānaṃ vā, tāni sarvāṇi yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / iti hi bho jinaputrā aprameyaṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ jñānavaipulyamapramāṇamevāsyāṃ bhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasyāvatārajñānam //
body.translated_text: the secret places [of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>]—he knows all of these as they truly are. He knows those knowledges of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> regarding the entry into and convergence of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages)—namely, the convergence of one <s>kalpa</s> and innumerable <s>kalpas</s>; the convergence of innumerable <s>kalpas</s> and one <s>kalpa</s>; the convergence of countable and innumerable <s>kalpas</s>; the convergence of innumerable and countable <s>kalpas</s>; the convergence of a mind-moment and a <s>kalpa</s>; the convergence of a <s>kalpa</s> and a mind-moment; the convergence of a <s>kalpa</s> and a non-<s>kalpa</s>; the convergence of a non-<s>kalpa</s> and a <s>kalpa</s>; the convergence of <s>kalpas</s> with <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>kalpas</s> without <s>Buddhas</s>; the convergence of <s>kalpas</s> without <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>kalpas</s> with <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.text: sa khalu punarbho jinaputrā bodhisattva evamimāṃ bodhisattvabhūmimanugato 'cintyaṃ ca nāma bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ pratilabhate / anāvaraṇaṃ ca nāma viśuddhivicayaṃ ca nāma samantamukhāvabhāsaṃ ca nāma tathāgatakośaṃ ca nāma apratihatacakrānugataṃ ca nāma tryadhvānugataṃ ca nāma dharmadhātugarbhaṃ ca nāma vimuktimaṇḍalaprabhāsaṃ ca nāma aśeṣaviṣayagamaṃ ca nāma bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ pratilabhate / iti hi bho jinaputrā imān daśa bodhisattvavimokṣān pramukhān kṛtvā aprameyāsaṃkhyeyāni bodhisattvavimokṣamukhaśatasahasrāṇi bodhisattvo 'syāṃ daśamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhitaḥ pratilabhate / evaṃ yāvatsamādhiśatasahasrāṇi dhāraṇīśatasahasrāṇi abhijñābhinirhāraśatasahasrāṇi pratilabhate / jñānālokaśatasahasrāṇi vikurvaṇaśatasahasrāṇi prasaṃvinnirhāraśatasahasrāṇi upāyaprajñāvikrīḍitaśatasahasrāṇi gambhīradharmanayapraveśaśatasahasrāṇi mahākaruṇāvegaśatasahasrāṇi bodhisattvavaśitāpraveśaśatasahasrāṇi pratilabhate //
body.translated_text: And furthermore, O sons of the Conqueror, this <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having followed this <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, attains the <s>Bodhisattva</s> liberation (<s>vimokṣa</s>) called 'Inconceivable' (<s>acintya</s>), and [the liberations] called 'Unobstructed' (<s>anāvaraṇa</s>), 'Examination of Purity' (<s>viśuddhivicaya</s>), 'Illumination of Universal Presence' (<s>samantamukhāvabhāsa</s>), 'Treasury of the <s>Tathāgata</s>' (<s>tathāgatakośa</s>), 'Following the Unhindered Wheel' (<s>apratihatacakrānugata</s>), 'Following the Three Times' (<s>tryadhvānugata</s>), 'Womb of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>' (<s>dharmadhātugarbha</s>), 'Radiance of the Sphere of Liberation' (<s>vimuktimaṇḍalaprabhāsa</s>), and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> liberation called 'Reaching All Domains Without Remainder' (<s>aśeṣaviṣayagama</s>). Thus indeed, O sons of the Conqueror, beginning with these ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> liberations, immeasurable and innumerable <s>Bodhisattva</s> liberations [are attained].

body.text: sa evaṃjñānānugatayā buddhyā apramāṇānugatena smṛtikauśalyena samanvāgato bhavati / sa daśabhyo digbhyo 'prameyāṇāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sakāśādekakṣaṇalavamuhūrtenā apramāṇān mahādharmāvabhāsān mahādharmālokān mahādharmameghān sahate saṃpratīcchati svīkaroti
body.translated_text: He, endowed with memory-skill (<s>smṛtikauśalya</s>) following such immeasurable knowledge and intellect, in a single instant, moment, or <s>muhūrta</s>, from <s>Buddhas</s> Blessed Ones in the ten directions, receives, accepts, and takes in immeasurable great illuminations of the <s>Dharma</s>, great lights of the <s>Dharma</s>, great clouds of the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: saṃghārayati / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputrāḥ sāgaranāgarājameghavisṛṣṭo mahānapskandho na sukaro 'nyena pṛthivīpradeśena soḍhuṃ vā saṃpratyeṣituṃ vā svīkartuṃ vā saṃdhārayituṃ vā anyatra mahāsamudrāt, evameva bho jinaputrā ye te tathāgatānāṃ bhagavatāṃ guhyānupraveśā yaduta mahādharmāvabhāsā mahādharmālokā mahādharmāmeghāḥ, te na sukarāḥ sarvasattvaiḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ prathamāṃ bhūmimupādāya yāvannavamībhūmipratiṣṭhitairapi bodhisattvaiḥ, tān bodhisattvo 'syāṃ dharmameghāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitaḥ sarvān sahate saṃpratīcchati svīkaroti saṃdhārayati / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputrā mahāsamudra ekasyāpi mahābhujagendrasya mahāmeghān sahate ... dvayorapi trayāṇāmapi yāvadaparimānāṇāmapi bhujagendrāṇāmekakṣaṇalavamuhūrtenāprameyān mahāmeghān sahate ... / tatkasya hetoḥ? apramāṇavipulavistīrṇatvānmahāsamudrasya / evameva bho jinaputrā asyāṃ dharmameghāyām bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhito bodhisattva ekasyāpi tathāgatasya sakāśādekakṣaṇa ... dvayorapi trayānāmapi yāvadaparimānāṇāmapi tathāgatānāṃ sakāśādekakṣaṇa ... / tata ucyata iyaṃ bhūmirdharmamegheti //
body.translated_text: Just as, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, a great mass of water released from the cloud of the <s>Sāgaranāgarāja</s> (Ocean-Serpent-King) cannot easily be borne, received, accepted, or held by any other region of the earth except the great ocean—even so, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, those secret penetrations of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> and Blessed Ones, namely the great illuminations of <s>Dharma</s>, the great lights of <s>Dharma</s>, the great clouds of <s>Dharma</s>—these cannot easily [be borne] by all beings, all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, nor even by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established from the first <s>bhūmi</s> up to the ninth <s>bhūmi</s>; but the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of <s>Dharma</s>) bears, receives, accepts, and holds them all. Just as, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the great ocean bears the great clouds of even a single great serpent-lord... of two, of three, up to immeasurable serpent-lords, bearing in a single instant, moment, or <s>muhūrta</s> immeasurable great clouds... For what reason? Because of the immeasurable, vast, and extensive nature of the great ocean. Even so, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Dharmameghā</s>, in a single instant... from even one <s>Tathāgata</s>, and from two, three, up to immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, in a single instant... Therefore this <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of <s>Dharma</s>).

body.text: vimukticandro bodhisattva āha - śakyaṃ punarbho jinaputra saṃkhyāṃ kartuṃ kiyatāṃ tathāgatānāmantikebhyo bodhisattvaikakṣaṇa ...? vajragarbho bodhisattva āha - na sukarā bho jinaputra saṃkhyā kartu gaṇanānirdeśena - iyatāṃ tathāgatānāmantikebhyo bodhisattvaikakṣaṇa ... / api tu khalvaupamyaṃ kariṣyāmi / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra daśasu dikṣu daśabuddhakṣetrānabhilāpyakoṭiniyutaśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamāsu lokadhātuṣu yāvat sattvadhātuniravaśeṣayogena saṃvidyate / tata ekaḥ sattvaḥ śrutagrahaṇadhāraṇīpratilabdho bhavettathāgatānāmupasthāyako mahāśrāvako 'gryaḥ śrutadharāṇām / tadyathāpi nāma bhagavato vajrapadmottarasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya mahāvijayo nāma bhikṣurevaṃrūpeṇa śrutakauśalyabalādhānena sa ekaḥ sattvaḥ samanvāgato bhavet / yathā ca sa ekaḥ sattvastathā niravaśeṣāsu sarvāsu lokadhātuṣu te sarve sattvāḥ samanvāgatā bhaveyuḥ / yaccaikenodgṛhītaṃ syānna dvitīyena / tatkiṃ manyase bho jinaputra bahutaraṃ teṣāmaprameyāpramāṇaṃ vā śrutakauśalyaṃ bhavet? vimukticandro bodhisattva āha - bahu bho jinaputra apramāṇaṃ tatteṣāṃ sarvasattvānāṃ śrutakauśalyaṃ bhavet / vajragarbho bodhisattva āha - ārocayāmi te bho jinaputra, prativedayāmi / yaṃ dharmameghāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhito bodhisattva ekakṣaṇalavamuhūrtenaikasyaiva tāvattathāgatasya sakāśāddharmadhātutryadhvakośaṃ nāma mahādharmāvabhāsālokameghaṃ sahate ... / yasya mahādharmāvabhāsālokameghasaṃdhāraṇakauśalyasya tat pūrvakaṃ śrutakauśalyaṃ ... kṣamate / yathā caikasya tathāgatasya sakāśāttathā daśasu dikṣu yāvanti tāsu pūrvikāsu lokadhātuṣu paramāṇurajāṃsi saṃvidyante, tāvatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ tato 'pi bhūya uttari aprameyāṇāṃ tathāgatānāṃ sakāśādekakṣaṇalavamuhūrtena dharmadhātutryadhvakośaṃ nāma mahādharmāvabhāsālokameghaṃ sahate ... / tata ucyata iyaṃ bhūmirdharmamegheti //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vimukticandra</s> said: "Is it possible, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, to reckon from how many <s>Tathāgatas</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s> [receives] in a single instant...?" The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s> said: "It is not easy, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, to state the reckoning by enumeration—from how many <s>Tathāgatas</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in a single instant... But I will make a comparison. Just as, O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, in the ten directions, in world-realms equal in number to the atoms of dust of inexpressible <s>koṭi-niyuta</s> hundreds of thousands of ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields, there exist beings to the full extent of the realm of beings. Among those, let one being be an attendant of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, a great <s>Śrāvaka</s> foremost among those who retain what they have heard, one who has attained the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of retaining what is heard—just like the monk <s>Mahāvijaya</s>, the attendant of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vajrapadmottara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One—let that one being be endowed with such power of mastery in learning. And as that one being, so let all those beings in all those world-realms without remainder be likewise endowed. And what is grasped by one would not be [the same as what is grasped] by the second. What do you think, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>—would the mastery of learning of those immeasurable and incalculable [beings] be great?" The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vimukticandra</s> said: "Great indeed, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, immeasurable would be the mastery of learning of all those beings." The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s> said: "I declare to you, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, I proclaim: what the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Dharmameghā</s>, in a single instant, moment, or <s>muhūrta</s>, from even one <s>Tathāgata</s>, bears [as] the great illumination-light-cloud of <s>Dharma</s> called the 'Treasury of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> and Three Times'... that former mastery of learning does not [even] bear comparison with the mastery of holding that great illumination-light-cloud of <s>Dharma</s>. And just as from one <s>Tathāgata</s>, so in the ten directions, from as many Perfectly Awakened Ones as there are atoms of dust in those former world-realms, and from still more immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s> beyond that, in a single instant, moment, or <s>muhūrta</s>, he bears the great illumination-light-cloud of <s>Dharma</s> called the 'Treasury of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> and Three Times'... Therefore this <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of <s>Dharma</s>)."

body.text: punaraparaṃ bho jinaputra dharmameghāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvaḥ svapraṇidhānabalādhānato mahākṛpākaruṇāmeghaṃ samutthāpya mahādharmāvabhāsagarjanamabhijñāvidyāvaiśāradyavidyudvidyotitaṃ mahāraśmimārutasamīritaṃ mahāpuṇyajñānaghanābhrajālasaṃdarśanaṃ vividhakāyaghanāvartasaṃdarśanaṃ mahādharmanirnādanaṃ namuciparṣadvidrāvaṇamekakṣaṇalavamuhūrtena daśasu dikṣu yāvanti tāsu lokadhātuṣu tāni paramāṇurajāṃsi saṃvidyante tāvanti lokadhātukoṭinayutaśatasahasrāṇi spharitvā tebhyo 'pi bhūyo 'prameyāṇi lokadhātukotinayutaśatasahasrāṇi spharitvā mahāmṛtakuśaladhārābhipravarṣaṇena yathāśayataḥ sattvānāmajñānasamutthitāḥ sarvakleśarajojvālāḥ praśamayati / tata ucyata iyaṃ bhūmirdharmamegheti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Dharmameghā</s>, through the power of his own aspirations, raising the cloud of great compassion, thundering with the great illumination of <s>Dharma</s>, flashing with the lightning of <s>abhijñā</s> (higher knowledges), <s>vidyā</s> (sciences), and fearlessnesses, stirred by the wind of great radiance, displaying the mass of dense clouds of great merit and knowledge, displaying the dense vortex of manifold bodies, resounding the great <s>Dharma</s>, routing the hosts of <s>Namuci</s> (Māra)—in a single instant, moment, or <s>muhūrta</s>, pervading as many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of world-realms as there are atoms of dust in those world-realms in the ten directions, and pervading still more immeasurable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of world-realms beyond that, he quenches all the dust-fires of defilements arisen from ignorance in beings, according to their dispositions, by raining down the great stream of the nectar of wholesomeness. Therefore this <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of <s>Dharma</s>).

body.text: punaraparaṃ bho jinaputra dharmameghāyāṃ bodhisattva ekasyāmapi lokadhātau tuṣitavarabhavanavāsamupādāya cyavanācaṃkramaṇagarbhasthitijanmābhiniṣkramaṇābhisaṃbodhyadhyeṣaṇamahādharmacakrapravartanamahāparinirvāṇabhūmiriti sarvatathāgatakāryamadhitiṣṭhati yathāśayeṣu sattveṣu yathāvaineyikeṣu, evaṃ dvayorapi yāvadyāvanti tāsu lokadhātuṣu paramāṇurajāṃsi saṃvidyante, tato 'pi bhūyo 'prameyeṣu lokadhātukoṭiniyutaśatasahasreṣu tāni paramāṇu ... vaineyikeṣu //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Dharmameghā</s>, even in a single world-realm, presides over the entire work of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>: from dwelling in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, descent, walking about, abiding in the womb, birth, going forth, perfect awakening, being entreated [to teach], turning the great <s>Dharma</s>-wheel, and the great <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>—according to the dispositions and trainability of beings. And in two [world-realms] likewise, up to as many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of world-realms as there are atoms of dust in those world-realms, and in still more immeasurable [world-realms]—according to the trainability [of beings].

body.text:
sa evaṃjñānavaśitāprāptaḥ suviniścitamahājñānābhijña ākāṅkṣan saṃkliṣṭāyā lokadhātoḥ pariśuddhatāmadhitiṣṭhati / pariśuddhāyā lokadhātoḥ saṃkliṣṭatāmadhitiṣṭhati / saṃkṣiptāyā lokadhātorvistīrṇatāmadhitiṣṭhati / vistīrṇāyāḥ saṃkṣiptatāmadhitiṣṭhati / evaṃ vipulamahadgatāpramāṇasūkṣmaudārikavyatyastāvamūrdhamatalādīnāṃ sarvalokadhātūnāṃ vṛṣabhatayānantamabhinirhāramadhitiṣṭhati / ākāṅkṣan ekasmin paramāṇurajasyekāmapi lokadhātuṃ sarvāvatīṃ sacakravālaparikhāmadhitiṣṭhati / tacca paramāṇurajo na vardhayati tāṃ ca kriyāmādarśayati / dve 'pi tisro 'pi catasro 'pi pañcāpi yāvadanabhilāpyāpi lokadhāturekasmin paramāṇurajasi sarvāḥ sacakravālaparikhā adhitiṣṭhati / ākāṅkṣan ekasyāṃ lokadhātau dvilokadhātuvyūhamādarśayati / ākāṅkṣan yāvadanabhilāpyalokadhātuvyūhamādarśayati / ākāṅkṣan ekalokadhātuvyūhaṃ dvayorlokadhātvorādarśayati / yāvadanabhilāpyāsu lokadhātuṣvādarśayati / ākāṅkṣan yāvadanabhilāpyāsu lokadhātuṣu yaḥ sattvadhātustamekasyāṃ lokadhātau saṃdadhāti, na ca sattvān viheṭhayati / ākāṅkṣan ekasyāṃ lokadhātau yāvān sattvadhātustamanabhilāpyāsu lokadhātuṣu saṃdadhāti ... / ākāṅkṣan anabhilāpyalokadhātugatān sattvānekavālapathe saṃdadhāti ... / ākāṅkṣan ekavālapathe ekaṃ sarvabuddhaviṣayavyūhamādarśayati / ākāṅkṣan yāvadanabhilāpyān sarvākārabuddhaviṣayavyūhānādarśayati / ākāṅkṣan yāvantyanabhilāpyāsu lokadhātuṣu paramāṇurajāṃsi tāvata ātmabhāvānekakṣaṇalavamuhūrtena nirmimīte / ekaikasmiṃśca ātmabhāve tāvata eva pāṇīn saṃdarśayati / taiśca pāṇibhirdaśasu dikṣu buddhapūjāyāṃ prayujyate / ekaikena ca pāṇinā gaṅgānadīvālikāsamān puṣpapuṭāṃsteṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ kṣipati / yathā puṣpāṇāmevaṃ gandhānāṃ mālyānāṃ vilepanānāṃ cūrṇānāṃ cīvarāṇāṃ chatrāṇāṃ dhvajānāṃ patākānāmevaṃ sarvavyūhānām / ekaikasmiṃśca kāye tāvantyeva śirāṃsi adhitiṣṭhati
/ ekaikasmiṃśca śirasi tāvatīreva jihvā adhitiṣṭhati / tābhisteṣāṃ
body.translated_text: Having thus attained mastery of knowledge, endowed with well-ascertained great knowledge and <s>abhijñā</s> (higher knowledge), if he wishes, he presides over the purification of an impure world-realm; he presides over making a pure world-realm impure; he presides over expanding a contracted world-realm; he presides over contracting an expanded one. Thus he presides with infinite development over all world-realms—vast, great, immeasurable, subtle, gross, inverted, upside-down, level, and so forth—as a bull [among them]. If he wishes, in a single atom of dust he places even one entire world-realm with its encircling <s>Cakravāla</s> mountains, and he does not enlarge that atom, yet he displays that feat. He places two, three, four, five, up to inexpressible world-realms, all with their encircling <s>Cakravāla</s> mountains, in a single atom. If he wishes, he displays in one world-realm the array of two world-realms; if he wishes, up to the array of inexpressible world-realms. If he wishes, he displays the array of one world-realm in two world-realms, up to in inexpressible world-realms. If he wishes, the entire realm of beings existing in inexpressible world-realms he gathers into one world-realm, without harming beings. If he wishes, the entire realm of beings in one world-realm he distributes into inexpressible world-realms... If he wishes, the beings of inexpressible world-realms he gathers into a single hair-pore... If he wishes, in a single hair-pore he displays the array of one entire <s>Buddha</s>-field; if he wishes, up to inexpressible arrays of <s>Buddha</s>-fields in all aspects. If he wishes, in a single instant, moment, or <s>muhūrta</s>, he creates as many bodies as there are atoms of dust in inexpressible world-realms. In each body he displays just as many hands. With those hands he engages in the worship of <s>Buddhas</s> in the ten directions. With each hand he casts before those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones heaps of flowers equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river. As with flowers, so with perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, pennants—and all [kinds of] arrays. In each body he establishes just as many heads; in each head, just as many tongues. With those [tongues], of those

body.text: buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ varṇaṃ bhāṣate / cittotpāde ca daśadikpharaṇaṃ gacchāti / cittakṣaṇe cāpramāṇā abhisaṃbodhīryāvanmahāparinirvāṇāvyūhānadhitiṣṭhati / apramāṇakāyatāṃ ca trayadhvatāyāmadhitiṣṭhati / svakāye cāpramāṇānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmaprameyān buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhānadhitiṣṭhati / sarvalokadhātusaṃvartavivartavyūhāṃśca svakāye 'dhitiṣṭhati / sarvā vātamaṇḍalīścaikaromakūpādutsṛjati / na ca sattvān viheṭhayati / ākāṅkṣaṃścaikāmapskandhaparyantaṃ lokadhātumadhitiṣṭhati / tasyāṃ ca mahāpadmamadhitiṣṭhati / tasya ca mahāpadmasya prabhāvabhāsavyūhena anantā lokadhātūḥ spharati / tatra ca mahābodhivṛkṣamādarśayati / yāvatsarvākāravaropetaṃ sarvajñānatvaṃ saṃdarśayati / svakāye daśadiṅmaṇividyuccandrasūryaprabhā yāvatsarvāvabhāsaprabhā adhitiṣṭhati / ekamukhavātena caikaikasyā diśaḥ pratidiśamanantā lokadhātūḥ kampayati, na ca sattvānuttrāsayati / daśadiśaṃ ca vātasaṃvartanīṃ tejaḥsaṃvartanīmapsaṃvartanīmadhitiṣṭhati / sarvasattvāṃśca ākāṅkṣan yathābhiprāyaṃ rūpāśrayālaṃkṛtānadhitiṣṭhati / svakāye ca tathāgatakāyamadhitiṣṭhati / tathāgatakāye ca svakāyamadhitiṣṭhati / tathāgatakāye svabuddhakṣetramadhitiṣṭhati / svabuddhakṣetre ca tathāgatakāyamadhitiṣṭhati / iti hi bho jinaputra dharmameghāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhito bodhisattva imāni cānyāni cāprameyāsaṃkhyeyāni ṛddhivikurvaṇakoṭinayutaśatasahasrāṇyādarśayati //
body.translated_text: <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones he proclaims the praise. In a single thought-moment, the [praise] pervades the ten directions. In a single mind-moment, he presides over immeasurable complete awakenings, up to arrays of the great <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>. He presides over immeasurable body-forms throughout the three times. In his own body he presides over the immeasurable arrays of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities of immeasurable <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones. He presides in his own body over the arrays of the formation and dissolution of all world-realms. From a single hair-pore he releases all wind-circles, without harming beings. If he wishes, he presides over a world-realm to the extent of one water-mass. In that he establishes a great lotus. By the radiance, light, and array of that great lotus, he pervades infinite world-realms. There he displays the great <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, up to displaying omniscience endowed with all excellent aspects. In his own body he establishes the radiance of the <s>maṇi</s>-jewel, lightning, moon, and sun of the ten directions, up to the radiance of all illuminations. With the breath of one mouth he shakes infinite world-realms in each and every direction, without terrifying beings. He presides over the wind of dissolution, fire of dissolution, and water of dissolution in the ten directions. If he wishes, he presides over all beings, adorned with form-bases according to their wishes. In his own body he establishes the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; in the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s> he establishes his own body. In the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s> he establishes his own <s>Buddha</s>-field; in his own <s>Buddha</s>-field he establishes the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Thus, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Dharmameghā</s> displays these and other immeasurable and innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of supernatural transformations.

body.text: atha khalu tasyāḥ parṣadaḥ keṣāṃcidbodhisattvānāṃ keṣāṃciddevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaśakrabrahmalokapālamaheśvaraśuddhāvāsānāmetadabhavat - yadi tāvadbodhisattvasyaivamapramāṇa ṛddhyabhisaṃskāragocaraḥ, tathāgatānāṃ punaḥ kiṃrūpo bhaviṣyatīti? atha khalu vimukticandro bodhisattvastasyāḥ parṣadaścittāśayavicāramājñāya vajragarbhaṃ bodhisattvametadavocat - saṃśayitā bateyaṃ bho jinaputra parṣat / sādhu, asyāḥ saṃśayacchityarthaṃ kiṃcinmātraṃ bodhisattvavyūhaprātihāryaṃ saṃdarśaya / atha khalu vajragarbho bodhisattvastasyāṃ velāyāṃ sarvabuddhakṣetrakāyasvabhāvasaṃdarśanaṃ nāma bodhisattvasamādhiṃ samāpadyate / samanantarasamāpanne vajragarbhe bodhisattve sarvabuddhakṣetrakāyasvabhāvasaṃdarśanaṃ bodhisattvasamādhim, atha tāvadeva sā sarvāvatī bodhisattvaparṣat sā ca devanāgayakṣaśuddhāvāsaparṣad vajragarbhasya bodhisattvasya kāyāntarībhūtamātmānaṃ saṃjānīte sma, tatra ca buddhakṣetramabhinirvṛtaṃ saṃjānīte sma / tasmiṃśca buddhakṣetre ye ākāravyūhāste na sukarāḥ paripūrṇayāpi kalpakoṭyā prabhāvayitum / tatra ca bodhivṛkṣaṃ daśatrisāhasraśatasahasraviṣkambhaskandhaṃ paripūrṇatrisāhasrakoṭivipulāpramāṇaviṭapodviddhaśikharaṃ tadanurūpaṃ ca tasmin bodhimaṇḍe siṃhāsanavaipulyaṃ tatra sarvābhijñāmatirājaṃ nāma tathāgataṃ bodhimaṇḍavaragataṃ samapaśyat / iti hi yāvantastatra vyūhāḥ saṃdṛśyante te na sukarāḥ paripūrṇayāpi kalpakoṭyā prabhāvayitum / sa idaṃ mahāprātihāryaṃ saṃdarśya tāṃ sarvāvatīṃ bodhisattvaparṣadaṃ tāṃ ca devanāga ... śuddhāvāsaparṣadaṃ punareva yathāsthāne sthāpayāmāsa / atha khalu sā sarvāvatī parṣadāścaryaprāptā tūṣṇīṃbhūtā tameva vajragarbhaṃ bodhisattvaṃ nidhyāyantī sthitābhūt / atha khalu vimukticandro bodhisattvo vajragarbhaṃ bodhisattvametadavocat - āścaryamidaṃ bho jinaputra,
body.translated_text: Then, among that assembly, some <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, some gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, world-protectors, <s>Maheśvara</s>, and <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> [gods] had this thought: "If the domain of supernatural transformation of even a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is thus immeasurable, what then will that of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> be like?" Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vimukticandra</s>, knowing the reflection of the mental dispositions of that assembly, said this to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s>: "This assembly is doubtful, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>. Please, for the sake of cutting through their doubt, display even a small portion of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s miraculous array." Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s>, at that very moment, entered the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called 'Displaying the Own-Nature of All <s>Buddha</s>-Fields and Bodies.' As soon as <s>Vajragarbha</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s> entered that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s>, that entire <s>Bodhisattva</s> assembly, together with the assembly of gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> [gods], perceived themselves as having entered within the body of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s>, and there they perceived a <s>Buddha</s>-field that had been brought forth. And the aspects of the array in that <s>Buddha</s>-field could not be described even in a full <s>koṭi</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. There they saw a <s>Bodhi</s>-tree whose trunk spanned a hundred thousand times ten <s>trisāhasra</s> (triple-thousand) world-systems, with branches spreading to the full extent of an immeasurable <s>trisāhasra</s> <s>koṭi</s>, with a summit of corresponding proportions; and on that <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening) a lion-throne of corresponding vastness; and there, the <s>Tathāgata</s> called <s>Sarvābhijñāmatirāja</s> (Supreme King of All Higher Knowledges), seated on the excellent <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>. All the arrays visible there could not be described even in a full <s>koṭi</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. Having displayed this great miracle, he restored that entire <s>Bodhisattva</s> assembly, together with the assembly of gods, <s>Nāgas</s>... and <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> [gods], to their original places. Then that entire assembly, struck with wonder, stood silent, gazing at the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s>. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vimukticandra</s> said this to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s>: "How wondrous this is, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>,

adbhutaṃ yāvadacintyopamasya samādhernimeṣavyūhaprabhāvaḥ / tatko nāmāyaṃ bho jinaputra samādhiḥ? vajragarbho bodhisattva āha - sarvabuddhakṣetrakāyasvabhāvasaṃdarśano nāmāyaṃ bho jinaputra samādhiḥ / vimukticandro bodhisattva āha - kaḥ punarbho jinaputra asya samādhergocaraviṣayavyūhaḥ? vajragarbho bodhisattva āha - ākāṅkṣan bho jinaputra bodhisattvo 'sya samādheḥ suparibhāvitatvādgaṅgānadīvālikāsamalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāni daśa buddhakṣetrāṇi svakāye ādarśayet, ato vā bhūya uttari / īdṛśānāṃ bho jinaputra bodhisattvasamādhīnāṃ dharmameghāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito bodhisattvo bahūni śatasahasrāṇi pratilabhate / tena tasya bodhisattvasya yāvad yauvarājyaprāptairapi bodhisattvaiḥ sādhumatībodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhitairna
sukaraḥ kāyaḥ kāyakarma vā jñātum / na sukarā vāgvākkarma vā jñātum / na sukaraṃ mano manaskarma vā jñātum / na sukararddhirjñātum / na sukaraṃ tryadhvavilokitaṃ jñātum / na sukaraḥ samādhigocarānupraveśo jñātum / na sukaro jñānaviṣayo jñātum / na sukaraṃ vimokṣavikrīḍitaṃ jñātum / na sukaraṃ nirmāṇakarma vā adhiṣṭhānakarma vā prabhākarma vā prabhākarma vā jñātum / na sukaraṃ yāvatsamāsataḥ kramotkṣepanikṣepakarmāpi jñātum / yāvat yauvarājya ... / evamapramāṇā bho jinaputra iyaṃ dharmameghā bodhisattvabhūmiḥ samāsanirdeśataḥ / vistaraśaḥ punarasaṃkhyeyakalpaśatasahasranirdeśāparyantākārato draṣṭavyā //
body.translated_text: How wondrous is the power of the array of the winking of this <s>samādhi</s> comparable to the inconceivable! What is the name of this <s>samādhi</s>, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>? <s>Vajragarbha Bodhisattva</s> said: This <s>samādhi</s>, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, is called 'the Displaying of the Own-nature Body of All <s>Buddha</s>-fields.' <s>Vimukticandra Bodhisattva</s> said: What, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, is the array of the domain and sphere of this <s>samādhi</s>? <s>Vajragarbha Bodhisattva</s> said: O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, if the <s>Bodhisattva</s> so wishes, through having well-cultivated this <s>samādhi</s>, he can display in his own body ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal in number to the atoms in world-realms as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, and even more beyond. Of such <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhis</s>, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Dharmameghā</s> obtains many hundreds of thousands. Therefore, for this <s>Bodhisattva</s>, even <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have attained the rank of crown prince and are established on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Sādhumatī</s> cannot easily know his body or bodily action; cannot easily know his speech or verbal action; cannot easily know his mind or mental action; cannot easily know his supernatural powers; cannot easily know his surveying of the three times; cannot easily know his entry into the domain of <s>samādhi</s>; cannot easily know his sphere of knowledge; cannot easily know his sport in the liberations; cannot easily know his work of emanation, empowerment, or radiance; and cannot easily know even in brief his actions of stepping forward and stepping back. Up to the crown-prince [stage]... Thus immeasurable, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, is this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Dharmameghā</s>, described in brief. In detail, however, it should be understood as having aspects extending to the end of innumerable hundreds of thousands of aeons of exposition.

body.text: vimukticandro bodhisattva āha - kidṛśo bho jinaputra tathāgatagocaraviṣayapraveśo yatredaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ caryāviṣayādhiṣṭhānamevamapramāṇam? vajragarbho bodhisattva āha - tadyathāpi nāma syādbho jinaputra kaścideva puruṣaścaturdvīpikāyā lokadhātordvau trīn vā kolāsthimātrān pāṣāṇān gṛhitvaivaṃ vadet - kiyatī nu khalu sā pṛthivīdhāturaparyantāsu lokadhātuṣu itaḥ pāṣāṇebhyo mahadgatatayā vā pramāṇatveneti? īdṛśamidaṃ mama tvadvacanaṃ pratibhāti / yastvamapramāṇajñānināṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ dharmatāṃ bodhisattvadharmatayā tulayasi / api tu khalu punarbho jinaputra yathā cāturdvīpikāyā lokadhātoḥ parīttā pṛthivīdhāturyā udgṛhītāpramāṇāvaśiṣṭā, evameva bho jinaputra asyā eva tāvaddharmameghāyā bodhisattvabhūmeraprameyān kalpānnirdiśyamānāyāḥ pradeśamātraṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ syāt, kaḥ punarvādastathāgatabhūmeḥ / ārocayāmi te bho jinaputra, prativedayāmi / ayaṃ me tathāgataḥ purataḥ sthitaḥ sākṣībhūtaḥ / sacedbho jinaputra daśasu dikṣu ekaikasyāṃ diśi aparyantalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇyevaṃbhūmiprāptairbodhisattvaiḥ pūrṇāni bhaveyuryathekṣuvanaṃ vā naḍavanaṃ vā veṇuvanaṃ vā tilavanaṃ vā śālivanaṃ va, teṣāmaparyantakalpābhinirhṛto bodhisattvacaryābhinirhāratathāgatasyaikakṣaṇajñānaprasṛtasya tathāgataviṣayasya ... / iti hi bho jinaputra evaṃjñānānugato bodhisattvastathāgatādvayakāyavākcitto bodhisattvasamādhibalaṃ ca notsṛjati buddhadarśanapūjopasthānaṃ ca karoti / sa ekaikasmin kalpe 'paryantāṃstathāgatān sarvākārābhinirhārapūjābhiḥ pūjayati / audārikānugatayā pūjayā
body.translated_text: <s>Vimukticandra Bodhisattva</s> said: What, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, is the entry into the domain and sphere of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, such that this empowerment of the domain of <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct is so immeasurable? <s>Vajragarbha Bodhisattva</s> said: It is as if, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, some person, having taken two or three pebbles the size of a <s>kola</s>-seed from a world-realm of four continents, were to say: 'How vast is this earth-element in the boundless world-realms compared to these pebbles, in terms of its greatness or measure?' Such appears to me this speech of yours—that you measure the <s>dharmatā</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones of immeasurable knowledge by the <s>dharmatā</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. But indeed, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, just as the earth-element of a world-realm of four continents that has been taken up is small, while the remainder is immeasurable—even so, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, even of this very <s>Dharmameghā Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>, when described over immeasurable aeons, only a fraction would have been described; how much less of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-stage! I declare to you, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, I make known: this <s>Tathāgata</s> stands before me as my witness. If, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, in each of the ten directions, <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal in number to the atoms of boundless world-realms were filled with <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who had attained such stages, as [dense as] a sugarcane grove, a reed grove, a bamboo grove, a sesame grove, or a rice grove—[still] the accomplishment of <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct accomplished over innumerable aeons by those [<s>Bodhisattvas</s>] would not [match] the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s domain emanating from a single moment of knowledge... Thus, O son of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who follows knowledge in this way, being non-dual in body, speech, and mind with the <s>Tathāgata</s>, does not abandon the power of <s>Bodhisattva samādhi</s> and performs the seeing, worship, and attendance upon the <s>Buddhas</s>. In each aeon he worships innumerable <s>Tathāgatas</s> with worship accomplished in all aspects, with worship of the most exalted kind,

teṣāṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmadhiṣṭhānāvabhāsaṃ saṃpratīcchati / sa bhūyasyā mātrayā asaṃhāryo bhavati dharmadhātuvibhaktiparipṛcchānirdeśaiḥ / anekān kalpānanekāni kalpaśatāni ... anekāni kalpakoṭinayutaśatasahasrāṇi / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra divyakarmārakṛtaṃ mahābharaṇopacāraṃ mahāmaṇiratnapratyuptaṃ vaśavartino devarājasyottamāṅge kaṇṭhe vā āvaddhamasaṃhāryaṃ bhavati tadanyairdivyamānuṣyakairābharaṇavibhūṣaṇopacāraiḥ, evameva bho jinaputra bodhisattvasyemāṃ daśamīṃ dharmameghāṃ bhodhisattvabhūmimanuprāptasya te bodhisattvajñanopacārā asaṃhāryā bhavanti sarvasattvaiḥ
sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ prathamāṃ bodhisattvabhūmimupādāya yāvannavamīṃ bodhisattvabhūmimanuprāptairbodhisattvaiḥ / asyāṃ ca bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya jñānavabhāsaḥ sattvānāṃ yāvatsarvajñajñānāvatārāya saṃvartate 'saṃhāryastadanyairjñānāvabhāsaiḥ / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra maheśvarasya devarājasyābhā atikrāntā bhavati sarvopapattyāyatanāni, sattvānāṃ ca kāyāśrayān prahlādayati, evameva bho jinaputra bodhisattvasya asyāṃ daśabhyāṃ dharmameghāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya jñānābhā asaṃhāryā bhavati sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ prathamāṃ bodhisattvabhūmimupādāya yāvannavamībodhisattvabhūmipratiṣṭhitairbodhisattvairyāvatsarvajñajñānadharmatāyāṃ ca sattvān pratiṣṭhāpayati / sa khalu punarbho jinaputra bodhisattva evaṃjñānānugato buddhairbhagavadbhistryadhvajñānaṃ ca saṃśrāvyate / dharmadhātuprabhedajñānaṃ ca sarvalokadhātuspharaṇaṃ ca sarvalokadhātvavabhāsādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca sarvasattvakṣetradharmaparijñānaṃ ca sarvasattvacittacaritānupraveśajñānaṃ ca sarvasattvayathākālaparipākajñānaṃ ca vinayānatikramaṇaṃ ca sarvadharmapravicayavibhaktijñānakauśalyaṃ ca samāsato yāvatsarvajñajñānāpramāṇatāṃ ca saṃśrāvyate / tasya daśabhyaḥ pāramitābhyo jñānapāramitā atiriktatamā bhavati, na ca pariśeṣāsu na samudāgacchati yathābalaṃ yathābhajamānam / iyaṃ bho jinaputra bodhisattvasya dharmameghā nāma daśamī bodhisattvabhūmiḥ samāsanirdeśataḥ / vistaraśaḥ punarasaṃkhyeyāparyantakalpanirdeśaniṣṭhāto 'nugantavyā / yasyāṃ pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo bhūyastvena maheśvaro bhavati devarājaḥ kṛtī prabhuḥ sattvānāṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvapāramitopadeśeṣvasaṃhāryo dharmadhātuvibhaktiparipṛcchānirdeśaiḥ / yacca kiṃcit ... // dharmameghā nāma bodhisattvabhūmirdaśamī //
body.translated_text: and he receives the illumination and empowerment of those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones. To an even greater degree he becomes unassailable in inquiries and expositions regarding the divisions of <s>dharmadhātu</s>—over many aeons, many hundreds of aeons... many hundreds of thousands of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>koṭis</s> of aeons. Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, a great ornamental adornment made by a divine craftsman, set with great jewel-gems, bound upon the crown or neck of <s>Vaśavartin</s>, the king of gods, becomes unassailable by all other divine and human ornamental adornments—even so, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has arrived at this tenth <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Dharmameghā</s>, those applications of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-knowledge become unassailable by all beings, all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have arrived from the first <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> up to the ninth. And the illumination of knowledge of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this <s>bhūmi</s> is conducive to the entry of beings into <s>sarvajña</s>-knowledge, unassailable by all other illuminations of knowledge. Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the radiance of <s>Maheśvara</s>, the king of gods, surpasses all realms of rebirth and refreshes the bodily supports of beings—even so, the knowledge-radiance of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on this tenth <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Dharmameghā</s> is unassailable by all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> and by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established from the first up to the ninth <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s>, and he establishes beings in the <s>dharmatā</s> of <s>sarvajña</s>-knowledge.
