Moreover, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who follows knowledge in this way is taught by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, the knowledge of the three times, the knowledge of the divisions of <s>dharmadhātu</s>, the pervading of all world-realms, the empowerment of the illumination of all world-realms, the complete knowledge of the <s>dharmas</s> of all being-fields, the knowledge of entry into the conduct of the minds of all beings, the knowledge of the ripening of all beings at the proper time, the non-transgression of disciplining, the skill in the knowledge of the examination and classification of all <s>dharmas</s>, and in brief, up to the immeasurability of <s>sarvajña</s>-knowledge. Among the ten <s>pāramitās</s>, <s>jñānapāramitā</s> (the perfection of knowledge) becomes the most prominent for him, though he does not fail to practice the remaining [<s>pāramitās</s>] according to his ability and share. This, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, is the tenth <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> called <s>Dharmameghā</s>, described in brief. In detail, however, it should be understood as extending to the end of innumerable and boundless aeons of exposition. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> established thereon predominantly becomes <s>Maheśvara</s>, king of the gods, accomplished, sovereign, unassailable in instruction regarding the <s>pāramitās</s> for all beings, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and in inquiries and expositions regarding the divisions of <s>dharmadhātu</s>. Whatever... The tenth <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> called <s>Dharmameghā</s>.

body.text: 11 parīndanāparivartaḥ /
body.translated_text: 11. The Chapter on Entrustment (<s>Parīndanāparivarta</s>).

body.text: imāstāḥ khalu punarbho jinaputrā daśa bodhisattvabhūmayaḥ samāsanirdeśato nirdiṣṭāḥ / vistaraśaḥ punaraparyantakalpanirdeśaniṣṭhāto 'nugatavyāḥ / yā atītānāgatapratyutpannairbuddhairbhagavadbhirbhāṣitāśca bhāṣiṣyante ca bhāṣyante ca, tāḥ khalu punarbho jinaputra, etā daśa bodhisattvabhūmayaḥ sarvākārasarvajñajñānānugatā draṣṭavyā anupūrvābhimukhatvāt / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra anavataptahradaprabhavaṃ pravahadvāri caturbhirmahānadīsrotomukhairjambūdvīpaṃ saṃtarpya akṣayaṃ bhūyo vivṛddhamaprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmupakārībhūtaṃ yāvanmahāsamudramarpayati, tacca vāri ādita eva mahāsāgarābhimukham, evameva bho jinaputra bodhicittamahāhradaprabhavaṃ pravahat kuśalamūlavāri mahāpraṇidhānanadīsrotomukhaiścaturbhiḥ saṃgrahavastubhiḥ sarvasattvadhātu saṃtarpya akṣayaṃ bhūya uttari vivṛddham aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāmupakārībhūtaṃ yāvatsarvākārasarvajñajñānamahāsamudramarpayati / tacca kuśalamūlavāri ādita eva sarvajñatāmahāsāgarābhimukham //
body.translated_text: These, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, are the ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmis</s>, described in brief. In detail, however, they should be understood as extending to the end of innumerable aeons of exposition. They have been spoken, will be spoken, and are being spoken by the <s>Buddhas</s> of the past, future, and present. These ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmis</s>, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, should be seen as following the omniscient knowledge in all aspects, by virtue of being progressively oriented [toward it]. Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, the water that flows from the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>, through the four great river-mouths, having satisfied <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, inexhaustible and ever-growing, having become beneficial to immeasurable beings, delivers [them] to the great ocean—and that water is from the very beginning oriented toward the great ocean—even so, the water of wholesome roots that flows from the great lake of <s>bodhicitta</s>, through the four great river-mouths of the means of gathering [beings], having satisfied the entire realm of beings, inexhaustible and ever-increasing, having become beneficial to immeasurable beings, delivers [them] to the great ocean of omniscient knowledge in all aspects. And that water of wholesome roots is from the very beginning oriented toward the great ocean of <s>sarvajñatā</s>.

body.text: tāḥ khalu bho jinaputra etā daśa bhūmayo buddhajñānaṃ pratītya prajñāyante / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra mahāpṛthivīṃ pratītya daśa mahāratnaparvatarājāḥ prajñāyante / tadyathā himavān parvatarājo gandhamādano vaidalya ṛṣigiriryugaṃdharo 'śvakarṇagirirnimiṃdharaścakravālaḥ ketumān sumeruśca mahāparvatarājaḥ / tara bho jinaputra tadyathāpi nāma himavān parvatarāja ākaraḥ sarvabhaiṣajyajātīnāmaparyantaḥ sarvabhaiṣajyajātigrahaṇatayā, evameva bho jinaputra pramuditāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito bodhisattva ākaro bhavati sarvalaukikakāvyaśāstramantravidyāsthānānāmaparyantaḥ sarvalaukikakāvyaśāstramantravidyopāyena / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra gandhamādano mahāparvatarāja ākaraḥ sarvagandhajātīnāmaparyantaḥ sarvagandhajātigrahaṇena, evameva bho jinaputra vimalāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito bodhisattva ākaro bhavati sarvabodhisattvaśīlasaṃvaracāritragandhānāmaparyantaḥ sarvabodhisattvaśīlasaṃvaracāritragandhasaṃgrahaṇena / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra vaidalyo mahāparvatarājaḥ śuddho ratnamaya ākaraḥ sarvaratnajātīnāmaparyantaḥ sarvalaukikaratnajātigrahaṇena, evameva bho jinaputra prabhākaryāṃ buddhabhūmau sarvalaukikadhyānābhijñāvimokṣasamādhisamāpattīnām, aparyantaḥ sarvalaukikadhyānābhijñāvimokṣasamādhisamāpattīnām, aparyantaḥ sarvalaukikadhyānābhijñāvimokṣasamādhisamāpattiparipṛcchānirdeśaiḥ / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra ṛṣigirirmahāparvatarājaḥ pañcābhijñānāmṛṣīṇāmaparyantaḥ pañcābhijñarṣigaṇanayā, evameva bho jinaputra arciṣmatyāṃ buddhabhūmau sarvamārgāmārgāntarāvatāranirdeśaviśeṣajñānānāmaparyantaḥ sarvamārgāmārgāntaraviśeṣajñānaparipṛcchānirdeśaiḥ / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra yugaṃdharo mahāparvatarājaḥ sarvayakṣamaharddhikānāmaparyantaḥ sarvayakṣamaharddhikagaṇanayā, evameva bho jinaputra sudurjayāyāṃ buddhabhūmau sarvābhijñarddhivikurvaṇaprātihāryāṇāmaparyantaḥ sarvābhijñarddhivikurvaṇaprātihāryaparipṛcchānirdeśaiḥ / tadyathāpi nāma bho aśvakarṇagirirmahāparvatarājaḥ sarvaphalajātīnāmaparyantaḥ sarvaphalajātigrahaṇena, evameva bho jinaputra abhimukhyāṃ buddhabhūmau
body.translated_text: These ten <s>bhūmis</s>, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, are known in dependence on <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, in dependence on the great earth, ten great jewel-mountain kings are known—namely, <s>Himavān</s> the mountain king, <s>Gandhamādana</s>, <s>Vaidalya</s>, <s>Ṛṣigiri</s>, <s>Yugaṃdhara</s>, <s>Aśvakarṇagiri</s>, <s>Nimiṃdhara</s>, <s>Cakravāla</s>, <s>Ketumān</s>, and <s>Sumeru</s> the great mountain king—here, O noble sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, just as <s>Himavān</s> the mountain king is an inexhaustible mine of all kinds of medicines through its grasping of all kinds of medicines, even so the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>bhūmi</s> <s>Pramuditā</s> is an inexhaustible mine of all worldly poetry, sciences, spells, and knowledge-systems through his skill in all worldly poetry, sciences, spells, and knowledge-systems. Just as <s>Gandhamādana</s> the great mountain king is an inexhaustible mine of all kinds of fragrances through its grasping of all fragrance-types, even so the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on <s>Vimalā</s> is an inexhaustible mine of all the fragrances of <s>Bodhisattva</s> morality, restraint, and conduct through his gathering of all fragrances of <s>Bodhisattva</s> morality, restraint, and conduct. Just as <s>Vaidalya</s> the great mountain king, pure and made of jewels, is an inexhaustible mine of all kinds of gems through its grasping of all worldly gem-types, even so the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on <s>Prabhākarī</s> [is an inexhaustible mine] of all worldly <s>dhyānas</s>, superknowledges, liberations, <s>samādhis</s>, and attainments, inexhaustible in inquiries and expositions regarding all worldly <s>dhyānas</s>, superknowledges, liberations, <s>samādhis</s>, and attainments. Just as <s>Ṛṣigiri</s> the great mountain king is inexhaustible for the five-superknowledge <s>ṛṣis</s> through the number of five-superknowledge <s>ṛṣi</s> assemblies, even so the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on <s>Arciṣmatī</s> is inexhaustible in the distinctive knowledges of entry into all paths and non-paths, through inquiries and expositions regarding all path and non-path distinctive knowledges. Just as <s>Yugaṃdhara</s> the great mountain king is inexhaustible for all great-powered <s>Yakṣas</s> through the number of all great-powered <s>Yakṣa</s> assemblies, even so the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on <s>Sudurjayā</s> is inexhaustible in all superknowledge-powers, miraculous transformations, and wonders, through inquiries and expositions regarding all such. Just as <s>Aśvakarṇagiri</s> the great mountain king is an inexhaustible mine of all fruit-types through its grasping of all fruit-types, even so the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on <s>Abhimukhī</s>

body.text:
pratītyasamutpādāvatāranirdeśānāmaparyantaḥ śrāvakaphalābhisamayaparipṛcchānirdeśaiḥ / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra nimiṃdharo nāma mahāparvatarājaḥ sarvanāgamaharddhikānāmaparyantaḥ sarvanāgamaharddhigaṇanayā, evameva bho jinaputra
dūraṃgamāyāṃ buddhabhūmau upāyaprajñānirdeśānāmaparyantaḥ pratyekabuddhaphalābhisamayaparipṛcchānirdeśaiḥ / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra cakravālo nāma mahāparvatarājaḥ vaśībhūtānāmaparyanto vaśībhūtagaṇanayā, evameva bho jinaputra acalāyāṃ buddhabhūmau sarvabodhisattvavaśitābhinirhārāṇāmaparyanto lokadhātuvibhaktiparipṛcchānirdeśaiḥ / tadyathāpi bho jinaputra ketumān nāma mahāparvatarājaḥ asuramaharddhikānāmaparyanto 'suramaharddhikagaṇanayā, evameva bho jinaputra sādhumatyāṃ buddhabhūmau sarvasattvapravṛttinivṛttijñānopacārāṇāmaparyantaḥ sarvajagatsaṃbhavavibhavaparipṛcchānirdeśaiḥ / tadyathāpi bho jinaputra sumerurmahāparvatarājaḥ sarvadevamaharddhikānāmaparyantaḥ sarvadevamaharddhikagaṇanayā, evameva bho jinaputra dharmameghāyāṃ buddhabhūmau tathāgatabalavaiśaradyāveṇikabuddhadharmāṇāmaparyanto buddhakāyasaṃdarśanaparipṛcchānirdeśaiḥ / yathā khalu punarime bho jinaputra daśa mahāratnaparvatā mahāsamudrasaṃbhūtā mahāsamudraprabhāvitāḥ, evameva bho jinaputra imā api daśa bhūmayaṃ sarvajñatāsaṃbhūtāḥ sarvajñatāprabhāvitāḥ //
body.translated_text: the instructions on entering dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) are boundless, as measured by the instructions and inquiries regarding the realization of the fruit of <s>śrāvakas</s>. Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, the great mountain king called <s>Nimiṃdhara</s> is boundless for all great-powered <s>nāgas</s> as measured by the count of great-powered <s>nāgas</s>, even so, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, on the [seventh] <s>Buddha</s> stage <s>Dūraṃgamā</s>, the instructions on skillful means and wisdom are boundless, as measured by the instructions and inquiries regarding the realization of the fruit of <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, the great mountain king called <s>Cakravāḍa</s> is boundless for those who have attained mastery, as measured by the count of those with mastery, even so, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, on the [eighth] <s>Buddha</s> stage <s>Acalā</s>, the accomplishments of all <s>bodhisattva</s> masteries (<s>vaśitā</s>) are boundless, as measured by the instructions and inquiries regarding the differentiation of world-systems. Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, the great mountain king called <s>Ketumān</s> is boundless for the great-powered <s>asuras</s>, as measured by the count of great-powered <s>asuras</s>, even so, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, on the [ninth] <s>Buddha</s> stage <s>Sādhumatī</s>, the approaches to knowledge of the activity and cessation of all beings are boundless, as measured by the instructions and inquiries regarding the arising and dissolution of the entire world. Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, the great mountain king <s>Sumeru</s> is boundless for all great-powered <s>devas</s>, as measured by the count of all great-powered <s>devas</s>, even so, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, on the [tenth] <s>Buddha</s> stage <s>Dharmameghā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s powers, confidences, and unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities are boundless, as measured by the instructions and inquiries regarding the display of the <s>Buddha</s>-body. Just as these ten great jewel mountains arise from the great ocean and are empowered by the great ocean, even so, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, these ten stages arise from omniscient knowledge (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) and are empowered by omniscient knowledge.

body.text: tadyathāpi bho jinaputra mahāsamudro daśabhirākāraiḥ saṃkhyāṃ gacchatyasaṃhāryatayā / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta anupūrvanimnataśca mṛtakuṇapāsaṃvāsataśca anyavārisaṃkhyātyajanataśca ekarasataśca bahuratnataśca gambhīraduravagāhataśca vipulāpramāṇataśca mahābhūtāvāsataśca sthitavelānatikramaṇataśca sarvameghavārisaṃpratyeṣaṇātṛptitaśca, evameva bho jinaputra bodhisattvacaryā daśabhirākāraiḥ saṃkhyāṃ gacchatyasaṃhāryatayā / katamairdaśabhiḥ? yaduta pramuditāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau anupūrvamahāpraṇidhānābhinirhāranimnataḥ / vimalāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau dauḥśīlyamṛtakuṇapāsaṃvāsataḥ / prabhākaryāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau laukikaprajñaptisaṃkhyātyāgataḥ / arciṣmatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau buddhabhedyaprasādaikarasataḥ / sudurjayāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau apramāṇopāyābhijñālokakriyābhinirhārabahuratnataḥ / abhimukhyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau pratītyasamutpādapratyavekṣaṇaduravagāhagāmbhīryataḥ / dūraṃgamāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau buddhipravicayakauśalyavipulāpramāṇataḥ / acalāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau mahāvyūhābhinirhārasaṃdarśanamahābhūtāvāsataḥ / sādhumatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau gambhīravimokṣajagaccaritayathāvatprativedhasthitavelānatikramaṇataḥ / dharmameghāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sarvatathāgatadharmāvabhāsamahāmeghavārisaṃpratyeṣaṇātṛptitaḥ //
body.translated_text: Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, the great ocean is counted by ten aspects of indestructibility. Which ten? Namely: its gradual deepening, its not tolerating a dead corpse, the unique taste of its waters being of one flavor, its being the abode of great treasures, the great beings dwelling in it, its not overflowing from the inflow of rivers, its immeasurability of water, its great extent, its being the dwelling of great creatures, and its receiving tides of the waxing and waning [moon]. Even so, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, this teaching of the ten <s>bodhisattva</s> stages is counted by ten indestructible aspects.

body.text: tadyathāpi bho jinaputra mahāmaṇiratnaṃ yadā daśa ratnagotrāṇyatikramya abhyutkṣiptaṃ ca bhavati kuśalakarmārasuparitāpitaṃ ca suparipiṇḍitaṃ ca supariśodhitaṃ ca suparyavadāpitaṃ ca sunirviddhaṃ ca ratnasūtrasvāviddhaṃ ca uccavaiḍūryamaṇiratnadaṇḍadhvajāgrāvaropitaṃ ca sarvāvabhāsapramuktaṃ ca rājānujñātaṃ ca bhavati, tadā sarvasattvānāṃ sarvaratnasaṃgrahāya pratyupasthitaṃ bhavati, evameva bho jinaputra yadā bodhisattvānāṃ sarvajñatāratnacittotpādo daśāryaratnagotrāṇyatikramyotpanno bhavati
body.translated_text: Just as, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, a great precious jewel, when it has transcended the ten classes of gems and has been extracted, well-heated by a skilled artisan, well-consolidated, well-polished,

body.text: dhūtaguṇasaṃlekhaśīlavratatapaḥsuparitāpitaśca dhyānasamādhisamāpattisuparipiṇḍitaśca mārgāṅgākārasupariśodhitaśca upāyābhijñāsuparyavadāpitaśca pratītyasamutpādasunirviddhaśca upāyaprajñāvicitraratnasūtrasvāviddhaśca vaśitāmahāvaiḍūryamaṇiratnadaṇḍadhvajāgrāvaropitaśca sattvacaritapratyavekṣaṇaśrutajñānāvabhāsasaṃprayuktaśca tathāgatadharmarājasamyaksaṃbuddhajñānābhiṣekānugataśca bhavati, tadā sarvasattvānāṃ sarvabuddhakāryaratnasaṃgrahāya pratyupasthito bhavati, tadā ca sarvajña ityākhyāyate // ayaṃ khalu punarbho jinaputra bodhisattvacaryāsamudānayanaḥ sarvākārasarvajñajñānaguṇasaṃcayo dharmamukhaparivarto nānavaropitakuśālamūlānāṃ sattvānāṃ śravaṇāvabhāsamāgamiṣyati //
body.translated_text: well-heated through the ascetic qualities, moral restraints, and austerities of purification; well-consolidated through <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>samādhi</s>, and <s>samāpatti</s>; well-polished through the aspects of the path-limbs; well-refined through skillful means and superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>);

body.text: vimukticandro bodhisattva āha - yeṣāṃ punarbho jinaputra ayaṃ sarvākārasarvajñajñānaguṇasaṃcayo dharmamukhaparivartaḥ śravaṇāvabhāsamāgamiṣyati, te kiyatā puṇyopacayena samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti? vajragarbho bodhisattva āha - yāvān bho jinaputra sarvajñajñānasya prabhāvastāvān sarvajñatācittotpādasaṃgrahālambanātpuṇyopacayaḥ syāt / yāvān sarvajñatācittotpādasaṃgrahālambanataḥ puṇyopacayastāvānevāsya dharmamukhaparivartasyābhimukhaḥ puṇyopacayo 'nugantavyaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi bho jinaputra śakyaṃ anyatra bodhisattvena ayaṃ sarvākārasarvajñajñānaguṇasaṃcayo dharmamukhaparivartaḥ śrotuṃ vā adhimoktuṃ vā pratyetuṃ vā udgrahītuṃ vā dhārayituṃ vā saṃdhārayituṃ vā / kaḥ punarvādo bhāvanākāraprayogodyoganiṣpādaneṣu? tasmāttarhi bho jinaputra sarvajñajñānamukhānugatāste saṃdhārayitavyāḥ, ye imaṃ sarvajñajñānaguṇasaṃcayadharmamukhaparivartaṃ śropyati, śrutvā cādhimokṣyante, adhimucya cādhārayiṣyanti, bhāvanākāreṇa prayokṣyante //
body.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vimukticandra</s> said: For those, O noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, to whom this chapter on the turning of the <s>Dharma</s> gateway, the accumulation of all aspects of omniscient knowledge and qualities, shall come to be heard and illuminated—what will they

body.text: atha khalu tasyāṃ velāyāṃ buddhānubhāvena dharmatāpratilambhena ca daśadiglokadaśabuddhakṣetrakoṭiparamāṇurajaḥsamā lokadhātavaḥ ṣaḍvikāramaṣṭādaśamahānimittamakampanta prākampanta saṃprākampanta / acalan prācalan saṃprācalan / avedhanta prāvedhanta saṃprāvedhanta / araṇan prāraṇan saṃprāraṇan / akṣumyan prākṣubhyan saṃprākṣumyan / agarjan prāgarjan saṃprāgarjan / divyāśca puṣpagandhamālyameghā abhiprāvarṣan / divyāśca vastrameghā divyāścūrṇameghā divyā ratnameghā divyā ābharaṇameghā divyā chatrameghā divyā dhvajameghā divyā patākāmeghā abhiprāvarṣan / divyaṃ ca sūryacakrātmabhāvamaṇḍalamaṇirājasumerumeghavarṣamabhiprāvarṣan / divyaṃ ca sarvarutaravitavādyamaṇirājasumerumeghavarṣamabhiprāvarṣan / divyaṃ ca jāmbūnadakanakavarṇaprabhāmaṇḍalamaṇirājasumerumeghavarṣamabhiprāvarṣan / divyāśca tūryatālāvacarasaṃgītimeghā nadanti sma / divyasamatikrāntāḥ sarvajñatābhūmyabhiṣṭavasaṃgītimeghā nadanti sma / yathā cāsyāṃ lokadhātau cāturdvīpikāyāṃ paranirmitavaśavartino devarājasya vimāne maṇiratnagarbhaprāsāde, tathā sarvalokadhātuṣu daśa diśaḥ spharitvā iyameva dharmadeśanā sarvatraiva pravartate sma / ... daśabhyo digbhyo daśabuddhakṣetrakoṭiparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ lokadhātūnāṃ pareṇa daśabuddhakṣetrakoṭiparamāṇurajaḥsamā bodhisattvā āgacchanti daśadiśaṃ spharantaḥ / te ca āgatyaivamāhuḥ - sādhu sādhu bho jinaputra, yastvamimāṃ bodhisattvabhūmidharmatāṃ sūcayati / vayamapi bho jinaputra sarve vajragarbhasamanāmakā eva vajraśrīnāmikābhyo
body.translated_text: Then at that moment, through the power of the <s>Buddha</s> and through the attainment of the nature of <s>Dharma</s>, world-systems equal in number to the atomic particles of ten <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions trembled with six kinds of earthquakes in eighteen great ways.

body.text: nānālokadhātubhya ihāgatā vajradhvajanāmakānāṃ tathāgatānāmantikebhyaḥ / sarvāsu ca tāsu lokadhātuṣu iyameva dharmadeśanā pravartate buddhānubhāvena evaṃrūpāsveva parṣatsu / ebhireva padairebhireva vyañjanairebhireva niruktairetamevārthamabhilaṣadbhiranūnamanadhikamanatiriktam, te vayaṃ bho jinaputra sākṣībhūtā buddhānubhāvenemāṃ parṣadaṃ saṃprāptāḥ / yathā ca bho jinaputra vayamimāṃ lokadhātuṃ saṃprāptāstathā ca daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣvekaikasyāṃ lokadhātau cāturdvīpikāyāṃ paranirmitavaśavartibhavane vaśavartino devarājasya vimāne maṇiratnagarbhaprāsāde saṃprāptā iti //
body.translated_text: having come from various world-systems, from the presence of <s>Tathāgatas</s> named <s>Vajradhvaja</s>. And in all those world-systems, this very <s>Dharma</s> teaching proceeds through the power of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: idamavocadvajragarbho bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'bhyanujñātastathāgatena / āttamanāḥ sā ca sarvāvatī bodhisattvaparṣat sā ca devanāga ... śuddhāvāsaparṣad bhagavāṃśca paranirmitavaśavartiṣu deveṣu viharannacirābhisaṃbuddho dvitīye saptāhe vaśavartino devarājasya vimāne maṇiratnagarbhe vajragarbhasya bodhisattvasya bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti //
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s>, approved by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Delighted was that entire assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and that assembly of <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, ... and <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> beings.

body.text: iti parīndanāparivarto nāmaikādaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh chapter called the Transfer (<s>Parīndanā</s>).

body.text: iti śrībodhisattvacaryāprasthāno daśabhūmīśvaro nāma mahāyānasūtraratnarājaḥ samāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus is completed the noble <s>Daśabhūmīśvara</s> (Lord of the Ten Stages), the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtras, [belonging to] the <s>Bodhisattvacaryāprasthāna</s>.

body.text: Daśabhūmikasūtre gāthāvibhāgaḥ /
body.translated_text: Verse section (<s>gāthāvibhāga</s>) of the <s>Daśabhūmikasūtra</s>.

body.text: 1 pramuditā nāma prathamā bhūmiḥ /
body.translated_text: 1. The first stage called <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful).

body.text: upakramaḥ /
body.translated_text: Introduction.

children.text: te śukladharmupacitāḥ kuśalopapetāḥ paryupāsitāḥ sugatamaitrakṛpānukūlāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who have accumulated bright qualities, endowed with merit, who have attended upon the <s>Sugata</s>, conforming to friendliness and compassion,

children.text: adhimuktyudāra kuśalāśaya śuddhabhāvāścittaṃ janenti atulaṃ jinajñānahetoḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: with noble inclination, wholesome resolve, and pure disposition—they generate the incomparable mind for the sake of the knowledge of the <s>Jina</s>. (1)

children.text: sarvajñabuddhabalaśodhanavīryasthāmā jinadharmaniṣpattijagatparitrāyaṇārthāḥ /
children.translated_text: With the strength and vigor of purifying omniscient <s>Buddha</s>-powers, for the sake of accomplishing the <s>Jina</s>'s qualities and protecting the world,

children.text: mahākṛpocayavartanadharmacakraṃ jinakṣetraśodhamupapadyati cittaśreṣṭham // 2 //
children.translated_text: for the turning of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel through the development of great compassion, for the purification of <s>Jina</s>-fields—the supreme mind arises. (2)

children.text: tryadhvaikavīkṣaṇavibuddhananirvikalpā nānāvidhe jagati kālaviśodhanārtham /
children.translated_text: Awakened through the examination of the three times in unity, without conceptualization, for the purpose of purifying the various times in the diverse world,

children.text: saṃkṣepasarvaguṇa eṣitu nāyakānām ākāśatulya samudeti udāracittam // 3 //
children.translated_text: encompassing all qualities of the Leaders in brief, equal to space, the noble mind arises. (3)

children.text: prajñādhipatya kṛpapūrvamupāyayuktam adhimukti-āśayaviśuddhabalāpramāṇam /
children.translated_text: With wisdom as sovereign, preceded by compassion, joined with skillful means, with pure inclination and resolve, with immeasurable strength,

children.text: āsaṅgatābhimukhatā-aparapraṇeyaṃ samatopapetasugataṃ varacittajātam // 4 //
children.translated_text: with non-attachment and directness, not led by others, endowed with equanimity toward the <s>Sugata</s>—the excellent mind is born. (4)

children.text: sahajāticittaratanaṃ sugatātmajānām atikrānta bālacari buddhacari hyupetaḥ /
children.translated_text: The innate mind-jewel of the sons of the <s>Sugata</s>, having transcended the conduct of the foolish, endowed with the conduct of the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: jātaḥ kule daśabalāna anodyapadyaḥ samatāṃ jine anugato niyatāgrabodhiḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: born in the family of the Ten-Powered Ones, arising effortlessly, having followed equanimity with the <s>Jinas</s>, fixed upon supreme awakening. (5)

children.text: ekasmi citta upapadyati bhūmilābho bhavate acalyu girirājasamāśayaśca /
children.translated_text: In a single mind-moment the attainment of the stage arises, and one becomes immovable, with a resolve like the king of mountains,

children.text: prāmodyaprītibahulaśca prasādavāṃśca utsāhavegavipulaḥ sadudagracittaḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text: abundant in joy and delight, endowed with faith, with great and vast energy, with an exalted mind. (6)

children.text: saṃrambhahiṃsavigataśca akrodhanaśca hrīgauravārjavataraśca susaṃvṛtaśca /
children.translated_text: Free from hostility and harm, without anger, endowed with modesty, respect, and uprightness, well-restrained,

children.text: jagatāyanaṃ smarati apratimānajñānaṃ prītiṃ janetyupagataspṛhameta sthānam // 7 //
children.translated_text: mindful of the refuge of the world, with incomparable knowledge, generating delight, having approached this state free from craving. (7)

children.text: pañcā bhayā apagatāḥ sahabhūmilābho ājīvikā maraṇa kīrtyatha durgatiśca /
children.translated_text: Five fears depart with the attainment of the stage: [fear regarding] livelihood, death, reputation, evil destinies,

children.text: parṣadbhayaṃ ca vigataṃ tatha chambhitatvaṃ kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tatha hi ātmaniketu nāsti // 8 //
children.translated_text: and fear of assemblies, and likewise timidity—for what reason? Because there is no notion of self. (8)

children.text: te chambhitatvavigatāḥ kṛpamaitrayuktāḥ śraddhāsagauravahriyopagatā guṇāḍhyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Free from timidity, endowed with compassion and friendliness, possessing faith, respect, and modesty, rich in qualities,

children.text: rātriṃdivaṃ kuśalapakṣa niṣevamāṇāḥ satyārtha dharmaniratā na tu kāmabhogaiḥ // 9 //
children.translated_text: day and night cultivating the side of merit, devoted to truth, meaning, and <s>Dharma</s>, not to sensual pleasures. (9)

body.text:
śrutadharmacintakuśalā aniketacittā lābhādaśīcittagatā uta bodhicittāḥ /
jñānābhilāṣi balaśodhanabuddhadharmā eṣanti pāramita varjitamāyaśāṭhyāḥ // 10 // yathāvādinastathakriyāḥ sthitasatyavākyā na tu dūṣaṇā jinakule cari bodhiśikṣām /

children.text: lokakriyāya vigatā niratā jagārthaṃ śuklairatṛpta bhumayottarimārabhante // 11 //
children.translated_text: Gone beyond worldly occupations, devoted to the welfare of the world, insatiable for bright [qualities], they undertake the stages further. (11)

body.translated_text:
Skilled in learning, <s>Dharma</s>, and reflection, with a mind free from attachment, not inclined toward gain and honor but toward the mind of awakening,
aspiring to knowledge, purifying the powers and <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, seeking the <s>pāramitās</s>, free from deceit and craft. (10)

children.text: te eva dharmaniratā guṇārthayuktā abhinirharanti praṇidhiṃ jinadarśanāya /
children.translated_text: Devoted to <s>Dharma</s>, endowed with qualities and purpose, they bring forth the vow (<s>praṇidhi</s>) for seeing the <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: saddharmadhāraṇa upasaṃkramaṇā ṛṣiṇām abhinirharanti praṇīdhiṃ varacārikāyām // 12 //
children.translated_text: They bring forth the vow for the excellent practice, approaching the preservation of the true <s>Dharma</s> of the sages. // 12 //

children.text: paripākasattvapariśodhanabuddhakṣetraṃ te cāsya kṣetra sphuṭikā jina aurasehi /
children.translated_text: The ripening of beings, the purification of <s>Buddha</s>-fields — and these fields are made radiant by the own sons of the <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: ekāśayā jinasutehi amoghatāyāḥ sarvatra bālapathi buddhiya hetumarthe // 13 //
children.translated_text: By the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> who are of one intention and of unfailing nature, everywhere on the path of the foolish, for the sake of the cause of <s>Buddhi</s> (awakened wisdom). // 13 //

children.text: etāṃśca naikapraṇidhīnabhinirharanti te co anantavipulāya anantatāyai /
children.translated_text: And they bring forth these manifold vows, for the sake of the infinite and vast infinitude,

children.text: ākāśadhātusattvadharmatanirvṛtaṃ ca loko hyaniṣṭha jinamutpadi jñānabhūmī // 14 //
children.translated_text: And the realm of space, beings, <s>Dharma</s>-nature, and <s>Nirvṛti</s> (cessation) — the world is without end, and the arising of <s>Jinas</s> is the ground of knowledge. // 14 //

children.text: cittasya no viṣayajñānapraveśaniṣṭhā yā vartani trividhaniṣṭha jagatyanantā /
children.translated_text: There is no end to the range of the mind's entry into knowledge; the path that is threefold in its end is infinite in the world,

children.text: praṇidhānaniṣṭhitu bhavenna mamaivarūpā yatha eta niṣṭha tatha carya samā labheyam // 15 //
children.translated_text: And the end of vows shall not be of such a form for me — as these are without end, so may I obtain equal practice. // 15 //

children.text: evaṃ sunirhṛtasumārdavasnigdhacittāḥ śraddheta buddhaguṇa sattva vilokayantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, with well-developed, gentle, soft, and tender minds, trusting in the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, beholding beings,

children.text: prītyāntulambhupagataḥ kṛpamaitratāṃ ca paritāyitavya maya sattva dukhārditāni // 16 //
children.translated_text: Having attained joy incomparable, and compassion and <s>Maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) — 'I must protect the beings afflicted by suffering.' // 16 //

children.text: teṣārthi tyāga vividhaṃ puna ārabhante rājyaṃ varaṃ vividharatnahayān gajāṃśca /
children.translated_text: For their sake they undertake various acts of generosity — excellent kingdoms, various jewels, horses, and elephants,

children.text: śirahastapādanayanā svakamātmamāṃsaṃ sarvaṃ tyajanti na ca dīnamanā bhavanti // 17 //
children.translated_text: Heads, hands, feet, eyes, their own flesh and body — they give up everything and do not become dejected in mind. // 17 //

body.text: eṣanti śāstra vividhānna ca khedamenti / śāstrajña lokacaritānyanuvartayanti /

children.text: lokajñatāmupagatā hriyatā dhṛtiṃ ca pūjyanti cāpratisamān gurugauraveṇa // 18 //
children.translated_text: Having attained knowledge of the world, with modesty and steadfastness, they honor with reverence the incomparable teachers. // 18 //

body.translated_text: They seek various <s>śāstras</s> (treatises) and do not become weary; knowing the <s>śāstras</s>, they follow the ways of the world,

children.text: eṣābhiyuktavidunā divarātri nityam uttapyate kuśala svarṇa yathaiva agnau /
children.translated_text: This [merit], constantly pursued by the wise day and night, is refined like gold in fire,

children.text: so cāpi eva parikarma daśāna bhūmī kṛtvā asaṅgatamupeti aviṣṭhihantā // 19 //
children.translated_text: And having thus performed the preparation of the ten stages, one attains the unattached state, standing firm. // 19 //

children.text: yatha sārthavāha mahasārthahitāya yukto pucchitva mārgaguṇa kṣematamabhyupeti /
children.translated_text: Just as a caravan leader, devoted to the welfare of a great caravan, having inquired about the virtues of the road, attains safety,

children.text: emeva bhūmi prathamā sthita bodhisattvaḥ kṛtaniṣkramo daśabhibodhimupetyasaṅgaḥ // 20 //
children.translated_text: Even so, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in the first stage, having made the departure, attains unattached <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening) through the ten [stages]. // 20 //

body.text: atra sthitā guṇadharā nṛpatī bhavanti dharmānuśāsaka ahiṃsaka maitrayuktāḥ /
body.translated_text: Those established here become kings endowed with virtues, teaching <s>Dharma</s>, non-violent, joined with <s>Maitrī</s> (loving-kindness),

body.text: jambudhvajaṃ sakalarājya praśāsayantaḥ sthāpenti tyāgi janatāṃ varabuddhajñāne // 21 //
body.translated_text: Governing the entire kingdom of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, they establish generous people in the excellent knowledge of the <s>Buddha</s>. // 21 //

children.text: ākāṅkṣamāṇa vṛṣabhā vijahitva rājyaṃ jinaśāsane upagatāścari ārabhantaḥ /
children.translated_text: The excellent ones, when desiring, abandon their kingdoms, enter the teaching of the <s>Jinas</s>, and undertake the practice,

children.text: labdhvā samādhiśata buddhaśataṃ ca paśyi kampenti kṣetraśatu bhāsi atikramanti // 22 //
children.translated_text: Having obtained hundreds of <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations), they see hundreds of <s>Buddhas</s>, cause hundreds of fields to tremble, illuminate them, and go beyond. // 22 //

children.text: śodhyanti sattvaśata dharmamukhān viśanti praviśanti kalpaśatakāyaśataṃ nidarśi /
children.translated_text: They purify hundreds of beings, enter the gateways of <s>Dharma</s>, enter hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), and display hundreds of bodies,

children.text: pūrṇaṃ śataṃ jinasutāna nidarśayanti bhūyottari praṇidhiśreṣṭhabalāpramāṇāḥ // 23 //
children.translated_text: They show a full hundred of sons of the <s>Jinas</s> — and beyond this, through the power of excellent vows, they are immeasurable. // 23 //

children.text: ityeṣā prathamā bhūmirnidiṣṭā sugatātmajāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus has been taught this first stage, O sons of the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones),

children.text: sarvalokahitaiṣīṇāṃ bodhisattvānanutamā // 24 //
children.translated_text: The unsurpassed [stage] of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who seek the welfare of all the world. // 24 //

body.text:
2 vimalā nāma dvitīyā bhūmiḥ /
upakramagāthāḥ /
body.translated_text:
2. The second stage called <s>Vimalā</s> (Stainless).
Introductory verses:

children.text: śrutvaitaduttamaṃ sthānaṃ bhūmyāḥ śreṣṭhaṃ manoramam /
children.translated_text: Having heard this supreme, excellent, and delightful station of the [first] stage,

children.text: prasannamanasaṃkalpaharṣitāḥ sugatātmajāḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Sugatas</s>, with pure mental resolve, were filled with joy. // 1 //

children.text: abhyutthitā āsanebhya abhyudgamya khagapathe /
children.translated_text: Having risen from their seats and ascending into the sky,

children.text: abhyokiranti kusumaiḥ sādhviti vyāharī girā // 2 //
children.translated_text: They shower flowers, uttering the word 'Excellent!' // 2 //

children.text: sādhu sādhu mahāprājña vajragarbha viśārada /
children.translated_text: Excellent, excellent, O greatly wise <s>Vajragarbha</s>, O skilled one,

children.text: yannirdiṣṭā tvayā bhūmi bodhisattvāna yā carī // 3 //
children.translated_text: That you have taught this stage, the practice of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! // 3 //

children.text: parṣaddhi viprasannā tu vimukticandraḥ pṛcchati /
children.translated_text: The assembly being well-pleased, <s>Vimukticandra</s> (Moon of Liberation) asks,

children.text: uttariṃ kīrtiyā bhūmiṃ dvitīyāṃ sugatātmajāḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: Further, proclaim the second stage, O sons of the <s>Sugatas</s>! // 4 //

children.text: kīdṛśā manasaṃkalpā dvitīyāmabhilakṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: What are the mental resolves with which one is characterized on the second [stage]?

children.text: pravyāhara mahāprājña śrotukāmā jinātmajāḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: Proclaim, O greatly wise one — the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> wish to hear! // 5 //

children.text: upasaṃhāragāthāḥ /
children.translated_text: Summary verses:

children.text: te mārdavārjavamṛdūkarmaṇīyacittāḥ kalyāṇa-āśaya damāśayatābhyupetāḥ /
children.translated_text: They whose minds are gentle, upright, soft, and workable, endowed with wholesome intention, self-control, and [mental] taming,

children.text: saṃsargapekṣavigatāśca udārabuddhi māhātmya āśayavid dvitīyākramanti // 6 //
children.translated_text: Free from regard for association, with noble understanding, knowing the greatness of intention — they enter the second [stage]. // 6 //

children.text: atra sthitā guṇadharāḥ kuśalopapetāḥ prāṇātipātavigatā avihiṃsacittāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those established here, endowed with virtues and meritorious qualities, have abandoned the taking of life and are of non-violent mind,

children.text: adattadānapagatāḥ paradāratāṃ ca satyānvitā apiśunaḥ puruṣapradhānāḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: Free from taking what is not given and from [coveting] others' wives, endowed with truth, not slanderous — they are foremost among men. // 7 //

children.text: parabhogabhidyavigatā vidu maitracittāḥ samyakpathe upagatā aśaṭhajñakāśca /
children.translated_text: Free from craving for others' enjoyments, wise ones of loving mind, established on the right path, without deceit in their knowledge,

children.text: nirmāṇakāyagrahaṇāśca supeśalāśca rakṣanti śāstuśaraṇaṃ sada apramattāḥ // 8 //
children.translated_text: Not grasping at the <s>nirmāṇakāya</s> (emanation body), and being courteous, they always guard the refuge of the Teacher, ever vigilant. // 8 //

children.text: duḥkhāni yāni niraye tatha tiryagyonau yamaśāsane jvalita-āśrayanityupetāḥ /
children.translated_text: The sufferings that exist in hell, in the animal realm, in the domain of <s>Yama</s>, with their blazing dwellings constantly present —

children.text: sarve ti pāpapatitākṣalāḥ prabhonti hantā vivarjiya upemahi satyadharmam // 9 //
children.translated_text: All those fallen into evil, the unwashed, are capable [of being saved] — 'Having abandoned destruction, may we attain the true <s>Dharma</s>.' // 9 //

children.text: ādau ca kṛtva manujānupapattimiṣṭāṃ yāvadbhavāgramaraṇāśayadhyānu śikṣām /
children.translated_text: Having first considered the desired human birth, training in the intention toward death at the summit of existence,

children.text: pratyekayānamatha śrāvakabuddhayānaṃ sarve ito daśabhi śuklapathaiḥ prabhūtam // 10 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Pratyekayāna</s> (solitary vehicle), and then the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Buddha</s> vehicles — all of this [arises] from the ten bright paths. // 10 //

children.text: evaṃ viditva satataṃ vidu apramattāḥ śīleṣu saṃsthita parānapi sthāpayanti /
children.translated_text: Thus knowing this constantly, the wise and vigilant ones, established in moral precepts, also establish others,

children.text: bhūyottare karuṇa-āśayatābhyupetāḥ sattvān viditva dukhitān kṛpa saṃjanenti // 11 //
children.translated_text: Endowed with ever-greater compassionate intention, knowing beings as suffering, they generate <s>Kṛpā</s> (compassion). // 11 //

children.text: hanto vidṛṣṭipatitā imi bālabuddhī krodhopanāhadrutacitta vivādaprāptāḥ /
children.translated_text: Alas! These [beings] fallen into wrong views, of childish understanding, their minds seized by anger and resentment, arrived at quarreling,

children.text: satataṃ atṛpta viṣaye bhuyu prārthayanti trinidāna sattva parimocayitavya ete // 12 //
children.translated_text: Constantly unsatisfied with sense objects, desiring ever more — these beings bound by the three causes must be liberated! // 12 //

children.text: maha-andhakāratamasāvṛta mohachannāḥ kāntāramārgapatitā mahadṛṣṭijāle /
children.translated_text: Covered by great darkness, concealed in delusion, fallen on the path of the wilderness, caught in the great net of [wrong] views,

children.text: saṃsārapañjaragatā ripu dharṣayanti mokṣāmyahaṃ namucipañjaramadhyaprāptān // 13 //
children.translated_text: Entered into the cage of <s>Saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), harassed by enemies — 'I shall liberate those caught in the cage of <s>Namuchi</s> (Māra)!' // 13 //

children.text: kleśormibhihriyata oghacaturnimagnā traidhātuke dukhaśataiḥ paripīḍyamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: Carried away by waves of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), submerged in the four floods, tormented by hundreds of sufferings in the three realms,

children.text: skandhālayābhyupagatā vṛta-ātmasaṃjñā teṣārthi yujyami ahaṃ dukhamocanārtham // 14 //
children.translated_text: Having resorted to the dwelling of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), bound by the notion of self — for their sake I shall apply myself, for the purpose of releasing them from suffering! // 14 //

children.text: avasṛjya śreṣṭhapravaraṃ ima buddhajñānaṃ sati eva niḥsaraṇi hīnamatiṃ janenti /
children.translated_text: Abandoning this supreme and excellent <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, though liberation exists, they generate inferior understanding,

children.text: sthāpemi tān vimalajñāni tathāgatānāṃ vīryārabhanti atulaṃ vidu bodhihetoḥ // 15 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall establish them in the stainless knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>' — the wise ones undertake incomparable effort for the sake of <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening). // 15 //

children.text: atra sthitā guṇaśatopacitā maharṣi paśyanti naikasugatānapi pūjayanti /
children.translated_text: Those established here, great sages enriched with hundreds of virtues, see and worship numerous <s>Sugatas</s>,

children.text: teṣāṃ śubhaṃ bhuyu uttapyati kalpakoṭyāṃ kāsīsakāñcanavaraṃ ca yathā nikṣiptam // 16 //
children.translated_text: Their merit is further refined over <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), like the finest gold of <s>Kāśī</s> when it is deposited. // 16 //

body.text: atra sthitā jinasutā nṛpacakravarti bhūtvā praṇenti daśabhiḥ kuśalebhi sattvān /
body.translated_text: Those established here, sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, becoming <s>Cakravartins</s> (universal monarchs), lead beings through the ten wholesome [paths],

body.text: yaccaiva saṃci śubhasaṃcaya saṃcinanti trātā bhavema jagato daśabhirbalāḍhyaiḥ // 17 //
body.translated_text: And whatever meritorious accumulation they gather — 'May we become protectors of the world, mighty with the ten powers!' // 17 //

children.text: ākāṅkṣamāṇa vijahitva ca rajabhogān pravrajya śāsanavare upagamya dhīrāḥ /
children.translated_text: When desiring, having abandoned royal enjoyments, going forth into the excellent teaching, the steadfast ones,

children.text: vīryānvitā labhiya śreṣṭhavaraṃ samādhiṃ buddhā sahasra paripūrṇa kṣeṇe dṛśanti // 18 //
children.translated_text: Endowed with energy, having obtained the supreme and excellent <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), see a full thousand <s>Buddhas</s> in an instant. // 18 //

children.text: evaṃvidhā gaṇanayā bhuyu anya nekā ādarśayanti vṛṣabhī sthita atra bhūmau /
children.translated_text: Of such kind, and by enumeration yet many more, the excellent ones established on this stage display,

children.text: ata uttari praṇidhijñānavarābhyupetā naikā vikurvitavidhau vinayanti sattvān // 19 //
children.translated_text: And beyond this, endowed with the excellent vows and knowledge, they discipline beings through manifold miraculous transformations. // 19 //

body.text: ityeṣā dvitiyā bhūmirnirdiṣṭā sugatātmajāḥ / sarvalokahitaiṣīṇāṃ bodhisattvānanuttamā // 20 //
body.translated_text: Thus has been taught this second stage, O sons of the <s>Sugatas</s>, the unsurpassed [stage] of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who seek the welfare of all the world. // 20 //

body.text:
3 prabhākarī nāma tṛtīyā bhūmiḥ /
upakramagāthāḥ /
body.translated_text:
3. The third stage called <s>Prabhākarī</s> (Illuminating).
Introductory verses:

children.text: evaṃ śruṇitva caribhūmimuttamāṃ bodhisattvaviṣaye acintiyām /
children.translated_text: Having thus heard this supreme practice-stage in the domain of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, inconceivable,

children.text: harṣita jinasutāḥ sagauravāḥ puṣpamegha nabhataḥ pramuñciṣuḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, joyful and respectful, released clouds of flowers from the sky. // 1 //

children.text: sādhu sādhu girisārasākaya (?) deśito viduna śīlasaṃvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Excellent, excellent, O essence of the mountain (?), the <s>śīla</s>-discipline (moral conduct) has been taught by the wise one,

children.text: sarvasattvakaruṇāya āśayo bhūmiśreṣṭha dvitiyāya gocaraḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: The intention of compassion for all beings, the domain of the excellent second stage. // 2 //

children.text: bhūtatattva vitathāmananyathā bodhisasattvacaraṇaṃ manoramam /
children.translated_text: The true reality, not false and not otherwise — the delightful practice of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>,

children.text: sarvalokahitaśaukhyacintanā deśitaṃ tu paramaprabhāsvaram // 3 //
children.translated_text: The contemplation of welfare and happiness for all the world — has been taught as supremely radiant. // 3 //

children.text: bhūyu bhūyu naradevapūjitāṃ bhūmiśreṣṭha tṛtiyāmudāhara /
children.translated_text: Further, proclaim the excellent third stage, honored by gods and men,

children.text: dharmajñānakriyamukti sūcaya yādṛśo 'nubhava tādṛ(śo) gocaraḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: Indicate the <s>Dharma</s>-knowledge, action, and liberation — as is the experience, so is the domain. // 4 //

children.text: dānaśīlacaraṇaṃ maharṣiṇāṃ kṣāntivīryaśamaprajñupāyatām /
children.translated_text: The practice of generosity and moral conduct of the great sages, patience, energy, tranquility, wisdom, and skillful means,

children.text: maitraśreṣṭha karuṇāya mārgaṇaṃ bhāṣadhvaṃ jinacarīviśodhanam // 5 //
children.translated_text: The excellent <s>Maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and the pursuit of compassion — speak of this purification of the practice of the <s>Jinas</s>! // 5 //

body.text: vimukticandra uvāca vajragarbhaviśāradam / tṛtīyā saṃkramantānāmāśayaṃ bhaṇa sūraṇa // 6 //
body.translated_text: <s>Vimukticandra</s> spoke to <s>Vajragarbha</s> the skilled one: 'Declare the intention of those entering the third [stage], O hero!' // 6 //

body.text: upasaṃhāragāthāḥ /
body.translated_text: Summary verses:

children.text: te śuddha-āśaya guṇākara tīkṣṇacittā nirviṇṇa rāgavigatā anivartiyāśca /
children.translated_text: Those of pure intention, repositories of virtues, sharp-minded, disenchanted, free from passion, and irreversible,

children.text: dṛḍhacitta taptadhṛtiyukti udāravegā māhātmyatāśayavidū tṛtiyākramanti // 7 //
children.translated_text: Of firm mind, joined with ardent steadfastness, of noble vigor, knowing the greatness of intention — they enter the third [stage]. // 7 //

children.text: atra sthitā vidu prabhākaribhūmideśe duḥkhaṃ anityamaśuciṃ ca pralopadharmam /
children.translated_text: Those wise ones established here, in the domain of the <s>Prabhākarī</s> (Illuminating) stage, [contemplate] suffering, impermanence, impurity, and the nature of destruction,

children.text: acirasthitāka kṣaṇikaṃ ca nirodhakaṃ ca vicinanti saṃskṛtagatīkamanāgatīkam // 8 //
children.translated_text: Not long-lasting, momentary, and subject to cessation — they investigate the conditioned, its coming and going. // 8 //

children.text: te rogabhūtasahaśokaparadevanaṃ ca sopāyasaṃ ca priya apriyatānubaddham /
children.translated_text: They [see] disease, danger, a hundred sorrows, lamentation, and wailing, and pain, bound to the pleasant and the unpleasant,

children.text: duḥkhadaurmanasyanilayaṃ jvalitāgnikalpaṃ paśyanti saṃskṛtamananta samujjvalanti // 9 //
children.translated_text: The abode of suffering and mental distress, blazing like fire — they see the conditioned as infinite and ablaze. // 9 //

children.text: udvigna sarva tribhave anapekṣacittā jñānābhilāṣa sugatānamananyabuddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Alarmed in all three existences, with minds free from attachment, longing for the knowledge of the <s>Sugatas</s>, with no other thought,

children.text: avicintiyaṃ atuliyaṃ asamantapāraṃ saṃpaśyate nirupatāpa jināna jñānam // 10 //
children.translated_text: They behold the knowledge of the <s>Jinas</s> — inconceivable, incomparable, boundless, free from affliction. // 10 //

children.text: te buddhajñāna nirupadravamīkṣamāṇā atrāṇa nātharahitā vrajate caranti /
children.translated_text: Beholding the <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge as free from calamity, [they see beings] without shelter, without a protector, wandering and moving about,

children.text: nityaṃ daridra tribhiragnibhi saṃpradīptā bhavacārake dukhaśatairvinibaddhacittāḥ // 11 //
children.translated_text: Always impoverished, ablaze with the three fires, with minds bound in the wandering of existence by hundreds of sufferings. // 11 //

children.text: kleśāvṛtāśca avilokana chandahīnāḥ sugatāna dharmaratanānupranaṣṭa bālāḥ /
children.translated_text: Covered by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), without vision, lacking desire [for liberation], foolish ones for whom the jewel of the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Sugatas</s> is lost,

children.text: saṃsārasrota-anuvāhina mokṣatrastā me trāyitavya dṛḍha vīrya samārabhante // 12 //
children.translated_text: Carried along in the stream of <s>Saṃsāra</s>, frightened of liberation — 'I must rescue them!' — they undertake firm and vigorous effort. // 12 //

children.text: jñānābhilāṣa anapekṣa jagārthacārī vyuparīkṣate katama hetu jagasya mokṣe /
children.translated_text: Longing for knowledge, without attachment, acting for the world's benefit, one investigates: 'What is the cause for the liberation of the world?'

children.text: nānyatra nāvaraṇajñāna tathāgatānāṃ jñānaṃ ca prajñaprabhavaṃ sugatānanantam // 13 //
children.translated_text: 'There is no [cause] other than the unobstructed knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and knowledge is born of <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom); the <s>Sugatas</s> are infinite.' // 13 //

children.text: prajñā śrutāttu iti cintayi bodhisattvo jñātvā tamārabhati vīrya śrutārthacārī /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> reflects: '<s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom) comes from learning' — knowing this, one undertakes effort, practicing what is learned,

children.text: rātriṃdivaṃ śravaṇahetu ananyakarmā arthārthiko bhavati dharmaparāyaṇaśca // 14 //
children.translated_text: Day and night, for the sake of hearing [the <s>Dharma</s>], with no other occupation — one becomes a seeker of meaning and devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>. // 14 //

children.text: maṇimuktiratnanilayān priyabāndhavāṃśca rājyaṃ ananta vividhān pura sthānaśreṣṭhān /
children.translated_text: Abodes of jewels, pearls, and gems, beloved relatives, kingdoms without end, various excellent cities and dwellings,

children.text: bhāryāsutāṃśca parivāra manonukūlān anapekṣacittu tyajate vidu dharmahetoḥ // 15 //
children.translated_text: Wives and sons, attendants agreeable to the mind — the wise one gives them all up with a mind free from attachment, for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s>. // 15 //

children.text: śira hastapāda nayana svakamātmamāṃsaṃ jihvā ca daṃṣṭra śrava nāsika śoṇitaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Head, hands, feet, eyes, one's own flesh and body, tongue, teeth, ears, nose, and blood,

children.text: hṛdayaṃ tupādya priya majja parityajanti nā duṣkaretamatha duṣkara yacchṛṇoti // 16 //
children.translated_text: Even the heart, dear [to one], marrow — they give up; nor is it difficult for them, yet what they hear of is [truly] difficult to do. // 16 //

children.text: yadi kaścidenamupagamya vadeyya evaṃ yadi agnigarbha prapate jvalitāpi ghoram /
children.translated_text: If someone were to approach and say thus: 'If you would plunge into the fiery pit, terrible and blazing,

children.text: prāpiṣya dharmaratanaṃ sugatopanītaṃ śrutvā adīnamanasaḥ prapate guṇārthī // 17 //
children.translated_text: You shall obtain the jewel of the <s>Dharma</s> offered by the <s>Sugata</s>' — hearing this, undaunted in mind, the seeker of virtue plunges in. // 17 //

children.text: ekasya dharmapada artha sumerumūrdhnā trisahasra agnirucitaṃ api brahmalokāt /
children.translated_text: For the meaning of a single word of <s>Dharma</s>, from the summit of <s>Sumeru</s>, even through fire blazing up to the <s>Brahmaloka</s>,

children.text: sūdūrlabhā imi jinasya udārabodhiḥ ye mānuṣyeṇa sukha labhyati evarūpam // 18 //
children.translated_text: 'This noble <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening) of the <s>Jina</s> is extremely rare to obtain — how fortunate that it is easily obtained through human [birth] of such a kind!' // 18 //

children.text: yāvattareṇa pavararṣiṇa jñānalābhastāvattaraṃ dukhamavīcikamutsahyami /
children.translated_text: 'To the extent that there is gain of knowledge for the excellent sages, to that extent I shall endure suffering, even that of <s>Avīci</s> [hell],

children.text: kiṃ vā punarvividhamānuṣaduḥkhaskandhaṃ hantābhyupemi varadharmipadārthiduḥkham // 19 //
children.translated_text: How much more then the manifold mass of human suffering — indeed, I shall undergo suffering for the sake of the excellent word of <s>Dharma</s>!' // 19 //

children.text: dharmaṃ ca śrutva puna yoniṣu cintayāti dhyānāpramāṇa caturaśca tathā arūpyā /
children.translated_text: And having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, one then reflects upon it thoroughly — the <s>Dhyānas</s> (meditations), the four <s>Apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables), and likewise the <s>Ārūpyas</s> (formless attainments),

children.text: pañcāpyabhijña pravarā abhinirharanti nā cāpi teṣu vaśitā upapadya yāti // 20 //
children.translated_text: They also bring forth the five excellent <s>Abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), yet they do not proceed to rebirth under their mastery. // 20 //

children.text: atra sthitā guṇadharā bahubuddhakoṭyaḥ pūjyanti niścitamanā śṛṇuvanti dharmam /
children.translated_text: Those established here, endowed with virtues, worship <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>Buddhas</s>, with resolute minds they hear the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: tanubhūtva mithyapagatāḥ pariśuddhayanti svarṇe yathā vigatadoṣa pramāṇatulyam // 21 //
children.translated_text: Having become subtle, free from error, they are purified — like gold freed from defects, of equal measure. // 21 //

children.text: atra sthitā guṇadharāstridaśādhipatyaṃ kārenti īśvara nivartitu kāmarāgāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those established here, endowed with virtues, exercise sovereignty over the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods, as lords, turning [beings] away from sensual desire,

children.text: marusaṃgha nekavividhān kuśalāna mārge sthāpentyananyamana buddhaguṇābhilāṣe // 22 //
children.translated_text: They establish multitudes of <s>Māras</s> of various kinds on the path of the wholesome, with single-minded longing for the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>. // 22 //

children.text: atra sthitā jinasutā viriyārabhante labdhvā samādhina sahasraśataṃ anūnam /
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Jinas</s> established here undertake effort, having obtained no less than a hundred thousand <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations),

children.text: paśyanti buddhavara lakṣaṇacitrigātrāṃ bhūyo ataḥ praṇidhiśreṣṭha guṇāpramāṇāḥ // 23 //
children.translated_text: They see the excellent <s>Buddhas</s> with bodies adorned with the [major] marks — and beyond this, through excellent vows, their virtues are immeasurable. // 23 //

body.text: ityeṣā tṛtiyā bhūminirdiṣṭā sugatātmajāḥ / sarvalokahitaiṣīṇāṃ bodhisattvānanuttamā // 24 //
body.translated_text: Thus has been taught this third stage, O sons of the <s>Sugatas</s>, the unsurpassed [stage] of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who seek the welfare of all the world. // 24 //

body.text:
4 arciṣmatī nāma caturthī bhūmiḥ /
upakramagāthāḥ /
body.translated_text:
4. The fourth stage called <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (Radiant).
Introductory verses:

children.text: evaṃ śrūṇitva caraṇaṃ vipulaṃ bhūmyuttamaṃ manuramaṃ pravaram /
children.translated_text: Having thus heard this vast, supreme, delightful, and excellent practice-stage,

children.text: saṃharṣitā jinasutāttamanā abhyokiranti kusumebhi jinam // 1 //
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, joyful and delighted, shower the <s>Jina</s> with flowers. // 1 //

children.text: saṃkampitā lavaṇatoyadharā iha dharmadeśanamudīrayatām /
children.translated_text: The salt-water-bearing [clouds] tremble as this <s>Dharma</s>-teaching is proclaimed,

children.text: marukanyakā abhimanorucirāḥ saṃgītiyukta varadharmaratāḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Māra</s>-maidens, exceedingly beautiful, are devoted to the excellent <s>Dharma</s>, engaged in song. // 2 //

children.text: vaśavarti devapatirāttamanā maṇiratna divya sugatasya kṣipī /
children.translated_text: <s>Vaśavartin</s>, the lord of the gods, delighted, casts divine jewel-gems before the <s>Sugata</s>,

children.text: vācaṃ abhāṣi atha eva jino utpanna artha guṇapāragato // 3 //
children.translated_text: And utters these words: 'The <s>Jina</s> has arisen, one who has gone to the far shore of purpose and virtue!' // 3 //

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tatha hi dharmavaraṃ saṃbodhisattvacaraṇaṃ paramam /
children.translated_text: For what reason is this excellent <s>Dharma</s>, the supreme practice of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>,

children.text: bhūmirvidū na iyamadya śrutā yasyāśravo durlabha kalpaśataiḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: This stage of the wise one, not heard today — hearing of which is rare even in hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons)? // 4 //

children.text: bhūyaḥ prabhāṣa naradevahitā caryāvarāṃ jinasutān vidū /
children.translated_text: Speak further of the excellent conduct beneficial to gods and humans, O wise sons of the <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: śroṣyanti te marutasaṃghagaṇā bhūtaṃ viniścayamananyapadam // 5 //
children.translated_text: the hosts and assemblies of <s>Maruts</s> shall hear the truth, the certain determination that has no other ground. // 5 //

children.text: vimukticandraḥ punarvīro ālapī sugatātmajam /
children.translated_text: <s>Vimukticandra</s>, the hero, again addressed the son of the <s>Sugata</s>:

children.text: caturthī saṃkramantānāṃ gocaraṃ bhaṇa uttamam // 6 //
children.translated_text: "Describe the supreme domain of those entering the fourth [stage]." // 6 //

children.text: upasaṃhāragāthāḥ /
children.translated_text: Summary verses (<s>upasaṃhāragāthāḥ</s>):

children.text: parikarmitā tṛtīyabhūmiprabhaṃkarāya sattvacaryaloka tatha dharma vicāryamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having been prepared for the third stage, <s>Prabhāṃkarā</s> (Radiant), contemplating the conduct of beings, the world, and the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: ākāśadhātu manadhātu trayaśca dhātu adhimukti āśaya viśuddhi samākramanti // 7 //
children.translated_text: they enter into the purification of the space-element, mind-element, and the three elements, of aspiration and intention. // 7 //

body.text: sahaprāptu arciṣmati bhūmi mahānubhāvaḥ saṃvṛttu śāstu kulu bhūyu vivartiyatve /
body.translated_text: Having attained the <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (Blazing) stage, the one of great power, established in the lineage of the Teacher, further advances in irreversibility,

body.text: abhedya buddharatane tatha dharmasaṃghe udayavyayasthiti nirīhaka prekṣamāṇaḥ // 8 //
body.translated_text: unshakable in the jewel of the <s>Buddha</s> and in the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Saṃgha</s>, observing arising, cessation, and stability without any agency. // 8 //

children.text: lokapravṛtti kriyakarma bhavopapattiṃ saṃsāranirvṛtivibhāvana kṣetrasattvān /
children.translated_text: The operation of the world, actions and deeds, birth and rebirth in existence, the contemplation of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation), realms and beings,

children.text: dharmāñca pūrvamaparānta kṣayānutpādaṃ saṃvṛttu bhāvayati śāstu kulānuvartī // 9 //
children.translated_text: <s>dharmas</s> of the past and future, their destruction and non-arising — established [thus], the follower of the Teacher's lineage cultivates [these]. // 9 //

children.text: so eṣu dharmu samupetu hitānukampī bhāveti kāyamapi vedana cittadharmān /
children.translated_text: He, having acquired these <s>dharmas</s>, compassionate for the welfare [of beings], cultivates body, feelings, mind, and mental phenomena,

children.text: adhyātmabāhyubhayathā vidu bhāvayāti smṛtyopasthānabhāvana niketavarjitā // 10 //
children.translated_text: the wise one cultivates internally, externally, and in both ways — the cultivation of the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), free from attachment. // 10 //

children.text: pāpakṣayātkuśaladharmavivardhitā ca samyakprahāṇa caturo vidu bhāvayanti /
children.translated_text: Through the destruction of evil and the increase of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, the wise ones cultivate the four <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions),

children.text: catuṛddhipāda bala indriya bhāvayanti bodhyaṅgaratna ruciraṃ tatha mārga śreṣṭham // 11 //
children.translated_text: they cultivate the four <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power), the powers, the faculties, the resplendent jewel of the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), and the supreme path. // 11 //

children.text: bhāventi tān janayatāṃ samavekṣya buddhim upastambhayanti praṇidhiṃ kṛtapūrvamaitrāḥ /
children.translated_text: They cultivate those, and for those who generate [wholesome qualities], examining with wisdom, they uphold the vow, having previously established <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness),

children.text: sarvajñajñānamabhiprārthana buddhakṣetraṃ balaśreṣṭhamuttamapathaṃ anucintayantaḥ // 12 //
children.translated_text: aspiring for the knowledge of omniscience, the <s>Buddha</s>-field, the supreme powers, and the highest path, contemplating [these]. // 12 //

children.text: vaiśāradaṃ api ca dharma ahārya śāstuḥ varavuddhaghoṣamabhiprārthayamāna dhīrāḥ /
children.translated_text: The steadfast ones, aspiring for the <s>vaiśāradya</s> (fearlessness), the irreversible <s>dharmas</s> of the Teacher, and the excellent voice of the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: gambhīramārgaratanaṃ ca vimokṣasthānaṃ mahatāmupāya samudāgama bhāvayanti // 13 //
children.translated_text: cultivate the jewel of the profound path and the station of liberation, the attainment of skillful means of the great ones. // 13 //

children.text: satkāyadṛṣṭivigatāśca dviṣaṣṭidṛṣṭī attāttamīyavigatāstatha jīvalābham /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the self-existent body) and the sixty-two views, free from [notions of] self and mine, and likewise [the view of] a life-soul,

children.text: skandhāstu dvāra tatha dhātuniketasthānaṃ sarvaprahāṇa viduṣaṃ catuthāya bhūmyām // 14 //
children.translated_text: the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), sense-doors, and elements as abiding places — all are abandoned by the wise ones on the fourth stage. // 14 //

children.text: so yānimāni sugatena vivarṇitāni karmāṇi kleśasahajāni anarthakāni /
children.translated_text: Those actions that have been described by the <s>Sugata</s> as innate to defilements and as purposeless,

children.text: tāni prahāya vidu āśayato viśuddhā dharmārabhanti kuśalaṃ jagaûtāyaṇārtham // 15 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned those, the wise ones, purified in intention, undertake wholesome <s>dharmas</s> for the welfare of the world. // 15 //

body.text: susnigdhacitta bhavatī vidu apramatto mṛducittu sārjava hitāsukha-āvahaśca /
body.translated_text: The wise one becomes tender-minded and vigilant, soft in mind, upright, and bringing welfare and happiness,

body.text: aparikliṣṭaśca parimārgati uttamārthaṃ jñānābhiṣekamabhilāṣi jagārthacārī // 16 //
body.translated_text: and unafflicted, seeking the supreme goal, aspiring for the consecration of knowledge, acting for the welfare of the world. // 16 //

children.text: gurugauraveṣupagataḥ pratipattikāmo bhavate kṛtajña sumanāśca akūhakāśca /
children.translated_text: Endowed with reverence for teachers, desiring practice, grateful, good-minded, and free from deceit,

children.text: nirmāyatāgahana āśayasūrataśca avivartyavīryu bhavate samudānayantaḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: free from the thicket of pretense, pure in intention, with irreversible vigor, they bring [qualities] to completion. // 17 //

children.text: tasyātra bhūmi rucirāya pratiṣṭhitasya adhyāśayaṃ api ca śuddhamupeti dharmam /
children.translated_text: For one established on this resplendent stage, the <s>Dharma</s> and pure aspiration are attained,

children.text: adhimukti tapyati vivardhati śukladharmo malakalmaṣaṃ vimati śaṃśaya sarva yānti // 18 //
children.translated_text: aspiration burns bright, white <s>dharmas</s> increase, and all stains, defilements, doubts, and uncertainties depart. // 18 //

children.text: atra sthitā naravararṣabha bodhisattvāḥ sugatānanekanayutānabhipūjayanti /
children.translated_text: Established here, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, bulls among the best of men, worship <s>Sugatas</s> in many <s>nayutas</s> (myriads),

children.text: śṛṇvanti dharma yatha śāsani pravrajanti asaṃhārya śakya kṛtakāñcanabhūṣaṇaṃ vā // 19 //
children.translated_text: they hear the <s>Dharma</s>, go forth in accordance with the teaching — they are as indestructible as ornaments made of refined gold. // 19 //

children.text: atra sthitāna vidunā guṇamāśayaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Of those wise ones established here, the qualities and intentions,

children.text: jñānaṃ upāya caraṇaṃ ca viśuddhimārgaḥ /
children.translated_text: knowledge, skillful means, conduct, and the path of purification

children.text: no śakyu māranayutebhi nivartanāya ratnaprabheva yatha varṣajalairahāryā // 20 //
children.translated_text: cannot be turned back by <s>Māra</s>'s myriads — like the luster of a gem that cannot be carried away by rain-water. // 20 //

children.text: atra sthitā naramarudgaṇapūjanārhā bhontī suyāmapatirīśvara dharmacārī /
children.translated_text: Established here, they are worthy of worship by hosts of humans and <s>Maruts</s>, becoming lords of the <s>Suyāma</s> [heaven], <s>Īśvara</s>, practicing the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: sattvāni dṛṣṭigahanādvinivartayanti saṃbhārayanti kuśalā jinajñānahetoḥ // 21 //
children.translated_text: they turn beings away from the thicket of wrong views and accumulate wholesome [merit] for the sake of the <s>Jina</s>'s knowledge. // 21 //

children.text: viryopapeta śatakoṭi mararṣabhāṇāṃ paśyantyananyamanasaḥ susamāhitatvāt /
children.translated_text: Endowed with vigor, they behold hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of the best of <s>Maras</s> (sages) with undistracted mind, due to perfect concentration,

children.text: tata uttariṃ bahukalpamabhinirharanti jñānākarā praṇidhiśreṣṭha guṇārthacārī // 22 //
children.translated_text: and further, over many <s>kalpas</s>, they bring forth [their vows] — mines of knowledge, with supreme vows, acting for the purpose of qualities. // 22 //

body.text: caturthī itiyaṃ bhūmirviśuddhā śubhacāriṇī / guṇārthajñānayuktānāṃ nirdiṣṭā sugatātmajāḥ // 23 //
body.translated_text: This fourth stage is pure, of beautiful conduct, declared for the sons of the <s>Sugata</s> who are endowed with qualities, purpose, and knowledge. // 23 //

body.text:
5 sudurjayā nāma pañcamī bhūmiḥ /
upakramagāthāḥ /
body.translated_text: 5. The fifth stage, named <s>Sudurjayā</s> (Very Difficult to Conquer). Introductory verses (<s>upakramagāthāḥ</s>):

children.text: caraṇamatha śruṇitvā bhūmiśreṣṭhāṃ vidūnāṃ jinasuta parituṣṭā harṣitā dharmahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard of the excellent conduct and the supreme stage of the wise ones, the sons of the <s>Jina</s>, delighted and joyful for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: gagani kusumavarṣaṃ utsṛjantī udagrāḥ sādhu sugataputra vyāhṛtaṃ te mahātmā // 1 //
children.translated_text: releasing showers of flowers in the sky, exultant [they cry]: "Well spoken, O son of the <s>Sugata</s>, O great-souled one!" // 1 //

children.text: marupati vaśavartī sārdha devāgaṇena svagagata sugatasya pūjānārthaṃ udagrā /
children.translated_text: <s>Marupati Vaśavartī</s> (the lord of gods who controls others), together with the host of gods, exultant for the purpose of worshipping the <s>Sugata</s> in his own sky,

children.text: vividharucirameghāḥ snigdha-ābhā manojñāḥ abhikira sugatasya harṣitāḥ prīṇitāśca // 2 //
children.translated_text: with various resplendent clouds, tender in radiance, delightful — they shower upon the <s>Sugata</s>, joyful and pleased. // 2 //

children.text: gītaruta manojñā vādyatūryābhinādā devavadhuprayuktāḥ śāstu saṃpūjanārtham /
children.translated_text: Delightful songs and sounds, the resounding of musical instruments and drums, employed by divine maidens for the worship of the Teacher,

children.text: jina puna tatharūpaṃ darśayanti sma sthānaṃ sarvarutasvarebhī eva śabdaḥ prayuktaḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Jina</s> then displays such a state: from all tones and voices, just this sound is produced: // 3 //

children.text: sucireṇa āśayu prapūrṇa muneḥ sucireṇa bodhi śiva prāpta jinaḥ /
children.translated_text: "After a long time, the aspiration of the Sage is fulfilled; after a long time, the <s>Jina</s> has attained auspicious awakening;

children.text: sucireṇa dṛṣṭa naradevahitaḥ saṃprāpta devapuri śākyamuniḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: after a long time, the benefactor of gods and humans is seen; <s>Śākyamuni</s> has arrived in the city of the gods." // 4 //

children.text: sucireṇa sāgarajalāḥ kṣubhitāḥ sucireṇa ābha śubha munni jane /
children.translated_text: "After a long time, the ocean waters are stirred; after a long time, the auspicious radiance [shines] among the Sage's people;

children.text: sucireṇa sattva sukhitāḥ sucireṇa śāsu śruta kāruṇikaḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: after a long time, beings are made happy; after a long time, the teaching of the Compassionate One is heard." // 5 //

children.text: sucireṇa saṃgamu mahāmuninā saṃprāpta sarvagūṇapāramitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "After a long time, there is meeting with the Great Sage who has attained all excellent qualities and <s>pāramitās</s>;

children.text: mada māna darpa prajahitva tamaṃ pūjārhu pūjima mahāśramaṇam // 6 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned the darkness of pride, conceit, and arrogance, let us worship the Great <s>Śramaṇa</s>, worthy of worship." // 6 //

children.text: (iha pūji kṛtva khagamārgagatā) iha pūji kṛtva sukha nekavidham /
children.translated_text: ("Having worshipped here, they go to the path of the sky") "Having worshipped here, there is happiness of many kinds;

children.text: iha pūji kṛtva dukhasarvakṣaye iha pūji kṛtva jina jñānavaram // 7 //
children.translated_text: having worshipped here, there is the destruction of all suffering; having worshipped here, there is the supreme knowledge of the <s>Jina</s>." // 7 //

body.text: gaganopamaḥ paramuśuddhu jinu jagatī aliptu yatha padmu jale /
body.translated_text: "The <s>Jina</s> is like the sky, supremely pure; unstained in the world like a lotus in water;

body.text: abhyudgato udadhi meruriva harṣitva cittu jina pūjayathā // 8 //
body.translated_text: risen above [the ocean] like <s>Meru</s> above the sea — with joyful hearts, worship the <s>Jina</s>!" // 8 //

children.text: athābravīdvajragarbhaṃ vimukticandro viśāradaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vimukticandra</s>, the confident one, addressed <s>Vajragarbha</s>:

children.text: pañcamyā bhūmya ākarān nirdiśasva viśārada // 10 //
children.translated_text: "Describe the characteristics of the fifth stage, O confident one." // 10 //

body.text: upasaṃhāragāthāḥ /
body.translated_text: Summary verses (<s>upasaṃhāragāthāḥ</s>):

children.text: evaṃ viśodhita caturṣu jinacarīṣu buddhayā triyādhvasamatā anucintayanti /
children.translated_text: Thus, having purified conduct in the four [stages] of the <s>Jina</s>, with wisdom they contemplate the equality of the three times,

children.text: śīlaṃ ca cittapratipattitu mārgaśuddhiḥ kāṅkṣāvinīta vidu pañcami ākramanti // 11 //
children.translated_text: morality, mind, practice, and purity of the path — the wise ones, freed from doubt, enter the fifth [stage]. // 11 //

children.text: smṛti cāpa indriya iṣu anivartitāśca samyakprahāṇa haya vāhana ṛddhipādāḥ /
children.translated_text: Mindfulness as armor, faculties as arrows, irreversible, the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions) as horses, the <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of power) as vehicles,

children.text: pañca balāḥ kavaca sarvapipū-abhebyāḥ śūrāṇivarti vidu pañcami ākramanti // 12 //
children.translated_text: the five <s>balas</s> (powers) as armor impenetrable to all enemies — like heroes, the wise ones enter the fifth [stage]. // 12 //

children.text: hyapatrāpyavastravidunāṃ śuciśīlagandho bodhyaṅgamālyavaradhyānavilepanaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: The garment of moral shame for the wise, the fragrance of pure morality, the garland of the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (awakening-factors), the ointment of fine meditation,

children.text: prajñāvicāraṇavibhūṣaṇupāyaśreṣṭham udyānadhāraṇita pañcamimākramanti // 13 //
children.translated_text: the adornment of investigation through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), the supreme skillful means, the garden of <s>dhāraṇī</s> — [thus] they enter the fifth [stage]. // 13 //

children.text: catuṛddhipādacaraṇāḥ smṛtiśuddhigrīvāḥ kṛpamaitraśreṣṭhanayanā varaprajñadaṃṣṭrā /
children.translated_text: With the <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of power) as feet, mindfulness-purity as neck, compassion and loving-kindness as supreme eyes, excellent wisdom as fangs,

children.text: nairātmyanāda ripukleśa pradharṣamāṇā narasiṃha samya vidu pañcamimākramanti // 14 //
children.translated_text: roaring the roar of non-self, vanquishing the enemy of defilements — like lions among men, the wise ones rightly enter the fifth [stage]. // 14 //

children.text: te pañcamīmupagatā varabhūmiśreṣṭhāṃ pariśuddhamārga śubhamuttari bhāvayanti /
children.translated_text: Having reached the fifth, the supreme and excellent stage, they cultivate the pure, auspicious, and higher path,

children.text: śuddhāśayā vidu jinatvanuprāpaṇārthī kṛpamaitrakhedavigatā anucintayanti // 15 //
children.translated_text: the wise ones of pure intention, seeking the attainment of <s>Jina</s>-hood, free from the weariness of compassion and loving-kindness, contemplate [thus]. // 15 //

children.text: saṃbhārapuṇyupacayā tatha jñāna śreṣṭhaṃ naikā upāya abhirocanabhūmya bhāsān /
children.translated_text: The accumulation of merit and the supreme knowledge, many skillful means, the splendors of the illuminating stage,

children.text: buddhadhiṣṭhāna smṛtimāṃ matibuddhiprāptā cattvāri satya nikhilānanucintayanti // 16 //
children.translated_text: empowered by the <s>Buddha</s>, possessed of mindfulness, understanding, and wisdom — they contemplate the four truths in their entirety. // 16 //

children.text: paramārthasatyamapi saṃvṛtilakṣaṇaṃ ca satyavibhāgamatha satyanitīraṇaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: The truth of ultimate reality (<s>paramārthasatya</s>) and the characteristic of conventional [truth] (<s>saṃvṛtilakṣaṇa</s>), the analysis of truth and the determination of truth,

children.text: tatha vastu sāsrava kṣayaṃ api mārgasatyaṃ yāvantanāvaraṇasatya samosaranti // 17 //
children.translated_text: likewise conditioned things with outflows, their destruction, and the truth of the path — they enter into the truth of non-obstruction. // 17 //

children.text: evaṃ ca satya parimārgati sūkṣmabuddhiḥ na ca tāvadanāvaraṇaprāptu vimokṣaṃ śreṣṭham /
children.translated_text: Thus one of subtle wisdom investigates the truths, yet does not attain the supreme unobstructed liberation,

children.text: jñānādhimuktivipulāttu guṇākarāṇām atibhonti sarvajagato arhapratyayānām // 18 //
children.translated_text: due to the vast aspiration and knowledge, those mines of virtues surpass all the world's <s>Arhats</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. // 18 //

children.text: so eva satya-abhinirhṛta tattvabuddhiḥ jānāti saṃskṛta mṛṣāprakṛtī asāram /
children.translated_text: He, with the wisdom of reality produced from those truths, knows the conditioned as false, without inherent nature, and without essence,

children.text: kṛpamaitra-ābha labhate sugatāna bhūyaḥ sattvārthikaḥ sugatajñāna gaveṣamāṇaḥ // 19 //
children.translated_text: he obtains the radiance of compassion and loving-kindness of the <s>Sugatas</s> further — seeking the welfare of beings, aspiring for the knowledge of the <s>Sugata</s>. // 19 //

children.text: pūrvāpare vidu nirīkṣatu saṃskṛtasya mohāndhakāratamasāvṛta duḥkhalagnā /
children.translated_text: The wise one examines the conditioned in its past and future: beings caught in suffering, enveloped in the darkness and gloom of delusion,

children.text: abhyuddharoti jagato dukhaskandhavṛddhān nairātmyajīvarahitāṃstṛṇakāṣṭhatulyān // 20 //
children.translated_text: he lifts up the world, burdened with heaps of suffering, devoid of self and soul, equal to grass and sticks. // 20 //

children.text: kleśādvayena yugapatpunarbhāsi tryadhvaṃ chedo dukhasya na ca anta samosarantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the twofold defilement, he illuminates the three times simultaneously; there is severance of suffering, yet they do not reach its end;

children.text: hanto praṇaṣṭa jana te 'tidayābhijātā saṃsārasrota na nivartati niḥsvabhāvam // 21 //
children.translated_text: "Alas, these beings are lost!" — born of great compassion, the stream of <s>saṃsāra</s> does not turn back, being without inherent nature. // 21 //

children.text: skandhālayā uragadhātu kudṛṣṭiśalyāḥ saṃtapta agnihṛdayāvṛta andhakāre /
children.translated_text: With the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) as abode, the elements as serpents, pierced by the thorns of wrong views, burning with the fire in their hearts, enveloped in darkness,

children.text: tṛṣṇārṇavaprapatitā avalokanatvāt jinasārthavāhavirahā dukha-arṇavasthāḥ // 22 //
children.translated_text: fallen into the ocean of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), without anyone to look upon [them], bereft of the <s>Jina</s> as caravan-leader, abiding in the ocean of suffering. // 22 //

children.text: evaṃ viditva punarārabhate 'pramatto
children.translated_text: Having known thus, he again exerts himself, vigilant,

children.text: taccaiva ārabhati sarvajagadvimokṣī /
children.translated_text: and undertakes that very [task] for the liberation of all the world;

children.text: smṛtimantu bhonti matimān gatimān dhṛtīṃ ca
children.translated_text: they become mindful, wise, possessed of understanding and fortitude,

children.text: hrīmāṃśca bhonti tatha buddhina prajñavāṃśca // 23 //
children.translated_text: and they are endowed with modesty, and with intelligence and wisdom. // 23 //

children.text: avitṛptu puṇyupacaye tatha jñāna śreṣṭhaṃ no khedavānna śithilo balameṣamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Insatiable in the accumulation of merit and in supreme knowledge, neither weary nor lax, seeking strength,

children.text: kṣetraṃ vidhāya jinalakṣaṇabuddhaghoṣam avitṛptasarvakriya sattvahitārthayuktaḥ // 24 //
children.translated_text: having established the field, the marks of the <s>Jina</s>, and the voice of the <s>Buddha</s>, insatiable in all activities, devoted to the welfare of beings. // 24 //

children.text: paripācanāya jagato vidu śilpasthānān lipimudrasaṃkhyagaṇadhātucikitsatantrān /
children.translated_text: For the maturation of the world, the wise ones [teach] the arts and crafts — writing, seals, mathematics, computation, metallurgy, and medical treatises,

children.text: bhūtagrahāviṣamaroganivartanārthaṃ sthāpenti śastra rucirān kṛpamaitrabuddhī // 25 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of averting possessions by spirits, poisoning, and diseases — they establish resplendent treatises, with minds of compassion and loving-kindness. // 25 //

children.text: varakāvyanāṭakamatiṃ vividhapraharṣān nadyodiyānaphalapuṣpanipadyasthānān /
children.translated_text: With the understanding of excellent poetry and drama, various delights, rivers, gardens, fruits, flowers, and groves,

children.text: sthāpenti nekakriya sattvasukhāpanārthaṃ ratnākarāṃśca upadarśayi naikarūpān // 26//
children.translated_text: they establish many activities for bringing happiness to beings, and display mines of jewels of various kinds. // 26 //

children.text: bhūmīcalaṃ ca graha jyotiṣa candrasūryau sarvāṅgalakṣaṇavicāraṇarājyasthānam /
children.translated_text: Earthquakes, planets, astrology, the moon and sun, examination of all bodily marks, and the domain of kingship,
