children.text: ārūpyadhyāna tathabhijña athāpramāṇā abhinirharanti hitasaukhyajagārthakāmāḥ // 27 //
children.translated_text: formless meditations, likewise <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and the <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables) — they bring these forth, desiring welfare, happiness, and the benefit of the world. // 27 //

children.text: iha durjayāmupajatā varaprajñacārī pūjenti buddha nayutā śṛṇuvanti dharmam /
children.translated_text: Having reached this <s>Durjayā</s> (Difficult to Conquer [stage]), practitioners of excellent wisdom worship <s>Buddhas</s> in <s>nayutas</s> and hear the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: teṣāṃ śubhaṃ punaruttapyati āśayaśca svarṇaṃ yathā musaragalvayasaṃvimṛṣṭam // 28 //
children.translated_text: their virtue and intention are further refined, like gold polished with <s>musāragalva</s> (coral). // 28 //

children.text: ratnāmayā grahavimān vahanti vātā te yehi tehi tu vahanti asaṃhṛtāśca /
children.translated_text: Winds carry jewel-made planetary vehicles, and by whatever [winds] they are carried, they are not destroyed;

children.text: tatha lokadharmi caramāna jagārthacārī asaṃhārya bhonti yatha padma jale aliptam // 29 //
children.translated_text: likewise, one practicing worldly <s>dharmas</s> while acting for the welfare of the world is indestructible, like a lotus unstained in water. // 29 //

children.text: atra sthitā tuṣita īśvara te kṛtāvī nāśenti tīrthyacaraṇān pṛthudṛṣṭisthānān /
children.translated_text: Established here, they become <s>Tuṣita</s> lords, <s>Īśvara</s>, accomplished ones; they destroy the doctrines of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (heretics) and the abodes of manifold wrong views;

children.text: yaccācaranti kuśalaṃ jinajñānahetoḥ sattvāna trāta bhavamo daśabhirbalāḍhyaiḥ // 30 //
children.translated_text: whatever wholesome [deeds] they perform for the sake of the <s>Jina</s>'s knowledge — "We shall be protectors of beings, endowed with the ten powers." // 30 //

children.text: te vīryamuttari samārabhi aramattāḥ koṭisahasra sugatānabhipūjayanti /
children.translated_text: They, vigilant, further exert supreme vigor and worship <s>Sugatas</s> in hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s>;

children.text: labdhvā samādhi vidu kampayi kṣetrakoṭī praṇidhīviśeṣu anubhūya guṇākarānām // 31//
children.translated_text: having attained <s>samādhi</s>, the wise ones cause <s>koṭīs</s> of fields to tremble, experiencing special vows, those mines of virtues. // 31 //

body.text: ityeṣā pañcamī bhūmirvicitropāyakoṭibhiḥ / nirdiṣṭā sattvasārāṇāmuttamā sugatātmajāḥ // 32 //
body.translated_text: This fifth stage, with its <s>koṭīs</s> of varied skillful means, has been declared as supreme for those whose essence is [the welfare of] beings, O sons of the <s>Sugata</s>. // 32 //

body.text:
6 abhimukhī nāma ṣaṣṭhī bhūmiḥ /
upakramagāthāḥ /
body.translated_text: 6. The sixth stage, named <s>Abhimukhī</s> (Facing Forward). Introductory verses (<s>upakramagāthāḥ</s>):

children.text: caraṇavara śruṇitvā bhūmiśreṣṭhaṃ vidūnāṃ gagani sugataputrā harṣitāḥ puṣpavarṣī /
children.translated_text: Having heard of the excellent supreme conduct and stage of the wise ones, the sons of the <s>Sugata</s> in the sky, joyful, [release] showers of flowers,

children.text: maṇiratana udārā ābhayuktā viśuddhā abhikira sugatasya sādhviti vyāharantaḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: with splendid gems and jewels, endowed with radiance, pure — they shower upon the <s>Sugata</s>, exclaiming: "Excellent!" // 1 //

children.text: maruta śatasahasrā harṣitā antarīkṣe diviya rucira citrā ratnacūrṇā udārāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of <s>Maruts</s>, joyful in the sky, with divine, resplendent, variegated, and splendid jewel-powders,

children.text: abhikira sugatebhyo gandhamālyānulepān chatradhvajāpatākāhāracandrārdhahārān // 2 //
children.translated_text: they shower upon the <s>Sugatas</s> fragrant garlands and ointments, parasols, banners, flags, necklaces, and crescent-moon ornaments. // 2 //

children.text: marupati vaśavartī sarvadevagaṇena upari khaga paṭhitvā megha ratnāmayāni /
children.translated_text: <s>Marupati Vaśavartī</s>, with all the host of gods, having spread above in the sky clouds made of jewels,

children.text: abhikiriṣu prasannaḥ pūjanārthaṃ jinasya sādhu sugataputrā vyāharī hṛṣṭacittāḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: showers them with devotion for the worship of the <s>Jina</s> — "Excellent, O sons of the <s>Sugata</s>!" they declare with joyful hearts. // 3 //

children.text: amaravadhusahasrāṇyantarīkṣe sthitāni gīta ruta manojñā vādyasaṃgītiyuktā /
children.translated_text: Thousands of divine maidens, stationed in the sky, with delightful songs and sounds, accompanied by musical concerts,

children.text: sarvarutasvarebhyo eva śabdā ravante jina kṛtu sumanojñaiḥ kleśatāpasya hantā // 4 //
children.translated_text: from all tones and voices, sounds resound: "The <s>Jina</s> has become the most delightful destroyer of the heat of defilements." // 4 //

children.text: śūnya prakṛtiśāntā sarvadharmānimittāḥ khagapathasamatulyā nirvikalpā viśuddhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Empty by nature, tranquil, all <s>dharmas</s> are without marks (<s>animitta</s>), equal to the path of the sky, free from conceptual elaboration, pure,

children.text: gatisthitivinirvṛttā niṣprapañcā aśeṣā tathatasama tathatvāddharmatā nirvikalpā // 5 //
children.translated_text: without course, abiding, or cessation, without proliferation, without remainder — equal to <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), by virtue of being such, <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of things) is free from conceptual elaboration. // 5 //

children.text: yaiḥ punaranubuddhāḥ sarvadharmeva teṣāṃ bhāvi tatha abhāve iñjanā nāsti kācit /
children.translated_text: Those by whom all <s>dharmas</s> are thus understood — for them, in being and non-being, there is no movement whatsoever;

children.text: kṛpa karuṇa jage ca mocanārthaṃ prayuktāste hi sugataputrā aurasā dharmajātāḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text: yet, impelled by compassion and <s>karuṇā</s> for the liberation of the world, they are indeed the natural-born sons of the <s>Sugata</s>, born of the <s>Dharma</s>. // 6 //

children.text: dānacari carante sarva hitvā nimittaṃ śīlasudhṛtacittāṃ ādiśāntā praśāntāḥ /
children.translated_text: They practice the conduct of <s>dāna</s> (generosity), having abandoned all marks; with well-maintained minds of morality, calmed from the beginning, tranquil,

children.text: jagati kṛta kṣamante akṣayā dharmajñānī viriyabalaupetāḥ sarvadharmāviviktāḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: they endure [all] in the world, inexhaustible, knowers of the <s>Dharma</s>; endowed with the power of vigor, [they know] all <s>dharmas</s> as not separate. // 7 //

body.text: dhyānanayapraviṣṭā jīrṇakleśā viśuddhāḥ sarvaviditavastū ādiśūnyādhimuktāḥ /
body.translated_text: Having entered the method of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), their defilements worn away, purified; knowing all things, with aspiration for primordial emptiness,

body.text: jñānakriyabalāḍhyā nityayuktā jagārthaṃ te hi sugataputrāḥ śāntapāpā mahātmāḥ // 8//
body.translated_text: Rich in the power of knowledge and action, ever devoted to the welfare of beings, these sons of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) are great beings with evil pacified. (8)

children.text: īdṛśā rutasahasra bhaṇitvā khe sthitāḥ sumadhurā surakanyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having uttered thousands of such verses, the divine maidens stood in the sky, sweet-voiced,

children.text: tūṣṇibhūta jinamīkṣi prasannā dharmagauravaratā marukanyāḥ // 9 //
children.translated_text: silent, gazing at the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) with serene faith, the celestial maidens devoted to reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>. (9)

body.text: vimukticandra abravīdvajragarbhaṃ viśāradam / kīdṛśākāraniṣpattiḥ pañcamāyāmanantaram // 10 //
body.translated_text: <s>Vimukticandra</s> addressed the wise <s>Vajragarbha</s>: What is the nature of the attainment that follows the fifth [stage]? (10)

children.text: upasaṃhāragāthāḥ /
children.translated_text: Summary verses (<s>upasaṃhāragāthāḥ</s>):

children.text: paripūrṇamārgacaraṇā vidu pañcamāyāṃ dharmānimittata alakṣaṇatā ajātā /
children.translated_text: The wise ones, having fulfilled the path-practice on the fifth [stage], [realize] that <s>dharmas</s> are signless, characteristicless, unborn,

children.text: anutpāda ādipariśuddhyatiniṣprapañcā bhāvetva jñānamati ṣaṣṭhi samākramanti // 11 //
children.translated_text: unproduced, primordially pure, free from conceptual elaboration; having cultivated the knowledge of the intellect, they ascend to the sixth [stage]. (11)

children.text: dharmā vivikta apratigraha nirvikalpā māyāsvabhāva dvayabhāvatu viprayuktā /
children.translated_text: <s>Dharmas</s> are secluded, ungraspable, free from conceptual discrimination, of the nature of illusion, disjoined from the state of duality,

children.text: anulomayanta avilomanta dharmanetrī jñānānvitāḥ pravara ṣaṣṭhi samākramanti // 12 //
children.translated_text: conforming and not opposing the eye of <s>Dharma</s>; endowed with knowledge, the excellent ones ascend to the sixth [stage]. (12)

children.text: tīkṣṇānulomasthita jñānabalopapetāḥ samudāgamaṃ vibhavu prekṣiṣu sarvaloke /
children.translated_text: Endowed with the power of knowledge established in keen conformity, they perceive the arising and passing of all in the world;

children.text: mohāndhakāraprabhavaṃ jagasaṃbhavātmā tasyaiva mohavigamena pravṛti nāsti // 13 //
children.translated_text: the nature of worldly existence arises from the darkness of delusion, and by the removal of that very delusion, there is no further arising. (13)

children.text: vicinanti pratyayakṛtiṃ paramārthaśūnyāṃ kriya hetupratyayasamajña kriyāvirodhau /
children.translated_text: They investigate the conditioned nature, empty in the ultimate sense; action and the conjunction of causes and conditions do not contradict activity;

children.text: yāthāvataḥ karakapetakriyāṃ viditvā vicinanti saṃskṛta ghanābhrasamaṃ nirīham // 14//
children.translated_text: having understood action as it truly is, devoid of an agent, they investigate the conditioned as resembling a dense cloud, purposeless. (14)

children.text: satyeṣu 'jñānu paramārthatu sā avidyā karmā ca cetanabalena vibhāgaprāptam /
children.translated_text: Ignorance in the [four noble] truths is that <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) in the ultimate sense; <s>karma</s> (action) is determined by the force of volition (<s>cetanā</s>);

children.text: cittaṃ niśritya sahajaṃ puna nāmarūpam evaṃmukhā bhavati yāva dukhasya skandhaḥ // 15 //
children.translated_text: consciousness (<s>citta</s>) depending [on that], then name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) arises conjoined—thus proceeds the aggregate of suffering. (15)

body.text: te cittamātra ti traidhātukamotaranti api cā bhavāṅga iti dvādaśa ekacitte /
body.translated_text: They penetrate the three realms as mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>), and the twelve limbs of existence (<s>bhavāṅga</s>) [arise] in a single mind-moment;

body.text: saṃrāgu jātu api cittu prabhāvitastu evaṃ ca saṃbhavakṣayaṃ puna cittabhāgam // 16 //
body.translated_text: attachment arises and consciousness is conditioned—thus the arising and cessation of existence is [understood as] a portion of mind. (16)

children.text: kāryaṃ avidyadvaya kurvati mohabhāve mohebhi hetu vahate puna cetanāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The twofold ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) produces its effect in the state of delusion; through delusions, the cause carries forward volition (<s>cetanā</s>);

children.text: evaṃ ca yāva jaradhvaṃsanaskandhabhedam anu sarva duḥkhaprabhavaṃ kṣayataḥ abhāvaḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: thus up to old age, destruction, and the breaking apart of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>)—following all this, the arising of suffering ceases through exhaustion into non-existence. (17)

children.text: ucchedu no bhavati pratyayatāmavidyā nocchedyatāpi kara prahāya saṃnirodham /
children.translated_text: There is no annihilation, [for] ignorance is [merely] conditioned; nor is there non-annihilation—having abandoned [both views], there is cessation (<s>nirodha</s>);

children.text: moho teṣu ca upādānaṃ kleśavartma karma bhavaṃ ca api cetana śeṣa duḥkhā // 18 //
children.translated_text: delusion in these, and clinging (<s>upādāna</s>), the path of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>karma</s> and existence, and volition—the remaining [links constitute] suffering. (18)

children.text: mohaṃ tu āyatana saṃskṛtaduḥkha teṣāṃ sparśaṃ ca vedana sukhādukhatāya duḥkhā /
children.translated_text: Delusion, the sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), conditioned suffering in these, contact (<s>sparśa</s>), and feeling (<s>vedanā</s>)—suffering of pleasure and pain;

children.text: śeṣānamaṅganapariṇāmaduḥkhavṛddhiḥ vyuccheda tasya duḥkhatā na hi ātmamasti // 19 //
children.translated_text: the remaining links' growth of the suffering of transformation; the cessation of that is [the truth of] suffering—for there is no self. (19)

body.text: adhveṣu pūrvaṃ tamacetanasaṃskṛtasya vijñāna vedana vivartati pratyutpannam

children.text: aparāntu teṣu prabhavo dukhasaṃbhaveyam āpekṣa cchedu prasaraṃ ca nirīkṣayantaḥ // 20 //
children.translated_text: in the future, among these is the arising of the origin of suffering—observing the cessation and continuation with mutual dependence. (20)

body.translated_text: In the three times: formerly, [there is] the conditioned of darkness and volition; consciousness and feeling evolve in the present;

children.text: mohasya pratyayatu saṃbhavate vibandhā vinibandhanavyayakṣaye sati pratyayānām /
children.translated_text: Through conditions, bondage arises from delusion; with the cessation and destruction of conditions and bonds,

children.text: hetośca mūlaprabhavaṃ na tu hetubhedaṃ vyuparīkṣate ca jina jñāna svabhāvaśūnyam // 21 //
children.translated_text: they investigate the root origin of the cause, not the splitting of causes; and [they see that] the knowledge of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) is empty of inherent nature. (21)

children.text: anuloma mohaprabhavaṃ ca prabhāvataśca pratilomahetu kṣayato bhava sarvacchedyam /
children.translated_text: In conformity, [they see] the arising from delusion and its power; in reverse order, [they see] the cessation of all existence through the exhaustion of causes;

children.text: gambhīrapratyayatamasya sato 'sataśca vyuparīkṣate daśavidhaṃ aniketabuddhiḥ // 22 //
children.translated_text: profound conditionality of the existent and non-existent—they investigate it in ten ways with a mind free from abode. (22)

children.text: saṃdhī bhavāṅgatu tathāpi ca karmasthānam avibhāgatastrividhu vartmani pūrvataśca /
children.translated_text: The junctures of the limbs of existence, and likewise the domain of <s>karma</s>, are undivided in the three paths and from the former [perspective];

children.text: triyahetu duḥkhavibhavā udaya vyayaṃ ca abhāvato 'kṣayata pratyaya ānulomam // 23 //
children.translated_text: three causes, the diversity of suffering, arising and passing away, and from non-existence and inexhaustibility—[this is] the conforming [investigation of] conditions. (23)

body.text: evaṃ pratītyasamutpāda samotaranti māyopamaṃ vitatha vedakarmāpanītam /
body.translated_text: Thus they penetrate <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) as like an illusion, false, devoid of a doer and <s>karma</s>;

body.text: svapnopamaṃ ca tathatā pratibhāsa caiva bālāna mohana marīcisamasvabhāvam // 24 //
body.translated_text: like a dream, and likewise as a reflection of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness)—delusive to the foolish, of the nature of a mirage. (24)

children.text: yā eva bhāvana sa śūnyata paṇḍitānāṃ rati pratyayāna bhavate idamānimittam /
children.translated_text: That very contemplation is <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) for the wise; delight in conditions becomes this signlessness (<s>ānimitta</s>);

children.text: jānitva jātu vitathaṃ praṇidhātu nāsti anyatra sattvakṛpayā upapadyanti // 25 //
children.translated_text: knowing that arising is false, there is no [object of] aspiration—except through compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>) for beings, they are reborn. (25)

children.text: evaṃ vimokṣamukha bhāvayi te mahātmā kṛpabuddhi bhūya tatha buddhaguṇābhilāṣī /
children.translated_text: Thus these great beings cultivate the gates of liberation (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>), with a mind of compassion, and aspiring to the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: saṃyogasaṃskṛtikṛta vyuparīkṣamāṇo niyatāśayo bhavati naikaguṇopapetaḥ // 26 //
children.translated_text: investigating the conjunction and conditioned activity, they become fixed in resolve, endowed with manifold qualities. (26)

body.text: pūrṇā sahasra daśa śūnyataye samādhī tatha ānimittavaradaṃ ca vimokṣa tāyī // 27 //
body.translated_text: Ten thousand <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations) of emptiness are fulfilled, and likewise the excellent signless and wishless liberations. (27)

children.text: pralhādayanti jagadāśaya candra-ābhā vahamānu vāta caturo asaṃhāryaprāptā /
children.translated_text: They gladden beings with the light of [their] resolve like the moon, carrying the four winds, having attained unshakability;

children.text: atikramya mārapathamābha jinaurasānāṃ praśamenti kleśaparitāpa dukhārditānām // 28 //
children.translated_text: transcending the path of <s>Māra</s>, [they are] radiant like the legitimate sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), pacifying the torment and suffering of those afflicted by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). (28)

children.text: iha bhūmideśupagatā marutādhipāste bhontī sunirmita kṛtāvadhimānaghātī /
children.translated_text: Established on this stage, they become lords of the <s>Marutas</s> (gods), of the <s>Sunirmita</s> [heaven], destroyers of the conceit of self-creation;

children.text: yaṃ caiva ārabhiṣu jñānapathopapetā asaṃhārya śrāvakagatī atikrānta dhīrāḥ // 29 //
children.translated_text: whatever they undertake, endowed with the path of knowledge, unshakable, having surpassed the <s>Śrāvaka</s> (hearer) course, they are steadfast. (29)

children.text: ākāṅkṣamāṇu sugatātmaja vīryaprāptāḥ koṭīśatasahasrapūrṇa samādhi labdhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Aspiring, these sons of the <s>Sugata</s>, endowed with heroic effort, having attained hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of complete <s>samādhis</s>,

children.text: paśyanti ekakṣaṇi buddha daśaddiśāsu pratapanti sūrya eva madhyagu grīṣmakāle // 30 //
children.translated_text: in a single instant they see <s>Buddhas</s> in the ten directions, and they blaze like the sun at midday in summer. (30)

body.text: gambhīra durdṛśā sūkṣma durjñeyā jinaśrāvakaiḥ / ṣaṣṭhī bhūmirmahātmānāmākhyātā sugatātmajāḥ // 31 //
body.translated_text: Profound, hard to perceive, subtle, difficult to know by the <s>Jina's</s> <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers)—this sixth stage of the great beings has been declared, O sons of the <s>Sugata</s>. (31)

body.text:
7 dūraṃgamā nāma saptamī bhūmiḥ /
upakramagāthāḥ /
body.translated_text: 7. The seventh stage called <s>Dūraṃgamā</s> (Far-Going). Introductory verses (<s>upakramagāthāḥ</s>):

children.text: atha vividharucirameghān marudgaṇo 'bhikiriṣu vegaprāptāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the host of <s>Marutas</s> (gods), having attained speed, began to scatter various beautiful clouds,

children.text: pravyāharanti madhurā girivara śubha prītisaṃpūrṇāḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: and they proclaim sweetly, the excellent mountains filled with joy and delight. (1)

children.text: sādhu varatīkṣṇacittā guṇaśatasamupetajñānavaśavartim /
children.translated_text: Well done! [You] of excellent keen mind, endowed with hundreds of qualities, abiding in the power of knowledge,

children.text: varacaraṇaṃ parituṣṭaṃ jagahitavarapuṇḍarīkāṇām // 2 //
children.translated_text: delighted in the excellent conduct, [you who are] the supreme lotuses for the welfare of the world. (2)

children.text: tada pravaramatulamābhā maheśvarāḥ khegatā naravarasya /
children.translated_text: Then the great lords (<s>Maheśvaras</s>), of supreme incomparable radiance, stationed in the sky of the best of men,

children.text: vararuciragandhameghānabhikiri kleśaughamapahartum // 3 //
children.translated_text: scatter clouds of excellent, beautiful fragrance to dispel the flood of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). (3)

children.text: pravyāharanti madhuraṃ marudgaṇā harṣakararuciraghoṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: The host of <s>Marutas</s> (gods) proclaim sweetly, with joyful, beautiful, and melodious voices:

children.text: paramasulabdhalābhāḥ śrutu yairayu bhūminirdeśaḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: Supremely fortunate are those by whom this exposition of the stages has been heard! (4)

children.text: tūrya madhuraghoṣayukta marukanyāḥ prīṇitamanobhiḥ /
children.translated_text: With instruments of sweet and melodious sound, the celestial maidens, with delighted minds,

children.text: sucarasugatānubhāvādvaracaririyamīdṛśī proktā // 5 //
children.translated_text: by the power of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), declare: Such is this excellent and beautiful conduct! (5)

children.text: sumanī sucaraṇaśreṣṭhaḥ sudānta damakāna lokamahitānām /
children.translated_text: Of good mind, foremost in excellent conduct, well-restrained, tamer of the tameable, honored by the world,

children.text: atikramya sarvalokaṃ lokacariṃ darśayī sūkṣmām // 6 //
children.translated_text: transcending the entire world, [yet] displaying subtle worldly conduct. (6)

children.text: darśenti kāya vividhān kāyākāyāṃśca dharmatopetāḥ /
children.translated_text: They display various bodies, and [truths about] body and non-body, endowed with the nature of <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: śamathaḥ samitivibhakto bhaṇati ghoṣaṃ na cākṣaraṃ ravati // 7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śamatha</s> (calm abiding) is distinguished by restraint; [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>] utters speech but does not produce syllables. (7)

children.text: kṣetraśatamākramante pūjenti nāyakān paramapūjiyān /
children.translated_text: They traverse hundreds of <s>kṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) and honor the supremely venerable guides (<s>Nāyakas</s>);

children.text: ātmajanitakṣetrasaṃjñā vidhunitvā jñānavaśavartī // 8 //
children.translated_text: having shaken off the notion of a self-created field, they abide in the power of knowledge. (8)

children.text: paripācayanti sattvānna cātmaparasaṃjña sarvaśa upenti /
children.translated_text: They ripen beings and yet do not approach [them with] any notion of self and other;

children.text: śubha saṃcinanti pravaraṃ na cāpi śubhasaṃcayaniketāḥ // 9 //
children.translated_text: they accumulate excellent merit, yet are not attached to the accumulation of merit. (9)

children.text: rāgarajadoṣamohaiḥ paśyitva sarvaloka jvalamānān /
children.translated_text: Seeing the entire world blazing with the dust of passion (<s>rāga</s>), fault (<s>doṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>),

children.text: varjeti sarvasaṃjñā vīryaṃ varamārabhī kṛpayā // 10 //
children.translated_text: they abandon all [false] notions and undertake supreme effort out of compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>). (10)

children.text: marukanyā devasaṃghāśca pūjentā varasvaram /
children.translated_text: The celestial maidens and the assemblies of <s>Devas</s> (gods), honoring the supreme voice,

children.text: tūṣṇīṃbhāvaratāḥ sarve prekṣante puruṣarṣabham // 11 //
children.translated_text: all delighting in silence, gaze upon the bull among men (<s>puruṣarṣabha</s>). (11)

children.text: pariṣadviprasanneyamavocat sugatātmajam /
children.translated_text: This assembly, filled with serene faith, addressed the son of the <s>Sugata</s>:

children.text: saptamyā bhūmerākārān nirdiśasva guṇākara // 12 //
children.translated_text: Describe the characteristics of the seventh stage, O treasury of qualities! (12)

children.text: upasaṃhāragāthāḥ /
children.translated_text: Summary verses (<s>upasaṃhāragāthāḥ</s>):

children.text: gambhīrajñāna paramārthapadānusārī ṣaḍbhūminiścitamatiḥ susamāhitātmā /
children.translated_text: Following the path of profound knowledge and ultimate truth, with mind firmly established on the sixth stage, with a well-concentrated self,

children.text: prajñāmupāya yugapadyabhinirharanto bhūmyākramanti vidu saptami caryaśreṣṭhām // 13 //
children.translated_text: bringing forth <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) simultaneously, the wise ones ascend to the seventh stage, the foremost in conduct. (13)

children.text: śūnyānimittapraṇidhīkṛpamaitrayuktā buddhānudharma sugatānuga pūjayantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Endowed with emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>), signlessness (<s>ānimitta</s>), wishlessness (<s>praṇidhi</s>), compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>), and friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>), honoring the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s>, followers of the <s>Sugata</s>,

children.text: jñānena śubhamahapuṇyabalebhyatṛptāstāmākramanti vidu saptami bhūmideśam // 14 //
children.translated_text: unsatisfied by the power of merit and knowledge, the wise ones ascend to the region of the seventh stage. (14)

children.text: traidhātukena adhivāsa vivekaprāptāḥ śāntaśca kleśabalaśāntijagābhikāṅkṣī /
children.translated_text: Having attained forbearance and seclusion within the three realms, peaceful, with the power of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) pacified, aspiring for the welfare of the world,

children.text: pratibhāsa māya supinādvayadharmacārī kṛpa darśayanti vidu saptamimākramanti // 15 //
children.translated_text: practicing the <s>Dharma</s> of non-duality as [mere] appearance, illusion, and dream, the wise ones who show compassion ascend to the seventh [stage]. (15)

children.text: śodhenti kṣetra khasamāśaya nirvikalpā jinalakṣanairupāgato 'caladharmatāyām /
children.translated_text: They purify <s>kṣetras</s> (buddha-fields), with resolve [vast as] space, free from conceptual discrimination, endowed with the marks of the <s>Jina</s>, having attained the immovable nature of <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: abhilāpyaghoṣavigatā jagatoṣaṇārthaṃ kṣaṇajñāna cittasya jināna samosaranti // 16 //
children.translated_text: free from the sound of verbal designation, for the purpose of comforting the world, with instantaneous knowledge of mind, they enter into [the presence of] the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors). (16)

children.text: abhāsaprāpta iti dharma vicārayanti ākrānta bhūmipravarāṃ jagadarthakārāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having attained radiance, they investigate the <s>Dharma</s>, having ascended to this excellent stage as workers for the welfare of the world;

children.text: te atra bhūmyasthita sattvacarī anantān vicinanti karma sugatān niyutāpramāṇān // 17 //
children.translated_text: established on this stage, they investigate the infinite conduct of beings, the <s>karma</s> [of] immeasurable millions of <s>Sugatas</s>. (17)

children.text: kṣetrāṃśca naikavidhadharmatha kalpasaṃkhyān adhimukti-āśaya ca cittavicitradhārān /
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣetras</s> (fields) of many kinds, and <s>Dharma</s>, and the reckoning of <s>kalpas</s> (eons), and the diverse streams of aspiration (<s>adhimukti</s>), resolve, and mind,

children.text: triyāṇadeśanamananta samosaranti asmābhi sattva paripācayitavyametat // 18 //
children.translated_text: they enter into the immeasurable teaching of the three vehicles: 'These beings must be ripened by us.' (18)

children.text: ye te jñānanicitā varamārgaprāptā īryāpathaiścaturbhi prajñamupāyamuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are established on the excellent path, rich in knowledge, [practicing] with the four modes of deportment, with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) released,

children.text: sarvasmi cittakṣaṇi bodhiguṇānuprāptāḥ paripūrayanti daśa pāramitāpradeśān // 19 //
children.translated_text: in every mind-moment attaining the qualities of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), they fulfill the regions of the ten <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). (19)

children.text: sarveṣu mārgakuśalasya ya eṣa dānaṃ śīlaṃ ca kleśapraśamaṃ kṣamamakṣatitvam /
children.translated_text: For one skilled in all paths, there is <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), the pacification of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>kṣama</s> (patience), imperturbability,

children.text: vīryaṃ ca bhūyu anu uttari ārabhante mārge acalyataya dhyānaguṇānvitānām // 20 //
children.translated_text: and <s>vīrya</s> (effort)—they undertake further and higher on the path, [being] unshakable, endowed with the qualities of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). (20)

body.text: anutpādakṣānti virajā varaprajña śreṣṭhā parṇāmupāya praṇidhī bhuyu kāṅkṣi lakṣmī /
body.translated_text: The patience of non-arising (<s>anutpādakṣānti</s>), stainless, the foremost excellent <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), dedication of merit (<s>pariṇāma</s>), skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), aspiration (<s>praṇidhi</s>), further aspiring for splendor,

body.text: ato 'mardayitva balajñānanitīraṇatvād evaṃ khu bodhiguṇa sarvakṣaṇenupenti // 21 //
body.translated_text: therefore, crushing [obstacles] through the determination of the power of knowledge, thus indeed the qualities of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) are attained in every moment. (21)

children.text: ālambanātu prathamā guṇapāripūri dvitīyā malāpanaya ūrdhva vibandhacchedam /
children.translated_text: The first [<s>pāramitā</s>] fulfills qualities through its support; the second removes stains; the third cuts bonds above;

children.text: caturthāya mārgu samatākriya pañcamāya anutpāda āhvaya viduḥ puna ṣaṣṭhavṛttiḥ // 22 //
children.translated_text: the fourth [brings] equality of path; the fifth [brings] practice; what the wise call non-arising is the function of the sixth. (22)

children.text: iha saptamīmupagatāḥ sakalaṃ guṇāni praṇidhāna naikavividhānabhinirharanti /
children.translated_text: Here, having reached the seventh, [the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>] bring forth complete qualities and various and manifold aspirations;

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ yaduta jñānakriyābhyupenti sā aṣṭamīprabhṛti sarvaviśuddhyupenti // 23 //
children.translated_text: for what reason? Because they attain the activity of knowledge—from the eighth [stage] onward, complete purification is attained. (23)

children.text: duratikramā dūraṃgamā bahusthānakarmā kṣetrāntaradvipathameva yathottaranti /
children.translated_text: Hard to surpass, far-going, of manifold activities in many domains—just as they cross the path between <s>kṣetras</s> (fields),

children.text: vicaranti saptasu alipta nṛpo yathaiva mārgasthitā na puna sarvatikrānta dhīrāḥ // 24 //
children.translated_text: they move through the seven [stages] unstained, like a king; established on the path, but the steadfast ones have not yet transcended all. (24)

children.text: yada aṣṭamīmupagatāḥ puna jñānabhūmim atikrānta cittaviṣaye sthita jñānakarme /
children.translated_text: When they have reached the eighth stage, the stage of knowledge, having transcended the domain of mind, established in the activity of knowledge,

children.text: brahmā na pekṣati jagannaramānuṣātmā evaṃ caranti vidu padmamivā aliptāḥ // 25 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> does not perceive the world and human selves—thus the wise ones move like a lotus, unstained. (25)

children.text: atra sthitā vividhakleśamatikramanti teṣāṃ na kleśacari no ca kṣayo 'nuprāptiḥ /
children.translated_text: Established here, they transcend the manifold <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions); for them there is neither the course of afflictions nor the attainment of their destruction;

children.text: mārgasthitā na tada kleśacariṃ caranti saṃpūrṇa āśaya jinajña kṣayo na tāvat // 26 //
children.translated_text: established on the path, they do not then follow the course of afflictions; their resolve is complete, [endowed with] the knowledge of the <s>Jina</s>, yet cessation [is] not yet [final]. (26)

children.text: ye laukikā vividhaśilpakriyāprayogā ājāti sarvavidunā sthita śāstrajñāne /
children.translated_text: Whatever worldly arts, crafts, and applications there are—[they master] all by birth, established in the knowledge of the <s>śāstras</s> (sciences);

children.text: dhyānā abhijña bala bhāvayanto 'bhyupenti bhūyaḥ samādhi vividhānabhinirharanti // 27 //
children.translated_text: cultivating <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and powers, they attain further and bring forth various <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations). (27)

children.text: atikrānta śravakacariṃ tatha pratyayānāṃ sthita bodhisattvacaraṇe vidu apramāṇām /
children.translated_text: Having surpassed the course of <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and likewise of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, established in the immeasurable conduct of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>,

children.text: pūrve hi āśayatayā iha jñānatāyā nṛpatīsuto yatha vivṛddhabalopapetaḥ // 28 //
children.translated_text: through their former resolve and through the knowledge [gained] here, like a prince grown mighty in power. (28)

children.text: gāmbhīryatāmupagatā bhuyu ārabhanti cittaṃ nirodhupagatā na ca sākṣikriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having attained profundity, they further undertake [practice]; the mind enters cessation, yet they do not realize [final] cessation;

children.text: yathā sāgare upagatāḥ sthita yānapātre pratyakṣa sarva udake na ca yānahāniḥ // 29 //
children.translated_text: just as those who have entered the ocean, established in a vessel, perceive all the water, yet the vessel is not lost. (29)

children.text: bhūyo upāyabalaprajñavarābhyupetā durjñeyasarvajagajñānakriyāguṇāḍhyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Further endowed with the excellent power of skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), rich in the qualities of knowledge and activity for all worlds, difficult to fathom,

children.text: pūjenti buddha niyutā bhuyu śuddhibhāvā yathā tadvibhūṣaṇavicitritu naikaratnaiḥ // 30 //
children.translated_text: they honor millions of <s>Buddhas</s>, with further purity of being—just as [an ornament] is adorned with various and manifold jewels. (30)

children.text: atra sthitāna vidunāṃ varaprajña ābhā śoṣenti tṛṣṇasalilaṃ yatha bhāskārābhāḥ /
children.translated_text: The radiance of the excellent wisdom of the wise ones established here dries up the waters of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) like the rays of the sun;

children.text: te atra bhūmyupagatā vaśavartinaśca bhonti kṛtī kuśala jñānaphalodeśaiḥ // 31 //
children.translated_text: established on this stage, they become lords endowed with mastery, accomplished in skill, through the fruits of knowledge [shared with] the world. (31)

children.text: ākāṅkṣamāṇa dṛḍhavīryabalābhyupetāḥ koṭīnayūtaśata buddhasahasra pūrṇān /
children.translated_text: Aspiring, endowed with firm heroic power, [seeing] complete hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: paśyanti sarvadiśatāsu samāhitatvād bhūyo 'pyataḥ praṇidhiśreṣṭha guṇāprameyāḥ // 32//
children.translated_text: they see [them] in all directions through their concentration; and further beyond this, their excellent aspirations and qualities are immeasurable. (32)

body.text: durjñeyā sarvalokena vaśipratyekacāribhiḥ / ityeṣā saptamī bhūmirupāyaprajñaśodhanā // 33 //
body.translated_text: Difficult to know by all the world, by masters, and by <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary realizers)—such is this seventh stage, purified through skillful means and wisdom. (33)

body.text:
8 acalā nāma aṣṭamī bhūmiḥ /
upakramagāthāḥ /
body.translated_text: 8. The eighth stage called <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable). Introductory verses (<s>upakramagāthāḥ</s>):

children.text: eva śrutva caraṇaṃ viduna śreṣṭhaṃ devasaṃgha muditā marupatiśca /
children.translated_text: Having thus heard the foremost conduct of the wise one, the assemblies of gods and the lord of the <s>Marutas</s> are joyful;

children.text: bodhisattva bahavo jagaddhitaiṣi pūjayanti sugataṃ jinasutāṃśca // 1 //
children.translated_text: the many <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, desiring the welfare of the world, honor the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) and the sons of the <s>Jina</s>. (1)

children.text: puṣpamālya rucirā dhvajāpatākā gandhacūrṇa rucirā ratanavastrā /
children.translated_text: Flowers, beautiful garlands, banners and pennants, fragrant powders, beautiful jewels and garments,

children.text: chatra naikarucirān maṇipratyuptān hārameghapravarānabhisṛjanti // 2 //
children.translated_text: various and beautiful parasols studded with gems, and excellent clouds of necklaces they send forth. (2)

children.text: manojñaghoṣamadhuraṃ suravandū mukta naikaturiyapravaranāṭān /
children.translated_text: With pleasing, sweet, melodious sounds, the celestial maidens, having released various excellent instrumental performances,

children.text: pūjanārthi jinaputra sugatāṃśca varṇaśreṣṭha munino udāharanti // 3 //
children.translated_text: in order to honor the son of the <s>Jina</s> and the <s>Sugatas</s>, they utter the foremost praises of the Sage (<s>Muni</s>). (3)

children.text: sarvi darśi vṛṣabhī dvipādaśreṣṭho darśi buddhaviṣayaṃ jagaddhitārtham /
children.translated_text: The All-Seeing One, the bull, the foremost among bipeds, who perceives the domain of the <s>Buddha</s> for the welfare of the world—

children.text: śabdamegha rucirān pratāḍamānāstūryatāla vividhāstada pramuktāḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: striking beautiful clouds of sound, various drums and cymbals are released. (4)

children.text: vālakoṭi sugatāḥ śatasahasrā gaṅgākoṭi nayutā rajaviśiṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of multitudes of <s>Sugatas</s>, <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Gaṅgā</s> river [sands] in distinction,

children.text: kṣemamapratisamāḥ pravaraśreṣṭhaṃ deśayanti vṛṣabhī virajadharmam // 5 //
children.translated_text: the incomparable bulls [among teachers] teach the supreme, foremost, stainless <s>Dharma</s> leading to well-being. (5)

children.text: preta tirya narakā manujadevāḥ yakṣa rakṣa bhujagā asurasaṃghā /
children.translated_text: <s>Pretas</s>, animals, hell-beings, humans, gods, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, serpents, and hosts of <s>Asuras</s>—

children.text: ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... nānakarmaviṣaye samanubhonti // 6 //
children.translated_text: ...they experience [results] in the realm of various <s>karmas</s>. // 6 //

children.text: sarvakṣetraviṣaye dhutarajānāṃ cakra śreṣṭhapravaraṃ tadanirvṛttam /
children.translated_text: In all the domains of the fields, for those free from dust, they turn the supreme and most excellent wheel, which is unproduced,

children.text: deśayanti madhuraṃ sugataghoṣaṃ saṃjñacitta jagatastatha vicāran // 7 //
children.translated_text: They teach the sweet sound of the <s>Sugatas</s>, investigating the perceptions, thoughts, and [dispositions] of beings. // 7 //

body.text: sattvakāyi sugatā vividhakṣetrā kṣetri sattvapravarāḥ punavipākāḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Sugatas</s> [appear in] various fields among the bodies of beings; in the fields [appear] the foremost beings and their ripened [fruits];

body.text: devamānuṣagatī tatha vicitrā jñātva sarva sugato bhaṇati dharmam // 8 //
body.translated_text: Having known the divine and human destinies in their variety, the <s>Sugata</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s>. // 8 //

children.text: sūkṣmasaṃjña bhavati vipulakṣetre vipulasaṃjña bhavati rajanimitte /
children.translated_text: A subtle perception arises in a vast field; a vast perception arises at the sign of a particle;

children.text: evamādi vividhāṃ sugata-ṛddhiṃ sarvaloka bhaṇato na kṣepayeyuḥ // 9 //
children.translated_text: Such manifold supernatural powers of the <s>Sugata</s>—all the worlds speaking could not exhaust them. // 9 //

children.text: īddaśaṃ vacamāhātmyaṃ vacitvā madhurasvaram /
children.translated_text: Having spoken such words of greatness in a sweet voice,

children.text: praśāntā pariṣatprītā prekṣate vadatāṃ varam // 10 //
children.translated_text: The pacified assembly, delighted, gazes at the best of speakers. // 10 //

children.text: praśānta parṣadaṃ jñātvā mokṣacandro 'bravītpunaḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowing the assembly to be pacified, <s>Mokṣacandra</s> spoke again:

children.text: aṣṭamyā bhūmi-ākārāṃ praveśaṃ ca nidarśaya // 11 //
children.translated_text: "Show the aspects and entry of the eighth <s>bhūmi</s>!" // 11 //

children.text: upasaṃhāragāthāḥ /
children.translated_text: Summary verses (<s>upasaṃhāragāthāḥ</s>):

children.text: te bhūmya saptasu viśodhita prajñupāyā mārgā susaṃbhṛta mahāpraṇidhānabaddhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who on the seven <s>bhūmis</s> have purified wisdom and means, whose paths are well-accumulated, bound by great aspirations,

children.text: supratiṣṭhitā naravarāḥ kuśalopapetā jñānābhilāṣi vidu aṣṭamimākramanti // 12 //
children.translated_text: Well-established, the foremost of men, endowed with merit, desirous of knowledge—the wise ones ascend to the eighth. // 12 //

children.text: te puṇyajñānupagatāḥ kṛpamaitrayuktā jñānāpramāṇapathagāḥ khagabuddhikalpāḥ /
children.translated_text: Endowed with merit and knowledge, equipped with compassion and loving-kindness, following the path of immeasurable knowledge, their intellect like a bird [in the sky],

children.text: śrutadharma niścitabalopagatā maharṣī kṣāntiṃ labhanti anutpādapraśāntisūkṣmām // 13 //
children.translated_text: Having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, the great sages endowed with ascertained strength attain the patience of the subtle, quiescent non-arising. // 13 //

children.text: ādāvajāta anutpāda alakṣaṇaṃ ca asaṃbhūtatamavinaṣṭata cāpravṛttam /
children.translated_text: Primordially unborn, non-arising, without characteristics, unproduced, indestructible, non-active,

children.text: bhāvasvabhāvavigatā tathatāvikalpā mama cittacāravigatāḥ khagatulyakalpāḥ // 14 //
children.translated_text: Gone beyond the own-nature of existence, free from conceptualization of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), gone beyond the activity of thought, like space. // 14 //

children.text: te eva kṣāntisamanvāgata niṣprapañcā gambhīracālya vidu śāntavicāraprāptāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those endowed with patience, free from elaboration, [established in] the profound and unshakable, the wise ones who have attained peaceful investigation,

children.text: durjñeya sarvajagatārahapratyayaiśca cittaṃ nimittagrahasaṃjñavibhāvitatvāt //
children.translated_text: Hard to know by all the world, by <s>Arhats</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, because of the nature [being free from] the grasping of signs and perception.

children.text: evaṃ sthitānamanucintavikalpa nāsti bhikṣurnirodhyupagato 'paprakalpaprāptaḥ /
children.translated_text: For those thus established, there is no subsequent thought or conceptualization; like a monk who has entered cessation, who has attained the absence of elaboration,

children.text: svapnoghaprāpta pratibuddha tathāvikalpā brahmāpure ratisaṅgarahito tathaiva // 16 //
children.translated_text: Like one who has reached the flood in a dream and then awakes—free from conceptualization; like one in the <s>Brahma</s>-world, free from the bond of pleasure. // 16 //

body.text: pūrvādhiṣṭhāna sugatā puna codayanti eṣā sa kṣānti paramā sugatābhiṣeke /
body.translated_text: Through former empowerment, the <s>Sugatas</s> then rouse him: 'This is the supreme patience, the consecration of the <s>Sugatas</s>;

body.text: asmāku jñāna vipulaṃ varabuddhadharmā te tubhya nāsti ta hi vīryu samārabhāyam // 17 //
body.translated_text: But our vast knowledge and the excellent <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>—those you do not yet have; therefore exert your energy!' // 17 //

children.text: kiṃcāpi śānta tava sarvakileśajvālā jvalitaṃ niśamya puna kleśagatibhya lokam /
children.translated_text: 'Although the flame of all your defilements is quenched, behold the world still blazing in the destinies of defilement;

children.text: praṇidhāna pūrva smara sattvahitaṃ vicārya jñānārthi prārthita kriyā jagamokṣahetoḥ // 18 //
children.translated_text: Remember your former aspirations, reflect on the welfare of beings; desiring knowledge, seek to act for the liberation of the world!' // 18 //

children.text: sada eṣa dharmata sthitā tathatāvikalpā sarveṣu buddhajinaśrāvakapratyayānam /
children.translated_text: 'This <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of things) always stands, free from conceptualization of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), for all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Jinas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>;

children.text: na hi etinā daśabalāna prabhāvu loke nānyatra jñānavipulaṃ tribhi adhvasaṅgam // 19//
children.translated_text: Yet the power of the ten-powered ones in the world is not [attained] by this alone—nowhere else [is found] vast knowledge unattached in the three times.' // 19 //

children.text: evaṃ tamapratisamā naradevapūjyā upasaṃharanti bahujñānamukhā vicārān /
children.translated_text: Thus those incomparable ones, worshipped by men and gods, present investigations with many doors of knowledge,

children.text: jinadharmaniṣpattipraveśamanantapāraṃ yasyā kalā na bhavate puna bodhicaryā // 20 //
children.translated_text: The entry into the accomplishment of the <s>Jina</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, infinite in its far shore, compared to which the prior <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice is not even a fraction. // 20 //

children.text: etāni prāpta vṛṣabhī varajñānabhūmim ekakṣaṇena spharate diśatāḥ samantān /
children.translated_text: Having attained this excellent ground of knowledge, the bulls [among beings] pervade the directions in every direction in a single moment,

children.text: jñānapraveśupagatā varabhijñaprāptā yatha sāgare vahanu mārutayānaprāptaḥ // 21 //
children.translated_text: Having entered knowledge, attained the excellent <s>abhijñās</s> (higher knowledges)—like a vessel on the ocean that has attained the wind. // 21 //

children.text: sābhogacittavigatāḥ sthitajñānakarma vicinanti kṣetraprabhavaṃ vibhavasthitiṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Free from effortful thought, abiding in the work of knowledge, they investigate the arising, existence, and cessation of fields,

children.text: dhātuścatvāri vinibhāgagatāna tāṃśca sūkṣmaṃ mahadgata vibhakti samosaranti // 22 //
children.translated_text: And the four elements in their differentiated aspects, subtle and great—they enter into the analysis [of these]. // 22 //

children.text: trisahasri sarvaparamāṇurajo taranti catvāri dhātu jagakāyi vibhaktitaśca /
children.translated_text: They traverse all the atoms of the <s>trisāhasra</s> (triple-thousand) [world-system], the four elements and the bodies of beings in their divisions,

children.text: ratnā vibhaktiparamāṇu suvargatīṣu bhinditva jñānaviṣayena gaṇentyaśeṣam // 23 //
children.translated_text: The atoms of gems in their divisions in the happy realms—having distinguished them, they enumerate all through the domain of knowledge. // 23 //

children.text: jñāne vibhāvitamanā vidu sarvakāyān sve kāyi tatra upanenti jagārthahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: With minds illuminated by knowledge, the wise ones bring all bodies into their own body for the sake of beings;

children.text: trisahasra sarva ca spharitva vicitrarūpān darśenti kāya vividhān tathanantaloke // 24 //
children.translated_text: Pervading the entire <s>trisāhasra</s> [world], they display various and manifold bodies in the infinite world. // 24 //

body.text: sūryaṃ śaśiṃ ca vahni māruta antarīkṣe svakamaṇḍalusya udake pratibhāsaprāptā /
body.translated_text: The sun, moon, fire, and wind, [reflected] in the sky, in the waters of their own sphere—reflections [that are] attained;

body.text: jñānottame sthita tathācaladharmatāyāṃ jaga śuddha-āśaya vidū pratibhāsaprāptā // 25 //
body.translated_text: Just so, established in the supreme knowledge, in the immovable <s>dharmatā</s>, the wise ones are reflections attained in the world of those with pure aspirations. // 25 //

children.text: yatha-āśayaṃ jagata kāyavibhaktitāṃ ca darśenti sarvapariṣe bhuvi sarvaloke /
children.translated_text: According to the dispositions of beings, they display the analysis of bodies, in all assemblies, on earth, in all worlds;

children.text: vaśipratyayāśraya jinātmajaśrāvakānāṃ darśenti te sugatakāya vibhūṣitāṅgān // 26 //
children.translated_text: Depending on mastery, they display to the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> and <s>Śrāvakas</s> the <s>Sugata</s>-bodies with adorned limbs. // 26 //

children.text: sattvāṃśca kṣetra tatha karmavipāka kāyān āryāśrayān vividhadharmajñānakāyān /
children.translated_text: Beings, fields, <s>karma</s>, ripened fruits, bodies, the bases of the noble ones, the knowledge-bodies of the manifold <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: ākāśakāya vṛṣabhī samatāmupetaṃ darśenti ṛddhi vividhān jagatoṣaṇārtham // 27 //
children.translated_text: The space-body—the bulls [among sages], having attained equanimity, display manifold supernatural powers for the delight of beings. // 27 //

children.text: vaśitā daśo vimalajñānavicāraprāptā anuprāpta jñānakṛta maitrakṛpānukūlāḥ /
children.translated_text: The ten masteries attained, having reached the investigation of stainless knowledge, arrived at knowledge-work with loving-kindness and compassion,

children.text: yāvacca sarvajinadharmamupādakarmā trisaṃvaraiḥ susthitameka acalyakalpāḥ // 28 //
children.translated_text: And [having entered] the accomplishment of all <s>Jina</s>-<s>dharmas</s> as the preliminary work—by the three restraints, well-established, each one immovable. // 28 //

children.text: ye cā balā jinasutāna daśa akṣobhyā tehī upeta avibandhiya sarvamāraiḥ /
children.translated_text: And the ten unshakable powers of the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>—endowed with them, they cannot be bound by any <s>Māras</s>;

children.text: buddhairadhiṣṭhita namaskṛta śakrabrahmaistatha vajrapāṇibalakaiḥ satatānubaddhāḥ // 29 //
children.translated_text: Empowered by the <s>Buddhas</s>, honored by <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>, and constantly accompanied by <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> and the powerful ones. // 29 //

children.text: ima bhūmideśupagatā na guṇānamanto no śakyate kṣayitu kalpasahasrakoṭyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Established on this <s>bhūmi</s>, the teaching of their qualities has no end; it cannot be exhausted even in thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: te bhūya buddha niyutān samupāsayante bhonto utapta yatha bhūṣaṇu rājamūrdhni // 30 //
children.translated_text: They further attend upon <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>; they are heated [in merit] like a crown-jewel on the head of a king. // 30 //

children.text: ima bhūmideśupagatā vidu bodhisattvā mahabrahma bhonti sahasrādhipatī guṇāḍhyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Established on this <s>bhūmi</s>, the wise <s>Bodhisattvas</s> become great <s>Brahmā</s>s, lords of the thousand-fold [world], rich in qualities,

children.text: trayayānadeśana akṣobhyasaṃhāraprāptā maitrāyanaḥ śubhaprabhā jagakleśaghātī // 31 //
children.translated_text: Unshakable and unsurpassed in teaching the three vehicles, friendly in approach, of radiant splendor, destroyers of the defilements of the world. // 31 //

children.text: ekakṣaṇena daśakṣetraśataḥsahasrā yāvā rajodhātu tattaka samādhyupenti /
children.translated_text: In a single moment, they enter <s>samādhis</s> equal in number to hundreds of thousands of ten fields,

children.text: paśyanti tattaka daśadiśi sattvasārān bhūyo ataḥ praṇidhiśreṣṭha vyūha nekāḥ // 32 //
children.translated_text: And they see the essence of beings in the ten directions in that many [worlds]; beyond this, [they display] many peerless arrays through the excellence of their aspirations. // 32 //

children.text: saṃkṣepa eṣa nirdiṣṭo aṣṭamāyā jinātmajāḥ /
children.translated_text: This is spoken in brief regarding the eighth [<s>bhūmi</s>], O sons of the <s>Jinas</s>;

children.text: vistaraḥ kalpakoṭībhirna śakyaḥ sarva bhāṣitum // 33 //
children.translated_text: In detail, even in <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> it cannot all be spoken. // 33 //

body.text:
9 sādhumatī nāma navamī bhūmiḥ /
upakramagāthāḥ /
body.translated_text: 9. The ninth <s>bhūmi</s> is called <s>Sādhumatī</s> (Good Intelligence). Opening verses (<s>upakramagāthāḥ</s>):

children.text: imāṃ bhūmiṃ prabhāṣatā kampitāḥ kṣetrakoṭayaḥ /
children.translated_text: As this <s>bhūmi</s> was being taught, <s>koṭis</s> of fields trembled;

children.text: adhiṣṭhānā narendrasya aprameyā acintiyā // 1 //
children.translated_text: The empowerments of the Lord of Men [were] immeasurable and inconceivable. // 1 //

children.text: ābhāsa rucirā muktāḥ kāyataḥ sarvadarśino /
children.translated_text: Beautiful radiant lights were released from the body of the All-Seeing One;

children.text: tayāvabhāsitāḥ kṣetrāḥ sattvāśca sukhitāstayā // 2 //
children.translated_text: By them the fields were illuminated, and beings were made happy by that [light]. // 2 //

children.text: bodhisattvasahasrāṇi antarikṣe sthitāni ca /
children.translated_text: Thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, standing in the sky,

children.text: divyātikrāntapūjāya pūjyante vadatāṃ varam // 3 //
children.translated_text: With divine and supreme offerings, worship the best of speakers. // 3 //

children.text: maheśvarā devaputrā vaśavartī praharṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Maheśvara</s> and the <s>Devaputras</s>, the <s>Vaśavartin</s> [gods], delighted,

children.text: nānāprakārapūjābhiḥ pūjenti guṇasāgaram // 4 //
children.translated_text: With various kinds of offerings, worship the ocean of qualities. // 4 //

children.text: tato 'psaraḥsahasrāṇi harṣitāḥ prīṇitendriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then thousands of <s>Apsarases</s>, delighted, with joyful senses,

children.text: divyā suyattā saṃgītāḥ śāstu pūjāmajagrayam // 5 //
children.translated_text: With divine, well-performed music, performed the utmost worship of the Teacher. // 5 //

children.text: tebhyaśca tūryanādebhya anubhāvānmaharṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: From those musical sounds, through the power of the great sage,

children.text: īdṛśā rutasahasrā ravantī madhurasvarāḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text: Such thousands of sounds resound with sweet voices: // 6 //

children.text: imi sarve jinasutā khilamalavigatā upagata bhuvi varasuruciracaraṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: "All these sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, free from defilement and stain, have reached the <s>bhūmi</s> of excellent and radiant conduct;

children.text: jagahita vicarati daśadiśa vṛṣabhī darśayi jinacari khagasamamanasā // 7 //
children.translated_text: The bulls [among them] wander in the ten directions for the welfare of beings, displaying the <s>Jina</s>'s conduct with minds like birds [in the sky]. // 7 //

children.text: narapuri marupuri bhujagapativiṣaye viyuha daśadiśi puṇyabalamudīritāḥ /
children.translated_text: In the cities of men, the cities of gods, the domains of serpent-lords, arrayed in the ten directions, propelled by the power of merit,

children.text: tata tu bhuyu jinasuta darśayi atulī jinasutaprabhava jinanupathaniratā // 8 //
children.translated_text: There the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> further display the incomparable power of the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, devoted to the path of the <s>Jinas</s>. // 8 //

children.text: ekakṣetri acalita sarvakṣetravirajā anugata jagahita śaśiriva pratibhā /
children.translated_text: Unmoved in one field, free from dust in all fields, following the welfare of beings like the reflection of the moon,

children.text: sarvaghoṣahānacitta praśamitamanasā viyahari kṛtaśataśrutipathagiribhiḥ // 9 //
children.translated_text: With minds that have abandoned all sounds, with pacified minds, they dwell [as stable as] mountains traversed by hundreds of streams of learning. // 9 //

children.text: yatra sattva hīnacitta dīna mānaniratāstatra vidu śrāvakācarī deśeti vṛṣabhī /
children.translated_text: Where beings are of lowly mind, wretched, devoted to pride—there the wise bulls teach the conduct of <s>Śrāvakas</s>;

children.text: yatra sattva tīkṣṇacitta pratyayānaniratāstatra jñāna pratyayāna darśayanti virajā // 10 //
children.translated_text: Where beings are of sharp mind, devoted to the [investigation of] causes—there the dustless ones display the knowledge of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle. // 10 //

children.text: ye tu sattvahitamaitramanasā (abhiratās) tatra tyaṃ(tvaṃ) jinaputrāna darśayanti caraṇam /
children.translated_text: But those who are devoted to the welfare of beings with minds of loving-kindness—to them they display the conduct of the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>;

children.text: ye tu sattva agra śreṣṭha matimānaniratāstatra amī buddhakāya darśayanti atulam // 11 //
children.translated_text: And those beings who are foremost, excellent, devoted to intelligence—to them they display the incomparable body of the <s>Buddha</s>. // 11 //

children.text: māyā yathā māyakāro darśeti jagahite yāya koṭi naikavidyā sarvabhāvavigatā /
children.translated_text: Just as a magician displays [illusions] for the welfare of beings—the end of which is manifold knowledge, devoid of all [real] existence—

children.text: eva vidū buddhasutā jñānamāyaniratā darśayanti sarvacarī sarvabhāvavigatā // 12 //
children.translated_text: Even so the wise sons of the <s>Buddha</s>, devoted to the magic of knowledge, display all conduct, devoid of all [real] existence. // 12 //

children.text: etādṛśā rutasahasrān bhaṇitva madhurāṃstadā marukanyakā jinaṃ dṛṣṭvā tūṣṇīṃbhūtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having uttered such thousands of sweet sounds, the celestial maidens, seeing the <s>Jina</s>, became silent;

children.text: parṣadviprasanneyamavocatsugatātmajam aṣṭamāyā bhaṇa ūrdhvaṃ cariṃ saddharmarājinām // 13 //
children.translated_text: The delighted assembly said to the son of the <s>Sugata</s>: "Speak of the conduct above the eighth [<s>bhūmi</s>], of the kings of the true <s>Dharma</s>." // 13 //

body.text: upasaṃhāragāthāḥ /
body.translated_text: Summary verses (<s>upasaṃhāragāthāḥ</s>):

children.text: te apramāṇabalabuddhi vicārayantaḥ susūkṣmajñānaparamā jagatā durjñeyā /
children.translated_text: Those who investigate immeasurable powers and wisdom, supremely subtle in knowledge, hard for the world to know,

children.text: tatha guhyasthāna sugatāna samosaranto bhūmiṃ kramanti navamīṃ jagato 'rthakarīm // 14 //
children.translated_text: Entering the secret places of the <s>Sugatas</s>—they ascend to the ninth <s>bhūmi</s> that accomplishes the welfare of beings. // 14 //

children.text: te dhāraṇīmukhi samādhisamāhitāgrā vipulā abhijñā api kṣetrapraveśanantam /
children.translated_text: Foremost in <s>dhāraṇī</s>-doors and <s>samādhi</s>-concentration, with vast <s>abhijñās</s> (higher knowledges) and infinite entry into fields,

children.text: balajñānaniścayamapi jinu dhairyasthānaṃ praṇidhīkṛpāśayavidū navamotaranti // 15 //
children.translated_text: With the ascertainment of the powers and knowledge, and the <s>Jina</s>'s station of steadfastness, knowing aspirations and compassion—the wise ones ascend to the ninth. // 15 //

children.text: te atra bhūmyanugatā jinakośadhārī kuśalāśca dharmakuśalāśca avyākṛtāśca /
children.translated_text: Established on this <s>bhūmi</s>, bearers of the <s>Jina</s>'s treasury, [they know what is] wholesome, and what is skilled in <s>Dharma</s>, and what is indeterminate;

children.text: ye sāsravā api ca laukika ye ca āryāścintyā acintiya vidū anubuddhyayanti // 16 //
children.translated_text: What is with outflows, what is worldly, and what is noble—the inconceivable and the inconceivable, the wise ones realize. // 16 //

children.text: niyatāṃśca dharmaniyatāṃ pravicārayanti trayayānasaṃpadakriyā paritārayanti /
children.translated_text: They investigate the <s>dharmas</s> that are determined and destined, and deliver beings through the accomplishment of the three vehicles;

children.text: bhūmidharma yathā-adhimukti pracārataśca abhisaṃskaronti yatha lokya tathotaranti // 17 //
children.translated_text: According to the <s>bhūmi</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, dispositions, and conduct, they fashion [their teaching] as suits the worldly and the supramundane. // 17 //

children.text: te evajñānanugatā varasūkṣmabuddhī sattvāna cittagahanaṃ parimārgayanti /
children.translated_text: Those who have thus followed knowledge, with supremely subtle wisdom, search out the depth of beings' minds,

children.text: (cittaṃ vicitrakṣaṇavartanivartatāṃ ca) cittaṃ anantaprabhavaṃ sada otaranti // 18 //
children.translated_text: The mind that turns in the moments of variety—they always enter the mind that is of infinite arising. // 18 //

children.text: kleśānanādina prayogasahāyatāśca ye paryutthānanuśayā gatisaṃdhitaśca /
children.translated_text: The defilements, beginningless, accompanied by exertion, the manifest and latent [defilements], and those connected with destinies,

children.text: tatha karmapraveśa vicitravibhaktitaśca hetū niruddhaphalanāśa samotaranti // 19 //
children.translated_text: And the entry into manifold <s>karma</s> in its divisions—they enter the causes, the cessation, and the non-destruction of fruit. // 19 //

children.text: indriya yā mṛdukamadhya udārataśca saṃbhedapūrvamaparānta samotaranti /
children.translated_text: The faculties—mild, middling, and superior—they enter the differentiation of past, present, and future;

children.text: adhimukti naika vividhā śubha āśubhataśca catvāri āśīti sahasra samotaranti // 20 //
children.translated_text: The resolves, numerous and varied, wholesome and unwholesome—they enter the eighty-four thousand [types]. // 20 //

children.text: dhātūpraveśa jaga bhāvitakleśadṛṣṭī gahanaṃ gatā anavarāgra acchedataśca /
children.translated_text: The entry into the elements, beings cultivated by defilements and views, deep, gone beyond, without beginning or end, unbroken,

children.text: ye āśayā anuśayā sahajapracārī cittāsamosṛta nibaddha accheda tanti // 21 //
children.translated_text: The dispositions and latent tendencies, congenital in their activity—they enter the mind-outflow, bound, unbroken. // 21 //

children.text: cittaṃ yathā anuśayā na ca dravyabhūto na ca deśasthā na ca vipravasanti āśayā /
children.translated_text: The mind—how the latent tendencies [exist] without being a substance, and the dispositions do not abide in a place nor depart,

children.text: durheya dhyānaviṣayānabhivartiyāśca chedaśca mārga vinayena na cānyamasti // 22 //
children.translated_text: Hard to abandon, revolving in the domain of <s>dhyāna</s> and beyond—their cutting by the path and discipline, and no other [means]. // 22 //

children.text: upapatti ṣaḍgati vibhaktipraveśataśca snehaṃ ca tṛṣṇamavidyāndhaka karmakṣetrā /
children.translated_text: The rebirths, the six destinies in their divisions and entries, the attachment and craving, the darkness of ignorance, the field of <s>karma</s>,

children.text: vijñānabījasahajāṅkuranāmarūpaṃ traidhātuke anavarāgra samotaranti // 23 //
children.translated_text: The seed of consciousness, the congenital sprout of name-and-form—in the three realms, without beginning or end, they enter. // 23 //

children.text: te vāsanāgati kileśa ca karma cittā suvihāratāya na punargatisanta kāmā /
children.translated_text: The <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions), destinies, defilements, <s>karma</s>, and mind—for the sake of excellent abiding, having no further desire for rebirth,

children.text: rāśitribhirniyatasattva samotaranti dṛṣṭīnimagnamapi jñāna samotaranti // 24 //
children.translated_text: They enter the fixed beings by the three heaps; they enter knowledge even of those sunk in [wrong] views. // 24 //

children.text: evaṃ visaraṇagatāḥ sthita atra bhūmyāṃ sarvasattva āśaya yathendriya yādhimuktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus established on this <s>bhūmi</s>, having gone forth in all directions, according to the dispositions, faculties, and resolves of all beings,

children.text: teṣāmarthe dharmavibhakti prakāśayanti pratisaṃvidarthakuśalāḥ pratibhā nirukti // 25 //
children.translated_text: They illuminate the analysis of <s>Dharma</s> for their benefit—skilled in the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges): meaning, eloquence, and etymology. // 25 //

children.text: te dharmabhāṇaka gatī anuprāpta (sthānaṃ) siṃhariṣabhanibhā girirājakalpāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having reached the station of <s>Dharma</s>-speakers, like lions and bulls, like kings of mountains,

children.text: abhipravarṣanti madhuramamṛtasya varṣaṃ bhujagendrasāgara yathā anupūrayanti // 26 //
children.translated_text: They rain down the sweet rain of nectar, filling [beings] like the great serpent-lord [fills] the ocean. // 26 //

children.text: hitārthajñānakuśalāstatha dharmatāyāṃ sarvaṃ niruktyanugatāḥ pratibhānaprāptāḥ /
children.translated_text: Skilled in the knowledge of benefit and purpose, and in <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of things), following all etymologies, endowed with eloquence,

children.text: te dhāraṇī daśa asaṃkhyasahasra labdhā dhāranti dharma yatha (sāgara varṣadhārī) // 27 //
children.translated_text: Having obtained ten times innumerable thousands of <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, they retain the <s>Dharma</s> as the ocean [retains] the rain-streams. // 27 //

body.text: evaṃ ca dhāraṇiviśuddhisamādhiprāptā ekakṣaṇena daśabuddhasahasra dṛṣṭāḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, having attained the purity of <s>dhāraṇī</s> and <s>samādhi</s>, in a single moment they see ten thousand <s>Buddhas</s>,

body.text: śravaṇena dharmaratanaṃ ca nideśayanti (ekaikamaṇḍalaviśuddhisvarāṅgagatāḥ) // 28 //
body.translated_text: And through hearing, they expound the jewel of <s>Dharma</s>, having attained the purity of voice and limbs in each and every assembly-circle. // 28 //

children.text: vyohārate trisahasramahalokadhātuṃ pariśeṣa sattva vividhāstrayaratanebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: They pervade the <s>trisāhasra</s> great-thousand world-realm, and the remaining beings, various, from the Three Jewels;

children.text: toṣenti sarva yathaindriya-āśayāśca catudvīpasāgara varṣā sama modayanti // 29 //
children.translated_text: They satisfy all according to their faculties and dispositions, delighting [them] like the rains [satisfy] the ocean of the four continents. // 29 //

children.text: (bhūyottariṃ guṇinu vīrya samārabhante) citta-anti vālaprasara asmi sucetanantāḥ /
children.translated_text: They exert yet greater energy toward qualities; within the mind, to the extent of a hair-tip, they are of excellent awareness;

children.text: deśeyu dharma sugatāḥ puna nānasattvaṃ śrutvā dharema yatha sarvada (bījadhārī) // 30 //
children.translated_text: Should the <s>Sugatas</s> teach the <s>Dharma</s> again to manifold beings, having heard, they would retain it as [the earth retains] all seeds. // 30 //

children.text: (yāvatakā) jagadiha praviśanti sattvāḥ (te sarva ekapariṣanmaṇḍale niṣaṇṇāśca) /
children.translated_text: However many beings enter the world here, all of them seated in one assembly-circle—

children.text: eṣāṃ ca ekakṣaṇi sarvi samotaritvā ekāṃ rutena imi tarpayitavya sarve // 31 //
children.translated_text: Having entered into all of them in one moment, all of them are to be satisfied by one utterance. // 31 //

children.text: (atra sthitā naramaruttama dharmarājā) bhontī dharmairjinasutāḥ paricālayanti /
children.translated_text: Established here, they are kings of <s>Dharma</s>, supreme among men and gods; as sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, they move [beings] with their <s>dharmas</s>.

children.text: rātriṃdivaṃ sada jinaiḥ śamathānuprāptā gambhīra śānta sthita jñānavimokṣadhīrā // 32//
children.translated_text: Day and night, always having attained <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) through the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones), they are steadfast in profound, peaceful, and stable knowledge and liberation. (32)

children.text: (te 'nekabuddhaniyutān paryupāsayante) bhontī uttapta paṇu (pāṇḍu) cakravartaḥprabhāvā /
children.translated_text: (They attend upon countless millions of <s>Buddhas</s>), becoming radiant with the splendor of a <s>Cakravartin</s> (Universal Monarch),

children.text: tasya kleśagahanāni prabhā samājya brahmaṇo va dvisahasrikalokadhātuḥ // 33 //
children.translated_text: their radiance pervading the dense thickets of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), like <s>Brahmā</s> over a two-thousandfold world-system. (33)

children.text: (atra sthitā guṇadharā) mahabrahmaloke bhontī (triyānadeśanaṃ viditānubhāvā /
children.translated_text: (Abiding here, endowed with qualities and virtues) in the great <s>Brahma</s>-world, they become (those who understand the power of teaching the three vehicles,

children.text: ) yaṃ caivamārabhati sarvajagaddhitāya sarvajñajñānupagatā guṇajñānaprāptā // 34 //
children.translated_text: ) and whatever they undertake for the benefit of all beings, they have attained the knowledge of all qualities, approaching omniscient wisdom. (34)

children.text: (kṣetrāpramāṇaparyāpanna) ekā rajāgre kṣaṇi eki (tattakasamādhi u)penti dhīrāḥ /
children.translated_text: (Encompassing immeasurable fields) in a single moment, at the tip of a particle, the steadfast ones enter (that many <s>samādhis</s>),

children.text: (dṛṣṭvā sarve diśi jināṃśca vacaḥ śṛṇonti) tato vikurvi praṇidhānanvitāpramāṇāḥ // 35 //
children.translated_text: (seeing all the <s>Jinas</s> in every direction and hearing their words,) thence they manifest miraculous transformations, endowed with immeasurable <s>praṇidhānas</s> (vows). (35)

body.text: ityeṣā navamī bhūmirmahājñānavicāriṇā / gambhīrā durdṛśā sūkṣmā nirdiṣṭā sugatātmajāḥ // 36 //
body.translated_text: Thus this ninth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage), the domain of great wisdom, profound, hard to perceive, and subtle, has been taught, O sons of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One). (36)

body.text:
10 dharmameghā nāma daśamī bhūmiḥ /
upakramagāthāḥ /
body.translated_text:
10. The tenth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage) named <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of Dharma).
Introductory verses:

children.text: eva śrutva caraṇamanuttamaṃ śuddhavāsanayutāḥ praharṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus heard of this unsurpassed conduct, those joined with the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes) gods, delighted,

children.text: antarīkṣasthita prīṇitendriyāḥ pūjayanti sugataṃ tathāgatam // 1 //
children.translated_text: standing in the sky with gratified faculties, worship the <s>Sugata</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>. (1)

children.text: bodhisattvanayutā acintiyā antarīkṣagatiprāptiharṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Countless tens of thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, inconceivable, delighted at having attained the ability to travel through the sky,

children.text: gandhamegha atulān manomayān dhūpayanti sattvakleśaghātinaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: offer incomparable mind-made clouds of incense that destroy the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) of beings. (2)

children.text: devarāja vaśavarti prīṇito antarīkṣa trisahasrakoṭibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Devarāja</s> (King of Gods) <s>Vaśavartin</s>, delighted, with billions throughout the three-thousandfold sky,

children.text: vastrakaiḥ samakarī sagauravā bhrāmayanti rucirān varān śatam // 3 //
children.translated_text: reverently offers and waves about hundreds of excellent and beautiful garments. (3)

children.text: apsarā bahava prīṇitendriyāḥ pūjayanti sugataṃ sagauravāḥ /
children.translated_text: Numerous <s>apsarās</s> (celestial maidens) with gratified faculties worship the <s>Sugata</s> reverently,

children.text: tūryakoṭinayutāḥ pravāditā evarūpa ravuyukta rāvataḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: tens of millions of musical instruments are played, sounding with such melodious tones. (4)

children.text: ekakṣetra sugato niṣaṇṇakaḥ sarvakṣetri pratibhāsa darśayī /
children.translated_text: The <s>Sugata</s>, seated in a single field, displays reflections in all fields,

children.text: kāyakoṭi vividhā manoramā dharmadhātuvipulān spharitvana // 5 //
children.translated_text: manifold and delightful millions of bodies, pervading the vast <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality). (5)

children.text: ekaromu sugatasya raśmayo niścaranti jagakleśa śāmyati /
children.translated_text: From a single hair-pore of the <s>Sugata</s>, rays of light stream forth, pacifying the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) of the world,

children.text: śakyu (kṣetrarajadhātu 'pi) kṣayī tasya raśmigaṇanā tvajānitum // 6 //
children.translated_text: and even if the particles of dust in all (fields) were exhausted, the count of those rays could never be known. (6)

children.text: keci buddhavaralakṣaṇaṃ viduḥ paśyayanti varacakravartinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Some know the excellent marks of the <s>Buddha</s> and behold the supreme <s>Cakravartins</s> (Universal Monarchs),

children.text: anyakṣetravaracarya uttamāṃ śodhayanti dvipadendra dṛśyate // 7 //
children.translated_text: others purify the supreme conduct of excellent fields — the Lord of Bipeds is seen. (7)

body.text: (tuṣitāyatanaprāpta nāyako) cyavamānu caṃkramāṇa dṛśyate /
body.translated_text: (The Leader, having arrived at the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven,) is seen descending and walking about,

body.text: garbhaprāpta bahukṣetrakoṭiṣu jāyamāna kvaci kṣetra dṛśyate // 8 //
body.translated_text: having entered the womb in billions of fields, somewhere in a field he is seen being born. (8)

children.text: niṣkramanta jagahetu nāyako budhyamāna puna bodhimuttamām /
children.translated_text: The Leader goes forth for the sake of the world, again awakening to the supreme <s>bodhi</s> (enlightenment),

children.text: (dharmacakravartanirvṛtāgato) dṛśyamāna buddhakṣetrakoṭiṣu // 9 //
children.translated_text: (having arrived at turning the <s>Dharmacakra</s> and <s>nirvṛti</s>,) he is seen in billions of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. (9)

children.text: māyakāra yatha vidyaśikṣito jīvikārtha bahukāya darśayī /
children.translated_text: Just as a magician trained in his art displays many bodies for the sake of livelihood,

children.text: tadva śāstu varaprajñaśikṣito sarvakāyabhinihartu (sattvana) // 10 //
children.translated_text: so too the Teacher, trained in supreme <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), manifests all manner of bodies (for beings). (10)

children.text: śūnya śānta gatadharmalakṣaṇā antarīkṣasamaprāptadharmatām /
children.translated_text: Empty, peaceful, with the characteristics of all <s>dharmas</s> gone beyond, having attained a nature equal to space,

children.text: buddhaśāstu paramārthatattvataṃ darśayī pravarabuddhagocaram // 11 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddha</s>-Teacher shows the ultimate truth, displaying the domain of the supreme <s>Buddhas</s>. (11)

children.text: yatha svabhāvu sugatānagocarā sarvasattva tatha prāpta dharmatām /
children.translated_text: Just as the own-nature of the <s>Sugatas</s> is their domain, so all beings have attained that same <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature);

children.text: lakṣalakṣa samalakṣa tādṛśā sarvadharma paramārthalakṣaṇāḥ // 12 //
children.translated_text: marked and unmarked, of equal character — such are the ultimate characteristics of all <s>dharmas</s>. (12)

children.text: ye tu jñāna sugatāna arthiṃke kalpakalpaparikalpavarjitam /
children.translated_text: Those who desire the knowledge of the <s>Sugatas</s>, free from conceptual elaboration upon elaboration,

children.text: bhāvabhāvasamabhāvabuddhayaḥ kṣipra bheṣyati nareśa uttamāḥ // 13 //
children.translated_text: with understanding of the equality of existence and non-existence, they shall swiftly become supreme lords among men. (13)

children.text: īdṛśān rutasahasrān bhaṇitva madhurasvarāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having uttered thousands of such melodious sounds with sweet voices,

children.text: marukanyā jinaṃ lokya tūṣṇībhūtāḥ śame ratāḥ // 14 //
children.translated_text: the celestial maidens, gazing upon the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One), became silent, delighting in tranquility. (14)

children.text: prasannaṃ parṣadaṃ jñātvā mokṣacandro viśāradaḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowing the assembly to be faithful, the wise <s>Mokṣacandra</s> (Moon of Liberation)

children.text: vajragarbhaṃ tridhāpṛcchajjinaputraṃ viśāradam // 15 //
children.translated_text: questioned <s>Vajragarbha</s>, the learned son of the <s>Jina</s>, in three ways: (15)

children.text: daśamī saṃkramantānāṃ kīdṛśaṃ guṇagocaram /
children.translated_text: "For those who are crossing over to the tenth [stage], what is the range of their qualities,

children.text: nimittaprātihāryāṃśca sarvamākhyā(hi) parikrama // 16 //
children.translated_text: and what are the signs and miraculous displays? Explain all of this in order." (16)

body.text: atha khalu vajragarbho bodhisattvo daśadiśaṃ vyavalokya sarvāvatīṃ parṣadaṃ vyavalokya dharmadhātuṃ ca vyavalokayan sarvajñatācittotpādaṃ ca saṃvarṇayan bodhisattvaviṣayamādarśayan caryābalaṃ pariśodhayan sarvākārajñatāsaṃgrahamanuvyāharan sarvalokamalamapakarṣayan sarvajñajñānamupasaṃharan acintyajñānaniryūhamādarśayan bodhisattvaguṇān prabhāvayan evameva bhūmyarthaṃ prarūpayamāṇo buddhānubhāvena tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s>, surveying the ten directions, surveying the entire assembly, contemplating the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), extolling the arising of the mind directed toward omniscience, displaying the domain of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, purifying the power of conduct, expounding the collection of knowledge of all aspects, removing the defilements of all worlds, gathering omniscient knowledge, displaying the emergence of inconceivable wisdom, and manifesting the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s> — thus elucidating the meaning of the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages), by the power of the <s>Buddhas</s>, at that moment spoke these verses:

body.text: upasaṃhāragāthāḥ /
body.translated_text: Summary verses:

children.text: śamadamaniratānāṃ śāntadāntāśayānāṃ khagapathasadṛśānāmantarīkṣasamānām /
children.translated_text: Of those who delight in <s>śama</s> (tranquility) and <s>dama</s> (self-restraint), whose dispositions are peaceful and controlled, who are like the path of birds, equal to space,

children.text: khilamanavidhutānāṃ mārgajñāne sthitānāṃ śṛṇuta cariviśeṣān bodhisattvāna śreṣṭhān // 17 //
children.translated_text: whose minds have shaken off all rigidity, who are established in the knowledge of the path — hear the distinguished conduct of the foremost <s>bodhisattvas</s>! (17)

children.text: kuśalaśatasahasraṃ saṃciyā kalpakoṭyā buddhaśatasahasrān pūjayitvā maharṣīn /
children.translated_text: Having accumulated hundreds of thousands of wholesome deeds over countless <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), having worshipped hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, the great sages,

children.text: pratyayajinavaśīṃścāpūjayitvā anantān sarvajagatahitāyā jāyate bodhicittam // 18 //
children.translated_text: and having worshipped the infinite <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> and sovereign <s>Jinas</s>, for the benefit of all the world, <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) arises. (18)

children.text: vratatapatapitānāṃ kṣāntipāraṃgatānāṃ hiriśiricaritānāṃ puṇyajñānodgatānām /
children.translated_text: Of those who have undergone vows and austerities, who have reached the perfection of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), whose conduct is marked by modesty and splendor, who have risen through merit and knowledge,

children.text: vipulagatimatīnāṃ buddhajñānāśayānāṃ daśabalasamatulyaṃ jāyate bodhicittam // 19 //
children.translated_text: of those with vast course and intellect, whose aspiration is for <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge — <s>bodhicitta</s> arises, equal to the power of the Ten-Powered One. (19)

children.text: yāva jina triyadhvā pūjanārthāya pūjaṃ khagapathapariṇāmaṃ śodhanaṃ sarvakṣetram /
children.translated_text: For the purpose of worshipping the <s>Jinas</s> of the three times with offerings, for the purification of all fields through the transformation like the path of birds,
